president-in-office of the council.– mr president, let me first say that i appreciate the many comments made during this this debate. i also understand some of the frustrations that were expressed by many members of different political persuasions. it is clear that the management of the flow of asylum seekers into europe is a stress test for all of us, for our countries and for the confidence within and between our societies. it makes no sense to use the asylum seeker debate for narrow political agendas or narratives. that is a luxury we simply cannot afford. blame games are easily played, and simplistic solutions are easily found, for what is in reality a very complex humanitarian problem. in my view, european cooperation and solidarity remain key. i agree with the many colleagues here who have said it is very good to have a lot on paper, but the question is how we put it into action. the presidency is extremely active with the member states in putting conclusions into action with turkey and greece on screening and border controls. concerning the western balkan road, we are working in partnership with lebanon and jordan to – as, i think, ms piri said – come up with a model which ends the cynical business model of smugglers, the reason why people are killed on the seas. that is what we have to stop, and it turns out to be a little bit more complex than we thought. i share all the frustrations that people have expressed here tonight – people are still dying on the seas every day. maybe there is no white smoke yet, but pessimistic panic does not help. there is no reason for complacency. let me say a few words about values, a few words about hot spots, about questions that were raised as to the future of schengen on the principle of non-refoulement and on the issue of turkey. first, on values. the point made here by most members, although others will not agree, is that we are faced with a stress test of our european values. we all have to realise that we cannot be comforted by the reactions on this issue in our societies from all sides right now. the council is perfectly aware of the difficult situation of refugees massively fleeing conflict regions or migrants who, for other reasons, are trying to reach to europe. we will do everything possible to improve the situation. i think mr pittella spoke about that. these are our values that are at stake, but the values are not so easy to put into practice, because it leads to confrontations in our societies, to fear and then to reactions to this fear. we will, therefore, have to balance the different identities that we have in our societies in a manner consistent with our democratic values. we could talk about it for much longer but it is key that we realise that together we must try to build a consensus around this. i have heard a lot of opposing views on this, and this is very legitimate; it is a common problem. we will have to search for solutions in our societies to deal with this. on external policy and external values, i can mention some measures that have already been adopted, such as the support given by the eu budget and by member states in particular to help the unhcr to respond to the needs of refugees in camps established close to their places of origin, in particular in iraq, jordan, lebanon and turkey. just yesterday i came back from addis ababa where i discussed this with the african union. discussions, and more, are also taking place about how we can conduct very practical follow-up to the valletta agreement. the commission is also providing additional support to its partners operating in origin or transit countries outside the european union. in parallel to these measures, the european union is contributing to the development of safe and sustainable reception capacities in the affected regions and the provision of lasting prospects and adequate procedures for refugees and their families until they can be returned to their country of origin, if possible. if necessary, we will examine and adopt measures aimed at improving their situation. a lot more can be said about the origins of this crisis as well, but we can leave that for another debate when we will discuss issues around syria and conflict resolution there. on hot spots, yes, it is true that progress has been too slow. we can all agree on this. a network of hot spots in italy and greece is a cornerstone of the eu’s efforts to ease the migratory pressure, ensure the identification of those third-country nationals in real need of international protection and facilitate return operations. well-functioning hot spots are crucial to stemming the migration flows and ultimately safeguard the schengen area. the european council expects a commission report assessing the progress in the set-up of the hot spot areas which will update the information presented in december 2015, and the council itself is also monitoring the situation on the ground, through integrated political crisis response (ipcr) reports. we are very proactive at the moment because that is a challenge right now. if you want to translate the declarations into actions you have to be very hands-on. in the european union we are used to more long-term issues of development and of development cooperation. here we have to react immediately, and our systems are not necessarily used to that, so we have to change that. with that hands-on way of working we can also counter some of the legitimate criticisms on things that are going too slowly. without prejudice to the commission’s upcoming report, we can say that since december progress has been achieved. we should also recognise this. in italy, two new additional locations were declared operational, in pozzallo in sicily and in trapani, and in greece work is under way to ensure that two hot spot areas, in theos and leros, are made operational soon. furthermore, the reception capacities in both italy and greece have increased, including through the support of member states and the specialised eu and un agencies. we are not there yet, but we must pursue this effort with renewed commitment, and we expect the european council to deliver a strong message to all relevant actors to make quick progress on the reception and identification of migrants. italy, for instance, reportedly now has a rate of 100% for registration and fingerprinting. this is important progress. it has also ensured that disembarkation is done via the hot spots. greece has informed us that migrants can only leave the hot spot areas by ferry if they can present registration papers. greece has put in place a number of measures to increase the security of documents and to check if the migrant is indeed registered. greece should also receive additional eurodac machines in the coming days. a lot of questions were raised around schengen, and correctly so. it is one of the cornerstones and success stories of european cooperation, if not european integration. the continuing flow of migrants over the past months has seen several countries temporarily re-imposing border controls – germany, followed by austria, denmark, finland, the netherlands, norway, slovakia and sweden. this temporary reintroduction of border controls is in line with the schengen acquis, subject to strict conditions involving a serious threat to public policy or internal security and time limitations. that is an issue. the migration pressure has not decreased, and time is running out. the only way to go beyond the maximum time limit during which internal border controls may be carried out is to adopt a council recommendation based on a commission proposal under article 26 of the schengen borders code. this is a scenario that involves an elaborate procedure under the schengen evaluation mechanism. this scenario should result in a series of measures protecting the overall functioning of the schengen system, a system which is at the heart of the european project and one of its greatest achievements, as i mentioned. on this basis, the eu interior ministers discussed the matter informally in amsterdam on 25 and 26 january 2015. there was broad support for inviting the commission to make a proposal for a recommendation under article 26 of the schengen borders code. we are committed. the presidency is committed to maintaining the schengen system. it will do all it can to find, in cooperation with the commission, parliament and the member states concerned, a solution to the current problems. coming back to the principle of non-refoulement, there were quite a few remarks on this issue. this remains a key principle of our politics. in order to ease the migratory pressure on front-line member states and to ensure the identification of those third-country nationals in real need of international protection, the council is working hard to operationalise the network of hot spots and to speed up the implementation of the relocation and resettlement mechanisms adopted in 2015. in that context, the issue of non-refoulement remains extremely important and a principle. on turkey, the establishment of the eu common list of safe countries of origin is, as many have stated here this afternoon, a very complex issue and one that the council preparatory bodies are currently discussing. the final decision will have to be reached later on the basis of a very precise assessment on the eu-turkey joint action plan, as welcomed by the european council at its meeting in october. this is, as you know, part of a comprehensive cooperation agenda based on shared responsibility, mutual commitment and delivery. i just wanted to answer a question from mr verhofstadt. this does not mean that money is automatically sent to the turkish government. that is not the case. we are in the process of working with the turkish government on assurances that this is not a blank cheque to the turkish government but funding for programmes that have to alleviate the conditions of refugees in turkey. i think mr olbrycht also mentioned the mff in this context. we had a conference in amsterdam last week where many speakers argued that the migration crisis demonstrates the need for more flexibility in the eu budget to allow us to have the resources available to meet unexpected challenges. we will try to move that forward within the time that we have in our presidency to see how much more flexibility we can bring to our budget, something which is so badly needed in this crisis.
in writing. we must now bring order out of chaos and stop the national football panic. some people think we should push refugees back to the open sea, others think we should open fire at the border. that is not how we see it at all. our priority remains to ensure that people do not drown at sea and that we have a handle on the flow of refugees. there's only one way to do that. the deployment of an eu border and coast guard to monitor the external borders and assess applications at hotspots at the external borders. we need to combine that with closer cooperation with turkey and investment in the refugee camps in syria's neighbouring countries, so that the living conditions there improve dramatically and the number of people coming here decreases dramatically. those plans are on the table. it is high time that at the next european summit in two weeks' time, we took big steps forward. we must stop blaming each other and the greek government must finally agree to european support for border control. if we do not, it will be at the expense of the most vulnerable, the war refugees, who need our help the most.

i do not think we need to repeat that endocrine disruptors are of course a matter of great concern, not only here in this parliament but to the population as a whole. it's about products that we use every day in clothing, furniture, electronics, adhesives, cosmetics, you name it, and so they're present every day. it is therefore essential that we remove this uncertainty and finally come up with clear scientifically based criteria. it is very good that you are announcing here that you will be putting those criteria into practice shortly before the summer, and as soon as possible, and it is also very good that we will be communicating very broadly and very clearly about this. it seems that everything is bad now and that nothing has happened yet, but perhaps it is useful to point out that we already have strict rules - you have already referred to this, commissioner - for the use of chemicals in toys and in plastics. and of course we have the reach regulations, which are systematically investigating the impact of endocrine disruptors. but it is indeed time now to take those steps forward. the judges' verdict - you said it yourself - leaves no doubt. in the context of maximum consumer protection, we must take these steps now so that not only consumers but also producers know what they are facing in the short term and so that they know what alternatives they have to come up with.
the whole headache about the criteria, the postponement and the conviction, of course, has everything to do with the lobby of the chemical industry. part of the controversy in this discussion is the industry's argument to bring in potency as one of the criteria. that's a perfidious political ploy to say, only the most potent, the strongest hormone disruptors can be considered. inspector, i have two bottles here, a bottle of poire williams eau de vie from france, 43 degrees. i have a bottle of belgian beer, a duvel, 8.5 alcohol. would you dare to say, commissioner, that the poire williams is alcohol and the bottle of duvel is not? well, that's exactly what the industry is trying to do with hormone disruptors. the hormonal disruptors with the most potency, the strongest, those will become hormonal disruptors and the others will not. commissioner, you know that we have a veto on the criteria you will put forward. i warn you that our group will veto the criteria if they mention potential.
the commission has already made a number of proposals to this effect. a lot of everyday objects contain what are called endocrine disruptors. think of the frying pan we use to cook, the painted wooden floor we walk on barefoot, the plastic butter bread box we take to school with our children, or the pesticides we use to protect our crops. the consequences of exposure to these substances may - as has been said many times - include infertility, breast cancer and diabetes. the commission has already made a number of proposals in this area. in december the ecj delivered the judgment just discussed; the commission therefore considered that scientific criteria for these substances should have been established by the end of 2013 at the latest. i pointed this out in a request for a written answer last year. so basically, it's about getting these dangerous substances strictly regulated, because there's really strong evidence that these substances are harmful and also have serious social consequences. for example, relevant economic studies have shown that the diseases caused cost our health budgets nearly 160 billion euros a year. a strict and appropriate legal framework can therefore contribute to a much better protection of human health. and that's exactly the precautionary principle. if there is the slightest doubt that an active substance is harmful to health, that active substance cannot be authorised in europe. it should be that simple. i therefore appeal to the commission to be the advocate of consumers and not the advocate of the big chemical companies. i'm sure the latter will find alternatives.
madam president, i imagine that 16 december 2015 will remain a date etched on the commission's tablets. this is the first time that the european court of justice has condemned the commission for failing to fulfil its obligations in the matter of endocrine disruptors. a fine thing, you'll admit, for the guardian of the treaties... however, the scientific community and the european parliament have long warned against the harmful effects of these substances on health. i abstained on the reach regulation ten years ago, in 2006, precisely because these endocrine disruptors were not defined by objective criteria. it has been ten years, commissioner, ten long years, and, strangely enough, three years now, since the commission has been obliged to provide these criteria. i listened to you very carefully, you said... "we have the firm intention to comply with the judgment of the court before summer". we take note, commissioner, but we will remain vigilant, vigilant as the sioux. you haven't given us any reason to trust you.
in writing. i would like to denounce the european commission for its inertia in the endocrine disruptors issue. these can cause cancer, hormonal imbalance, impaired sperm quality, and premature puberty. the commission, by not publishing the scientific criteria for defining these disruptors and by not proposing an update of the legislation, has become outlawed in the eyes of european law. worse still, the european commission, by its ineffectiveness in this matter, bears a share of responsibility for each new victim caused by this scourge which affects the health of millions of europeans. the commission, which was found guilty by the court of justice of the european union, justified its decision by stating that it was prepared to carry out an impact assessment. what a bad joke! the commission would like to save time and play into the hands of the industrial mega-groups which it would not otherwise have taken up. it is unacceptable to treat the health of europeans with such disrespect! science must continue its research, but the citizen must not be a guinea pig! we must regulate these substances!
on behalf of the alde group. madam president, i will immediately echo mr groote's remarks. so far, clinical trials have always had good press. those who participate, often medical staff or medical students, are happy to contribute to biomedical research. then there was this accident in rennes on sunday, january 10: one death and five people hospitalized during the testing of a painkiller product carried out in phase 1, that is, on a small group of healthy volunteers. an extremely rare, but serious, accident, which justifies our discussing it tonight. i would also like to express my deepest sympathy to the families of the victims and to those who are still fighting for their health. this is an opportunity to remind you that these clinical trials are more than ever an essential step before any medicines are put on the market and that europe must remain a strong player in this research. i hope that my country of origin, belgium, which produces 15% of european medicines, will continue to be recognised for its expertise in this field. i would also like to ask our commissioner two questions on transparency. is it true, commissioner, that the publication of all drug test results, one of the key measures of the new european regulation that parliament has negotiated so hard, is being postponed from may 2016 to 2018? is it also true that the current trend in laboratories in europe is to set up parallel groups in phase 1, i.e. groups where patients are given a higher dose straight away without any prior testing? in any case, this is what happened in rennes, the six victims being precisely those who had received the so-called higher doses. we know that europe is facing increasing competition from elsewhere in this sector, but you will of course agree with us that the race to validate its clinical trials should never be at the expense of the health and safety of european citizens.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the proposal for a regulation on the application of the safeguard clause and the anti-circumvention mechanism allowing for the temporary suspension of the tariff preferences provided for in the association agreement between the european union and the european atomic energy community and their member states, of the one part, and the republic of moldova, of the other part. the purpose of this proposal is to create the legal instrument allowing the application of the safeguard clause and the anti-circumvention mechanism provided for in the agreement already concluded with moldova. as regards safeguard measures, they could only be adopted if the product concerned is imported into the union in such increased quantities and under such conditions as to cause or threaten to cause serious injury to union producers of like or directly competing products. as regards the anti-circumvention mechanism, the proposed regulation provides for the possibility of suspending preferential customs duties for a period of up to six months when imports of certain agricultural and processed agricultural products reach the annual import volumes defined in the agreement. implementing powers shall be conferred on the commission in order to ensure uniform conditions for the adoption of safeguard measures.
in writing. the introduction of safeguard measures is a mandatory step to protect our companies from possible abuses and to prevent any negative impact on the european market. the safeguard clause provided for in that report allows the temporary suspension of the application of the tariff preferences provided for in the association agreement between the union and moldova in the event that, following the elimination of the tariff barriers concerning them, certain products from moldova are imported into the union in excess quantities, thus causing economic injury to european producers. on the other hand, the anti-circumvention mechanism is important to prevent imports into the union of non-moldovan products via moldova, thus benefiting from the benefits of the agreement, from circumventing the obligations on rules of origin. this mechanism allows the reintroduction of the mfn rate when the volume of imports of certain agricultural products from moldova exceeds a certain ceiling without a valid justification of their exact origin. this mechanism therefore imposes an obligation of transparency on rules of origin when the volume of imports is high, thus protecting european companies from possible abuses.
in writing. ‒ the association agreement between the european union and the republic of moldova was signed on 24 june 2014 and has been provisionally applied since 1 september 2014. it introduces a preferential regime for trade in goods, creating a deep free trade area. council regulation (ec) no 55/2008 establishes autonomous trade preferences for the republic of moldova and will continue to apply in parallel until 31 december 2015. the eu is moldova's largest trading partner, accounting for 46.4% of its trade, followed by russia (21.9%) and ukraine (11.8%). trade with moldova represents 0.1% of the total trade of the union. the commission established the volume of imports from the prc on the basis of eurostat data. the latter represent a significant share of all union imports from moldova. the main exports from moldova to the union are oilseeds, nuts, apple juice and cereals, while the union mainly exports spirits, certain fruits and vegetables such as citrus fruits, as well as pork and feed.
in writing. ‒ a regulation of the european parliament and of the council is needed to incorporate these instruments into eu law and to allow the application of the bilateral safeguard clause and the anti-circumvention mechanism. the association agreement with moldova, like most of our trade agreements, contains a bilateral safeguard clause. this instrument allows the temporary suspension of preferences in the event of an unforeseen and significant increase in imports and economic injury to the domestic industry of the importing party (in other words, it allows either the suspension of further tariff liberalization or the reintroduction of the most-favoured-nation tariff rate). the agreement also provides for an 'anti-circumvention mechanism' which allows the reintroduction of the most-favoured-nation tariff rate when the volume of imports of certain agricultural products from moldova exceeds a certain ceiling without a valid justification of their exact origin.
in writing. ‒ the adoption of the safeguard clause and the anti-circumvention mechanism is necessary in the context of the association agreement with moldova to enforce certain obligations and, if necessary, to protect european producers or directly competing companies against a sudden increase in imports of a particular product that could cause them serious damage.
in writing. i welcome the adoption by the european parliament of the report on the establishment of an anti-circumvention mechanism with regard to georgia. as in the case of moldova, it is important to protect european companies from possible abuse of the tariff preferences granted under the association agreement with georgia. the mechanism, which is designed to limit the risk of customs duty evasion through transit through georgia, sets thresholds above which the tariff preferences provided for in the agreement may be suspended. this is essential in order to preserve our businesses. the anti-circumvention mechanism for sensitive agricultural products thus allows the reintroduction of the most-favoured-nation rate of customs duty when the volume of imports of certain agricultural products from georgia exceeds a specified ceiling without their exact origin being validly justified.
in writing. ‒ the association agreement between the european union and georgia was signed on 27 june 2014. the agreement introduces an ambitious preferential regime for trade in goods between the two parties, by establishing a deep free trade area. the union is now georgia's largest trading partner, with 27.2% of its trade with the union (neighbouring turkey and azerbaijan occupying second and third places respectively). at the same time, trade with georgia represents 0.1% of the total trade of the union. the eu-georgia association agreement discussed this afternoon provides for an 'anti-circumvention mechanism' which allows the most-favoured-nation tariff rate to be reintroduced when the volume of imports of certain agricultural products from georgia exceeds a certain ceiling without their exact origin being validly justified. it is necessary that a regulation of the european parliament and of the council establishes, within the framework of union law, the instrument for applying the anti-circumvention mechanism.
in writing. ‒ this report will help to improve parliamentary scrutiny of the commission's implementation of the common commercial policy and its transparency. the proposal for a regulation requires the commission to submit to the co-legislators, before making it public, an annual report on the application and implementation of the regulation. the european parliament may invite the commission to attend an ad hoc meeting of its committee responsible in order to explain or make explicit any point relating to the implementation of the regulation.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this anti-circumvention mechanism because it provides for the possible reintroduction of customs duties when imports of agricultural products from georgia exceed certain thresholds without adequate clarification of the exact origin of these products.
in writing. the european union and the member states signed the marrakesh treaty in april 2014 and have made a political commitment to ratify it. the aim of this treaty is to facilitate access to published works by the blind, visually impaired and other print disabled. the world health organization estimated in 2010 that there were 2.5 million blind people and 23.8 million visually impaired people in all of europe. moreover, only 5% of all books published in developed countries and less than 1% in developing countries are produced in accessible formats. the european union should therefore be encouraged to take all appropriate measures to ratify and implement this treaty as soon as possible and also to ask the council and the member states to speed up the ratification process. i support this project because it is important that the right of disabled people to education without discrimination and on the basis of equal opportunities is respected.
in writing. ‒ the marrakesh treaty aims to facilitate access to books and other printed matter for blind or visually impaired people. in europe, there are more than 26.35 million citizens who are visually impaired or blind. however, only 5% of all books published in the member states (and... less than 1% in developing countries) are produced in accessible formats. the text i voted for deplores the fact that seven member states of the union have formed a blocking minority to obstruct the process of ratification of the treaty and calls on the council to speed up ratification.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution which, on the one hand, recalls that articles 24 and 30 of the un convention emphasise the right of persons with disabilities to education, without discrimination and on the basis of equal opportunities, and the need to ensure that laws protecting intellectual property rights do not constitute an unreasonable or discriminatory barrier to access by persons with disabilities to cultural goods, and, on the other hand, notes with deep indignation that seven member states of the european union have constituted a minority bloc obstructing the treaty ratification process. we call on the council and the member states to speed up the ratification process without making ratification conditional on the revision of the union's legal framework or the decision of the court of justice of the european union.
in writing. ‒ the resolution calls on the council to speed up the ratification process of the marrakesh treaty as a matter of urgency, given that it was signed two and a half years ago. at the same time, we also call on those member states which have not yet ratified the convention to do so as a matter of urgency. that is why i voted for this resolution.

in writing. ‒ this resolution not only opposes the admission of a specific gmo to the eu market, but advocates a de facto moratorium on gmos pending a new approval procedure and an amendment to regulation (ec) no 1829/2003. the n-va did not support the objection. the approval procedure for gmos is strict. the efsa risk assessment plays a crucial role in this. the n-va strongly believes in science-based and evidence-based policy. approval of the text presented would undermine the credibility of the efsa. in addition, the european commission did not exceed its mandate in this implementing act: if the member states do not reach a qualified majority, the european commission is empowered to approve the gmo on the basis of a positive opinion from efsa. it is noted that there is no scientific consensus on glyphosate. i recognize the concerns about glyphosate and i call for a thorough discussion of this controversial substance. it is important to distinguish between gmo technology and application. it is also clear that the (possible) use of gmos must always be part of an agricultural policy that integrates the protection of human health, the environment and biodiversity, where an integrated pest management system is essential for the sustainable use of pesticides and non-chemical alternatives.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the objection of the european parliament's committee on the environment, public health and food safety (envi) against three european commission decisions authorising the marketing of feed containing transgenic soybeans produced by monsanto and bayer. these three genetically modified soya beans have the unique ability to tolerate herbicides containing glyphosate, including monsanto's roundup, a substance classified as a probable carcinogen by the world health organization. considers that the three authorisation decisions are not compatible with the european union's objectives in the field of human and animal health, as defined in legislative texts. that is why i welcome today's vote and the clear majority in the european parliament to veto the marketing of genetically modified soy products.
in writing. when the international agency for research on cancer (iarc) published its full study at the end of july 2015, the european commission asked the european food safety authority (efsa) to take it into account in its assessment of the renewal of glyphosate at european level. a belgian toxicology expert also collaborated in the analysis of this study by efsa. the commission finally published its opinion on glyphosate on 12 november 2015 and concluded that glyphosate is unlikely to be carcinogenic to humans. efsa has based its assessment on the report of the rapporteur member state, germany, but also on relevant studies published over the last 10 years and with the collaboration of representatives of member states' risk assessment bodies. this conclusion, although contrary to the iarc's opinion, confirms the conclusions of the majority of international toxicological bodies.

in writing. the reasons why the european food safety authority (efsa) does not agree with the international agency for research on cancer (iarc) opinion that glyphosate is genotoxic and could be a "probable" cause of cancer in humans are questionable. this is because these two bodies have a different approach to the classification of chemicals. the eu system evaluates each individual chemical substance and each commercial mixture separately. the iarc assesses generic agents, including related chemical groups, as well as occupational or environmental exposure, and cultural or behavioural practices. in the context of gmos, a precautionary and science-based approach is required.
in writing. ‒ the european parliament voted by 201 votes to one against the placing on the market of mon 87705 x mon 89788 soybeans. behind this series of numbers is a glyphosate-tolerant gmo. however, this active substance, which is found in commercial products such as the weed killer roundup, was classified as a 'probable carcinogen' for humans on 20 march 2015 by the world health organisation. and more specifically, by his international cancer research center. the scientific battle is still as fierce, however, as the european food safety authority recently considered the risk posed by glyphosate unlikely. meps are clearly at odds with efsa on the subject. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of genetically modified organisms. the political signal from the meps is clear, but in the absence of a veto it has no effect on the commission's discretionary right to authorize genetically modified soybeans, rapeseed or maize on a case-by-case basis. the european parliament must think about changing its strategy.
in writing. ‒ this afternoon i voted for the european commission not to allow the use of three genetically modified soya beans that tolerate glyphosate in food and feed products. glyphosate is a herbicide classified as a 'probable carcinogen' by the world health organisation (who) since 20 march 2015. the three genetically modified soya beans that have already been authorised by the european commission in food and feed products are fg72, mon 87708 x mon 89788 and mon 87705 x mon 89788. in the vote today i supported each of the three objections which call for their rejection.

in writing. ‒ i voted against the objection to accepting the genetically modified soybean. we must rely on science and our european food safety authority. they believe this crop is safe. with a growing population and increasing climate threats, we need modern plant breeding in europe. among other things, these modern techniques for growing crops and other plants can contribute to a better diet for the world's population and a better climate.
the emissions from cars, especially those of particulate matter and nitrogen, are particularly harmful to public health. the recent environmental performance index from yale and columbia universities in the united states shows that belgium scores particularly poorly on air pollution. every year, 12 000 people die prematurely, mainly from particulate matter. in flanders, the flemish government is making efforts to tackle this problem by greening the auto taxation system. a low-emission zone is being developed in the city of antwerp. however, more european action is needed, as the eu's strict legislation to limit harmful emissions has not yet led to much improvement in practice, mainly because of the lack of practical tests to measure real emissions on the road. we need to get those field tests done as soon as possible. however, linking these to a relaxation of the euro 6 standard is unacceptable. a better agreement is necessary and technically feasible. there are european engines that meet the euro 6 standard of 80 milligrams of nitrogen per kilometer. encouraging that innovation is essential and for those reasons i supported the objection.

in writing. ‒ the present objection is directed against a decision of the european commission and the member states which provides that in future the measurement of vehicle exhaust gas values will no longer be carried out in the laboratory but also in road traffic. instead of allowing the original 50% exceedance of the applicable limits, deviations of more than twice that amount (a correction factor of 2,1) were agreed until 2020. the majority of the environment committee in the european parliament then considered that correction factor too generous and put this objection to the vote in plenary. i have agreed to this objection because i am in favour of strict and clear emission standards and appropriate controls to protect consumer health and the environment. the automotive industry should also learn that it too has to follow established rules, which in turn can create a surge of innovation that drives our economy forward.

in writing. ‒ on wednesday, the european parliament rejected an objection to an increase in the maximum limits for nitrogen oxides (nox) emitted by diesel cars. i personally supported this objection, as i had done in the vote in the committee on the environment last december. the commission's resignation is a real sign of pressure from certain member states, which, more concerned with the interests of car manufacturers than the health of millions of europeans, proposed at a technical committee last october that the euro 6 emission standards, which they themselves had negotiated with parliament in 2007, be exceeded by 110% in 2017 and then by 50% from 2020. it was precisely to reject this absurd initiative that parliament had to decide: it was 59 votes short of rejecting this highly political decision, which is difficult to understand, especially since it is part of the wake of the vw engine rigging scandal. finally, the very existence of the euro 6 standard is called into question: what good is a standard that is allowed to be exceeded, or worse, cast in bronze?
in writing. ‒ this objection by the european parliament to block a decision by the european commission to accept nitrogen oxide standards up to 110% higher than what is allowed by european legislation (euro 6) was unfortunately rejected this afternoon. i regret its rejection because it was in particular a response to the pressure exerted by the european parliament after the volkswagen scandal. the objection, raised by the european parliament's committee on the environment, public health and food safety, considered the commission's decision to be illegal, a view which was further confirmed by the european parliament's legal services and then by the parliament's committee on legal affairs. this decision was drawn up by experts from the commission and the member states. it found that car manufacturers did not appear to be able to meet the emission standards for nitrogen oxides set out in the euro 6 standard and allowed them to exceed those emission standards for nitrogen oxides by 110% until 2019 and by 50% from january 2020.

in writing. ‒ i voted against the tisa resolution because despite the positive declarations of intent contained in it it contains clauses which would make it difficult for our children in the future to take corrective action in the event of fears arising (so-called lock-in and suspension clauses). in general, free trade agreements (similar to ceta and ttip) should be more concerned with the pros and cons: the potential jobs to be created (pros) on the one hand and the potential losses in quality, price increases and missed investments (cons) on the other, which should not be equated in the debates. the european legislator should analyse past liberalisations and privatisations in detail, both what was originally promised and what was not, in order to enable policy-makers to make the best possible decisions for the benefit of the citizens.

in writing. ‒ the economic and banking crisis has reduced public investment by more than 20%, and austerity policies have had a very negative socioeconomic impact on disadvantaged regions, especially the islands. the joint resolution, which i have approved, therefore calls on the commission to identify the handicaps and strengths of these island regions in order to take appropriate measures to promote economic, social and territorial cohesion.
in writing. the island regions are groups of islands within the eu that share common characteristics such as permanent nature, cultural diversity, environmental diversity. they have been hit hard by the economic and migration crises and have become particularly vulnerable. the economic, social and environmental gaps should therefore be closed in order to ensure their development, in particular by fully exploiting their high potential for the production of renewable energy. reducing the gap between these regions means not only supporting agriculture, livestock and fisheries, which are major sectors for island economies, but also strengthening connectivity by improving sea routes, port access and air transport services. the project submitted to us will improve economic growth, job creation and sustainable development; the european union is a global economy, with a global economic system.
in writing. ‒ yesterday we voted a resolution on island regions to draw the attention of the european commission to the specificities and handicaps faced by europe's islands. the resolution also calls for the eu to take action to ensure that the eu's citizens are able to access the internet and to use it to make their own decisions. in this context, we have asked the commission: - to define clearly the type of permanent natural or demographic handicaps referred to in article 174; - to identify the specific instruments and means of cohesion policy to correct the handicaps of insularity; - to clarify the means it intends to use to verify compliance with the conditions referred to in article 174; - to take into account indicators other than gdp, which would take into account the specificities of island regions, such as the regional competitiveness index.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the text. the commission must now clearly define the permanent geographical, natural and demographic handicaps referred to in article 174 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union (tfeu) which are likely to affect island regions. it must also indicate how it intends to apply the terms of article 174 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union in the light of the permanent handicaps which hamper the natural development of island regions and prevent them from striving for economic, social and territorial cohesion.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution which sets out the european parliament's priorities on the specific characteristics and features of island regions and the implications of these specific characteristics and features for these islands. some of these characteristics should be recognised as permanent disabilities and should receive tailor-made treatment from the european commission.
in writing. ‒ as a representative of a border region, i can tell you from experience that local and regional authorities are close to the needs of the people. this ensures that projects are implemented with meaningful objectives and that controls can be simplified. municipalities and regions often rely on european funds to finance their projects. in many countries, investment by municipalities accounts for the lion's share of total investment. in my home country of belgium, the figure is as high as 40 percent. the municipalities contribute only 5% of the total debt. in view of the so-called sec standards, which represent a major challenge for many municipalities, the commission and the investment bank must propose concrete and practicable solutions to the local authorities in order to continue to facilitate investment. in the case of crossborder projects, too, municipalities and regions often play a pioneering role. we must continue to encourage them to do so, rather than preventing them by excessive bureaucracy.
in writing. ‒ i naturally supported this resolution which underlines the important role that local and regional authorities play in the management of the esi funds and in eu policies in general. for example, my municipality of farciennes is obviously involved in both the definition and the management of the important european projects deployed in its territory and which are vital for its revitalization.
in writing. the union's cohesion policy remains, for the 2014-2020 programming period, the main investment instrument covering all regions of the european union. local and regional authorities have a central role in the design and implementation of eu strategies. this type of governance at all levels must therefore be encouraged. it is by being as close as possible to the citizens that we can best identify their needs, whether economic or social. the principle of subsidiarity is fundamental to help social progress, sustainable development and economic growth. of course, the local and regional authorities must be given sufficient resources. i believe that a public consultation on multi-level governance would be one of the tools to best identify their needs in order to strengthen their capacity and efficiency.
in writing. ‒ yesterday, we voted with a show of hands a resolution to strengthen the role of local and regional authorities in the management of the european structural and investment funds for 2014-2020, but which also asks the commission to launch a public consultation - followed by a possible initiative - to reflect on the means available to enable such a strengthening.
in writing. – i am in favour of this resolution. i am also in favour of synergies and complementarity between the esi funds and other eu programmes, in which local and regional authorities can play a useful role in attaining the objectives of cohesion policy. the european parliament stresses, however, that any reprogramming of esi funds should be done in accordance with cpr rules and that new initiatives should not weaken the core of the esi funds. we point to the reinforced partnership principle and the european code of conduct on partnership, which set out the legal involvement of local and regional authorities and provide for minimum requirements for their involvement in all phases of the preparation and implementation of operational programmes; recognise that, although local and regional authorities were consulted in most cases during the negotiations on the partnership agreements and operational programmes, their involvement did not amount to full partnership; urge the member states, therefore, to fully comply with these requirements and increase efforts to address deficiencies.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution, which contains a series of recommendations on the role of regional and local authorities in the european structural and investment funds. local and regional authorities play a crucial role in shaping and implementing european strategies and policy objectives.
in writing. ‒ i am extremely concerned about the alarming deterioration of the humanitarian situation in yemen: the risk of famine, indiscriminate attacks on civilians, medical personnel and humanitarian workers, the destruction of civilian and medical infrastructure as a result of the intensification of airstrikes, ground fighting and artillery fire. more than 2.51 million yemenis have been internally displaced. 21.1 million people, or 80% of the population, are in need of protection or humanitarian assistance in one form or another. more than 2.2 million children are suffering or at risk of malnutrition. in the face of this alarming situation, i support the call for coordinated humanitarian action under the auspices of the un, a contribution from all countries to meet the humanitarian needs of yemen and to allow access to emergency aid for the population.
in writing. ‒ failing to pursue a political path of cohesion, yemen has become entangled in intensifying tribal tensions and a violent war between iran-backed houthi rebels and saudi arabia, which is waging a military campaign against the rebels that is plunging the entire region directly into a complex conflict that has been going on for several months. meanwhile, saudi arabia sees houthi rebels in yemen as an iranian proxy force, while iran has condemned the saudi-led offensive and called for an immediate halt to its airstrikes. parliament expressed its deep concern at the violence currently raging in yemen and the resulting humanitarian crisis affecting millions of innocent children, women and men. it deplores the loss of life caused by the conflict and the suffering of those caught up in the fighting.

in writing. ‒ the 1965 hague convention establishes a system for the service of judicial and extrajudicial documents in civil and commercial matters in other signatory states. it applies only to documents intended for or originating in non-eu countries. 26 member states already apply the convention. following the adoption of european legislation on the crossborder service of documents, the union has acquired exclusive external competence in this area. it must therefore authorise the member states concerned to act on its behalf in order to accede to the convention. i have approved this recommendation which is in favour of the accession of austria and malta to the said convention.
in writing. ‒ the hague convention of 15 november 1965 establishes a system for the service of judicial and extrajudicial documents in civil and commercial matters in other signatory states. this convention applies only to documents intended for or emanating from countries outside the european union. twenty-six of the 28 member states already apply the convention. the two member states which have not yet applied it, namely austria and malta, have expressed their wish to join. since the hague convention of 15 november 1965 has proved its usefulness in relation to the crossborder service of documents and since it is in the interest of both the european union as a whole and the two member states concerned to have a uniform system in this area in their relations with third countries, i voted this afternoon for parliament to give its approval to the decision authorising the accession of austria and malta to the convention.

in writing. ‒ i naturally voted in favour of the december 2015 agreement between the eu and the republic of san marino on the automatic exchange of financial account information to increase tax cooperation and compliance at international level. this is an important step in the current efforts to combat tax fraud and evasion, as san marino can be considered as a major tax haven. the new agreement provides that the eu and san marino will automatically exchange information on the financial accounts of their respective residents as of 2017. the ultimate aim is to prevent a taxpayer from concealing capital corresponding to income or assets on which tax has not been paid. in particular, san marino will have to comply with the standards foreseen by the oecd in 2014 for the automatic exchange of information on financial accounts.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the agreement signed in december 2015 between the eu and san marino to combat tax fraud and evasion. under the agreement (which will enter into force on 1 january 2017), san marino will now apply stricter measures, equivalent to those in place in the eu since march 2014. the agreement is also in line with the 2014 oecd global standard on the automatic exchange of financial account information. the information exchanged will not only relate to income, such as interest and dividends, but also to balances and proceeds from the sale of financial assets. the tax administrations in the eu member states and in san marino will thus be able to correctly and unequivocally identify the taxpayers concerned, manage and enforce their tax laws in cross-border situations, assess the likelihood of tax evasion being perpetrated and avoid unnecessary further investigations.

in writing. ‒ following the terrible terrorist attacks that struck tunisia last year, the country is currently experiencing serious economic difficulties. in this context, the commission presented to parliament, at first reading, a sensible proposal for a regulation introducing urgent autonomous trade measures for tunisia. the text introduces a duty-free quota of 35 000 tonnes of virgin olive oil produced entirely in tunisia for 2016 and 2017. however, after half the time, the impact of this trade measure on the olive oil market in the union will also be evaluated. should the commission find that the union market is affected, it may take corrective measures.
in writing. ‒ in order to help tunisia in the wake of the sousse attack last june, this report proposes to offer, as an exceptional and temporary measure, a zero-duty tariff quota of eur 70 000 over two years for exports of olive oil from tunisia to the union, in the form of autonomous trade measures, without increasing the overall volume of imports. a mid-term review of the impact on the union market will be carried out. i approved this report.
in writing. ‒ to help strengthen the economy of tunisia, which was hit by terrorist attacks in 2015, the european parliament today voted on an emergency plan, which i supported, to allow the duty-free import of an additional 70 000 tonnes of its virgin olive oil into the eu in 2016-17. tunisia has come a long way since the arab spring and has been the target of terrorist attacks precisely because it is on the path to consolidating its democracy. these attacks have had a huge impact on the tourism sector and the economy in general at a time when tunisians were already facing a difficult economic crisis, with a high unemployment rate. that is why it is crucial that europe expresses its solidarity with the tunisian people and helps them with concrete measures, such as the one voted on this afternoon, which will immediately and directly stimulate their economy.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the text. the european union wishes to reaffirm its support by taking concrete action to support tunisia's economic development.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the mobilisation of the european globalisation adjustment fund to help 412 workers who lost their jobs following the closure of two production sites at agc europe sa and saint-gobain glass benelux. the total amount of aid the european union is providing to help these people enter the labour market is more than one million euros.
in writing. ‒ i have of course supported this decision to allocate more than €1 million from the european globalisation adjustment fund to help the socio-professional reintegration of workers who have been made redundant at agc roux and saint gobain glass. the reconversion units implemented in hainaut are obtaining very positive results in the actions carried out with the trade union partners. the egf's support further increases their capacity to act. the egf will also help 100 young people under 25 who are not in education, employment or training (neets) to integrate into the labour market. this will in particular help to intensify our efforts in charleroi to promote employment and thus the future for all.
in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of the european globalisation adjustment fund to help 412 workers made redundant following the closure of two glass factories in belgium owned by agc europe sa and saint-gobain glass benelux. the amount of money provided by the european union to help these people get back to work is over €1 million. i am glad that the european parliament has decided to provide funds to help belgian workers get back on their feet, but i can only deplore the fact that there are more plant closures in a historic sector in wallonia. i cannot say this enough: industry must be at the heart of our concerns. a strong industrial base is, in my view, a necessary condition for strengthening the whole economic fabric and for creating many jobs in europe. i am also pleased to see that the european globalisation adjustment fund will help 100 young people who are unemployed, out of school and without training to be better prepared to enter the labour market.
in writing. ‒ it is only natural that europe has made its contribution to help workers. in recent years, trade in glass products in the union has been severely disrupted. between 2000 and 2010, employment in the overall glass sector in europe decreased by 32%. in wallonia, which has a strong glass manufacturing experience, several large companies have experienced difficulties in recent years: the number of jobs in the glass sector fell by 19% between 2007 and 2012 in the provinces of hainaut and namur and the number of job losses in the whole region amounted to 1 236 in 2013 and 1 878 in 2014.
in writing. - i voted for this resolution. in order to adapt to globalisation, the belgian glass industry needs additional resources to train and guide the often young people working in this sector in their search for a new job.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the european semester report which, for the first time, sets out the guidelines for policies to be pursued during the year, calls for more investment and a balanced tax policy alongside austerity measures. it also takes account of social problems and suggests ways of solving them. since the economic crisis of 2008, the european right has been imposing drastic austerity measures on us. it has now been almost eight years since these measures were introduced and nothing has changed! the debt of the states continues to rise, the unemployment rate remains at a historically high level and the gap between rich and poor is widening by the day. however, since the beginning of this year we have seen encouraging signs of change and this report is yet another proof of this. investment is becoming a priority and we can only be satisfied with that. i can only welcome this change of direction in europe and hope that it will help to revive the european economy and with it growth and employment.
in writing. ‒ the annual growth analysis report of the 2016 european semester unfortunately calls for the inflation of budget deficits, the creation of a euro-zone budget and the enlargement of the eu budget. since the report also contains good elements, such as the recognition that the high public and private debt makes us particularly vulnerable and the focus on structural reforms, the n-va delegation decided to abstain.
in writing. ‒ the european parliament adopted the resolution this afternoon by 395 votes to 203, with 50 abstentions. the resolution also calls for the eu to take a more active role in the fight against terrorism and to ensure that the eu is able to play a more active role in the fight against terrorism. the text also calls for a reduction in taxation on labour, for better national follow-up of country-specific recommendations, for more national investment in countries with large current account surpluses and for measures against aggressive corporate tax planning. in the context of multiple crises, it is necessary to strengthen the internal cohesion of the european union by means of a stronger and more balanced economic recovery (not forgetting the social one, which was the subject of another report today).
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this text and hope that all actors will actively engage with the european semester 2016 in order to achieve a stronger economic recovery and a better resilience of the european social market economy to structural shocks and difficulties, thus proving that european democracy works and is able to ensure sustainable and broadly shared prosperity.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the employment report on the european semester, which recalls that the priority of national and european policies must be the creation of quality jobs and the generation of growth. here, too, the emphasis is on a balance between structural reforms, fiscal consolidation and sustainable investment, alongside an analysis of the social and economic impacts.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the european semester for economic policy coordination which paid particular attention to employment and social aspects in the context of the annual growth survey 2016. while the economic forecasts for 2016 are encouraging, it is clear that unemployment levels are still very high in the european union, especially among young people. while i am in favour of coordinating economic policies in europe, i am also in favour of better integrating the social objectives of the europe 2020 strategy into the european semester. it is on this basis that we must coordinate economic policies in europe. i am therefore pleased to see that a majority of my european colleagues have joined me in calling for 'a stronger role for the europe 2020 strategy' and for 'social objectives to be reflected equally in all the instruments of the european semester, including the country-specific recommendations'. more than ever, we need to coordinate our economic policies to improve the social conditions of all european citizens.

in writing. - i voted in favour of the text. to align european and national growth policies and ensure their relevance on the ground, it is crucial to strengthen the role of the social partners at both european and national level. to move towards upward convergence and to achieve a balance between competitiveness and equity, the social dialogue should be pursued at all stages of the european semester. in this regard, i welcome the commission's efforts to relaunch the social dialogue and the simplified approach presented by the eac 2015. however, it should be remembered that in many member states the situation remains weak at national level.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the european semester in the context of the single market as the pillar of the european economy. further development of the european single market is essential to help create jobs in the european union. the completion of the single market would produce economic gains of between eur 651 billion and eur 1 100 billion per year, equivalent to between 5% and 8.63% of the union's gdp. competition is also an essential element of the report and all forms of competition, including digital, are examined.
in writing. ‒ in this resolution, adopted by 462 votes to 166, with 7 abstentions, the european parliament called once again for the inclusion of the single market pillar in the european semester, with a regular monitoring system, an identification of country-specific obstacles to the single market, and an assessment of its integration and competitiveness, with particular emphasis on the importance to be given to growth and employment, especially smes. let us not forget that the single market is an indispensable resource on which europe's economic prosperity depends. its untapped potential is estimated at eur 1 trillion. in order to achieve real results in terms of jobs, growth and competitiveness, progress in the integration of the single market within the member states must be accompanied by better governance and greater transparency, including the implementation and enforcement of existing european legislation.
in writing. ‒ we strongly believe that easy access to information for businesses and consumers is a prerequisite for good governance of the single market. the interest of the work of the commission and the member states on a number of information portals for different users: businesses, citizens and consumers is recognised. we believe that a simple, user-friendly and accessible umbrella portal, such as the single digital portal, is necessary to streamline and simplify access to information and promote existing user platforms, provided that national and regional public authorities make the portal accessible and publicly inform citizens about its use.
in writing. ‒ the n-va delegation voted in favour of the report on the internal market policy within the european semester 2016. the report focuses on the major benefits of the single market for both consumers and businesses. the single market contributes to job creation and growth. consumers can enjoy a wider choice of quality products and services at lower prices, and businesses benefit from access to a larger market. the n-va believes that strong efforts must be made to tackle existing barriers in the member states which impede the efficient functioning of the internal market. this is sufficiently reflected in the report, which also pays special attention to smes. finally, we are very pleased with the emphasis in the report on better regulation, which looks first and foremost at the effective application and enforcement of existing rules and instruments, before simply creating new rules.
in writing. ‒ although employment in europe has improved slightly, more labour market reforms are needed if we are to see a greater decline in unemployment in the long term. that is why i voted against this report.

in writing. ‒ the european ombudsman (or european ombudsman) investigates complaints about maladministration in the institutions and bodies (except the european court of justice) of the european union. this includes, for example, irregularities in administration, discrimination, abuse of power or failure to reply to letters. any eu citizen, company, association or other body established in the eu can lodge a complaint. since 1 october 2013, the office of the eu ombudsman has been held by emily o'reilly, who was re-elected by the european parliament on 16 december 2014. in 2014, 23 072 citizens used the services of ombudsmen. it dealt with 2079 complaints, initiated 342 investigations and closed 400 investigations. the european commission was the most frequently requested complaint or inquiry, followed by eu agencies. i welcome the annual report 2014 and the work of mrs o'reilly, and congratulate her not only on her achievements but also on her good cooperation with parliament. the commission's recent efforts to make the authorization of plant protection products by the european commission transparent are commendable.
in writing. ‒ i have approved the 2014 annual report of the european ombudsman. it highlights in particular the investigations it has opened on transparency within the eu institutions, on the transparency of lobbying activities, on fundamental rights, on ethical issues, on trade negotiations, etc.
in writing. ‒ in this report on the activities of the european ombudsman in 2014, parliament welcomes the inquiries opened by the ombudsman, stating that the main themes emerging from these inquiries were transparency within the eu institutions, transparency of lobbying activities and clinical trials, fundamental rights, ethical issues, citizen participation in the eu decision-making process, eu-funded projects and programmes and eu competition policy. the report states that the ombudsman's emphasis on transparency is essential to ensure good administration. it was asked to investigate transparency issues concerning parliament's early access to relevant commission documents on infringements and on the union's pilot procedure, in particular when they are linked to existing petitions. parliament also welcomed and supported the fact that the ombudsman had made greater use of her power to open strategic inquiries on her own initiative.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the text. the ombudsman's main priority is to ensure that citizens' rights are fully respected and that the right to good administration reflects the highest standards expected of the union's institutions, bodies, offices and agencies. it should play a key role in helping the european institutions to improve their openness, efficiency and proximity to citizens with a view to strengthening their trust in the union.
in writing. ‒ ms o'reilly has done an excellent job as ombudsman, especially with regard to the transparency of the ttip negotiations. i hope that it will continue to work in this way to help the european institutions to become more efficient, more transparent and more accountable.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the annual report 2014 of the european central bank. despite the central bank's independence, a debate on the correctness of its policies remains important. the forecasts for growth within the eu are currently at 1.7%. however, high unemployment rates remain a concern. i therefore believe that it is particularly important to give consistent support to small and mediumsized enterprises, which are important job creators in the eu. the low interest rate tactic also remains controversial, especially for pension savers and savings account holders. the objectives pursued are the right ones: to help the countries to get out of the debt crisis and to strengthen the single currency.

in writing. ‒ i supported the motion for a resolution on the opening of negotiations on a free trade agreement with australia and new zealand because i believe that strengthening relations between the eu and the asia-pacific region can have a beneficial effect on european economic growth. australia and new zealand are key players in this region. enlarging and developing trade with these partners can help to boost the economic growth of the three partners, especially as australia, new zealand and the eu share common values and are committed to promoting prosperity and security within a rules-based international order. in addition, the eu, australia and new zealand are currently engaged in multilateral negotiations to further liberalise trade in environmental goods and trade in services. finally, australia and new zealand took part in the negotiations on the trans-pacific partnership, which have just been concluded. i would not understand why the eu is not also involved in the conclusion of modern, ambitious, balanced and comprehensive free trade agreements. i would, however, like to see negotiations conducted in a transparent manner and in compliance with european environmental, health and social standards.
in writing. ‒ the european parliament has given its consent to the launch of negotiations for free trade agreements with australia and new zealand. the conclusion of these agreements will maximise the growth potential of the enhanced relations between the union and the asia-pacific region and will allow for increased cooperation on standards without levelling food safety, environmental protection, social protection or worker protection from the bottom up. the european parliament also called for the interests of smes to be taken into account and for a 'serious and ambitious' chapter on sustainable development to be included, incorporating the core labour standards, the four priority ilo governance conventions and the multilateral environmental agreements. the text of the resolution also stresses that agriculture is a 'very sensitive sector' and calls for balanced final results in agriculture and fisheries to take due account of the interests of all union producers (in particular in the meat, dairy, sugar, cereals and textile sectors).
