in writing. ‒ it is in the interest of the european economy that we strengthen ties with australia and new zealand and promote free trade with these two countries. that is why i voted for this resolution.
pets make their owners happy every day and are surrounded by the best care. but sadly, more and more animals are also falling victim to illegal trade practices, with devastating consequences for their welfare. we must put an end to these practices. the identification and registration of pet animals is an essential tool in this respect. flanders is one of the leaders in europe in the registration of dogs and cats. this not only allows us to return stray animals to their owners and thus tackle the problem of stray animals, but also to put an end to this illegal trade. but that trade doesn't stop at the borders. that is why my party, the n-va, has long been a party calling for more european action. although many member states have mandatory systems for pet registration, there are major differences. the call for better coordination is therefore a strong and necessary signal from parliament to reduce this illegal trade in the interests of animal welfare.
in writing. ‒ with this non-legislative resolution, parliament wants to ensure that national databases for the registration of dogs and cats are compatible with each other. the aim is to combat illegal trade in pets, which is increasingly linked to organised crime. i have agreed to this text because i too believe that compulsory registration of dogs and cats can not only reduce counterfeiting and illegal trade but also promote animal welfare.
in writing. ‒ i have approved this joint resolution which calls for the implementation of a compatible system for the identification and registration of pet animals throughout the union, which will not only help to combat illegal trade in animals but also to identify the origin of disease outbreaks or to combat animal abuse.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution, which asks the commission to ensure compatibility between member states' databases on cats and dogs and to consider establishing databases for other pets as well. i believe that compulsory registration of pets and the sharing of information at european level would reduce the possibilities of falsifying documents, help to combat illegal trade, identify the source of disease outbreaks and combat animal abuse and mistreatment. many member states already have compulsory systems for the identification and registration of pet animals, but there are disparities in the type of information held or the animals concerned. all national databases should therefore be made compatible.
in writing. ‒ the european parliament has underlined the positive role that pets play in the lives of millions of people and families throughout the union and reaffirms that owners must be able to travel with their pets throughout the union in a safe and controlled manner. we are generally satisfied with the improvements to the animal travel scheme introduced by regulation (eu) no 576/2013, including the additional security features in the pet passport and future improvements to be implemented once the animal health legislation has been adopted by the co-legislators.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution because i believe that there should be minimum standards across europe on how we treat our pets. the legislation on and treatment of pets in the eu is very diverse, ranging from belgian legislation to the situation in the romanian capital bucharest, where hundreds of dogs roam free. there is still much to improve, but minimum rules are absolutely necessary.
in writing. ‒ in this resolution, parliament expresses its deep concern at the deterioration of the humanitarian situation in yemen, which is currently being ravaged by a terrible civil war. the question of a general arms embargo against saudi arabia is a choice between plague and cholera, given the precarious security situation in the arabian peninsula. the crimes committed by the saudi arabian state are, of course, unacceptable. i therefore voted in favour of the resolution as a whole and also of the sections which state that arms deliveries should not be authorised if there is a clear risk that they will be used to commit serious violations of international humanitarian law and that this must be controlled by inspectors. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the arms exports are not disrupted by the threat of a nuclear war. i therefore believe that a general arms embargo is not appropriate for the purposes of this coalition at the present time.
in writing. ‒ i supported this joint resolution which first of all underlines the dire humanitarian situation (21 million yemenis need humanitarian aid in one form or another) in which the country has found itself since the beginning of a conflict in which nearly 6 000 people have already been killed and more than 28 000 injured, notably as a result of airstrikes by the saudi-led coalition and acts by the houthis. parliament therefore stressed the importance of international humanitarian aid, stressed its concern at the air strikes by the saudi-led coalition, called on all parties to respect humanitarian law and human rights and on the union to promote these values, particularly in its political dialogue with saudi arabia. it stressed that only a negotiated and non-exclusive solution could restore peace and added that all parties should engage as soon as possible in peace negotiations under the auspices of the united nations.
in writing. ‒ the n-va delegation votes in favour of the amendment requesting the eu high representative to take the initiative for an eu arms embargo against saudi arabia if necessary following proven violations of international humanitarian law in yemen by saudi arabia. we do believe that such an arms embargo should apply to military goods in their own right and not to so-called dual-use goods.
in writing. ‒ i am extremely concerned about the alarming deterioration of the humanitarian situation in yemen: the risk of famine, indiscriminate attacks on civilians, including medical and humanitarian personnel, the destruction of civilian and medical infrastructure as a result of the intensification of airstrikes and the use of cluster bombs. more than 2.51 million yemenis have been internally displaced. 21.1 million people (80 per cent of the population) are in need of protection or humanitarian assistance in one form or another. more than 2.2 million children are suffering or at risk of malnutrition. in the face of this alarming situation, i support the call for coordinated humanitarian action under the auspices of the un and for all countries to contribute to meeting yemen's humanitarian needs. i also support the call for the union to promote effective respect for international humanitarian law in its political dialogue with saudi arabia and its partners, but also with iran, as both states have a key role to play in resolving the crisis.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the text of this resolution, which expresses parliament's grave concern at the deterioration of the humanitarian situation in yemen. the failure of successive governments to respond to the aspirations of the yemeni people for democracy, stability and security has led to the current crisis, which has left 21 million yemenis (82 per cent of the total population) in need of humanitarian assistance and prevented two million children from attending school. the text voted at noon today calls on the warring parties in yemen to respect a ceasefire agreement to allow emergency aid, such as food and medicine, to reach the yemeni people. it also called on all parties to avoid directly targeting civilian infrastructure, medical facilities and water supply networks. i believe that only a political, inclusive and negotiated solution can restore peace and preserve the unity of yemen.
in writing. ‒ failing to pursue a political path of cohesion, yemen has become entangled in intensifying tribal tensions and a violent war between iran-backed houthi rebels and saudi arabia, which is waging a military campaign against the rebels that is directly plunging the entire region into a complex conflict that has been going on for several months. saudi arabia sees houthi rebels in yemen as an iranian proxy force, and iran has condemned the saudi-led offensive and called for an immediate halt to its airstrikes. the deteriorating security situation in yemen, where at least 5,700 people, nearly half of them civilians, have been killed since the conflict escalated in march 2015, is raising growing international concern. houthi soldiers are accused of using heavy weapons in populated areas, while the saudi-led coalition is accused of conducting several airstrikes on hospitals and other civilian buildings. this text expresses the european parliament's concern and solidarity with the yemeni people.
in writing. ‒ i support this resolution because i want to call on high representative federica mogherini to impose an arms embargo on saudi arabia. the situation in yemen is extremely worrying. not only is there a regional conflict with many casualties, but the threat of terrorism from this region remains real. several ngos, as well as unesco and unicef, have already sounded the alarm. the un has tried to mediate, to no avail so far. yemen has become a place where regional powers are fighting their own war with ruthless opponents who are slaughtering civilians. the saudi-led coalition has also committed violations of international humanitarian law.
the rapporteur. madam president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, it is with great pride that i present to you today the new scheme for the distribution of fruit and vegetables and milk in schools, the culmination of a year and a half of work. this result is the result of intensive collaboration with the rapporteurs of the political groups, to whom i am very grateful: mrs sofia ribeiro, mrs ulrike müller, mr james nicholson, mr bronis ropé, mr marco zullo and mr matt carthy. i would also like to congratulate the european commission teams, who made an excellent proposal under the leadership of mr joost korte, and the luxembourg presidency, represented by mr franck schmidt, with whom we have worked closely. the new programme is based on two pillars: the health of children and the teaching of healthy eating habits from an early age through schools, and support for farmers. in the first pillar, we have ensured that the distribution of fresh produce - fruit, vegetables and milk - is an obligation for the member states participating in the programme. the member states participating in this programme - i would remind you that participation is voluntary - will have the possibility of extending the list of products, but under very strict conditions. for example, we have secured the ban on artificial sweeteners and flavourings and the strengthening of the role of national health authorities. i would remind you that one of the main objectives of this new programme is to combat childhood obesity and to improve the health of children. the educational measures, in writing. ‒ with this resolution, parliament adopted a legislative proposal aimed at establishing rules for the prevention and control of animal diseases transmissible to animals or humans. i voted in favour of and welcome the creation of a single, simplified, transparent and clear legal framework.
in writing. ‒ i supported this resolution which approves the proposal for a regulation aimed in particular at strengthening the prevention of transmissible animal diseases and reducing the administration of antibiotics to animals. without prejudice to the requirements of this regulation, member states are also invited to commit to collecting relevant, comparable and sufficiently detailed data on the effective administration of antimicrobials to animals and to transmit such data to the commission, with the aim of achieving a more prudent administration of antimicrobials to animals and thus contributing to the reduction of the risk of antimicrobial resistance. the text also includes provisions on animal welfare. thus, all disease control measures should take into account animal welfare and avoid inflicting any pain, distress or suffering on the targeted animals.
in writing. certain transmissible animal diseases are a serious animal health problem that can also be dangerous for humans. preventing outbreaks of diseases such as swine fever and avian influenza should therefore be a priority for both the scientific community and policy-makers. i welcome the position adopted by parliament on the proposal for a regulation on transmissible animal diseases. i am particularly pleased that the link between animal health and animal welfare has been clearly established. compliance with good animal husbandry practices and european animal welfare standards is an essential corollary to animal health and therefore human health. the prudent and controlled use of antibiotics in animals is also part of a responsible policy for animal health and therefore public health. finally, i welcome the work on simplification and legislative coherence which has now culminated in the adoption of this legislation. it merits the merits of merging almost 40 legislative acts into one.
in writing. ‒ the regulation voted at noon today will make it possible to better prevent and control animal disease outbreaks in the union. with 13.7 million livestock farms in the territory, it was important to provide a strong european response to these threats that know no borders. animal diseases cause losses of hundreds of thousands of euros to producers each year and pose a serious public health risk if transmitted to humans. the text simplifies european legislation by replacing some 40 pieces of legislation, gives priority to prevention measures, clarifies the responsibilities of animal health actors and combats over-medication of animals, which is responsible for bacteria resistance to antibiotics. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'common carrier' to cover all transport services.
in writing. ‒ yesterday we approved the text on transmissible animal diseases. the measures adopted, informally agreed between the european parliament and the council of ministers of the union in june 2015, aim to prevent and stop outbreaks of animal diseases such as avian influenza and african swine fever. this draft eu legislation on diseases transmissible to animals, and potentially also to humans, focuses on prevention and should help professionals to keep pace with scientific progress. the regulation will be published shortly in the official journal of the union, will enter into force 20 days after its publication and will then apply for five years.
in writing. ‒ the initially strong report lost some of its plumage after the first reading following the negotiations with the commission and the council, but remains defensible. the green paper on the mandatory identification of dogs with a chip was not included from 2018. on the other hand, professional breeders and sellers of pets are required to register without exception. other matters are covered by other legislation. for example, inspections on the identification of farm animals are included in the regulation as official controls and the objective of reducing antibiotic use is linked to the legislation on veterinary medicines. i voted in favour of the proposal because the strong link between animal health and the presence of high animal welfare standards is still in the proposal. the fact that antimicrobial resistance should be considered when imposing disease prevention and control measures also remains a strong reference. the 'master list' of diseases covered by this legislation will be established by a delegated act (and not by implementing measures, as the commission wanted) and there is a commitment to preserve biodiversity and valuable genetic material. finally, disease control measures should, as far as possible, aim at avoiding pain, misery and suffering.

in writing. ‒ the european parliament approved (584 votes in favour, 94 against and 32 abstentions) yesterday in strasbourg the compromise text on the community programme for the distribution of fruit and vegetables and milk in schools. the eligible products are: fruit and vegetables and fresh products; drinking milk and lactose-free variants; processed fruit and vegetable products; cheese, etc. in order to ensure the effectiveness of the programme, member states will have to provide for accompanying educational measures such as farm visits, distribution of a wider choice of agricultural products, education of children on related topics (healthy eating habits, local food chains, organic farming, sustainable production or combating food waste). the eu budget for this is €250 million per year (for six years): €150 million for fruit and vegetables and €100 million for milk. the council has yet to formally approve the new regulation, which will apply from 1 august 2017.

in writing. ‒ a resolution to improve gender equality in the work of the european parliament was voted by a large majority. gender mainstreaming aims at equality between men and women and at combating discrimination. it was also decided that parliament will regularly adopt and implement a strategic plan for gender mainstreaming within parliament, which pursues the overall objective of promoting gender equality.
in writing. ‒ article 2 of the treaty on european union guarantees equality between women and men. furthermore, following a resolution adopted in 2003 by the european parliament, each parliamentary committee appoints one of its members to be responsible for gender mainstreaming. but it is a fight that must be constantly remembered. i therefore naturally supported this resolution, which stresses in particular the need for amendments on gender mainstreaming, gender impact assessments and its budgetisation in order to mainstream the gender dimension in all policy areas.
in writing. ‒ asylum policies and procedures, including the assessment of asylum applications, must take gender equality into account. forms of gender-based violence, including rape, sexual violence, female genital mutilation, forced marriage and domestic violence, should be a valid reason for seeking asylum in the eu, says the report we voted on yesterday in plenary. the text also recommends various measures to ensure that the specific needs of women are met throughout the asylum procedure and in reception centres, providing for: female translators and interpreters; specialised trauma counselling services for women who have suffered gender-based violence; childcare services during selection and asylum interviews; providing information to women on their right to make an asylum application independently of their spouse and to have a legal status independent of that of their spouse; gender-sensitive training for staff and legal support for women in reception centres.
in writing. ‒ the n-va delegation abstained from voting on this report. the n-va stands for an inclusive society with equal rights and obligations for all, and for a policy of equal opportunities tailored to and taking into account all the various target groups. this applies to all genders, particularly women and girls, but also to people with disabilities, older people, lgbtiqs, etc. we cannot accept any infringement of this equality, whether at work or in private life, including within the european parliament. the nva delegation is concerned that some of the measures proposed in the report could lead to more bureaucracy and an increase in the budget. they do not address the causes of discrimination and inequality. the n-va believes that a structural solution must be found and that, for example, the appointment of a permanent rapporteur on gender mainstreaming is not the answer to a more women-friendly european legislation.
in writing. ‒ i voted for this text, the content of which should be self-evident... the charter of fundamental rights contains specific provisions on the transversal principle of gender equality and article 6 of the eu treaty gives the charter the same legal value as the treaties. we must change attitudes, we must push for this change, and it will not happen by itself.
in writing. ‒ while gender equality may be recognised as a fundamental right in our european union, gender inequality still exists in our society today. i voted in favour of this report because i believe that the integration of a gender perspective must be a necessary part of all policy-making and an absolute prerequisite for creating equal opportunities between men and women. the european parliament should therefore implement the principle of gender mainstreaming in its work. in that respect, this report is a necessary step in the right direction.
in writing. ‒ with this resolution, parliament voted for a reform of migration and refugee policy in terms of gender-specific measures. it was particularly important to guarantee the safety of female asylum seekers, who often travel with young children. given the difficult situation of female refugees, i believe that the procedures and the examination of asylum applications need to take into account gender-specific elements such as the provision of female interlocutors and interpreters . that is why i supported this resolution.
in writing. ‒ of the one million migrants who arrived in the eu in 2015, 35% were women and children and today 55% of refugees arriving in greece are women. i have of course supported this report which seeks to meet the specific needs of protection of women who attempt a perilous journey in search of a better life or simply protection. this requires a new comprehensive set of guidelines on the gender dimension in the context of asylum and migration. but this also requires that migrant women receive precise information on the asylum procedure, their rights and the specific benefits that apply to them. they must be protected during their stay in refugee camps and, in the context of their asylum applications, have the right to request an investigator and an interpreter and to conduct an individual interview away from any third party.
in writing. ‒ in the unprecedented influx of migrants arriving in europe, the share of women and children has doubled, from a quarter to more than half of refugees since the beginning of 2016. i supported this report because it highlights the vulnerability of these women refugees who fled persecution in their home countries and who continue to be exposed, during their journey, to terrible physical and psychological attacks, sexual violence and human trafficking. on arrival at reception centres, these women often face new obstacles that make them even more vulnerable, especially as some eu member states deliberately degrade their reception conditions to deter migrants from showing up at their borders. for this reason, i support calls for all measures to ensure that the specific needs of women are taken into account throughout the asylum procedure and in reception centres. more generally, i renew my call for safe and legal routes to the eu to increase the safety of refugee women and to discourage the trafficking and exploitation of migrants by smugglers.
in writing. there is a real need to protect women and children. according to the un refugee agency, women and children accounted for up to 55 percent of refugees in january 2016. women are now arriving in greater numbers in europe. their vulnerability requires special attention it is about combating sexual exploitation, trafficking and prostitution. we must promote the detection of trafficking, identify lovers, train people who can detect trafficking, especially in ngos. we'll get through this if we all work together. only a comprehensive long-term strategy can overcome this crisis. we can only regret that our memory of the past is not long enough to provide an answer to the universal values we defend, to the ethics we advocate. this crisis must not destroy the europe of solidarity, justice and equality. it is about the dignity of women, the dignity of man and the dignity of the eu. if europe does nothing, history will record that it has turned away from its values.

in writing. i voted in favour of the straightforward codification of the proposal for a european parliament and council directive on a reduction in the sulphur content of certain liquid fuels. this proposal for a directive has not been substantially amended. the codification has the double merit of clarity and conciseness. it allows users to consult only one authentic text and reduces the volume of the 'acquis communautaire', which includes all the binding legal acts adopted by the european institutions.
in writing. ‒ the purpose of this directive is to reduce sulphur dioxide emissions from the combustion of certain types of liquid fuels and thereby to reduce the harmful effects of these emissions on man and the environment. acidification and the release of sulphur dioxide into the atmosphere cause damage to fragile ecosystems, decrease biodiversity, reduce amenity value and harm crops and forest growth. sulphur dioxide pollution can also have significant effects on human health, especially among the population suffering from respiratory conditions. the text adopted, which i supported, therefore sets the maximum sulphur content of heavy fuel oil, gas oil, marine gas oil and marine diesel used in the union.

in writing. ‒ this proposal for a directive is part of the package to strengthen the rights of individuals in criminal proceedings. the package includes, in addition to this proposal, a directive on the strengthening of certain aspects of the presumption of innocence and a directive on legal aid for persons prosecuted in criminal proceedings. the report, which i have approved, is important because, for example, today only six member states have prosecutorial bodies dedicated to children and nine countries do not even have specialised courts. the proposal for a directive and the amendments to this report will therefore bring a considerable increase in certain member states in the procedural guarantees afforded to children. examples include: children's right to full and comprehensible information from the beginning of the proceedings, right to legal assistance at every stage of the proceedings, right to see parental authority before any questioning, right to be subject to a personalised assessment from the beginning of the proceedings, right to separation between adults and children in the event of provisional detention, medical examination from the beginning of the proceedings to improve the health or well-being of the child, etc.
in writing. ‒ i supported the adoption of provisions to ensure that children prosecuted for an offence can benefit from a fair trial. it is a complex issue which requires a balance between the need to establish the responsibility for the offence and the need to take into account the vulnerability and specific needs of minors. i am satisfied with the guarantees provided, starting with the right to be assisted by a lawyer and to be accompanied by the holder of parental responsibility during most of the proceedings; the right to an individual assessment by qualified staff and to a medical examination if the minor is deprived of liberty; ensuring that deprivation of liberty is imposed on children only as a last resort and for the shortest appropriate period of time; the right of the minor to be informed promptly of his or her rights and of the progress of the proceedings; the right to privacy during criminal proceedings or specific training for judges, prosecutors and other professionals involved in criminal proceedings involving children.
in writing. i welcome the adoption by parliament of its position on the draft directive on procedural guarantees for children suspected or prosecuted in criminal proceedings. as an essential tool of the right to a fair trial, this new legislation represents a significant step forward in the protection of persons prosecuted in criminal proceedings. given the vulnerability of children and the need to prioritise the best interests of the child, the establishment of common european minimum standards was a necessity to strengthen the protection of minors involved in legal proceedings. it is essential that these children enjoy the same level of protection and the same rights throughout the union. the provisions on the deprivation of liberty of minors are of particular importance: detention should be used only as a last resort and, where appropriate, the child should be detained separately from adults. in general, it is important that all decisions taken in relation to minors in criminal proceedings take due account of the best interests of the child. i am also pleased that this legislation has taken a further step towards the creation of a european area of justice.
in writing. ‒ i voted with my whole political group for this text which harmonises the legal protection of children suspected or accused of a crime, promising them a fair trial wherever they are in europe. it is currently impossible to obtain european statistics on the number of children who are brought to justice each year. in belgium, in 2010, 2 062 minors were convicted of criminal activity and they represented 0.8% of the prison population. perhaps more worryingly, 96 children were tried by adult courts in criminal cases in 2011, a 72% increase from the previous year. in such circumstances, it is important that the child understands the legal procedure he or she is facing, that he or she is accompanied by a lawyer and a parent, and that he or she is given a right to individual assessment in order to prioritise the prevention of reoffending. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environment from harmful substances.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report on a proposal for a directive which aims to establish an updated body of legislation, adapted to the specificities of the veterinary sector, while safeguarding public health, animal health, food safety and the environment. the rapporteur shares the commission's objectives and its desire to clearly differentiate the market for veterinary medicinal products from that for human medicinal products, which follows a very different logic. the commission has also chosen to focus on product availability and administrative simplification, without sacrificing the imperatives of public health and environmental protection. however, the commission has not gone far enough on certain points. the draft report thus specifies the conditions under which veterinary health professionals are allowed to prescribe and sell antibiotics or stresses that antibiotics and medicines cannot be sold via the internet.
in writing. ‒ the increasing resistance to human and animal antibiotics is a major public health problem. by 2050, it is estimated that ten million people worldwide will die each year from the effects of resistant bacteria, due to overuse and misuse of antibiotics. the warnings from both the world health organization and the european centre for disease prevention and control (ecdc) are well known. if we are to avoid antibiotics becoming useless, measures are needed at several levels. the updating of the legislation on veterinary medicines approved by the european parliament today sends a strong signal in this regard that the n-va delegation supports: in order to reduce antimicrobial resistance drastically, the preventive use of antibiotics in animals should be restricted. at the same time, innovation, research and competitiveness must be fully stimulated to increase the availability of medicines and administrative burdens must be reduced.
in writing. antimicrobial resistance, which is increasingly present worldwide, poses a serious threat to public health. in the years ahead, therefore, antibiotic-resistant bacteria will pose a real health challenge. closely linked to the administration of antibiotics to farm animals, the problem of antibiotic resistance must be tackled at source. the european legislator must therefore adopt provisions on veterinary medicinal products as soon as possible. as such, i welcome the adoption by parliament of its position on the legislative proposal on veterinary medicinal products. the use of antibiotics in farms should be strictly controlled to limit it to what is strictly necessary and to avoid any excessive, indiscriminate or systematic use of antibiotics in animals entering the food chain. in addition to the management of antibiotic use, the emphasis should be on the search for alternatives to these medicines. innovation must be encouraged to ensure that antibiotics are used as little as possible and that their effects are sustained. this is an urgent problem to which we must devote all our efforts. it's about our health.
in writing. ‒ meps adopted the draft update of the eu veterinary medicines legislation this afternoon. an important vote in a worrying context of antimicrobial resistance. in this regard, the european centre for disease prevention and control (ecdc) recently warned that bacteria in humans and animals continue to show resistance to the most widely used antimicrobials. resistance to ciprofloxacin, an antimicrobial extremely important for the treatment of infections in humans, is particularly problematic. the main points were agreed, the first of which was the prohibition in principle of the prophylactic use of antibiotics. this means that the preventive administration of medicinal products to animals is only authorised on an individual basis and only when justified by a veterinarian. the latter remains at the heart of the system, it is essential, and can continue to prescribe and deliver the medicines. other limits have been set by the european parliament, such as the ban on the veterinary use of antibiotics critical for human medicine and the desire to end the sale of antibiotics and prescription vaccines on the internet. an agreement with the council at first reading is now within reach.
in writing. ‒ the european parliament adopted the amendments to the european commission's original proposal on veterinary medicines in plenary on thursday 10 march. the council also adopted a resolution on the situation in the former yugoslavia, which calls for the immediate release of all political prisoners and the immediate release of all political prisoners. the amendment aims to combat antibiotic resistance in farms more effectively, in particular by prohibiting purely preventive use (prophylaxis) and by making metaphylaxis (treatment of an entire herd when only one animal is sick) subject to conditions. i also personally supported an amendment which aims to add the fact that the medicinal product contains gmos to the grounds for refusing marketing authorization (given that 19 vaccines containing gmos are already on the market).

in writing. ‒ the banking union is one of the main achievements since the financial crisis in 2008 that can ensure security and resilience in the financial and banking sectors and restore confidence, investment in the real economy and a high level of protection for citizens in the event of the failure of banks and financial corporations. we have supported the first steps: the single supervisory mechanism (ssm), which has been operational since 2014, and the single resolution mechanism (srm) since the beginning of this year. the third pillar a common system of insurance deposits is unfortunately still missing and the common fiscal backstop which should be available as a last resort to support the single resolution fund has not yet started. in the absence of these missing elements, the banking union cannot be considered complete and capable of fulfilling its ambition and reducing risks. this should be our priority for the years ahead.
in writing. one of the biggest european constructions in the aftermath of the crisis is the banking union. the aim of the directive is to stabilise the financial sector by ensuring common rules and guarantees and supervision at european level. it is now operational, in particular through the single supervisory mechanism and the single resolution mechanism. some 128 banks in the euro area have thus been placed under the ecb's supervision. the banking union is not, however, finalised. it also requires the creation of a common bank deposit guarantee. this reform is in progress, as the commission has tabled a legislative proposal on this subject.
in writing. ‒ this afternoon, european financial integration was in the spotlight with the vote on the gualtieri report on banking union. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environment from harmful substances. a fair system based on a cascading approach: when a bank needs to be rescued, it is first its owners (shareholders) who will be called upon to contribute, then, in a second step, the creditors and, finally, the holders of deposits of more than eur 100 000. there is still progress to be made. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'competent authority' to cover the whole of the eu. the european parliament also stressed the importance of strengthening the capital of banks without affecting lending capacity and the distribution of credit. a change in this regard is crucial as in recent months banks have 'closed the tap' on access to finance for individuals and entrepreneurs creating growth and jobs.

a few days after the dutch referendum with its well-known result - two thirds of the population voted against any european union measure - it seems to me useful to reiterate the principle of subsidiarity once again. ideally, subsidiarity should prevent the european union from ever enlarging, from encroaching on itself and from appropriating powers which do not belong to it or which should not be dealt with at european level. what is the juri committee doing to us? a text which states - and i quote - 'that the union may act in areas not falling within its exclusive competence only if and to the extent that the objectives of the proposed action cannot be sufficiently achieved by the member states at central, regional or local level, but can be better achieved by the union because of the scale or effects of the proposed action'. with a little bit of that, ladies and gentlemen, you can go all the way. with such a phrase in the hands of the adepts of the european union, we are moving towards an enlargement and further centralisation of that european union. the commission's proposal is to be submitted to the council for approval, and the council will be consulted on the matter. the european union is being given a blank cheque here, even in this european parliament, on this very important principle, to continue its plans for a federal europe. the ever closer union continues here today and we can hardly prevent it, unless we have referendums like the dutch ones, which will wake up all of you here as followers of federal europe. the objective, namely a federal europe with a phrase like this, justifies all means and the fact that subsidiarity turns out to be a piece of paper in the end.

i am pleased to present the report on better regulation in the internal market today. it's been a long process. the least we can say today is that the european union is in trouble. we have the euro crisis, the refugee crisis, the security crisis, brexit, grexit and last week the referendum in the netherlands. i would therefore like to say that the time for blindfolded europeans to see 'more europe' as the solution to all this is over! when people ask me, 'what can europe do to reconnect with its citizens?' i always answer that europe has a responsibility to prove its relevance. it is only when europe can show that it matters that people will see its added value. it is therefore a shared responsibility of the european institutions to be guided by this principle, translated into the principle of subsidiarity, when deciding whether or not to act, to decide how best to act when regulation is needed, and ultimately to ensure that the regulation adopted is simple and easily applicable. this is the starting point of the report on better regulation in the internal market. the single market is one of the cornerstones of european cooperation. it is therefore important that the legislation adopted is also implemented and transposed by the member states. in order to support the achievements of the internal market and also to take up the challenges of the digital single market, institutions need to show determination. if not, then efforts to achieve better regulation may be thwarted by regulatory drift. simply and effectively implementing legislation and also continuously evaluating legislation to ensure that the objectives are being achieved, that is the message. improving the internal market does not mean abolishing regulation, but creating a competitive regulatory environment that keeps jobs and businesses in europe. a single market that does not frustrate but stimulates production, innovation and trade. dare to ask questions, dare to be critical, without taboos. in this way, we will be working towards a strong and dynamic internal market which contributes to long-term growth in europe and thus to the prosperity of european citizens. that is what i had in mind with this report. i hope that i can count on your vote tomorrow.
the commission has already taken a number of measures to combat fraud. mr president, i would first of all like to congratulate the two rapporteurs on their excellent and comprehensive work, which contains all the strategic elements of a truly coherent and responsible european asylum policy. it is a matter of organizing legal access routes to avoid the sad massacres we are witnessing in the mediterranean. it calls for a fairer distribution of refugees to avoid the overload and suffocation of the first host country resulting from the dublin system. it contains - and i agree with it - the need for stronger border controls, a more effective fight against smugglers and the return to their countries of origin of people who cannot claim the right to asylum. it also contains - and i particularly welcome this - the outline of a fully integrated asylum policy. the asylum must in future be a european asylum. you must be able to apply for asylum in the european union. the european agency easo is responsible for examining applications. all procedures, appeals and time limits must be harmonised. the commission's proposal is to be submitted to the council for approval. i would like to ask the commissioner if he can confirm today that the commission - i will speak to you when you hear me - intends to propose, in the context of the revision of the multiannual financial framework, the additional resources necessary for the european union to be able to assume its responsibilities in the field of asylum.
for the ecr group this report, which was intended to set out a strategic vision on asylum and migration for this legislature, is a missed opportunity. first of all, asylum and legal migration are two totally different issues that each deserve its own treatment. but it turned into a soup! secondly, where the report contains new proposals, they are completely unrealistic. turning the dublin system into a distribution mechanism is all very well, but doing so without restrictions and stringent conditions attached to it, without maximum quotas and barely a word about return? but what about new legal routes to the eu? hello common sense! we must take off our blinders and finally put forward realistic and well-thought-out solutions. we must work in several areas at the same time. so on the one hand, we have to ensure that our borders are well guarded and that each member state applies the dublin rules. on the other hand, we must work towards the successful integration of recognised refugees into our society.
blue-card question.– i am very glad to hear that you are also talking about the embargo. i want to ask you: how far can we go to find a solution to the russian embargo on fruit and vegetables? i have said it already many times here in plenary: i think the priority for the agricultural sector should be that the russian boycott should stop. can your party support all the initiatives to ban the boycott?
mr president, commissioner, we have been talking about this crisis for over a year now, and the solutions we have found are only "measures" in view of the scale of the problem. i would remind you that farmers are asking for two things: regulation of the markets, which is being turned away from, not only by the commission, but also by a majority of european governments, who do not want any more regulation. they are also partly responsible for this disaster. the farmers also demand a fair wage for their work. the cap is now going against the grain of the world's major agricultural policies. while the european union bases its policy on decoupled support for production, in large producer countries such as the united states, brazil and china, in particular, support for farmers is directly linked to price, production volume or input use. in the light of these observations, i think it is important to emphasize two things: we must be particularly attentive to the impact of free trade agreements which could further increase the instability of the most important agricultural markets - i am thinking of ttip and mercosur - and, finally, we must think about the introduction of counter-cyclical tools to help farmers in this cap which no longer meets its objectives.
in writing. ‒ a series of products originating in certain acp (africa, caribbean and pacific) countries may be granted more favourable access to the eu market, including the abolition of import duties through surveillance and safeguard measures. i voted in favour of this proposed codecision regulation because it will allow the commission to adopt delegated acts which may limit surveillance and safeguard measures to one or a few member states and not to the whole of the european union. i think that this targeting is more appropriate as long as the measures taken do not disrupt the functioning of the internal market, which would then penalise the other member states and undermine the desired effect.
in writing. i welcome the vote in favour of the report on the codification and recasting of the european 'market access regulation' for products originating in certain acp countries. in adopting this report, parliament endorsed the commission's proposal to codify the regulation, which has already been amended nine times since its adoption in 2007. this codification makes the regulation clearer, more coherent and easier to read. it is an effective technique that ensures the transparency and simplification of union legislation when a legal instrument is subject to multiple amendments.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report, which incorporates the commission's proposal to codify council regulation (ec) no 1528/2007 of 20 december 2007. the market access regulation applies to products originating in certain states belonging to the african, caribbean and pacific (acp) group of states the arrangements provided for in agreements establishing or leading to the establishment of economic partnership agreements. it applies to products originating in the regions and states listed in annex i, which provides for more favourable access to the union market rules for a number of products defined in the regulation. it should be noted that this new regulation will replace the various acts incorporated in it, whilst fully preserving the substance of those acts. at the same time, it was also necessary to introduce certain substantive amendments to empower the commission to adopt delegated acts and to adapt the rules on exceptional measures with limited territorial application.
in writing. ‒ the objective of codification is to ensure the transparency, clarity and simplification of union legislation when a legal instrument is subject to multiple amendments. since its adoption in 2007, the market access regulation has already been amended nine times, notably in the context of the 'post-lisbon' alignment through the omnibus trade act ii and subsequent commission delegated regulations. i therefore voted in favour of the text tabled by my colleague mr walesa.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report as it is a codification of the 'market access regulation'. with this decision, we are bringing more clarity and transparency to this regulation.
in writing. ‒ the new protocol negotiated between the union, the government of denmark and the home rule government of greenland setting out fishing opportunities and financial compensation establishes an eu-greenland joint committee which would be responsible for expressing the union's position and monitoring its application and proper implementation. the commission would be empowered to approve amendments to the said protocol after negotiations with greenland. i voted in favour of the conclusion of this protocol because i believe that fishing opportunities and financial compensation must be monitored with the greatest care and that the position expressed on behalf of the union can be reviewed as and when the latest relevant statistical and biological information is taken into account in order not to interfere with the agreements reached.
in writing. i welcome the european parliament's approval of the conclusion of the protocol to the fisheries partnership agreement between the european union and greenland. the continuation of this fisheries agreement, which is of particular importance to both parties, will contribute to the strengthening of cooperation in the field of sustainable fisheries. to this end, this agreement - as well as all other fisheries partnership agreements - must be fully in line with the objectives of the common fisheries policy and in particular with its precautionary principle and the responsible exploitation of marine resources. the union is a key player in the field of fisheries and therefore has a duty to promote, in particular through the fisheries agreements it concludes, the sustainable management of global fisheries resources.
in writing. ‒ the original fisheries agreement between the european union, on the one hand, and the government of denmark and the home rule government of greenland, on the other, dates back to 1985. this agreement was extended for a long time until it was finally replaced by the current gpa. almost all of greenland's exports of fishery products are destined for the european union; denmark accounts for more than 90% of the union imports. the european union shall pay a fixed annual financial compensation for access, irrespective of the fishing opportunities provided for in the protocol. the current protocol provides for a financial contribution of eur 17.85 million per year. the greenland agreement is the third agreement of economic importance for the union. the new protocol between the government of denmark and the home rule government of greenland is in line with the objectives of the fisheries partnership agreement and strengthens cooperation between the union and greenland. it also promotes a partnership framework for the development of a sustainable fisheries policy and the responsible exploitation of fisheries resources in the greenland fishing zone. this shall be done in the interest of both parties, in accordance with the relevant conservation and management measures and within the limits of the available surplus.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the text, following the experts in our group. the new protocol is in line with the objectives of the fisheries partnership agreement; enhance cooperation between the union and greenland and promote a partnership framework for the development of a sustainable fisheries policy and the responsible exploitation of fisheries resources in the greenland fishing zone, in the interest of both parties. the fisheries protocol would cover a period of five years from the date of provisional application i.e. from the date of its signature and at the earliest on 1 january 2016. it provides for fishing opportunities for union vessels in the greenland fishing zone, in accordance with the relevant conservation and management measures and within the limits of the available surplus. to that end, the protocol sets an indicative annual level of fishing opportunities granted by greenland to union vessels (in tonnes).
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this partnership agreement because it provides significant economic benefits for both parties and ensures greater coherence in eu fisheries policy.
in writing. ‒ on 23 november 2013, the commission negotiated on behalf of the union an agreement on certain aspects of air services with the government of the macao special administrative region of the people's republic of china. relations between the eu and macao have been based on a trade and cooperation agreement since 1992. since then, the union has been making its best contribution to the economic and political development of this autonomous region. i voted in favour of this act because it strengthens the union's links with this customs territory which is separate from the rest of the people's republic of china.
in writing. i welcome the vote in favour of the conclusion of the agreement between the european union and the macao special administrative region of the people's republic of china. the conclusion of this agreement by the european union will harmonise air transport relations, which have long been governed by bilateral air services agreements. this agreement replaces certain provisions of the 15 existing bilateral air services agreements concluded between the member states of the union and the macao special administrative region. it puts all member states on an equal footing and thus prevents unfair competition between them. this is a step towards more europe in the field of air transport.
in writing. ‒ this agreement between the european union and macao was signed on 23 november 2013. the council needs the consent of the european parliament to conclude this agreement. in accordance with rule 99 and rule 108 (7) of its rules of procedure, the european parliament votes in one vote, which it did yesterday.
in writing. - i agree with mr koch on this point. international relations in the field of air transport between member states and third countries have so far been governed by bilateral air services agreements. the court of justice of the european union ruled in 2002 that the traditional designation clauses in member states' bilateral air services agreements were contrary to european union law. they allow a third country to refuse, withdraw or suspend the licences or authorisations of an air carrier which has been designated by a member state but which is not substantially owned or effectively controlled by that member state or its nationals. the court found that this situation constituted discrimination against union carriers established in the territory of a member state but owned and controlled by nationals of other member states. this is a breach of article 49 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union, which guarantees nationals of member states who have exercised their freedom of establishment the same treatment in the host member state as that accorded to nationals of that member state.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this agreement because it aims to give all european airlines access to air routes between the european union and third countries in a non-discriminatory manner. the agreement also aims to bring bilateral agreements between member states and third countries into line with european law.
in writing. ‒ this report will allow for better international regulatory cooperation, more transparency, accountability and democratisation. the mandate of each organisation should be clarified, as well as the ways in which they operate and are financed, including voluntary contributions, gifts and donations, in order to ensure the legality of decisions and the absence of special interests. this sixth extension maintains the existing situation, which is satisfactory, and provides legal certainty to stakeholders, while allowing the entry into force of the definitive vat regime for intra-eu trade on the basis of a revised set of rules for normal and reduced vat rates. the vat directive provides that from 1 january 2011 until 31 december 2015 the standard rate may not be lower than 15%. the commission's proposal to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'competent authority' to cover the whole of the eu, was rejected by the committee on economic and monetary affairs and industrial policy. however, they propose that the current provisions be extended for a period of three years, i.e. until 31 december 2018 (instead of 31 december 2017 as proposed by the commission).
in writing. the aim of this report is to extend for a period of two years the existing situation in which member states apply a standard vat rate of at least 15%. the vat directive provided for the end of this floor rate on 31 december 2015. it should therefore be renewed until december 2017. however, the commission will publish an action plan in june 2016 to reform the current system. this revision will give member states greater flexibility in setting rates and will deal with the concept of temporary derogations.
in writing. ‒ the text adopted endorses the european commission's proposal to retain retroactively the principle of a minimum standard vat rate of 15% and proposes that the current provisions be extended for a period of three years, until 31 december 2018. the european parliament is of the opinion that this time limit provides the necessary legal certainty for the parties concerned and allows for a more in-depth examination of vat rates in the context of the forthcoming vat action plan.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the text. the action plan will set out the orientations for future work in the light of the results achieved since the 2011 communication. it will define the main features of the definitive vat regime for intra-eu trade that the commission intends to propose, as well as the reforms it envisages to adapt the existing rules on vat rates to a definitive regime characterised by the destination principle.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the minimum standard vat rate because i believe that this will lead to a better functioning of the internal market.

in writing. ‒ i have endorsed this report which welcomes the decision of the united nations general assembly to develop, under the united nations convention on the law of the sea, a legally binding international instrument on the conservation and sustainable exploitation of marine biodiversity in areas beyond the limits of national jurisdiction. it stressed the importance of making progress in the development of this new instrument and meeting the target of finalising the text by the end of 2017. meps believe that the eu and the international community should act to conserve and sustainably use marine biodiversity by, inter alia, implementing modern and sustainable concepts of marine ecosystem management and ocean governance principles through:• the controlled exploitation of marine resources (whether mineral exploitation, energy drilling, etc.) and fisheries; • science-based marine governance; • restoring stocks and maintaining them above levels which can produce the maximum sustainable yield; • ecosystem-based management and conservation of marine biodiversity; • the application of existing legislation and the precautionary principle.

in writing. ‒ in 1992, the united nations mentioned the importance of protecting the world's waters in the document entitled 'action 21', which was published at the end of the united nations conference on environment and development held in rio de janeiro, brazil, that year. the international community thus recognized the need for an international strategy to combat pollution and the growing threats to marine biodiversity. the johannesburg declaration on sustainable development and the plan of implementation were adopted at the united nations world summit in south africa in september 2002. in 2012, in the document known as rio+20, the international community reaffirmed its determination to tackle environmental problems and the need for sustainable development. in 2004, a special working group was established by united nations general assembly resolution 59/24, paragraph 73. in january 2015, the working group submitted its report, highlighting the need for a comprehensive system at the global level and recommending the development of a legally binding international instrument on the conservation and sustainable use of marine biodiversity in areas beyond national jurisdiction. the report adopted today uses the same language.

in writing. ‒ the eu's zootechnical legislation on the production of farmed animals (bovine, porcine, ovine, caprine and equine species) and their germinal products is composed of various standards that may restrict trade and import into the union. i voted in favour of this proposed codecision regulation because it provides for legal harmonisation of the principles governing the process of rearing high-quality animal species. this single legal framework will allow greater fluidity in their trade and imports.
in writing. – i voted in favour of this legislative resolution. europe’s genetic biodiversity is indispensable to a healthy europe and therefore needs to be protected. as the biodiversity of one member state affects that of the other, this can only be achieved through harmonised eu-wide legislation. however, at the same time, we need to leave enough breathing space for science and innovation. in its current form, this resolution will do both these things. it will protect our valuable local breeds both efficiently and effectively, where needed. with regard to innovation, it calls for harmonisation and simplification. the combination of these two will result in a healthier, more competitive livestock industry, increasing the eu’s competitiveness and ensuring the food-safety of our citizens. it will be easier to import animals and their genetic material for the sake of breeding, according to specific, transparent and harmonised rules, that are safeguarded by one central authority.
in writing. the purpose of this revision of the current legislation is to bring together the separate and specific rules on trade, import and registration of breeding animals and derived products traded for breeding purposes into a single legal framework. this revision has the advantage of providing greater clarity for all those involved in the sector, while maintaining competitiveness.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report, which includes the following measures: introducing special provisions for rare and endangered breeds; seeking a balanced approach as regards the grounds for derogation from the approval of a breeding body, between the preservation and management of purebred breeds and the internal market; a guarantee of a minimum level of rights and obligations for breeders and breeding establishments and bodies, as well as additional rights in the event of membership and seasonal movement of animals; the application of the principle of subsidiarity to dispute settlement (national law and private settlement mechanisms); and simplification of official controls and of controls carried out by the commission without compromising efficiency and quality.
