in writing. ‒ i have of course supported this report, which advocates a pluralist and open approach to migration. the report stresses the fundamental importance of continuing search and rescue operations at sea and calls for the replacement of the dublin system by a centralised european system based on solidarity, which would distribute refugees in a solidarity-based and mandatory manner among member states. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environmentally friendly use of energy. finally, it advocates adequate funding for humanitarian aid.
in writing. – the situation in the mediterranean is dire. the only way we can find a solution is to adopt an approach at eu level. that is why i voted in favour of this parliamentary resolution. it does not just focus on the usual negative aspects – such as smuggling and human trafficking – of this issue. it investigates how we could actually resolve the situation, such as the cooperation with third countries through regional protection programmes and by developing legal economic migration channels. in addition, it stresses the importance of taking responsibility in adhering to the systems that are in place, for example, by stressing the importance of how emergency funds are spent and the effective implementation of the common european asylum system. most importantly, it indicates which steps are needed in order for the common european asylum system (ceas) to become a uniform and therefore efficient system. in this regard the resolution calls upon going even further, stressing that article 78 (2) on ‘a uniform status of asylum’ that would be valid throughout the union, is fully implemented. finally, it acknowledges the necessity of reinforcing frontex and of the new european border and coast guard.
in writing. i welcome the adoption by parliament of its report on the need for a holistic european approach to migration. the report, which is the fruit of long but fruitful work in the libe committee, expresses parliament's position on european migration policy and sets out the paths for future reforms. these are in line with what the alde group has been advocating for several months: adoption of a resettlement mechanism, a complete overhaul of the dublin system to ensure a fair sharing between member states and substantial strengthening of the european asylum support office (easo) are all measures that will have to be taken to ensure the coherence and effectiveness of our asylum policy.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the long-term management of migration in the european union, which calls for a radical revision of the dublin system. the text of the report also calls for safe and legal channels for the entry of third country nationals into the union without the latter having to resort to smugglers and risk their lives. the vote on this text was also an opportunity to point out the failure of the european asylum system to cope with the ever-increasing number of migrants arriving. the radical reform required of the so-called dublin rules proposes to create a central system for collecting and distributing asylum applications. the system could include a quota for each eu member state and would operate on the basis of access points (hotspots) from which refugees would be distributed.
in writing. - i voted for my colleague's report. i share the view that the approach to migration in europe needs to be radically and permanently changed. any viable long-term strategy must cover all aspects of migration and asylum, including foreign and diplomatic policies, the global crime economy, the delivery of humanitarian aid and better assistance to people already in europe. in addition, the gender dimension must be integrated into all policy areas.
in writing. ‒ i was responsible for this dossier in the liberal group. the current refugee crisis proves again and again that our current system of migration is no longer workable in today's reality. in europe, we urgently need a collective european response to this crisis. only in this way can we solve the dramatic humanitarian situation today.
in writing. ‒ the principles of subsidiarity and proportionality are important for a coherent and structured policy. the first determines the most appropriate level of intervention in areas of shared competence between the european union and its member states, while the second guides the union's actions in the exercise of its competence. i voted in favour of these annual reports, which are an examination of the strict application of the principles of subsidiarity and proportionality because they must be respected, especially at a time when the institutions of the european union are criticised as being too intrusive in the political action of the national, regional and local authorities of the member states.
in writing. the principles of subsidiarity and proportionality are fundamental principles of the eu, under which the union may act in areas not falling within its exclusive competence only 'if and to the extent that the objectives of the proposed action cannot be sufficiently achieved by the member states, either at central, regional or local level, but can rather, by reason of the scale or effects of the proposed action, be better achieved at union level' and provided that 'the content and form of the union's action do not exceed what is necessary to achieve the objectives of the treaties'. in order to promote a genuine 'culture of subsidiarity' within the union, i believe it would be appropriate to extend the period of consultation of national parliaments from 8 to 12 weeks for subsidiarity analyses, as in most cases national parliaments have internal priorities imposed by national legislation. this extension of the consultation period would imply an amendment of the treaty and should therefore entail a revision of the treaty.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report, which welcomes the increased participation and involvement of national parliaments in the european legislative process in recent years, but notes that efforts still need to be made in this regard. for example, the text adopted suggests that, as a first step, the european commission should hold an annual debate with each national parliament to strengthen its dialogue with them.
in writing. ‒ we note that the existing preferential trade agreements have shown that they can be beneficial to the european economy and generate growth and jobs. the effects of trade agreements are dependent on the outcome of the negotiations and therefore projections of impact are always based on assumptions. the commission should therefore carry out the sustainable development impact assessments before the opening of negotiations on trade agreements as part of an ex ante impact assessment exercise to analyse the economic, social and environmental impacts on union citizens and businesses, and in particular on smes. member states should also play a crucial role in assessing the potential benefits and impacts of preferential trade agreements on their own economies. i stress the crucial importance of an adequate mechanism for consultation, dialogue and participation of citizens, businesses (in particular smes) and civil society in the decision-making process on the union's trade policy.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of these annual reports because the principles of subsidiarity and proportionality are a key guide for european policy-making. these reports provide a great deal of information on the activities of the european institutions in relation to these two principles.
in writing. - i abstained on this report by my colleague kaufmann. on the one hand, i would like to emphasize the quality of this report, which makes it clear on several occasions that simplification of european legislation cannot undermine environmental, health and social standards and must respect the implementation of agreements between the social partners. on the other hand, we still regard the refit programme as a potential danger to the health of workers and the protection of the environment, which is why i abstained.
in writing. it is essential to strengthen and improve the european regulatory framework in order to move towards a 'sharp' european union regulation which is part of the 'better lawmaking' interinstitutional agreement. better legislation is about working for a dynamic europe that creates growth and jobs. it is to work for effective, transparent and legible legislation for businesses, in particular smes and micro-enterprises. it is also working in the interests of workers' rights. in order to strike the right balance, impact assessments of legislative proposals must be carried out in a systematic and rigorous manner. replacing 28 national standards with a european standard requires working with all the european bodies and all the actors concerned.
in writing. ‒ 74% of europeans think that the european union generates too much bureaucracy. in response to this concern, the commission has in recent years been working to streamline legislation and reduce regulatory constraints. this is even more true under the commission chaired by jean-claude juncker. a desire to reduce the 'law-making machine' which sometimes has a negative impact on an entire chain of economic activity and which contributes to the citizens' distrust of the european union. it is therefore natural that i have supported the kaufmann report on the annual progress in implementing the programme for a sharper and more efficient regulation (refit). i also supported, like the majority of members, paragraph 47 rejecting the nutritional profiles. an interesting idea, but one that has proved impossible to implement since the first discussions on the subject in 2006. in practice, when the sugar, saturated fatty acids and sodium thresholds are exceeded, products would no longer be allowed to claim their other nutritional characteristics. to illustrate: a cheese that is too high in fatty acids could no longer emphasize the fact that it is also high in calcium. that's a bit much to ask.
in writing. ‒ i have decided to vote against the kaufmann report in plenary. while pursuing better regulation should be one of our objectives as meps, i remain concerned about the negative impact that a programme such as refit can have. firstly, because at times this text tends to encourage the commission not to adopt proposals which would have a negative impact on competitiveness without taking into account the potential benefits for workers and citizens. i am also concerned about the possibility for the commission to withdraw a legislative proposal if the council has not yet decided on it. i must admit, however, that this report also contains important advances aimed at defending the interests of consumers, workers and citizens more generally. i say and i repeat that i am in favour of regulatory simplification which can provide relief to smes without harming workers, consumers and citizens. this message is beginning to be heard, and i can only rejoice to see the lines moving on this.
in writing. - i abstained in the final vote. i am very much against this way of doing legislation and politics, and i am very much against what refit has become, namely a legislative proposal for all. however, i must admit that the text does make some important progress. that explains my decision.
in writing. ‒ european regulations are often too complex and too opaque. moreover, european rules all too often lead to an additional administrative burden. this is especially true for smes, which often cannot benefit from relevant european regulation because of the administrative costs and the lack of clarity about the regulation. i therefore voted in favour of this proposal, since it aims to simplify european union law and its possible transposition considerably.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this report, which in my view favours too much of a liberal view of the functioning of the single market, without paying sufficient attention to the social, human and environmental dimensions of the european project.
in writing. – it should come as no surprise that i strongly approve this parliamentary resolution. i always grasp the opportunity to improve single market legislation. this resolution stresses the importance of delivering a competitive regulatory environment in order to ensure the competitiveness of the eu. in this regard, the resolution focuses on every step of the policy process. concerning impact assessments, it stresses the importance of their effectiveness and importance as a policy tool, followed by the necessity of transparency and inclusiveness during the consultation process. the whole process would of course, be useless if there were no actual full implementation of the single market legislation. therefore, the resolution reminds the commission of the importance of regularly executing its monitoring function. it hereby reminds us of the commission’s complementary role as a problem-solver.
in writing. the single market is 508 million consumers and a huge potential market for businesses. this pillar of the european construction is the basis of our prosperity and influence in the world. we have a highly skilled workforce, which makes europe competitive. but to stay that way, it has to keep innovating. europe alone is the solution to the sometimes frightening challenges that too often leave us in doubt and uncertainty. but a successful europe is one which innovates, which works in transparency, which applies the principle of subsidiarity and proportionality, which tends to be closest to the needs and expectations of the citizens. it is also a europe that is willing to challenge itself in order to create and maintain favourable conditions for our businesses. impact assessments will help to identify more effectively the legislation that is truly effective, modern and capable of delivering concrete results.
in writing. ‒ i voted against the van bossuyt report because i do not share the report's view of what better regulation of the internal market should be. as a committed european, i am of course in favour of better regulation for our internal market. the rapporteur, however, believes that better regulation should concern only businesses and consumers and should be aimed at improving competitiveness. the involvement of smes and consumers is as important as that of workers. unfortunately, it seems that the rapporteur does not share my view. as regards impact assessments, i am rather in favour of the european institutions having the means to help them in their choices. however, these analyses cannot in any way replace political analyses and decisions. unfortunately, some passages in this report tend to give these impact assessments an importance they should not have. other elements in this report do not correspond to the vision of society which i am advocating in this parliament, which is why i have decided to vote against this report.
in writing. ‒ many in europe now believe that more efficient and in some cases less regulation will ensure the proper functioning of the internal market. this report by mr van bossuyt illustrates that parties can exploit this discourse to push for complete deregulation. the report 'towards better regulation of the internal market' does not seek better regulation. on the contrary, it seems to want to block any form of european regulation. the proposal to introduce a 'red card system' allowing national parliaments to delay the legislative process was blocked. however, there are many other elements, including the disregard for the european level of regulation of the internal market, which make this report unacceptable. we have tried to steer this report in the right direction by means of amendments. we stressed the need for european regulation in the pursuit of sustainable development and consumer protection. we stressed that only unjustified barriers to trade should disappear and called for a multidimensional approach to policy outcomes that takes into account social and environmental aspects. unfortunately, all the amendments we tabled were rejected. that is why i voted against this report.
in writing. - i voted against the text. i cannot share the rapporteur's view of the matter. improved regulation of the single market must be dealt with differently and, among other things, by putting workers' rights at the centre of priorities!
in writing. ‒ more than 20 years after its creation, the internal market is still too fragmented. it is time now to commit ourselves to a full internal market based on the principle of shared responsibility. that is why i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ according to a 2014 eurobarometer survey, 44% of eu citizens feel they have only a limited understanding of how the union works. the report proposes a series of initiatives to better integrate the european dimension into education systems. among these initiatives, the report - which i have approved - calls for better integration of european integration into teaching and extra-curricular material, for providing teachers with materials and resources to enable them to incorporate an eu dimension in their teaching, and for promoting multilingualism and intercultural skills among educators.
in writing. ‒ i supported the adoption of this report calling on member states to strengthen the european dimension in education. many european citizens do not feel close to the european project. this distance is linked in particular to a lack of knowledge about the european union. a survey shows that 44% of europeans do not understand how the european union works and many feel that they cannot make their voices heard. at a time when we are experiencing a major identity crisis and witnessing an alarming rise in euroscepticism everywhere, it seems to me essential to better integrate the european dimension into school curricula and to integrate this dimension with the other subjects taught so that current and future generations are better aware of their rights, learn about the history of europe and are informed about the many ways in which they can get involved in a better europe.
research shows that 44% of citizens feel they do not know how europe works. 52% of european citizens also think that their vote does not count in the eu. the eu is still not sufficiently known. it is plausible that this sometimes leads to confusion, disappointment and misunderstanding about the functioning of the eu. it is therefore advisable to bridge the information gap that has arisen between the citizens of europe and the european institutions. education is an important lever to help young people bridge that gap and better understand the eu. in order to better understand the impact of the eu on people's daily lives, this report calls for a more intensive and visible integration of the eu dimension into teaching material. in addition to the transfer of knowledge about europe, it is desirable to teach young people skills that promote european citizenship. in this way, young people are taught to think critically about european decision-making, while encouraged to promote the sense of community and the eu's fundamental values.
in writing. ‒ this afternoon's vote calls for europe to be taught in schools in a more coherent way in each member state and in a way that is more complementary to the other subjects taught. forty-four per cent of europeans do not understand how the eu works: this is unacceptable. how can citizens know their rights, make their voices heard, and get involved in shaping the europe of tomorrow if the democratic institutions and mechanisms that serve them remain a mystery to them? a 2013 icf ghk survey found that 85% of member states were already talking about europe to their schoolchildren. what today's report wants to do is to reinforce these figures and make europe's learning more coherent and structured. this demand is part of a real effort to open up the institutions and combat euroscepticism, to make european democracy live!
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the drăghici report on learning about the european union in school because i am convinced that there is a real need to know and understand europe in order to allow it to evolve and even change the way it works. from an early age, european citizens need to learn about the history and values of the eu, as this knowledge is essential for understanding each other and for jointly developing - and involving - the european project. the commission is asked to propose a common framework for learning about the european union and to strengthen the european mobility of learners. member states retain their primacy in education, so they will have to facilitate 'intercultural, non-discriminatory and inclusive education' and promote the values of citizenship in their school and university curricula. it is by deconstructing prejudices and caricatures through knowledge, while promoting critical thinking, that we can, together, make the european project more enchanting.
in writing. ‒ the report rightly emphasises that the eu is made up of its member states, each with a unique history and culture. it is also positive that the emphasis is on informing citizens. this should enable critical reflection and debate on the importance of european cooperation. although the report recognises the competence of the member states in matters of education and training policy, it seems to ignore this in certain paragraphs. in particular, the report is often too prescriptive when it comes to education in relation to the past and future of european integration. the nva delegation therefore abstained from voting.
in writing. - i am of course in favour of this initiative. the growing importance of a european dimension in education across the different disciplines and levels and forms of education should be emphasised, while stressing the need for a broad and thorough understanding of the concept which takes account of its complex, dynamic and multidimensional nature, with learning about the union at school being an essential element.
in writing. ‒ according to a eurobarometer survey, 71% of all europeans feel that they do not understand how the european union works. moreover, 52% of all european citizens feel that their vote does not count in europe. i therefore voted in favour of this proposal because i believe that this measure can reduce these disastrous figures in the long term.
in writing. ‒ i have endorsed this report, which calls in particular for the removal of all socioeconomic barriers that undermine equal access for all to vocational education and training (vet) opportunities and calls on the commission, in particular, to increase the visibility of vet programmes or to promote the european mobility of apprentices. the persisting level of unemployment in the union requires that vocational training, which is an essential tool in combating school dropouts, skills mismatches and any other reason that prevents access to employment for thousands of european citizens, be strengthened by all relevant levers.
in writing. – the competitiveness of the eu depends on the quality of our workforce. in order to answer to the needs of our companies, it is essential that it is as flexible as possible. an important tool that helps us to achieve this goal is the erasmus+ exchange programme of which we can already reap the benefits. after having this programme in force for several years now, it was time for an evaluation. although the programme is overall successful, some apparent problems came to light. one of these is the gap between academic and vocational educational training (vet). systems such as europass and ecvet were designed to address these problems but have encountered opposition themselves. this makes the accreditation between educational institutions of various countries more difficult. such imbalances are also reflected in the unemployment data from across the eu. following the report of 4 march, this resolution stresses the need for a more extensive and more qualitative erasmus+ programme, for a more varying number of students. to incentivise the programme, a list of 10 objectives has been created, which will serve as a guideline. having taken all of the above into account, i have approved of this parliamentary resolution.
in writing. the european student exchange programme, erasmus, is one of the success stories of the european union. in 2012-2013, some 270 000 young people completed part of their academic course in another european university through this programme. in addition to the opportunity to refine language learning, erasmus is a unique experience of openness to europe. 'erasmus+': with a budget of €14 billion for the period 2014-2020, it offers 4 million young europeans the opportunity to study or train abroad. this new programme covers not only training, education and youth but also, for the first time, sport. under erasmus+, students who have not had the chance to win a scholarship will have the opportunity to receive a loan on favourable terms to study a master's degree in another eu country. i would like the union to go even further in the field of the use of languages. in my view, the system in place in european schools (learning several languages from an early age) should be the basis of the curricula in the member states.
in writing. ‒ this vote extends the erasmus+ programme to include apprenticeships and vocational training. erasmus+ is an eu programme for education, training, youth and sport in europe, established in 1987. it has a budget of €14.7 billion and helps to provide over four million europeans with the opportunity to study, train, gain experience or volunteer abroad. parliament today called for better coordination of this great asset for young people, and for local authorities, businesses, chambers of commerce and trade unions to develop inclusive and ambitious learning partnerships. it also called for the validation of skills to be better recognised, including when developed in the context of vocational or non-formal learning. life paths are changing and lifelong learning is a growing phenomenon that needs to be encouraged and facilitated. in this respect, erasmus+ is an essential tool for social cohesion, innovation, growth and jobs across the union.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the maragall report on erasmus+, to which i contributed, because the objectives of the eu 2020 strategy are far from being achieved in the field of education and there is more need than ever to promote mobility for all learners, particularly in the vocational pathways of alternance education. in the european parliament, with members from the different political parties, we are setting up a pilot project for erasmus pro, convinced that mobility and alternance, supported at national and european level, open a royal road to learning leading to employment. we also suggest that the commission should create a 'european student e-card' and bring about the european apprenticeship.
in writing. ‒ the n-va delegation voted in favour of this report. erasmus+ deserves our attention and support. investments in education, training and informal learning are important to give people the opportunity to develop and develop continuously, i.e. to learn throughout their lives. this will benefit labour mobility and subsequently the level of employment. the nva delegation would like to emphasise that it is the eu member states that are responsible for education and training policy.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the amendment on erasmus+ and other tools to promote mobility in vocational education and training: a lifelong learning approach. i am pleased that an overwhelming majority of members voted in favour of the proposal.
in writing. ‒ as a student, i studied in madrid for three months under the erasmus programme and it was a wonderful experience. that is why i was very pleased to vote for the erasmus+ report. this will also enable students in vocational training to benefit from an erasmus experience.
in writing. ‒ this report will allow for better international regulatory cooperation, more transparency, accountability and democratisation. the mandate of each organisation should be clarified, as well as the ways in which they operate and are financed, including voluntary contributions, gifts and donations, in order to ensure the legality of decisions and the absence of special interests.
in writing. – i voted in favour of this parliamentary resolution because it offers specific and targeted guidelines for the eu to follow if it wants to address the challenges of tomorrow. we live in a globalised world at a rapid pace. for the eu, such an environment means that it is ever more important to adapt ourselves to this changing environment. this resolution calls for this to be done, by for example taking the 2030 agenda for sustainable development into account. our priority should lie in defending our union and the values it stands for. at the same time, we need to ensure that our neighbourhood regains its stability and remains stable, facilitating the de-escalation of conflicts. in order to do so, the eu needs to be a strong actor in an environment of multilateral global governance. this resolution correctly implies that only a unified europe can achieve this goal. in addition, it mentions what is specifically needed to achieve these goals: strengthened eu competences and resources in csdp and cfsp, and a more prominent role for the vice-president / high representative in conflict resolution and crisis management. finally, the resolution stresses the importance of engaging eu citizens in the process, which is something i can only applaud.
in writing. the current financial situation calls for action at european level, but above all at global level. the fragmentation and diversity of international financial institutions make it difficult to achieve genuine global governance. regulatory cooperation should therefore be considerably strengthened, for example by ensuring better policy coordination between global institutions. common standards will have to be established. the european union must be at the forefront of these issues. by its construction it has a background which enables it to better understand the necessary dynamics which will enable the various international actors to cooperate. we need to be proactive and propose initiatives to respond, in particular, to the transformation of the shadow banking system and to systemic risks.
in writing. ‒ the report is clear: european action in international economic and financial forums must be streamlined, and more room for transparency and democracy. three of the points in this text seem to me particularly important. first, the stability of the international financial system depends on the observance of rules of conduct which apply to all. secondly, the change in scale and the international nature of these negotiations cannot justify opacity or a dilution of responsibilities. finally, the eu and the euro area must now, more than ever, give each other the means to defend their strategic interests. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'competent authority' to cover all the activities of the european union. they reaffirmed the central role of the european parliament, the democratic body of the union, in defining the guidelines of european positions. finally, they called for national parliaments to be able to play their full role in monitoring representatives in the member states.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report which calls for a rationalisation of the representation of the european union's interests in international financial organisations. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'competent authority' to cover the whole of the european union. beyond the imf alone, a gradual rationalization of the union's representation should be implemented over the next few years, first by means of enhanced coordination and then, after an evaluation, by unification of seats. parliament also calls for, and i welcome this, a thorough assessment of the dual presidencies of the european council and the european commission in the g20 to determine to what extent these arrangements weaken europe's credibility abroad.
in writing. ‒ it is important to strengthen regulatory cooperation at global level, with strong involvement of the european parliament. the text also raises concerns about the lack of coherence caused by the fragmentation and diversity of organisations/bodies and the delays in the implementation of rules and guidelines adopted at international level.
in writing. ‒ this report is very clear: the european union's action in international economic and financial institutions and bodies must be more streamlined, transparent and democratic. that is why i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ coastal fishing accounts for 80% of the european fleet. it is therefore an extremely important source of employment and income for many european regions. i therefore endorsed this report, which calls on the commission to take account of small-scale coastal fishing in island societies, to support innovative projects for coastal areas and to take measures to support groups of seafarers by encouraging their participation in all areas related to fishing.
in writing. i welcome the adoption by parliament of this report on innovation and diversification of small-scale coastal fishing in fisheries-dependent regions. the coastal fisheries are of crucial importance for their social, economic and environmental benefits and should be preserved as far as possible. innovation and diversification will both contribute to the economic development of coastal fishing areas. as regards innovation, improved collection of reliable and up-to-date data and their accessibility will be an essential prerequisite for the development of innovation. in terms of diversification, sustainable tourism has the potential to play a particularly beneficial role for coastal communities. marine and underwater tourism can combine awareness of the environment and biodiversity with the economic development of regions dependent on coastal fishing.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because coastal fishing in the european union is important in more than one way: not only is it a sector that provides jobs in coastal areas, but it is also socially and ecologically sustainable. the areas which depend on coastal fishing therefore require specific measures and support to ensure their growth and development. the 2013 regulation on the common fisheries policy focused on the economic development of these coastal regions. it also recognises the importance of the island regions on the high seas which depend on fisheries and which need to be supported so that they can survive and develop.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this proposal which asks the commission to adapt the definition of coastal and small-scale coastal or traditional fisheries to the socioeconomic characteristics and specificities of the different territories, and not just to the size and power of fishing vessels, because the existing eu provisions are unsatisfactory. we would also like to use regionalisation to adapt the definition of coastal fisheries to the specificities of each fishery.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because i believe that support for small-scale coastal fishing is important for the viability of certain communities and will lead to an improvement in maritime tourism on european islands.
in writing. ‒ i am realistic that a global problem requires a global solution. the climate crisis is the best example of this, and we need to move forward to live in a greener world. another is sustainable management of fisheries resources. this can only be achieved through international cooperation, through multilateral and bilateral agreements that will stand together for good governance of the seas and oceans. i voted in favour of this report because it will ensure coherence between fisheries policy, environmental policy, trade policy and development cooperation, while at the same time strengthening the social and environmental standards of the european union in its internal and external fisheries policy.
in writing. i welcome the adoption of the report on common rules for the application of the external dimension of the common fisheries policy, including fisheries agreements. the external fisheries policy of the union, whether in the framework of bilateral agreements or within the rfmos, will be of paramount importance for the conservation of global fisheries resources and hence for the sustainability of fishing opportunities. the responsible management of marine resources at global level can only be achieved jointly, through increased consultation and cooperation between countries. the union must therefore use all its influence and intensify its efforts to persuade them to apply to their fleet the principles which guide the union's policy in this area, including sustainability and the precautionary principle.
in writing. ‒ the european union is currently the world's largest market for fishery products. the marketing of fishery products in the union is subject to strict measures in terms of traceability, verification of catches and the fight against illegal, unreported and unregulated (iuu) fishing. the significant improvements that the iuu regulation has brought to the legislation and fishing activities of many countries around the world are proof that this 'top-down approach' can work, if the european union shows the political will and gives the necessary impetus and if it helps developing countries to meet the new requirements.
in writing. ‒ the union's new cfp is making significant progress and, if properly implemented, will improve standards in european long-distance fishing. in view of the treaty's requirements for development policies, we can only welcome this. given its influence in the world of fisheries, as a flag state and, more particularly, a trading state, the european union is well placed to encourage other actors, whether coastal or long-distance fishing states, to improve their own fisheries policies, not only in theory but also in practice. the considerable effectiveness with which the iuu regulation has improved the legislation and fishing activities of many countries around the world is proof that this 'top-down approach' can work, if the european union shows the necessary political will, sufficient leadership and objectivity, and if it helps developing countries to meet the new requirements. that is why recent signs of a weakening of the union's resolve to combat iuu fishing, notably by the elimination of korea, are worrying.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution because it will promote the sustainability of the european fisheries sector.
on behalf of the alde group. – mr president, the first thing i would like to do is to thank jean-claude juncker for his words for my country, belgium. i agree with him that what we must not do now is repeat the ritual of using strong words and making solemn declarations. now is the moment to act and to make a number of changes. i fully agree with him. this is the opposite of what mr kamall is saying; it is fragmentation which is the problem in europe, and our intelligence services and police services have to work better with each other. well, i can tell you, mr kamall, that we have been hearing this so-called recipe for decades. it is not a recipe. we need european capacities; this is also the lesson from history. in america the federal bureau of investigation was created in 1901 after the terrorist attack where president mckinley, the president of the usa at that time, was killed. in germany it was exactly the same story. the bundeskriminalamt was upgraded and was created as a federal agency after the rote armee fraktion attacks. that was their lesson from history, and it is time, mr kamall, that your group also learned that lesson, and that we created european capacities and european capabilities to solve the problem. let us be honest. let us face the reality. i have here the long list of all the terrorist attacks in recent years. in madrid the perpetrators were known to the french and british police. in london the attackers responsible for the bombing were followed and even partially arrested by the french police. the attack on a jewish museum in brussels was by a french terrorist known to the french authorities and even by the german intelligence services. it is the same story for charlie hebdo. they were known by the british authorities before the attacks. the same goes for abdeslam, who was not stopped at the roadblock in cambrai because the french did not have him in their files, while the belgians knew very well who he was. the same goes for what the germans did a few weeks before the attacks in paris. they found weapons and did not inform their french colleagues at that time. the same is now true again in the attacks in brussels, where apparently the swedish had information and did not send it to the belgian authorities. how many attacks, mr kamall, are still needed before everybody understands that we need a real investigation capacity at european level as quickly as possible? let us face the reality. we have the possibility to do so. terrorists do not know borders. it is our police services and our intelligence services who know borders. we have the possibility now to change that and to build that up, mr avramopoulos, because we have the file on europol. we have finished the second reading. my proposal is to use the second reading between parliament and council to make a few amendments; not to delay it again until the end of the year, but to act immediately in the coming weeks. there are three changes that can be made. first of all, change the regulation of europol in articles 1 and 3 and give them the possibility of having an investigation capacity and not only a coordination role. that is the first proposal. my second proposal is that we amend article 6 of the regulation to finally give europol the possibility to launch an investigation or oblige national authorities to do so. they do not even have that possibility today. finally, and maybe the most important problem, article 7 of the regulation, mr avramopoulos, currently says that the national authorities of europol have to filter the information to europol. i thought what they had to do was the opposite, namely to transfer the relevant data to europol. so my proposal is that, instead of talking again about coordination, coordination, cooperation, cooperation – enough of these words – we use the europol file to put that in place and also to change the role of the european prosecutor, because the european prosecutor cannot only be responsible for financial fraud. we need to change that so that the prosecutor is also responsible for transnational crimes like, for example, terrorism. so that is my proposal: rather than making minor fixes to an old europol file, to use it in the coming weeks to make a leap forward and to do what the americans did 115 years ago. mr president, i am definitely choosing to see the glass as half full this afternoon. it is a good time to protect the health of europeans: by saying no to the renewal of the authorization of glyphosate for 15 years proposed by the commission, and by voting instead for the resolution i am one of the authors of, our parliament has just shown that it is on the side of the citizens, that it is on the side of innovation and that it is on the side of less intensive agricultural practices. that's the role, that's our role, the role of politicians to make choices, especially when the science doesn't allow for conclusions and when the opinions of the experts who are charged with informing us differ. in conclusion, even if parliament is unfortunately just a figurehead here, our message is clear: we say no to the commission's maximalist option, to this blank cheque for 15 years and to the ban on one co-formulant out of every five hundred. the seven-year authorization voted this afternoon is far too broad in my view, but that is the important signal here, and it is clear that the commission must do its homework again and propose a new text to us, to the member states, who will be responsible for taking the decision.
mr president, what did we vote on? this is an objection that parliament has made to the european commission's proposal to renew the use of this dangerous substance, glyphosate, for 15 years. it was irresponsible, and we were right to object. let us keep the positive aspect of what we have done and the message we have sent today, which is that there is no question of renewing an authorization for a dangerous product for 15 years without further analysis. it also includes a ban on co-formulants, which increase the hazard of the product. but i regret the adoption of amendment no 11 requested by the ppe group, which is aimed at obtaining a renewal for a period of seven years. it's like we're crossing a river and we stop in the middle. it doesn't make sense! it distorts and weakens the message that should have been given today. that is why the belgian socialists ultimately abstained on this resolution, which they obviously consider relevant, while regretting, unfortunately, that the message loses its force because of the authorization granted for seven years.
in writing. ‒ as long as there are serious concerns about the carcinogenic effects of glyphosate, further scientific studies need to be carried out. anything else would be contrary to the precautionary principle in the eu. i therefore supported an amendment to that effect. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's financial resources are used to the full. it seems that there was a majority of doubt about the correct use of the herbicide, otherwise no restriction of the authorization for professional use would have been required. but when health is endangered, it is in home gardening as well as in agriculture. i therefore consider that parliament's present position is inconsistent. it is also essential that the commission and the member states finance research and innovation in cost-effective solutions in the field of pest control products. this is the only way to achieve a high level of protection of human and animal health and the environment in the future.
in writing. ‒ parliament has rightly objected to the commission's intention to renew the authorisation of the dangerous substance glyphosate for 15 years. unfortunately, the epp has tabled an amendment to obtain a seven-year licence. that is why the belgian socialists abstained in the final vote.
in writing. – i have voted against this resolution because it undermines the trust in the european food and safety authority efsa, a key eu agency. efsa was created in 2002 after it had become clear that there was great necessity of such an agency, as member states individually failed to effectively prevent a number of food crises. i strongly believe in the expertise and trustworthiness of this agency and therefore do not agree to the criticism that this resolution brings towards it. the main argument by opponents of glyphosate was its probability of being carcinogenic. after having taken knowledge of the fact that efsa has taken into account hundreds of studies, i have again no other choice than placing my trust in efsa. specifically, they base their studies on the fact that there is great difference in the study results depending on whether the product is used in a concentrated or a diluted form. in addition, glyphosate is of great importance to our agricultural sector and therefore for food security in the eu. in sum, i believe that emotions should not prevail over scientific evidence in such matter, and that it is therefore not the politician’s place to question efsa’s competences when it is clearly doing its job.
in writing. ‒ i did not support the resolution calling for the renewal of the licence of the active substance glyphosate for 7 years. there is no scientific consensus at present on the hot topic in this dossier, namely whether or not glyphosate is carcinogenic. the european food safety authority (efsa) and the international agency for research on cancer (iarc) of the world health organization have reached different conclusions. it is also possible that glyphosate has endocrine disrupting properties. i therefore call for more research to assess in depth the role of the so-called co-formulants or excipients. these excipients are an important explanation for the scientific disagreement. while efsa focused its analysis on the active substance glyphosate (in line with its mandate), iarc also analysed excipients. the starting points of the risk analyses are therefore different. everyone knows that apples are not like pears. the european commission also seems to be aware of this: why else would the commission link the possible renewal of the licence for glyphosate to a ban on tallowamine as a co-formulant? more research and more transparency are needed to remove the many uncertainties in this area in the interests of public health and the environment.
in writing. ‒ given the lingering concerns about the carcinogenicity and endocrine disrupting properties of glyphosate, i strongly disagreed with the renewal of its marketing authorisation for 15 years. i was in favour of a short extension period (2-5 years) of this authorisation, which should allow farmers in particular to have access to alternative solutions. as the first amendment put to the vote provided for a period of 7 years and for professional purposes only, i voted in favour of it for fear that the objection would be ultimately rejected.
the authorisation of the weed killer glyphosate in europe expires at the end of june. the commission then made a proposal to allow glyphosate to be re-authorised after 1 july for a period of 15 years. the possible harmful effects of glyphosate use have been the subject of heated debate between proponents and opponents of the weedkiller for many years. opponents claim that exposure to glyphosate is carcinogenic. proponents rely on studies that show no harmful effects. the commission based its proposal on the findings of efsa, which are based on numerous scientific reports indicating that glyphosate is unlikely to be harmful to health. in a non-binding opinion to the commission, a majority in the european parliament has called for the authorisation period for glyphosate to be limited to 7 years. personally, i am in favour of the commission's original proposal because the proposed deadline provides scope for continuing to innovate in plant protection in a sustainable and economically responsible way.
in writing. ‒ the european commission's proposal to renew the approval for the use of glyphosate (a substance contained in roundup in particular) for 15 years was not acceptable due to concerns related to its use in the composition of agricultural and household products. the european parliament's committee on the environment and public health had taken up the matter and a section of the scientific community had highlighted the likely health risks of the use of widely used products containing glyphosate. today, in the vote in plenary in strasbourg, this objection was not accepted and i regret it: a majority of members supported a renewal agreement for 7 years, whereas i was personally opposed to it. in my view, by granting the commission this 'semi-blanc-seing', the european parliament is sending the wrong signal. it is now up to the commission and then the states to take account of the reservations expressed and i will continue to advocate a reformulation of the proposal which takes into account the potential hazardousness of this substance, while allowing a sustainable transition for farmers and economically and ecologically responsible alternative products.
in writing. ‒ i voted against the objection to the renewal of the approval of the active substance glyphosate. while many have pointed to the potential carcinogenic risks to mammals, and thus to humans, the european food safety authority stated in 2015 that glyphosate is unlikely to pose a carcinogenic hazard to us. the current seven-year extension contains the dissolving condition that if it should still prove that this substance does have carcinogenic effects, this decision can be reversed.
in writing. ‒ the recent attacks on european soil have deeply shocked citizens around the world who believe in a model of society based on freedom and tolerance. i voted in favour of this report because i believe that the european union must provide concrete answers to this security challenge without, however, impeding the exercise of public freedoms. in the face of the macabre ingenuity of terrorist organisations such as daesh, the political authorities must find the means to prevent new 13 november and 22 march incidents while preserving fundamental freedoms.
in writing. i welcome the adoption of this report, which puts the european union's primary missions back at the heart of the concerns. the preservation and defence of peace, humanist and european values, the promotion of global governance, respect for international law and the stabilisation of the immediate neighbourhood are all part of an ambitious and hopeful european policy. the threats facing all member states and the many challenges they face require solidarity, cohesion and consistency in action by each member state. the threat of terrorism, the migration crisis, financial crime and cybercrime all call for a structured and comprehensive response from the european union, for increased cooperation in defence and security, and for the eu to position itself as a strategic, effective and indispensable international actor and partner.
in writing. ‒ this report, entitled 'the european union in a changing global environment - a more connected, contested and complex world', is the european parliament's contribution to the new overall eu security strategy that the vice-president/high representative was tasked by the european council to develop last summer. this report aims to: defend europe's states, societies and values the union's primary objective is to ensure the security of its citizens and territory, while preserving its values and societal model and defending its fundamental interests; - stabilise europe's wider neighbourhood (the union must assume its responsibilities by closing the security gap in its neighbourhood and in our neighbours' neighbours and respecting its enlargement commitments); - become a more present player in a multipolar world the union should aim to become a 'decision-maker' that sets effective rules for global multilateral governance, which requires enhanced cooperation with regional actors, in particular on global threats, and finally greater interaction with european citizens and national actors.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution proposing elements for a new strategy in this area. the european union aims to preserve peace, safeguard its values and promote the well-being of its peoples by guaranteeing the security of its citizens and territory. the union should therefore ensure its internal and external resilience, its ability to anticipate, prevent and respond to foreseeable challenges and threats (by being ready to take swift action in the face of unforeseeable challenges and threats) and its ability to recover from different types of attacks, while preserving its security of energy and raw materials supply and taking into account, in doing so, the effects of climate change, which require urgent action, given the union's leading role in the global fight against climate change and in supporting sustainable development. a new strategy is therefore essential.
in writing. ‒ this report reflects the new global strategy of the european union in the light of today's global challenges. i voted for this report because the union must be able to meet the challenges of the future. strengthening our defence capabilities and the exchange of information between intelligence services is essential to our security.
in writing. ‒ in 2007, the european union strengthened its relations with the countries of central asia (kazakhstan, kyrgyz republic, tajikistan, turkmenistan, uzbekistan) with the aim of strengthening ties and cooperation in the face of common threats and challenges. in 2012, a follow-up report supported the relevance of this strategy between these countries and the european union. i voted in favour of this new implementation because i think it is essential to have diplomatic relations which are stable over time and offer greater peace for the member states. this mutual commitment is also important for security issues, which are now taking a prominent place in meetings between european and asian actors.
in writing. – central asia is becoming increasingly important to the eu. it is therefore that i voted in favour of this resolution. our interests in the region are of both a political and economic nature. the resolution reiterates what the eu envisages in central asia, which is peace, prosperity, democracy and environmental sustainability. positive relations between us will lead to economic and other benefits to both of us. while central asia has important resources to offer, the eu has the technology and know-how to build up the region’s infrastructure and to support it. thus economic integration, trade and sustainable development are key. however, democracy, the rule of law and human rights also remain at the centre of the discussion. especially with regard to gender equality there is still work to be done. but i strongly believe that through economic prosperity and innovation, the first steps will be taken in the modernisation of the region in the direction of gender equality. the resolution also recognises that there are many differences across the region. therefore, i am delighted to see that a list has been included, with specific issues regarding every country in the region, and thereby recognising their individual situation.
in writing. in an increasingly interconnected world, central asia is a region of growing strategic importance for the eu because of its geographical location at the crossroads between europe, asia and the middle east and its significant energy resources. the strengthening of cooperation between the european union and central asia is mutually beneficial in achieving fundamental objectives such as peace in afghanistan, an effective fight against terrorism and the development of dynamic trade and economic relations between our two regions. for most central asian states, relations with the union are defined by partnership and cooperation agreements. given the political and economic heterogeneity of the central asian countries and the low level of interregional cooperation, europe must favour a targeted approach, based on the needs and interests of the individual countries, while giving priority to european values. the progress of the central asian countries towards democracy is positive, although much remains to be done in the areas of the rule of law, good governance, the fight against violence against women, etc.

in writing. ‒ on 1 february 2016, the world health organisation declared the zika virus outbreak to be a public health emergency of global concern. cases have been reported sporadically in africa, the americas, asia, the pacific, and in european regions such as martinique, french guiana, guadeloupe, and saint martin. i voted in favour of this report because it takes account of two action plans to combat this devastating virus: on the one hand, action to raise awareness and promote appropriate behaviour and, on the other hand, further medical research. it is essential that the commission prevents the spread of zika in the european union and helps the countries already affected
in writing. – the reason i voted in favour of this resolution is obvious. as both policy makers and citizens have probably realised in recent months there has been an outbreak of the zika virus in latin-america, posing a potential threat to other regions of the world. the resolution reminds us that the european centre for disease prevention and control (ecdc) has stated that around 80% of the infections remain asymptomatic. in addition, it calls for specific action, for example, for the set-up of improved communication plans and increased research on preventive measures. in addition, i strongly welcome the trust that is put in the ecdc and its efforts to continuously monitor the situation and the commission decision to increase the funding available to spend an additional eur 10 million on researching the virus. in the end, the resolution shows us the importance of continuous research and innovation. in this case, it will save lives.
in writing. the rapid spread of the zika virus, its modes of transmission and its serious consequences for public health, especially for women and children, make it a serious threat. while the who believes that there is a plausible link between the contamination of pregnant women and the increase in cases of microcephaly in children and that a vaccine is not yet available, i strongly encourage the implementation of preventive measures that will preserve the health, well-being and comfort of these two most vulnerable groups. in this context, i am enthusiastically in favour of better information for women on reproductive health, safe access to abortion and the use of condoms. i would also like to draw attention to the essential symbolic dimension of these measures. through these, we are sending a positive message by advocating for women's rights to their bodies while promoting and working to improve health in countries affected by the virus. the same way we're educating our populations about the risks of pandemics.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution calling for the european union to have an action plan on the zika virus. the zika virus is transmitted by mosquito bites (of the aedes aegypti type) and is suspected of causing malformations in the foetus of infected pregnant women and causing guillain-barré syndrome. it was declared a "public health emergency of global concern" by the world health organization (who) on 1 february 2016. the resolution calls for more coordination in the eu in the face of this virus. it recommends, for example, that the european centre for disease prevention and control establish an expert committee on tropical communicable diseases to effectively coordinate and supervise all necessary measures in the eu. it also called on the commission to present an action plan 'with sufficient targets for the free distribution of mechanical barriers, such as nets to protect against mosquito bites and condoms to prevent sexual transmission'.
in writing. ‒ zika virus is mainly transmitted to humans through the bite of an infected mosquito of the genus aedes, mainly the species aedes aegypti in tropical regions, which also transmits dengue, chikungunya and yellow fever. the european centre for disease prevention and control has assessed that in the absence of treatment or vaccine, and because the mosquitoes that transmit the zika virus bite both indoors and outdoors, mostly during the day, prevention currently relies on personal protection measures, such as wearing long-sleeved t-shirts and permethrin-treated trousers, sleeping and resting in rooms with mosquito nets or air-conditioning, or using a mosquito net.
in writing. ‒ unfortunately, the zika virus is spreading rapidly in latin america. that is why i supported this report calling on the european union to take up the fight against this virus. the european union must support research into and development of a treatment and a vaccine.
in writing. ‒ i have endorsed this joint resolution for at least three reasons. first, it recalls at the outset that it is essential to guarantee full respect for the common european values set out in article 2 as well as the rule of law, democratic principles and human rights. too many member states seem to forget this! secondly, it supports the commission's decision to launch a structured dialogue on poland under the rule of law framework, which should clarify whether there is a systemic threat to democratic values and the rule of law in poland. thirdly, it said it expected the commission to monitor the situation in all member states in the same way as regards respect for democracy, the rule of law and fundamental rights, thus avoiding double standards and reporting to parliament.
in writing. – i voted in favour of the resolution on poland for the following reasons. while we must always adhere to the principle of subsidiarity, it is also the eu’s responsibility to uphold those values enshrined in article 2 of the teu. as this resolution states, these values are effectively under threat in poland. it rightly mentions that the paralysis of poland’s constitutional tribunal is a danger to many of these values and to poland’s constitutional democracy. in addition, not safeguarding these principles would be a violation of the charter of fundamental rights and the echr. in sum, i can only support a resolution that calls on the government of poland to respect, publish and fully implement the constitutional tribunal’s decisions, thereby respecting poland’s constitutional framework, and restoring the rule of law.
in writing. with the venice commission of the council of europe having just delivered its conclusions and the dialogue between the european commission and the polish authorities continuing, it was crucial for the european parliament to denounce the paralysis of the constitutional tribunal and the threats it poses to the rule of law in poland. the rule of law and the balance of power are the basis of any democratic society and principles to which all the member states of the european union have subscribed. the union's response to the constitutional crisis we are witnessing in poland today must be tailored to the seriousness of its potential impact on our european values. as regards the amendments in plenary relating to the draft abortion law, i and my group have chosen to abstain in order to keep the text focused on the political and constitutional crisis. i would like to add my voice to that of all those who are most concerned about this bill which would ban abortion altogether. such a retreat in women's rights has no place in europe and parliament will therefore have to look into this matter.
in writing. ‒ the attitude and decisions of the polish government are not only undermining relations between poland and the european union, they are shaking the rule of law at its very foundation, which is democratic values. the dialogue with this member state must be continued in order to bring it back to reason. i am concerned, however, that the ruling political party in warsaw, pis, is ignoring the commission's hand in refusing to review the reform of the functioning of the constitutional tribunal and, worse, putting pressure on the judges who rightly consider it unconstitutional. as mr timmermans has said, we cannot allow 'two parallel legal systems' within the union. it has been a month since the venice commission of the council of europe called into question the measures decided by the government in power. in the absence of rapid and significant progress, the rule of law mechanism will have to apply to sanctions against warsaw.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution because it contains a strong message from the european parliament to the current polish government. the resolution urges the polish government to publish the judgment of the constitutional tribunal and to comply with the venice commission's recommendations on the reform of the functioning of the polish constitutional court.
today, we finally take a step forward. the 1995 data protection directive, after more than 20 years, no longer corresponded to the needs and realities of the present day. it is therefore good that we have agreed today on a new instrument adapted to the challenges of the present time. this harmonization is a step forward for consumers and businesses alike. consumers will know their rights and enjoy adequate legal protection and redress throughout the eu. companies are given clarity on what they can and cannot do. they can also carry out cross-border activities more easily. the right to privacy and the internal market are thus a complementary force. one small note, though: the key to the success of this regulation is clearly in its implementation, which must be done in an appropriate manner, especially for smes.
i think that there are very few people in the chamber to debate matters on which so much ink has already been spilled. i can tell you that we, as liberals and defenders of the freedom and privacy of citizens, are actually quite happy with this regulation and this directive and that they are being adapted to the present situation. moreover, this is absolutely necessary if we are to invest in our entrepreneurs, in our industry and in our internal market. moreover, it is absolutely necessary if we are to fight terrorism. this will make it easier for our police departments to share that data. for us liberals, therefore, the agendering of pnr in conjunction with these files was very important. i hope that a few more people will come to the plenary before the debate on the pnr.
we all know that fighters from syria or iraq are returning to europe with plans to carry out deadly attacks. the pnr system is crucial in the fight against terrorism because it helps us to detect such individuals. the pnr system maps behavioural patterns and thus provides our own security services with a wealth of information. the member states have already done their homework. but the european parliament was unnecessarily delayed. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council and parliament on the subject of the future of the european union. we now need short-term solutions, such as the exchange of personal data from passenger flights. some parties considered that linking pnr to the data protection package was essential. however, the pnr file contains sufficient guarantees for data protection. the vote on the pnr has therefore been unnecessarily delayed for five years. i hope that all the groups will show common sense tomorrow and prefer security to political games. we don't have to give up our privacy for that. moreover, the data protection package is almost complete. there is no reason to delay or vote against this case any longer.
mr president, the nrp we are discussing today is neither a magic potion against terrorism, as some would have us believe, nor a freedom-destroying monster, as others denounce it. the pnr is only one instrument, or rather one of the instruments needed to help our intelligence and security services collect and process information useful in the fight against terrorists and major criminals. of course -- and we know this -- this instrument is not perfect. i am sorry to say that this is not a true european pnr, but 28 national pnrs, which have yet to be linked. i regret that the exchange of information between them is not compulsory and that the transposition period is too long. but i'd rather have a tool, even if it's imperfect, if it can save lives, than no tool at all. and i don't see why we wouldn't want to collect for ourselves the information that we've been passing on, even today, for years, in the united states, canada and australia. yes, i will vote in favour of the nrp and reject the amendments, indeed all the amendments, which could jeopardise its entry into force.
i am actually glad that we can finally vote on the pnr tomorrow, although i have to say that i do feel that the mountain has given birth to an elephant. yes, it is good that passenger data is being exchanged, but i do regret a little that there will be 28 databases, that the countries themselves can decide whether to share the data voluntarily and that this will not be mandatory. but it is so. rome wasn't built in a day, either! we shall therefore vote tomorrow with conviction on the pnr and data protection files. but i 've heard it here many times today: if we think that pnr will be the panacea against terrorism, then we will have to endure a lot of attacks. we must, ladies and gentlemen of the council and commission, commit ourselves to what we heard in the debate yesterday: the european union must be able to take action to combat terrorism.

member of the commission.– mr president, i would like to start by thanking the rapporteur, mr meszerics, for this very comprehensive report, which confirms once again that poverty is a complex phenomenon with several causes, such as the increasing household costs in europe. i share your concerns about the rise in the number of people at risk of poverty or social exclusion in the european union. between 2008 and 2013 the prolonged crisis exacerbated the existing social challenges: poverty, exclusion and inequality. as a result, instead of progressing, we have drifted further away from the europe 2020 target for reducing poverty. however, there are now some signs of stabilisation, and with concerted efforts we can still make real progress. i take note of your recommendation to invest fully in the fight against poverty and social exclusion – social inclusion is, of course, what we want. the commission has put social fairness at the core of our agenda, and work has already started to deliver on this commitment. i am convinced that it is only by ensuring that social considerations are better integrated in all of the european policy areas that we can truly achieve the social europe that we want. i am glad that your report supports our commitment to ensuring a social triple a for the union. the european pillar of social rights lies at the core of our efforts to achieve that social triple a. the commission launched a wide-ranging consultation on 8 march. we are counting on you and on parliament to contribute to this discussion on the social values and rights that should underpin the social model in the 21st century. the draft european pillar of social rights puts a strong focus on fighting poverty and social exclusion. it sets out principles to ensure access to adequate social protection, including minimum income, social housing and activating and enabling benefits and services. it emphasises the work-life balance and family-friendly policies such as childcare and long—term care. greater prominence is also being given to social considerations in and during the whole european semester process. we acknowledge the rapporteur’s recommendation to carry out impact assessments of national minimum income schemes and we would like to stress that over the years the commission has provided policy guidance to the member states. i would like to mention here the 2008 recommendation on active inclusion, the 2013 social investment package and the various country—specific recommendations addressed to several member states within the european semester process. furthermore, the commission is providing support to greece to help it phase in a guaranteed minimum income scheme. in 2015 the commission finalised a pilot project aimed at developing a methodology for comparable reference budgets across the member states. a second phase of this project will be launched later this year. furthermore, the commission has been funding the development of the european minimum income network. i am glad that the report highlights the importance of skills. i would like to stress that one of the most profound challenges we are facing, and one of our key goals, is to make sure that people in europe have skills for jobs – skills for jobs which will improve their life chances. this will be at the core of the proposal that i will be presenting on a new skills agenda for europe. i also take note of your call to hold a summit on poverty reduction. over the last 15 years, the commission has been helping to organise the european meetings of people experiencing poverty. these annual gatherings aim to step up the participation of people experiencing poverty in policy—making processes at local, national and eu level. i can confirm that they facilitate exchanges and mutual learning, stimulate joint projects and aim to assess different approaches to combating poverty in the light of experience on the ground. they feed directly into the annual convention for inclusive growth to ensure that the voices of people experiencing poverty are heard. they have also been tackling homelessness, which you rightly mention in your report as an extreme form of social exclusion. we are currently finalising an eu—wide study on housing evictions. another study on cost—efficient housing policies will be ready by june this year. we have launched a joint project with the oecd to build a housing database entry and we are working together with the mutual information system on social protection (missoc) and eurostat to further improve housing data. a social experimentation peer review of housing first was hosted in march this year by belgium. finally, we take note of your recommendation to submit a communication on energy poverty. as announced in the communication setting out a new deal for energy consumers, the commission is exploring how to improve european union-wide data collection and monitoring of energy poverty. furthermore, with the review of the energy efficiency directive and the energy performance of buildings directive, the commission intends to focus on customer protection, following up the analysis of the member states’ implementation of their national action plans for the protection of vulnerable energy consumers. in conclusion, i would like to stress once more that it is the commission’s firm intention to steer the union more firmly towards social fairness. this means that no one should be left behind. this is a social, political and economic imperative. i therefore express our strong commitment to using all means at the union’s disposal to fight poverty and social exclusion. i am very grateful that this report is stimulating the debate and helping us to stay on the right path.
