in writing. ‒ i have of course approved this regulation which will give citizens more power over the use and processing of their personal data. the new rules include provisions on the right to be forgotten, the clear and explicit consent of the data subject to the use of his or her personal data, the right to be informed in the event of data breaches, a stricter implementation of fines of up to 4% of a company's worldwide turnover, and the guarantee that privacy policies are explained in clear and understandable language.
in writing. – personal data is becoming increasingly important and so is its processing. as a legislator, i can only approve of adopting a regulation that increases the protection of our citizens in this regard, while at the same time ensuring the free movement of data. it will facilitate the well-functioning of the digital single market and ensure the protection of the eu citizen’s personal data. to name only a few of these positive consequences; this regulation will give increased legal certainty to businesses across the eu, while giving the consumer the right of being informed when his/her information was to be hacked. in addition, there will be a smoother, easier exchange of information between both member states and these businesses. i put my trust in the committee on civil liberties, justice and home affairs (libe), which has negotiated this deal thoroughly with the council, resulting in an almost full consensus.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the agreement reached between parliament and the council on a new data protection regulation, better adapted to the digital age and replacing the current directive, which dates from 1995. the provisions of the regulation create a high and uniform level of data protection across the union, thereby providing greater clarity and certainty for businesses. they also give citizens greater control over their own private information and allow them to decide for themselves what personal information they wish to share. these new rules include provisions on the right to be forgotten, the data subject's clear and explicit consent to the use of their personal data, the right to transfer their data to another service provider, the right to be informed in the event of data breaches, the guarantee that privacy policies are explained in clear and understandable language, and a stricter framework to discourage breaches of the rules with fines of up to 4% of a company's total global turnover.
in writing. i welcome the adoption by parliament of the general data protection regulation. the new regulation, which updates legislation dating back to 1995, has the merit of adapting the protection of personal data to the new realities of the digital age and its consequences for the personal data of natural persons. these new rules strengthen both the rights of the persons whose personal data are processed and the obligations of those who process them. the legal certainty and the penalties for infringements have improved considerably, and i welcome this.

in writing. ‒ i have approved this directive, which will set minimum standards for data processing for police purposes in each member state for the first time. this should make it possible to increase significantly the exchange of personal data between law enforcement authorities in the member states and thus to work more effectively in the prevention of terrorist acts, while respecting fundamental rights.
in writing. – a coherent data protection framework also plays an important role in the prevention of crime. having common standards as to how to share this information will only facilitate this. in essence, clear, cohesive, uniform and transparent legislation was needed in order to create a pleasant and efficient business environment. at the same time, we have now set up a framework within which our government agencies can operate, using data, in order to prevent crime. this precarious balance is the result of long negotiations.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the directive on the transfer of data for police and judicial purposes, which for the first time sets minimum standards for the processing of such data within each member state. the new rules aim to protect individuals by providing clear rights and limits on the transfer of data for the purposes of the prevention and detection of criminal offences, the investigation and prosecution of criminal offences or the execution of criminal penalties. they also include safeguards and preventive measures against threats to public security, while facilitating easier and more effective cooperation between law enforcement authorities. the new directive will apply to both cross-border and strictly national processing of such data and leaves member states the possibility to provide for stricter safeguards than those set out in the directive. it also provides for the right of data subjects to obtain compensation if they suffer damage as a result of processing which does not comply with the rules.

in writing. ‒ i have approved this provisional statement of parliament's 2017 revenue. the report stresses that the european parliament must have sufficient resources to fulfil its primary role as a legislative body and budgetary authority and that, in the current economic context, these resources must be managed with rigour, pragmatism and efficiency. the report also notes that, while the desire to ensure a sufficient level of parliamentary funding is appropriate for the exercise of european democracy, efforts to find ways of making savings and making even more efficient use of public funds are strongly encouraged. it also stressed that the bulk of parliament's budget and its annual indexation were set by legal or contractual obligations which the european parliament could not influence during the budgetary procedure.

in writing. ‒ like almost all of the alde group, i voted against the estimates of the european parliament's budget for 2017 for three reasons. from a procedural point of view, it is surprising that the last arbitration resulted from a singular head-to-head between the rapporteur of the committee on budgets (whose competence i do not dispute) and the secretary-general of parliament without any involvement of the fictitious rapporteurs representing the various political groups. the reductions in the content do not seem to me appropriate in view of the way parliament works. others, more justified, have fallen into the trap. as far as the building policy and safety are concerned, no serious information has been provided to the committee on budgets to justify the amounts requested. all these reasons, in my view, clearly justify my voting against.
in writing. ‒ in difficult times, budgetary, economic and social, when great efforts are required of european citizens, it is the duty of every public authority to set a good example. the budget must be fair and balanced, and it must first of all take account of its own expenditure. and in this respect, this report is also absolutely lacking. the estimate of the revenue and expenditure of the european parliament for the financial year 2017 is not lower but is 3.9% higher than in 2016, according to this report. in view of the terrorist threat, additional security measures are indeed necessary. but the budget for this must first be sought within the existing resources. moreover, an increase of 3.9% is completely disproportionate. parliament has again failed to examine sufficiently where it can work more efficiently, and the report has also failed to look for the cheapest option in new proposals. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament should be given the right to vote on the proposals for directives and to adopt them. the n-va meps therefore voted against this report.

in writing. – i abstained from voting on this resolution. the objective of the initiative is righteous and a target to work to. household incomes should increase and the fight against poverty is a continuous concern of us all. for all of these reasons, i did not vote against the resolution. however, i do not believe that the proposals made will reach this objective. they go against the free market principle and offer therefore only short-term solutions for which we will pay a high price in the long run. in sum, my goal is to reduce poverty and to increase household income. in addition, i completely agree that renewable energy should play a more prominent role in our lives. however, the only way to achieve these goals is research and development which will lead to employment. this requires large sums of investment that can only be attracted by creating an investor-friendly environment in a free market economy.
europe has set itself ambitious energy targets. to meet international environmental commitments while reducing its dependence on energy supplies from neighbouring countries, the eu is seeking to increase the use of renewable energy sources, optimise energy efficiency and reduce greenhouse gases. in pursuing these objectives, we cannot lose sight of the other ambition of europe, namely to guarantee decent living conditions for all european citizens. and that is why we must build bridges between the eu's energy policy and its social policy. the introduction of a european moratorium on the shutdown of heating during winter can save vulnerable families from social exclusion. however, to reduce the risk of energy poverty, support for structural measures such as energy efficiency in housing is needed. equal access to energy and the benefits of energy efficiency, and thus reducing energy poverty, will also make it easier for the eu and its member states to meet ambitious energy and climate targets.
in writing. ‒ the fight against poverty in all its forms requires us to overcome partisan divisions. it must be a priority for ethical and humanitarian reasons, but also because poverty is a real economic waste. the main tools in this struggle are the development of employment and the guarantee of an income that allows a decent living. the eu 2020 objectives are far from being achieved. if the european union is to achieve its 'triple a' social status, it is essential to reverse this trend. we need to be aware that poor households are particularly impacted by different types of costs. this is the case for energy or housing, but also for food, healthcare or public services. we need coherent policies that integrate all the drivers of poverty. families living in poverty do not need speeches; they need concrete and practical actions. i hope that this own-initiative report will be understood by the commission and the member states as a call to action.
in writing. ‒ the n-va delegation fully supports the european fight against poverty, but regrets the approach envisaged in the report. she therefore abstained. the n-va believes that member states should achieve european poverty reduction targets, and the union has a supporting role in this. however, the principle of subsidiarity requires that member states be left free to decide how they achieve these objectives. the n-va cannot therefore support a european minimum income scheme. the report also takes a rather one-sided approach to increasing public spending, without, for example, focusing on avoiding the 'unemployment trap'. the commission has also proposed that the member states should be able to provide for the possibility of a reduction in the amount of energy consumption in the form of a reduction in the amount of energy used in the production of electricity. the aim is to make people self-reliant rather than dependent on benefits; benefits should go to those who really need them.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the text which calls on the commission and the member states to invest fully in the fight against poverty and social exclusion and to adopt an integrated approach to tackle its various forms through a comprehensive approach combining economic policies, education policies, employment policies, energy policies, transport policies and social policies on the basis of best practice. we call, among other things, on the member states to sign a moratorium on winter heating cuts so as to ensure that no household can be without electricity for a defined winter period and that those who are without electricity are reconnected, stressing that the costs arising from this are by nature a matter of public responsibility since social policies are primarily the responsibility of the authorities. states should also assess the measures needed to meet the thermal comfort standards set by the world health organisation.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report which underlines that private sector investment in development can contribute to the achievement of the un sustainable development goals. but the report also argues that this should be achieved by private sector commitments to good governance, poverty reduction and wealth creation through sustainable investment, reduction of inequalities, and action to promote human rights, environmental standards and the empowerment of local economies. the report also stresses the importance of supporting the local private sector in developing countries, for example through access to finance and action to promote entrepreneurship.
in writing. ‒ this report, which i voted for, takes up a commission communication and proposes a framework for action to strengthen the role of the private sector in developing countries. the private sector provides 90% of jobs in developing countries and is therefore a key partner in the fight against poverty. the private sector also plays a key role as an investor in sustainable agricultural production (and thus attempting to meet the challenge of feeding 9 billion people by 2050...). a recent evaluation of eu private sector development assistance between 2004 and 2010 confirmed the commission's significant contribution to private sector development in partner countries and identified ways to improve future programmes and strategies, in particular with a view to focusing on decent job creation and mainstreaming private sector participation in all eu support activities.
in writing. ‒ the increasing pressure on public finances and the need for additional resources to address global challenges is leading european policymakers to increasingly see the private sector as a co-development actor. the report also calls for greater public-private partnership and the creation of an attractive investment climate in developing countries. but as greens, we do not blindly believe in the private sector and the trickle-down effect of private investment in the development sector. private funding can be useful, but it should never be a substitute for public development funds. public resources and public-public partnerships must remain the first option of the european union's development efforts. the commission can only use the private sector as a second option and under strict conditions. the deployment of private resources must be transparent and contribute to the central objectives of european development policy. human rights violations and tax evasion must be avoided at all times. thanks to an alternative majority, we have substantially revised the pro-business discourse in this report. it now takes account of the dangers of private involvement and provides for the necessary safeguards. only under these conditions can we see a role for the private sector.
in writing. - i voted for the text. indeed, as we begin to reassess our commitments abroad, the role of the private sector in development is increasingly a prominent part of the debate. despite many successes, it is estimated that annual global spending in developing countries will be usd 2.4 trillion higher than it is today - a burden that the already heavily taxed taxpayer is unlikely to be willing to bear. as imperfect as a public-private partnership may be, there is no development project in the world today that is not implemented in consultation and cooperation with private investors. moreover, population growth and rising incomes in developing countries are expected to lead to a strong growth in the global middle class, estimated at 5 billion people by 2030, leading to a significant increase in consumption levels. demand for food, water and energy is expected to increase by 50%, 40% and 30% respectively by 2030. it's time to act.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report, which aims to mobilise private capital in new and innovative ways to fight global poverty, as part of a broader approach to development.

in writing. i support the council resolution on the conclusion of a protocol amending the euro-mediterranean agreement on air services between the eu and israel to take account of the accession of croatia to the european union. this agreement was negotiated on the basis of the council decision adopted in april 2008 and signed on 10 june 2013, and is the first step in establishing a common airspace with israel, a major partner in the mediterranean. the vote today will allow croatia to join the eu-israel common mediterranean airspace agreement and to include some linguistic adaptations to it. this new protocol is therefore required and is in line with the act of accession of croatia to the union negotiated in 2013 and with european council decision 13351/12 and forms part of the 'acquis communautaire', which is essential for european integration.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the draft council decision on the conclusion, on behalf of the union and its member states, and provisional application of a protocol amending the euro-mediterranean agreement on air services between the european union and its member states, of the one part, and the government of the state of israel, of the other part, to take account of the accession to the european union of the republic of croatia. the purpose of the protocol is to enable the republic of croatia to become a party to the euro-mediterranean agreement on air services between the european union and its member states, of the one part, and the government of the state of israel, of the other part, and to define the linguistic adaptations to be made to the agreement by reason of the accession of croatia. the protocol does not make any substantial changes to the euro-mediterranean air services agreement.
in writing. ‒ with this agreement, croatia will have to respect the convention on mutual assistance and cooperation between customs administrations, as all eu member states do.
in writing. in view of the act of accession of croatia to the union and the proper observance of the procedures based on article 34 teu, i welcome the recommendation of the commission and the council on the accession of croatia to the convention of 18 december 1997 on mutual assistance and cooperation between customs administrations. although this recommendation is only aimed at determining a date for accession to the convention, i am convinced that administrative customs cooperation is essential to the proper external and internal functioning of the union in order to achieve an ever more integrated europe. i also believe that we must facilitate the accession of new member states to the international and european conventions and treaties which form the union's acquis communautaire.

in writing. ‒ following the unanimous decision of the committee on legal affairs, i have approved the waiver of mr piecha's parliamentary immunity.
in writing. i voted in favour of the waiver of mr piecha's parliamentary immunity in respect of a traffic offence committed in poland before the start of his term as an mep. it is true that parliamentary immunity is important and fundamental to allow members to exercise their mandate and all that follows from it in an independent and unhindered manner. there is a clear article to that effect (article 9 protocol 7) in our code of privileges and immunities of the european union, which guarantees the immunity of each member of parliament within his national territory, provided that the act in question is drawn up in the course of the performance of his duties. in the present case, that is not the case, since the infringement was committed before the beginning of the term of office of the person concerned. furthermore, mr piecha admitted the facts as he agreed to pay the fine for the infringement.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the waiver of mr boleslaw g. piecha's immunity, so that the polish judiciary can carry out its work, in strict respect of the rights of the defence, on the understanding that this request, which relates to speeding in urban areas, is clearly not linked to mr piecha's office as a member of parliament and is not motivated by the desire to harm the member's political activity.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the waiver of the immunity of my colleague for the simple reason that he will be able to explain himself before his national court.
in writing. ‒ this resolution brings the debate on how to safeguard the interests of children in particular situations within the union. the resolution proposes new approaches to judicial proceedings relating to the placement of a child, the placement and adoption of children, and also to cases of crossborder parental abduction. it is obviously essential to protect children and to have harmonized systems for child welfare services, especially in an open europe!
in writing. i welcome the adoption by parliament of this resolution on the protection of the best interests of the child throughout the union on the basis of petitions to the european parliament. this resolution, which highlights the large number of petitions relating to children received by parliament, focuses in particular on crossborder cases involving children. these cases, whether they concern conflicts between parents of different nationalities, kidnappings, placements or adoptions, require full cooperation between the member states. in this respect, the lack of mutual recognition between member states of decisions involving children, such as adoption decisions, is a shortcoming which needs to be addressed as soon as possible. another area addressed by the resolution, which cannot suffer from a lack of cooperation between member states, is that of child abductions with a cross-border dimension. it is therefore imperative that we exploit the full potential of police and judicial cooperation to strengthen our action and to always act in the best interests of the child.
in writing. ‒ in this resolution, which was voted yesterday, we asked for specialised chambers within the high courts or crossborder mediation bodies to ensure the rapid handling of crossborder cases involving children. the text, approved with a show of hands, recommends that the legal loopholes in the brussels ii regulation on family law be closed. the european parliament called on the member states to improve their legal cooperation and on the commission to help provide clear information to all european citizens on legal procedures relating to children, such as parental rights in different european countries. parliament also stressed that children caught in crossborder family disputes have the right to maintain regular and direct contact with their parents, unless this contact is harmful to them.
in writing. ‒ the n-va delegation believes that the best interests of the child always come first and has therefore supported this report. the n-va stands for an inclusive society with a tailor-made equality policy that takes account of all the various target groups. this applies to all genders and particularly to the rights of children. the report contains many good elements. it emphasises that the best interests of the child must be taken into account in all decisions and at all levels, while respecting the principle of non-discrimination. the report is concerned with the fact that it seems to be at times contrary to the principle of subsidiarity. for the n-va, this principle is fundamental and policy must always be conducted at the appropriate level.
in writing. ‒ with today's vote we wanted to invite member states to set up monitoring and evaluation systems (with relevant socioeconomic and nationality-based statistics) within a national coordination framework on cross-border conflicts involving children. we also recommend that the commission coordinate the transfer of information between the relevant authorities in the member states.

in writing. ‒ the agreement should allow railway undertakings and manufacturers of railway equipment across the union to achieve further economies of scale. this will reduce administrative costs and speed up procedures, while maintaining the current high level of security. it will also significantly reduce the volume of national rules in areas where harmonised regulation at union level has been put in place.
in writing. the european parliament approved, at first reading, the council's position with a view to adopting a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on the european union agency for railways and repealing regulation no 881/2004. it is essential to improve the quality and efficiency of rail services. significant changes have already been made through the three previous railway packages. these have helped to increase the competitiveness and interoperability of european railways while maintaining a high level of safety. unfortunately, the sector still has some shortcomings in terms of competition, discrimination and the absence of a liberalized, dynamic and business-friendly environment. in order to improve the performance and efficiency of the sector, the commission has presented this fourth railway package. the proposal for a regulation on the tfa is the technical part of this package. this is to improve the technical compatibility of infrastructure, rolling stock, signalling and other parts of the railway system and to simplify the procedures for authorising rolling stock for use on the whole railway network.
in writing. ‒ the european railway agency (era), created in 2004 and located in valenciennes, needs to be strengthened. this is in any case the choice made by the members of the european parliament this afternoon with the adoption of the fourth railway package. today, the management of technical and safety requirements is shared between the tsa and the national authorities, which increases costs, especially for new companies in the railway sector. the commission believes that the package of measures (single window, enhanced role in the implementation of the european rail traffic management system (ertms) etc.) should allow for a 20% acceleration of procedures for new entrants and a 20% reduction in the costs and time required for the issuing of authorisations for rolling stock by 2025. that's an estimated savings of 500 million euros. the other important measures of the agreement reached by parliament and the council in june 2015 include the dual system for the issuing of vehicle authorisations and safety certificates for railway undertakings. if the tso is solely responsible for cross-border operations, it should share its prerogative with the national safety authorities for domestic traffic.
in writing. ‒ the aim of this recommendation, which was voted, is to amend the existing regulatory framework in order to define the new tasks of the european railway agency in the fields of interoperability and safety. new objectives including:•to further develop and ensure the proper functioning of a single european railway area without frontiers, ensuring a high level of railway safety and interoperability, while improving the competitive position of the railway sector; •monitor the development of national railway rules to support the achievements of national railway safety and interoperability authorities and promote the optimisation of procedures. where provided for in the safety and interoperability directives, the agency shall act as the union authority responsible for issuing authorisations to place vehicles and types of railway vehicles on the market and for issuing single safety certificates for railway undertakings. on 10 december 2015, the council adopted its position at first reading on all three draft directives. the european parliament formally approved the whole thing yesterday at second reading.
in writing. ‒ this regulation on the european railway agency (era) not only extends the agency's powers, it also clarifies its role. this role is essential to achieve the benefits of a single railway market. this proposal, which forms the technical pillar of the railway package together with the directives on interoperability and railway safety, introduces simplified procedures and centralises a number of information flows, thus significantly improving the service provided by the esb. in this way, this initiative will also benefit all eu citizens in the long run.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the text, following the opinion of the tran expert. the agreement should allow railway undertakings and manufacturers of railway equipment across the union to achieve further economies of scale. this will reduce administrative costs and speed up procedures, while maintaining the current high level of security. at the same time, the agreement will help to avoid any hidden discrimination, in particular against firms wishing to enter a market. it will also significantly reduce the volume of national rules in areas where harmonised regulation at union level has been put in place. however, full effectiveness will require the agency and national authorities to work together, sharing expertise and information. even if the creation of a strong, well-resourced and efficient european railway agency is a condition for the development and proper functioning of the european market, it is certain that the agency cannot and should not do everything.
in writing. the european parliament has approved, at first reading, the adoption of the directive of the european parliament and of the council on the interoperability of the rail system within the european union (recast). over the last decade, the gradual introduction of three railway legislative packages has significantly changed the railway market in the european union. in 2013, the commission decided to present the fourth railway package on the quality and efficiency of rail services by removing the obstacles to the creation of a single european railway area. interoperability is part of this fourth package and aims to remove existing administrative and technical barriers. the aim is therefore to establish common safety and interoperability rules, to reduce administrative costs by speeding up procedures and to avoid disguised discrimination. all this while maintaining the current high level of security. with the agreement, companies will no longer have to submit several applications for registration, the projects for the european rail traffic management system will be interoperable, we will have a single point of sale, etc. this project will bring europe closer to a single european railway area.
in writing. ‒ the rail sector has so far responded only too little to consumer demand and has consequently seen its market share decline. improving interoperability, i.e. the possibility of running trains without hindrance on different rail networks, in particular networks located in different states, is one of the pillars of the fourth railway package voted on this afternoon by the european parliament. technical problems clearly identified included signalling, electrification, train length and gauge, and rail gauge. it seems absurd that in the 21st century there are still four different gauge standards on the main rail network in europe. the same applies to the direction of traffic: in germany, trains run on the right, in belgium on the left. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the internal market is not a one-way street. as violeta bulc, commissioner for transport, has rightly pointed out, from 2023 onwards: 'the end of monopolies and the introduction of public procurement will encourage rail operators to respond better to customer needs and to improve the quality of their services'. belgian commuters will have to wait a little longer!
in writing. ‒ the recommendation voted on yesterday concerns the european directive which aims to establish the conditions to be met in order to achieve interoperability of the union's rail system in order to:• define an optimal level of technical harmonisation; • to facilitate, improve and develop rail transport services within the union and with third countries; • to contribute to the completion of the single european railway area and the progressive completion of the internal market. those conditions concern the design, construction, commissioning, upgrading, renewal, operation and maintenance of the elements of that system, the professional qualifications of the personnel contributing to its operation and maintenance, and the health and safety conditions applicable to such personnel. the intention is to increase the efficiency of the vehicle authorisation procedure by encouraging the recognition of interoperability authorisations throughout the union and by making national legal frameworks applicable to interoperability-related aspects of the internal rail market more consistent. on 10 december 2015, the council adopted its position at first reading on all three draft directives. the european parliament therefore formally approved the whole thing yesterday at second reading.
in writing. ‒ the present directive supports the further integration of the european railway market by eliminating multiple applications. this is not only easier, but it also prevents other national agencies from being sought when the outcome of an application is undesirable. the reduction in the number of national technical requirements contained in the directive is also welcome in this respect. the directive thus provides for harmonisation, with the added value of an initiative at european level being very clear.
in writing. ‒ over the last decade, the union rail market has been profoundly changed by the gradual introduction of three railway legislative packages designed to open up national markets and increase the competitiveness and interoperability of railways at union level, while maintaining high levels of safety. however, despite the considerable enrichment of the union acquis establishing an internal market for rail transport services, the modal share of rail in transport within the union remains modest. at present, the overall share of rail transport in the union market is stagnating at 6%, and according to eurobarometer, 54% of users are not satisfied with the services provided by rail. this explains the creation of the fourth railway package, which aims to improve the quality and efficiency of rail services by removing the remaining market barriers to the creation of a single european railway area.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of establishing a common regulatory framework for railway safety to continue efforts to create a single market for rail transport services. member states have developed their safety rules and standards mainly on the basis of national criteria, based on national technical and operational concepts. in addition, differences in principles, approaches and cultures make it difficult to overcome technical barriers and to establish international transport services. this revision therefore represents a major step towards the establishment of a common regulatory framework in the field of railway safety.
in writing. as rapporteur michael cramer said, it is welcome that 'from now on there will be a single framework for train authorisation and safety certification, replacing the patchwork of 26 national systems'. we can be satisfied that we have contributed to the harmonization of road traffic conditions. it is also clear that we are moving towards sustainable development, since the railway is more environmentally friendly than the road.
in writing. ‒ by adopting the 4th railway package this afternoon, meps have put rail services on track to improve quality and competitiveness in the interests of passengers. it has taken two years of tough negotiations with the council since the publication of three legislative proposals by the commission in january 2013 to reach an agreement covering interoperability, safety and the role of the european railway agency (era). the desired objective of creating a single european railway area is gradually being achieved. however, while the european rail network is gradually becoming more interoperable, reliable and safe, the focus must now be on the adoption of common european union standards for passenger safety, both in stations and on trains. the terrorist attacks on the brussels metro and zaventem international airport on 22 march and the terrorist attack on a thalys train on 21 august 2015 have sadly reminded us of the urgent need to strengthen security in public transport. all initiatives undertaken by the commission in collaboration with the national railway police and the railway police within the union, via the railpol network, should therefore be encouraged.
in writing. ‒ the recommendation voted on yesterday in plenary concerns the proposal for a recast of directive 2004/49/ec on railway safety, which, together with the proposal for a recast of directive 2008/57/ec on interoperability and the proposal for a regulation on the european railway agency, forms the technical part of the 4th railway package, focusing on the removal of the remaining administrative and technical obstacles in the railway sector. it aims to establish a common approach to safety in order to increase economies of scale for railway undertakings operating across the union, and to simplify and reform the administrative procedures for issuing safety certificates, which would end the fragmentation of rules across the union. more specifically, the aim of the railway safety directive is to amend the existing regulatory framework and to clarify the roles and responsibilities of the various actors in the railway system, in order to ensure adequate control of risks at all levels. on 10 december 2015, the council adopted its position at first reading on all three draft directives. parliament therefore formally approved the whole thing at second reading yesterday.
in writing. ‒ a sound railway safety policy is a prerequisite for further integration into a fully-fledged european railway market. safety first! it goes without saying that the safety of transnational rail transport must be organised according to the same high european standards. the proposal will address this by providing safety certificates by the european railway agency (era) when activities are set up across borders. the introduction of best practices in informing the families of victims and in the cooperation of the emergency services is also essential in the development of the single railway market.
in writing. - i voted for the railway safety part. in order to continue efforts to create a single market for rail transport services, it is necessary to establish a common regulatory framework for railway safety. member states have developed their safety rules and standards mainly on the basis of national criteria, based on national technical and operational concepts. in addition, differences in principles, approaches and cultures make it difficult to overcome technical barriers and to establish international transport services.
in writing. ‒ benchmarks are susceptible to manipulation where conflicts of interest and discretionary assessments are involved and not properly monitored. the objectives of the regulation are to improve the governance and controls applicable to the benchmark development process, in particular by ensuring that administrators avoid conflicts of interest or at least manage them appropriately. improve the quality of underlying data and the methods used by administrators; ensure that benchmark contributors and the data they provide are subject to adequate controls, in particular to avoid conflicts of interest; protect consumers and investors by enhancing transparency and providing adequate redress.
in writing. i am pleased that the european union has taken up such an important task as the manipulation of benchmarks in financial instruments and contracts. recent cases of manipulation of interest rate benchmarks such as the london interbank offered rate (libor) and the euro interbank offered rate (euribor) have shown a real flaw in our system. however, many financial instruments and contracts are directly linked to benchmarks. these indices are used, for example, to establish the price of oil or the exchange rate of the euro. cases of fraud and manipulation have allowed these indices to be influenced in a discretionary manner. this is unacceptable and harmful to our economic system. it was therefore essential to create a single regulatory framework. i am glad that europe is the first continent to do so.
in writing. ‒ amid scandals over the manipulation of libor in london, the european parliament voted this afternoon on a text that streamlines the process of calculating financial benchmarks, increases transparency and prevents conflicts of interest. these indices, the best known of which are libor and euribor, influence a very wide range of financial instruments, from mortgages to futures contracts and foreign exchange rates. the value of derivative contracts based on libor alone is estimated to exceed eur 350 000 000 000. this new european regulation, which is applicable immediately throughout the european union, creates three categories of benchmarks, subject to different supervisory regimes depending on the risks of destabilising financial markets they entail. in general, parliament has imposed stronger supervision of the actors involved in setting the indices, improved calculation methodologies, and ensured a high level of protection for consumers and investors using these indices.
in writing. ‒ the european parliament adopted new legislation by 505 votes to 113, with 31 abstentions, to streamline the process of calculating benchmarks, increase transparency and avoid conflicts of interest such as those that have led to the libor manipulation scandals in recent years. the levels of benchmarks such as libor have major implications, particularly for european citizens who wish to take out a loan. these indices are also used to establish the price of oil and the exchange rate of the euro. therefore, given the important implications of these indices for the daily lives of european citizens, it is crucial that they are fully reliable. as this legislation offers advances in supervision, methodology and transparency, i have decided to support this text.
in writing. ‒ the manipulation of libor and exchange rate indices, as well as the alleged manipulation of other indices, have highlighted the importance of the indices as well as their weaknesses. in the wake of these revelations, the european union has revised its market abuse legislation to clarify the illegality of index manipulation and to include this type of behaviour in the criminal law. however, a comprehensive approach to preventing evidence manipulation must go beyond the mere recognition of the illegality of such acts. it should also take into account the macroprudential risks associated with the manipulation of commonly used indices. indeed, the excessive use of a small number of very broad indices, including where the vulnerabilities and shortcomings of those indices are known or suspected, underlines the importance of certain indices for the smooth functioning and stability of financial markets, commodity markets, and other types of markets, and of the economy as a whole. such systemic considerations justify the need for additional legislation, at least for the most frequently used indices, in order to improve governance and limit conflicts of interest and other weaknesses.

in writing. ‒ i have approved the report adopted unanimously by the committee on budgetary control which calls on parliament to postpone its decision on the discharge to be given to the secretary-general of the council in respect of the implementation of the budget of the european council and of the council for the financial year 2014. this is the consequence of a lack of transparency on the part of the council as regards the funds entrusted to it. parliament therefore asked the council to forward to it its annual activity report containing a detailed overview of all the human resources available to the two institutions, broken down by category, grade, sex, nationality and vocational training. the report also highlights the worrying lack of transparency in the legislative process, negotiations, member states' positions and meetings. it called on the council to publish the relevant documents and to put in place a clear reporting system which would enable the public to follow legislative procedures in an open and transparent manner.
in writing. i have decided to postpone my decision on the discharge to the general secretariat for the implementation of the budget of the european council and of the council for the financial year 2014 until autumn, due to insufficient information. i remain concerned about the high percentage of unused appropriations in almost all areas. i therefore call for the development of key performance indicators to improve budgetary planning. the council must be more transparent by participating fully in the discharge procedure, as indeed do the other institutions. since 2009, the council has no longer been subject to this discharge exercise, refusing to provide the necessary information, to answer written questions and to attend hearings and debate on the implementation of its own budget. the dialogue between the two institutions must be improved, because it is our duty to respect the provisions of the treaty and to be accountable to the citizens.
in writing. ‒ in adopting this report yesterday, the european parliament decided to postpone its decision on the discharge to be given to the secretary-general of the council in respect of the implementation of the budget of the european council and of the council for the financial year 2014. the ep stresses that since 2009 the council has refused to submit to the parliament's budgetary discharge exercise by refusing to provide the necessary information, to answer written questions and to attend hearings and debates concerning the implementation of its budget. as it stands, more than three billion euros of european public funds have been effectively spent in the dark! parliament therefore calls on the council to participate in the eu transparency register. it also reiterated its call on the european council and the council to forward to it their annual activity reports, including a detailed overview of all human resources available to the two institutions. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'competent authority' to cover all the activities of the european union.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the discharge and would like to underline the important and high-quality work carried out by the s&d experts on amendments and explanations, as well as during the negotiations.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report of the committee on budgetary control which recommends giving discharge to the eu agencies for the implementation of their budgets for the financial year 2014 in respect of performance, financial management and control. the report stresses the need for autonomy for agencies, in particular regulatory agencies and those responsible for collecting information independently. it also stressed the need for a common approach (parliament, commission, council) on decentralised agencies, which should allow for more balanced governance, greater efficiency and accountability, and greater coherence. the report also notes that 80% of decentralised agencies have an internal fraud strategy. the report also calls for the eu to take action to ensure that the eu's citizens are protected from unfair competition.
in writing. the missions of the union agencies have a direct impact on the daily lives of european citizens. they employ 6578 permanent and temporary staff and about 3200 contract or seconded staff. despite their recognised autonomy, in particular that of the regulatory agencies and those charged with collecting information independently, i would like to recall that article 54 of the common approach provides that 'all aspects of external audits carried out by external auditors shall remain the sole responsibility of the court of auditors, which shall manage all the administrative and tendering procedures required'. i very much regret that the new method of audit using private sector auditors has resulted in an 85% increase in administrative burden at a time when there is an emphasis on administrative simplification. this new audit method resulted in more than 13000 additional hours, or on average 3.5 full-time equivalents, compared to the previous audit carried out by the court of auditors. it may be appropriate to merge some smaller agencies that perform similar tasks in order to achieve efficiency gains.
in writing. ‒ the european parliament adopted yesterday the 2014 discharge for the european agencies, which focuses, among other things, on the issues of the reliability of accounts, the legality and regularity of transactions, internal control and budget implementation. the scale of carryovers is one of the most frequently identified problems and is generally considered to be contrary to the budgetary principle of annuality. the report adopted, however, notes that these postponements are often the result of factors which are wholly or partly beyond the control of the agencies, or of the multiannual nature of operations, public procurement procedures, projects, etc.; the report adopted notes that the vast majority of agencies already share services with other agencies or institutions. the agencies have reviewed their internal administrative processes, in line with previous recommendations of parliament, and continue to seek synergies, exchange best practices and share services in order to improve the efficiency of their activities and optimise the use of their resources.

in writing. ‒ this vote approves the 2014 discharge for clean sky, a joint eu technology initiative to develop innovations for cleaner airspace. clean sky was launched in 2008 and is the largest aviation project ever launched in europe. it takes the form of a first-of-its-kind public-private partnership between the commission and the private sector, which is intended to enable the eu to invent the technologies of tomorrow to increase the environmental performance of air transport and thus reduce noise pollution and energy consumption, and bring the union closer to the environmental objectives of the single european sky project. the european discharge is an annual ritual in which parliament acts as the guardian of the accounts to check that european appropriations have been spent in accordance with the rules. it is the only authority that can grant, postpone or refuse discharge, which is a mandatory step for the formal closure of the accounts of all european organisations. the four political institutions - parliament, commission, council and european council - are involved, as are nearly 50 european agencies and institutes. the commission has also proposed that the council should adopt a decision on the establishment of a european union agency for fundamental rights.

in writing. ‒ as every year, the parliament has embarked on the european discharge ritual. in practice, following the recommendations of the committee on budgetary control, the task is to verify that european appropriations have been spent in accordance with the rules. in a sense, the european parliament is the accounting officer and the only authority that can grant, postpone or refuse discharge, which is a requirement for the formal closure of the accounts of all european organisations. the four political institutions - parliament, commission, council and european council - are involved, as are nearly 50 executive agencies and european institutes. among them is the sesar joint undertaking, which was established in 2007 to be the technological pillar of the eu's single sky programme to harmonise and modernise air traffic management in europe. the differences between countries in this area are estimated to cost €4 billion annually and cause several million minutes of flight delays, which is unnecessary fuel consumption that could be avoided. thanks to sesar, the environmental impact per flight is being reduced by 2.8%, the risk of accidents by 40% and the capacity of the european sky increased by 27%.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this discharge, which, on the basis of the court of auditors' report on the annual accounts of the sesar joint undertaking for the financial year 2014, having regard to the statement of assurance as to the reliability of the accounts and the legality and regularity of the underlying transactions provided by the court of auditors and having regard to the report of the committee on budgetary control and the opinion of the committee on transport and tourism, gives the executive director of the sesar joint undertaking discharge in respect of the implementation of the budget of the sesar joint undertaking for the financial year 2014.

in writing. ‒ the eib's investment programme is directly linked to supporting the political objectives of the european union. in view of the current economic situation, the european union decided in september 2014 to launch an investment plan. in this context, it is essential that the eib prioritises investments that accelerate recovery and increase productivity while encouraging youth employment, innovation and smes! other aspects need to be considered, such as improving environmental sustainability and action to combat climate change. these projects must therefore comply with specific environmental standards.
in writing. the economy will only do well if there are investments. the european investment bank plays a major role in this respect, particularly in guaranteeing medium- and long-term investment. the eib plays a key role in european integration and is responsible for ensuring social, economic and territorial cohesion. but to do so, the eib's investment programme must be based on the political objectives of the european union. as the report points out, the eib's priorities should include recovery, productivity growth, employment, innovation and sustainable development. in 2014, the eib financed 285 000 small and medium-sized enterprises, safeguarding 3.6 million jobs. that's a great thing, but it's just a first step. the european fund for strategic investments (efsi), which emerged from the juncker plan, must now reach its cruise speed in order to operate efficiently, transparently and fairly.
in writing. ‒ this vote follows an agreement with the european investment bank (eib) which demonstrates very good interinstitutional cooperation and will allow parliamentary scrutiny of the work of the european union bank. the eib is the world's largest multilateral institution in terms of lending volume. its investors are the member states whose interests it represents. it plays a leading role in the implementation of european policies and in particular the juncker plan for investment and growth in europe. in 2014, the eib financed 285 000 small and medium-sized enterprises, safeguarding 3.6 million jobs, and signed contracts for a total of 413 projects worth €69 billion in the eu where it concentrates 90% of its activity. the eib is central to the recovery of the european economy, which justifies the possibility of external regulatory oversight by meps. the latter will be able to request details of the results achieved through the various eib financial instruments and receive replies from the president within pre-established deadlines, as is already the case with the european central bank.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the european investment bank, which makes a number of recommendations to improve its functioning. i believe that this institution of the european union is of major importance because it contributes to the achievement of the union's policy objectives by supporting sound and sustainable investment projects. the report stresses in particular the importance of prioritising investments that accelerate recovery and increase productivity, of encouraging youth employment, innovation and smes, of improving environmental sustainability and action to combat climate change, of promoting economic and social cohesion and convergence, etc. it also makes a number of recommendations to strengthen the eib's governance, transparency and control framework. i am convinced that this report and the recommendations it contains can add value to the eib's operations and i have decided to support it.
in writing. ‒ as the european union's bank, the eib's core activity is to contribute financially to projects in the union's interest which contribute to the balanced development of the internal market and to social, economic and territorial cohesion, and thus to the strengthening of european integration and employment, making it an extremely important player in boosting the union's competitiveness. in its text, parliament called on the eib to step up its technical support at the pre-approval stage for member states with a lower rate of project approval and encouraged the eib to facilitate exchanges of good practice between member states with regard to successful project development. in addition, the bank is invited to focus on investments in the real economy with a view to stimulating employment and growth in the union.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution which deplores the lack of respect for international humanitarian law. indeed, in many conflicts, the protagonists no longer respect international standards that prohibit and condemn attacks on hospitals and schools. this statement reaffirms the interests of these rules.
in writing. ‒ the n-va delegation voted in favour of this resolution. it condemns the attacks on civilian institutions such as hospitals and schools. these attacks are prohibited by international humanitarian law (ihr). such acts may also constitute grave breaches of the 1949 geneva convention and may be considered war crimes under the rome statute of the international criminal court. the n-va therefore supports european and international initiatives to combat them. it also supports the call on the eu high representative to take the initiative of an arms embargo against the countries responsible for these violations of the ihr. the nva, however, believes that humanitarian aid must be linked to political, economic and security considerations.
in writing. i condemn in the strongest terms the attacks on hospitals, medical centres, clinics, schools and, beyond that, all civilian infrastructure, which are all flagrant violations of the geneva conventions and international humanitarian law and therefore constitute war crimes. there is no justification for killing civilians who have a right to medical care. similarly, humanitarian organizations must be protected. there can be no impunity. in december 2015, un security council resolution 2254, adopted unanimously, called for an immediate cessation of all attacks against civilian targets and hospitals. i hope very much that the appeals of the un secretary-general, mr ban ki-moon, will be heard and supported at the first humanitarian summit in istanbul in may.
in writing. ‒ i am deeply shocked when attacks on hospitals and schools are carried out in the context of armed conflicts. these attacks are contrary to international humanitarian law, as i have already said in the resolution i adopted on this subject in the european parliament's plenary session. in less than a month, the world humanitarian summit will be held in istanbul. the european parliament sees the summit as an opportunity to reorganise the international humanitarian system to adapt it to new challenges and make it more efficient. it is also essential that the principle of the inviolability of international humanitarian law be loudly reaffirmed at this summit. we cannot tolerate serious violations of humanitarian law by certain countries, whether eu partners or not. in view of these factors, as well as the other proposals and comments made in this resolution, i did not hesitate for a second to support this text.
in writing. ‒ the international community has witnessed a series of heinous attacks on hospitals and schools in situations of armed conflict around the world in recent years, as evidenced by the recent attacks on doctors without borders (msf) health centres in kunduz, afghanistan on 3 october 2015, razah, yemen on 10 january 2016, and in a number of syrian cities during the ongoing conflict. we condemn the attacks on hospitals and schools, which are prohibited by international law, and recognize that such acts may constitute grave violations of the 1949 geneva conventions and war crimes under the rome statute of the icc. we are convinced that the preservation of health and educational facilities as neutral and protected spaces in the context of armed conflict must be guaranteed by means of transparent, independent and impartial investigations into the brutal attacks that have occurred and by the effective enforcement of the obligation for all parties involved who have committed crimes to answer for their acts.

in writing. i welcome the adoption by the european parliament of this resolution on public access to documents for the period 2014-2015. the resolution recalls that the right of access to documents is enshrined in the charter and the treaties and cannot be dissociated from good governance, which is also enshrined in european texts. in this regard, the union should continue its work on accessibility of documents, in particular by making online access to documents easier and by harmonising the different search portals of its websites. this increased accessibility must be accompanied by a greater dissemination of the union's policies. to this end, new technologies such as social networks have extraordinary potential to bring the union's action closer to citizens. now we must exploit it.

in writing. ‒ the issue of domestic workers and domestic helpers is above all a question of respect for the dignity of persons and in this case of women. it is true that this report suggests measures to protect women, and when we speak of workers we mean women workers, but it goes without saying that the measures proposed here should apply to all workers in these sectors, since dignity is not a privilege linked to sex, even though in most cases it is perhaps women who are deprived of it most severely.
in writing. ‒ i am pleased that the kuneva report on women domestic workers, domestic helpers and childcare workers in the european union, which aims to better protect these workers, has been adopted by the european parliament. i am particularly pleased that i was able, as a fictitious rapporteur, to negotiate the opinion of the committee on employment and social affairs. it is urgent that all the member states of the european union ratify and apply convention 189 of the international labour organization in order to improve the working conditions of people in the sector. it is unacceptable that many workers in this sector are still forced to work underground, with the consequent loss of social rights. in this report, the european parliament also calls for a directive on carers' leave and a framework for the recognition of the status of non-professional carers and childcare workers. it also calls on member states to include domestic workers, domestic helpers and child-care workers in all national legislation on labour, health care, etc. the ball is now in the court of the commission and the member states.
in writing. ‒ the n-va stands for an inclusive society with equal rights and obligations for all, and for a policy of equal opportunities tailored to and taking account of all the various target groups. this applies to all genders and particularly to women. we cannot accept any violation of this equality, whether at work or in private life. this report contains many good elements. it is important, for example, to combat undeclared work, a phenomenon which affects domestic workers severely. the n-va also supports the content of ilo convention no 189, which provides, inter alia, for effective and accessible complaint mechanisms and tools to ensure compliance with national laws and regulations on the protection of domestic workers. unfortunately, the report is at odds with the principle of subsidiarity and some paragraphs go too far in granting rights to domestic workers and carers outside a contractual employment relationship (e.g. au pairs). the nva delegation therefore abstained from the final vote.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the text as a member of the committee on gender equality. i believe that there should be a common recognition at union level of the profession and the value of domestic and care work as a form of professional activity in its own right, since the recognition of this professional sector is likely to reduce undeclared work and promote social integration, and therefore calls on the european union and the member states to establish common standards for domestic and care work.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the european parliament resolution on gender equality and women's empowerment in the digital age. the european parliament's conclusion on this issue is that the digital revolution benefits men more than women. if we look at the figures for the ict sector, we see that only 30% of the workforce are women. in addition, women often hold jobs that are less well-paid and less skilled than men. in order to remedy this problem, parliament called on the member states to draw up multiannual action plans and to put an end to the pay gap between men and women, preferably by means of legislation. another proposal made by the european parliament in this resolution is the introduction of a right to disconnect when the conventional working time is exceeded. while it is true that the development of digital technology makes it possible to develop systems to better balance work and private life, the risk of the development of unstable forms of work is real and must be taken into account.

in writing. i welcome the proposal of the european parliament and the council on the defence of subsidised imports from non-eu countries. the purpose of this regulation is to codify the existing texts (regulation (ec) no 597/2009) without changing their content, but by making the few formal amendments required by the codification and simplification act itself. the original 2009 council regulation on this subject has undergone many important amendments. in line with the commission's instructions on the importance of codification in 1987, the interinstitutional agreement on the expedited procedure for codified acts in 1994 and in order to clarify union law and make it more accessible to our fellow citizens, it is therefore essential to draw up a clear regulation which would replace the many others already in existence. in addition to the codification of existing texts, one of the objectives of this proposal is to incorporate into eu law the rules contained in the wto-approved 'subsidies agreement'. the conditions for granting a subsidy are set out in detail, as are the principles governing the imposition of countervailing duties and the way in which they are calculated.

in writing. ‒ in recent years, the european union has signed a number of fisheries partnership agreements (fpas) and protocols with 'third countries'. through the ppps, the union provides financial and technical support in exchange for fishing rights for a wide range of fish stocks in the partner country's exclusive economic zone (eez). this sustainable fisheries partnership agreement, which i have approved, is the first agreement to be signed between the european union and the republic of liberia, which has 570 km of coastline along the atlantic ocean. it will help to increase the fight against illegal fishing and to disseminate the cfp objective of sustainable management of fisheries and aquaculture activities.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this proposal because it is beneficial for both the union and liberia. the agreement provides for access for 34 european vessels to liberian territorial waters on payment of an annual fee for five years. it took effect on 9 december 2015 and had yet to receive the endorsement of the european parliament. on the one hand, the european fleet needs access to new fishing areas, particularly to be able to follow the migration of certain fish species, notably tuna. in liberia, more than half the population lives in coastal areas and depends on fishing. however, the country reports that vessels flying both asian and european flags are illegally fishing in its waters. the eu will pay an annual fee of approximately €650,000 on average to liberia. almost half of this amount will be allocated to the fight against illegal, unreported and unregulated (iuu) fishing. finally, the commission stresses the sustainability of fisheries, which will not endanger liberia's fish stocks and will provide long-term income for the country.
in writing. i welcome the european parliament's approval of the conclusion of the sustainable fisheries partnership agreement with liberia. in the fisheries sector, liberia is pursuing the objectives of sustainability and responsible management of resources, as is the union. i therefore welcome this new partnership and the positive consequences it should have, inter alia, on the fight against illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing. in this particular area, cooperation is essential. the proper management of fisheries resources can only be achieved in a multilateral manner. i therefore encourage the establishment of such partnerships and the strengthening of their provisions on transparency of fishing activities. i would also like to stress the importance of the support given by the union to the development of the fisheries sector in the partner countries with which it concludes such agreements.
in writing. ‒ a first in the european parliament, this afternoon, with the adoption by 584 votes in favour of a fisheries agreement between the eu and liberia. it opens liberian waters to 28 european tuna seiners and six surface longliners, in return for a contribution of €3.25 million over five years. this will help liberia to better manage its fisheries resources and improve the implementation of its fisheries regulations. the country still suffers from a flawed monitoring system that hinders its fight against illegal, unreported and unregulated (iuu) fishing. the efforts made are important in cooperating with the international community in this area, modernising its fishing sector and developing local communities. liberia has a strong interest in fostering such partnerships. the figures speak for themselves: more than half of its population lives on its 570 km of coastline, and the fishing sector accounted for 3% of its gdp in 2014. its stocks of bluefin, albacore and bigeye tuna are particularly attractive to european fleets, which catch 10% of their tuna catches in the atlantic and gulf of guinea.
in writing. ‒ the european parliament yesterday approved the conclusion of the first sustainable fisheries partnership agreement between the european union and the republic of liberia. the report, which was adopted by a large majority, supports the arrangements which allow eu vessels to catch tuna in the waters of this third country, which has 570 km of coastline along the atlantic ocean. the conclusion of a fisheries agreement with liberia would undoubtedly help the european union to achieve its objectives in the fight against illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing. the new agreement was initialled in june 2015 for a period of 5 years from the date of provisional application, i.e. the date of their signature. the protocol provides for fishing opportunities in the following categories: 28 purse seiners and 6 surface longliners. it provides for a union financial contribution of eur 715 000 for the first year, eur 650 000 for the second, third and fourth years and eur 585 000 for the fifth year (with a reference tonnage of 6 500 tonnes).

in writing. ‒ this vote validates a new fisheries agreement which regulates access to mauritanian waters in return for compensation of almost €60 million per year. this agreement improves on the previous one, which expired in 2014 and is rarely applied in practice due to the restrictions imposed. it guarantees the union fishing conditions similar to those granted to third countries, in particular as regards fees. the contribution to mauritania is reduced from eur 67 million to eur 55 million per year. the other part of the compensation to promote the sustainable development of the fisheries sector and the protection of maritime areas is increased from eur 3 million to just over eur 4 million per year. a joint committee is hereby established which will be required to revise the quotas allocated to the union in the event of surplus stocks. the commission notes that the mauritanian authorities have not provided any evidence that the measures provided for in this decision are in conformity with the union's obligations under the wto agreement on trade in goods, as amended by the wto agreement on trade-related aspects of goods, and that the commission has not provided any evidence that the measures provided for in this decision are in conformity with the wto agreement on trade-related aspects of goods. the agreement is the most important fisheries protocol concluded by the union with a third country and, for parliament, should serve as an example for future agreements.

in writing. ‒ the report, which i approved, highlights two new territorial tools in the context of cohesion policy. local development led by local actors (lda) is a new instrument for infraregional use. it builds on the experience of the leader method of local development led by actors and is based on a bottom-up approach: it aims to strengthen synergies between local actors, both public and private. integrated territorial investment (iti) will contribute to the implementation of integrated territorial strategies insofar as it allows the pooling of funds from several priority axes of one or more operational programmes. it can be used to achieve the sustainable development goal in urban environments. member states should indicate in their partnership agreements how they intend to use the iti and the dlal and the types of areas and challenges that these mechanisms will address.
in writing. innovation is not just a matter of bringing new products to the market or introducing new production processes. policy also needs innovation and sometimes the innovative nature of a new approach lies in the introduction of obvious elements and actors into the decision-making process. this report rightly advocates a bottom-up approach to cohesion policy. prioritizing local knowledge to address local problems with local solutions can help to improve the efficiency and effectiveness of public action. this helps you to anticipate the specific needs of the people in an area. tackling youth unemployment and caring for an ageing population are current challenges where the knowledge of local actors can make a significant contribution to achieving sustainable local employment and social cohesion. community-led local development, with technical and financial guidance and support from the regional, national and european levels, increases the chances of a successful cohesion policy.
in writing. ‒ the efficient use of public money, the fight against corruption and mismanagement are golden rules from which no public policy should deviate. the adoption of the tomasic report on new territorial development tools in the context of cohesion policy 2014-2020 should therefore be welcomed. local development led by local actors (lda), which aims to strengthen synergies between local actors, both public and private, and integrated territorial investment (iti), which allows for the pooling of funds from several priority areas to achieve sustainable development objectives, are the two new tools for territorial cohesion. clear strategic choices have been made, with at least 5% of erdf resources now being invested in urban areas. the dutch presidency of the council's strong support for the future european urban agenda through the drafting of the amsterdam pact is a step in the right direction. it is also a sign of the union's renewed determination to commit itself resolutely to a more innovative and cost-effective cohesion policy for cities and urban areas.
in writing. ‒ the text adopted yesterday calls on the member states to put an end to their mistrust of territorial authorities and to better integrate them into the use of these two new instruments of cohesion policy. recalling the lack of financial and human resources suffered by several local and regional authorities, parliament called on the commission and the member states to support local and regional authorities, including through training and advisory services for the smallest entities in particular, in order to limit territorial discrimination. the text also calls on the commission to draw up a european table of practices and to disseminate them as widely as possible, in particular through online platforms, and encourages small administrative entities to come together to streamline resources in order to make the most of the opportunities offered by these instruments. the european council welcomes the commission's proposal to establish a european union-wide network of information centres for the protection of the environment.
in writing. ‒ a concrete involvement of regional and local actors from the earliest stages, their commitment and ownership of territorial development strategies and the judicious delegation of responsibilities and resources to lower decision-making levels are essential to the success of the bottom-up approach. i believe that the participation of partners can also strengthen the integrated and territorialised approach, especially in cases of low adherence to the iti and dlal instruments. however, local actors need technical and financial support at regional, national and european level, especially in the early stages of the implementation process. it is in this context that the european parliament intends to adopt this text.
