in writing. i voted in favour of this european parliament resolution for the following reasons. while territorial cohesion is an important objective of the eu, we have not yet achieved all our objectives in this area. this is particularly true of two instruments: the community-led local development (clld) and integrated territorial investments (iti) programmes, which play a major role in this policy, are also part of the programme. as regards the clld, we have come to the conclusion that it is a very complex concept, that it is considered superfluous by some member states and that a downward vertical movement of power in some of them is also very difficult. in addition, many member states fear the administrative burden associated with the implementation of these mechanisms. these problems are also experienced in relation to the iti. it is therefore clear that i support a resolution which points out these problems and makes clear suggestions on how they can be solved. it is emphasised that the initiatives should follow a bottom-up approach and therefore aim at sufficient participation of local actors. in addition, such an approach should be holistic and inclusive. particular attention should be paid to youth unemployment in the eu.
in writing. ‒ the balance of payments records all economic transactions between resident and non-resident entities during a given period. since the adoption of the original regulation and its successive amendments, international capital flows have both increased and become more complex. more specifically, the increased use of special purpose entities and legal arrangements for the transfer of capital inflows and outflows has increased the difficulties in controlling these capital flows in order to ensure their traceability and to avoid double or multiple accounting, thereby making it more difficult to combat tax evasion and aggressive tax planning. the aim of this report is to update the legislation in force in relation to this phenomenon.
in writing. ‒ the treaty of lisbon has brought about a series of changes in the way the european union works and the powers of the various institutions. it shall be kept under constant review by the commission. some supplement certain non-essential elements of a legislative act, while others are a tool available when uniform conditions for the implementation of legally binding acts are needed. the report aims to give the commission both these powers in specific areas relating to community statistics on balance of payments, international trade in services and foreign direct investment. the question here is therefore to apply the treaty of lisbon in the context of international trade.

in writing. ‒ the regulation on community statistics on balance of payments, international trade in services and foreign direct investment is part of the union's overall framework for monitoring economic developments in each member state and in the union as a whole. the production of reliable statistics in these areas serves in particular to monitor key aspects such as developments in current accounts and financial flows within and beyond the union. thus, these statistics help to certify the consistency of the economic policies of the member states with the union's broad guidelines, as well as with the legal obligations deriving from the union's economic governance framework. in particular, the reliability of statistics is essential for the monitoring exercise established in the framework of the macroeconomic imbalance procedures. since the adoption of the original regulation and its successive amendments, international capital flows have both increased and become more complex. a revision was therefore necessary.

in writing. ‒ the eu's mountain regions are rarely given specific attention in cohesion policy. yet these regions represent a significant part of the territory of the european union (about 30%), and the whole of the union depends on their ecosystem services. the present report, which i have approved, therefore calls on the commission:- to draw up a 'programme for european mountain regions', which should form the basis of a european strategy for the long-term development of these regions and to present a white paper on the subject;- to encourage the use of financial instruments in mountain regions in order to achieve concrete results;- to regularly assess the state of mountain regions in the union and to analyse the results of the implementation of the operational programmes of cohesion policy.
in writing. the eu's mountain regions have been treated as stepmothers so far. the eu has no specific policy for mountain areas and their adjacent areas, perhaps because it was assumed that mountain areas, because of their tourist strength and a locally rooted economic fabric, are self-sufficient, require little care and that member states do take the challenges of these areas to heart. in recent years, the understanding of the strengths and challenges of these mountain areas has increased to the extent that their potential contribution to the achievement of european objectives in the fields of energy, climate control and employment must be translated into policy. these unexplored areas, with their high biodiversity, natural resources and abundance of renewable energy sources, deserve their place in the european approach to climate change and the development of green jobs. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's environmental policy is properly implemented. parliament rightly calls on the commission to draw up an agenda for mountain areas. it is logical that the development of mountain areas and their adjacent areas should be included in eu policies and programmes.
in writing. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'competent authority' to cover all the activities of the european union's institutions. let us begin by adopting a common definition of 'mountain areas'. and there is a definition of mountains in the european fund for rural development, which is specific to agriculture but which could easily be transposed into regional policy. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environmentally friendly use of energy. and too often european decision-makers prefer to leave the member states to deal with the mountains and their issues themselves. however, of the €351.8 billion allocated to cohesion policy for the period 2014-2020, or almost one third of the total eu budget, a small part can still be made available to mountain regions to meet their specific needs: climate change, seasonal employment, tourism development and environmental protection. the territorial, economic and social cohesion of the union is at that price!
in writing. ‒ by voting overwhelmingly for this report, the european parliament wanted to call on the european commission to draw up a programme for the eu's mountain regions for the next financial programming period (after 2020). the text calls on the european commission to publish a communication containing a programme for the mountain regions of the european union and then a white paper devoted exclusively to the development of mountain regions, based on good practice and integrating all decision-making levels. the text also calls on the commission to initiate a territorial impact study and to undertake a regular and in-depth assessment of the state of mountain regions in the european union, including indicators on changes in the quality of life and demography, with a view to optimising the rate of investment.
in writing. ‒ i share the view of my colleague, ms iotova, and join her in calling on the commission to start the process of creating an operational definition of mountain regions in the context of cohesion policy, complementing the definition of mountain areas used in the context of the european agricultural fund for rural development, with a view to improving the coordination of the relevant policies and measures. such a definition must be broad and inclusive, taking into account various factors such as altitude, accessibility and slope. the commission must develop a comprehensive definition covering also volcanic regions in islands and the outermost regions, as well as areas which, being non-mountain, are largely integrated into mountainous areas. in this context, the idea, taken up in the european union's strategy for the alpine region, of including non-mountain areas in the strategy is a good initiative.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report, which highlights how mountain areas in the european union can contribute to achieving eu objectives such as europe 2020.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the text on exemptions for commodity traders. the derogations shall expire on 31 december 2017. a time-out clause was initially introduced in the crr to allow regulators time to define a prudential regime tailored to the risk profile of commodity traders. the term 'commodity trader' covers a wide range of energy and commodity market participants: for some, comparable to investment firms in terms of functions and risks, the trading of commodity derivatives contracts is the only activity; for others, it is only a side activity of the production of raw materials.
in writing. i have agreed to this text on the exemption for commodity traders. a derogation from this regulation applies to traders in raw materials in certain situations. this was already included in the original version, but it only applies until 31 december 2017. future, adapted legislation will have to provide a specific framework for commodity traders. this new legislation can of course only be created on the basis of a thorough evaluation by the european commission of investment firms in the eu. however, it is expected that this report will not be ready by the deadline of 31 december 2017. the group of traders protected by the exemptions would then be covered by a completely new legislative framework, with potentially negative consequences. in order to ensure the continued positive effect of the regulation and to avoid potential negative side effects, we have extended the operation of this exemption until 31 december 2020. in this way, potential destabilising effects created by an uncertain legislative framework are avoided.

in writing. ‒ the european police office, europol, will soon be able to step up its efforts to fight terrorism, cybercrime and other criminal offences, and to respond more quickly to threats, thanks to new governance rules we adopted this afternoon. the new powers will be accompanied by robust safeguards in terms of data protection and tools for democratic control. to avoid information gaps in the fight against organised crime and terrorism, the new rules stipulate that member states should provide europol with the data the office needs. europol will also be required to submit an annual report to the european parliament, the council, the commission and national parliaments on the information provided by member states, with a view to encouraging the sharing of information.

i'm the reporter. mr president, it is a pity that the commissioner is not here, i hope she can join us despite the traffic. we have a report today on parental leave. we looked at a directive that dates back to 1995 and has been in place since 2010 to evaluate and make a number of recommendations on parental leave. parental leave is, of course, one of the tools that helps to better reconcile private and professional life. this parental leave is important because it allows families to make the choice not only to have children but also to go to work. today in europe we have two challenges: the challenge of the birth rate, which is important, but also the challenge of the employment rate for all men and women. in the present situation, we have identified a number of difficulties with respect to these various challenges and the application of this directive. firstly, we continue to see real discrimination against women in employment, because they are locked into traditional roles and seen as a risk to maternity and therefore a cost to the employer. according to eurostat data, we see that men take less parental leave and, in general, take less care of everything related to the private sphere. but for parental leave, the phenomenon is even more pronounced: only 2.7% of men take parental leave. so you see the disparity between a woman's reality and a man's reality. finally, i will quote the figures in relation to the employment rate, which still show a real disparity between the employment rates of women and men, the disparity also in wages, the disparity in pensions and the disparity in careers. parental leave must be able to respond to all these. of course, not alone, and we look forward to working on the commission's roadmap on reconciling private and professional life. but we have made a number of recommendations in this report to correct the situation in terms of parental leave. the first obvious thing in this analysis of parental leave is the question of its transferability. it appears that when parental leave is fully transferable, traditional models are reinforced, namely that women carry the social model and men the economic model. this transferability, when left entirely free, reinforces this pattern: it is women who take parental leave, and only 2.7% of men are in this situation. we therefore recommend that parental leave should not be transferable or at least should be transferable, as far as possible, in a framework which does not reinforce traditional roles. flexibility, yes, but not a flexibility which accentuates the situations in which women as well as men find themselves today. the second recommendation is the question of treatment. it is a little too easy to propose leave when it is unpaid, because it also creates a reinforcement of the traditional role, i.e. the person who takes on the social role will take it - he will be forced to take it because he has no choice - and the person who takes on the economic role will not be able to get rid of this economic role because he is not paid to do so. we therefore call for the right to be paid for parental leave when it is granted. in the report on poverty which we have drawn up, we see that women suffer much more from poverty because they have to take a certain number of leave days which are not properly paid. the question of remuneration also arises in this case. the third question is protection. taking leave parental leave often means quitting your job when you return to the work environment. we must therefore protect the worker who decides to take parental leave so that when he or she returns to work, he or she can not only return to his or her rightful job but also benefit from parental leave protection. finally, we also propose an extension of the age and duration of leave, because those who have children know this a child does not stop at 6 years old. unfortunately, a child, he continues to grow, and i feel like saying "luckily a child continues to grow". we must therefore also work on the age and duration of parental leave. all these recommendations are made, and i think they should help both the social partners in finding agreements on such parental leave, but also the commission in the work it is doing in the framework of the roadmap on work-life balance". i hope the commissioner will support these proposals.

in writing. ‒ smes currently pay 30% more taxes than multinational enterprises (mnes) on a pro rata basis. this is because ngos operate in different countries and use this to their advantage. of course, a distinction should be made between tax avoidance, which is clearly illegal, and aggressive tax planning, which is legal but contrary to the spirit of the law. it is particularly in the area of tax avoidance that the current legal framework is no longer sufficient. the member states currently lack the transparency needed to enforce the principle of paying taxes where profits are made. the bill calls for more transparency. this not only leads to effective enforcement of the national tax framework, but also supports the competitiveness of smes. however, this increased transparency will only help if member states have easier access to this information from other member states. only if mnes are transparent to national tax authorities can they meet their obligations regarding the mandatory exchange of tax information. i also see the automatic exchange of tax information as a positive step in the fight against aggressive tax planning. i therefore support this report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this text, which is crucial in the fight against aggressive tax avoidance and optimisation by large groups. this is an essential step towards transparency in order to restore fiscal fairness. country-by-country reporting requires multinationals to report to states their economic and tax information in each state or tax jurisdiction: activity, turnover, pre-tax profits, taxes paid, etc.
in writing. ‒ i welcome the commission's proposal for an automatic exchange of information on corporate taxation between national tax authorities. it is a further step towards tax transparency and an important step forward in the fight against unfair tax practices, in particular aggressive corporate tax planning. however, i do not think that this kind of progress can be achieved by the member states on an individual basis. this requires joint action. the european commission should therefore participate in the exchange of country-by-country reports and have access to the information exchanged between member states' tax authorities, which would allow it to assess whether member states' tax practices are in line with state aid rules. this is particularly important for smes operating in one country. the available data show that in general these companies are subject to an effective tax rate much closer to the statutory rates than that proposed for multinationals. in my view, national companies cannot be systematically disadvantaged because of their size or the absence of crossborder trade.
in writing. ‒ the automatic exchange of information on business taxation between national tax authorities is an important and necessary step. member states retain their prerogatives in terms of taxation but in a common area such as that of the european union it is essential to avoid national policies which are harmful to other member states. by increasing transparency, we will better combat unfair tax practices between member states and reduce harmful tax competition. it is in this context that the european parliament has adopted a proposal which obliges multinational companies (with a minimum of €750 million) to file a country-by-country report in the member state in which the parent entity is resident for tax purposes. this member state will then have to communicate to all the other member states the following information: turnover, profit, taxes paid, capital, retained earnings, tangible assets and number of employees.

in writing. ‒ in 2001, china joined the wto as a non-market economy. as it did not meet the criteria of a market economy, the accession protocol provided for several temporary derogations from wto rules. those derogations will expire at the end of 2016. many of them have already expired. but china is still not a market economy at present. it meets only one of the five criteria defined by the eu. china is a key strategic partner for the eu. however, for it to remain and for good relations to be maintained, we must ensure that the eu has the capacity to effectively combat unfair dumping practices. the european commission will shortly publish an impact assessment on this issue. i am concerned about the adverse impact that the end of the derogations will have on our economy. i therefore call on the council to define its position urgently on the reform of european tools to combat dumping in international trade. as a liberal, i want to stress the importance of respecting the rules in a globalised economy. if these are not respected, we must have effective tools to respond appropriately.
in writing. ‒ the european parliament adopted by a very large majority an ambitious resolution on china's market economy status. a resolution which the european commission cannot ignore when it makes a choice as to whether to grant china market economy status and the method of calculating anti-dumping duties to be applied to unfair exports from china. the european parliament does not consider china to be a market economy. moreover, it meets only one of the five technical criteria defined by the european union for market economy status. that is why i fully support the european parliament's position that a specific anti-dumping calculation method should continue to be applied to unfair exports from that country. the resolution also stressed the 'imminent' need to reform the eu's trade defence instruments. we need to defend our european industry against unfair competition from other countries. it is high time that the council took up its responsibilities in this matter, otherwise our industry and its workers will continue to bear the consequences.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the text. it is important to stress that the eu-china strategic partnership must be based on fair trade relations, in full respect of wto rules, mutual respect and fair and equitable cooperation, and aim to improve human rights and labour rights standards.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution on china's market economy status. we find that china still does not meet the prescribed criteria for market economies. as long as this is not met, china cannot be granted market economy status.
in writing. i voted in favour of the resolution on china's market economy status. i am well aware that the eu concluded an agreement with china in december 2001 regarding the granting of this status in 2016. this is a complex problem with multiple facets. we must look at the legal implications and there are major interests at stake for european industry, but also for our trade relationship with china, one of our most important trading partners. it is mainly about how we deal with chinese dumped goods in our market. we must also ensure that the european commission's proposal on this subject is also in line with the eu's international commitments.

in writing. ‒ the n-va delegation voted against the resolution on mandatory origin labelling of, among other things, milk and meat as an ingredient. we are calling for further work on the voluntary labelling of origin, which is already being applied in a cost-effective way. that is also the view of the european commission. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's trade in agricultural products is not affected by the current situation. origin labelling indicates the origin but does not increase quality or traceability and does not prevent fraud. it also has a taste for protectionism, which is contrary to the principles of the single european market and is particularly detrimental to smaller export-oriented regions such as flanders and border regions. the operational and practical feasibility is an obstacle, as are additional administrative costs and burdens which ultimately lead to a higher price for the consumer, who may consider origin labelling to be relatively important but not willing to pay extra for it. the n-va regrets the lack of realism in the adopted text and believes that the solution to the breach of consumer confidence is not to be found in additional rules, but in more controls, strict enforcement of existing agreements and heavier sanctions.

it is more specifically about the gendered approach to poverty. what is the poverty situation of women in europe? unfortunately, more than 64 million women in europe are living in poverty today. 48% of them single women are unable to cope with unexpected expenses. these single women are considered to be the most vulnerable to poverty. single-parent families in which women are the head of household more often than men are also at greater risk of poverty and social exclusion, leading to a vicious cycle of poverty for their children and their families. today, 27% of european children are at risk of poverty. this represents 22 million children living in poverty. we have seen that the austerity measures, which are often blind austerity measures, taken in recent years in europe have accentuated inequalities and, also, the risks of poverty for women and children. the wage gap persists today. we also have the question of the working poor, precarious status and, finally, the pension gap, which represents a 39% gap and which leads to risks of poverty for older people and women. is it worth recalling that the europe 2020 strategy aims to reduce by at least 20 million the number of people at risk of poverty? we are far from that today. we must break the vicious circle of poverty which today affects 127 million people in europe, including 22 million children. and it should be noted that, particularly as regards adults, women are more affected by this cycle. finally, we have put forward a series of recommendations to ensure that the cycle of poverty can be broken. the first recommendation calls for the guarantee of quality public services and free access to education, health and justice. it is indeed demonstrated that when public services are of good quality and have a good first line, there is a better efficiency and a better redistribution of wealth, which is a real social net to fight poverty. the second recommendation is to combat discrimination in employment, which is a source of poverty for women. we therefore ask that there be coordination of parental leave - maternity leave, paternity leave and parental leave - to combat the precarious situations experienced by women in precarious contracts. the third recommendation is that we should give serious thought to the minimum income as an instrument for combating poverty. so we are not asking today in the report that there should be a minimum income - although that could have been the case - but we are asking for an analysis of minimum income systems throughout europe and identifying good practice in this area as a tool to fight poverty. a fourth claim: when we don't know the phenomenon, we can't provide the solutions. we therefore call for more reliable statistical monitoring of the problem of poverty in europe today. we also ask that there should be a child guarantee system, as we have been able to achieve with the youth guarantee, that is to say that wherever there are important centres of poverty in europe today, it is absolutely necessary to provide budget lines and specific actions to combat child poverty in particular. finally, we are asking - and this is in connection with the report which was discussed just before - for social tariffs for basic necessities, such as access to energy and water, which will actually prevent us from falling into this poverty trap. finally, we ask that there be tax incentives to fight poverty. i would like to thank all the members who have taken part in drawing up this report for all the recommendations. it was a very constructive discussion and i hope that tomorrow it can be voted on by a large majority. this would send an important signal to the commission.

in writing. in the european union, more women than men are affected by poverty. it affects 64.6 million women and 57.6 million men. it is also important to note that single-parent families are more exposed to poverty and social exclusion. the economic crisis and the various austerity policies that have followed in recent years have only made the situation worse by exacerbating inequalities. to break this dynamic, it is now essential that family-friendly working conditions, such as flexible working hours and the possibility of telecommuting, be put in place to ensure that women can be as active as men in the labour market. i also call for european legislative action to meet the needs of fathers and mothers on the different types of leave, whether maternity leave, paternity leave, parental leave or leave for carers.
madam president, commissioner, minister, all the findings are in the same direction. for the last 18 months we have been living under a price regime which has been falling steadily and which is abnormally low, being below the farmers' production costs. so, of course, the voluntary regulation of milk production, as proposed, is a small step in the right direction, but it is largely inadequate, because we need mandatory regulation, with penalties for member states that do not play along. if it is voluntary, there will always be those who will not play the game and who will, of course, frustrate the efforts of those who want to play it. better activation of article 222 is fundamental, with reasoned competition. but clearly, today, over-liberalisation is not working. it may seem archaic to argue for a return to quotas, with of course some adjustments for certain countries - i am thinking of italy in particular, which had a quota that was far too low in relation to the high quality production it needs. yet, adjusting quotas to economic realities is the only viable solution. the quotas worked for 25 years. since we abandoned them, it doesn't work anymore. i may be archaic, but i'm willing to be archaic by advocating for the return of dairy quotas.
mr president, the report as it stands today is a response to what the european commission has proposed earlier to improve the functioning of the internal market. i think everyone agrees today that the single market is not yet complete, and it is therefore a step in the right direction that this strategy pays much attention to those sectors where there is still a lot of work to be done. i am thinking in particular of the services sector. we must make it easier for consumers and businesses alike to move within that single market: the commission has already taken a number of measures to combat fraud. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. i am glad that the principles of better regulation are also reflected in several places in a number of paragraphs in the text. on the other hand, i would like to express my concern about the paragraphs relating to taxation, because that is still a national competence. in general, i think that this report is a step in the right direction towards a better functioning internal market. i shall therefore vote in favour of the report.
mr president, madam commissioner, we socialists and democrats can be proud of the substantial improvements our group has made to mrs comi's report, in order to give a new social impetus to this text, which at its core summed up the commission's proposal very well. it was necessary to continue to guarantee a high level of consumer protection, equal treatment and the creation of sustainable jobs. beyond these aspects, i would like to highlight some priorities that are important to me and to our group in the single market strategy, namely equal protection for consumers buying online or offline, the definition of the concept of a social economy enterprise, but also a legislative proposal on the protection of geographical indications for non-agricultural products and, finally, the promotion of craft industries. as for the services passport, we must be vigilant, because it risks being a tool of unfair competition by promoting social dumping within the european union. do you want to be the gravediggers of a europe which is already sick of unfair competition in the internal market?
in writing. ladies and gentlemen, i would ask you to vote in favour of this report because it contains important elements, particularly for european consumers and workers. firstly, the introduction at european level of a compulsory system for the provision of essential information on handicrafts and industrial products. this system would be a real added value for consumers and i hope that the european commission will heed our call. finally, the principle of equal pay for equal work in the same place is an important tool in combating market distortions. the citizens and workers of europe expect europe to fight social dumping more effectively, and the respect of this principle in the context of the posting of workers would be a first step forward. in view of all this, it seemed to me important that the european parliament should support this text. i also hope that the commission will be able to show ambition on both these subjects. thank you for your attention.
in writing. ‒ seven years after the creation of bitcoins, it seemed appropriate to make an owninitiative report on this new type of currency. this technology, in principle, allows a decentralization of the means, fast, flexible and fairly secure to record any kind of transaction and the history of previous transactions in a "distributed ledger". the main possibilities of virtual currencies and distributed ledger technology (dlt) in the area of payments relate to reducing transaction costs and ease of use while ensuring resilience and privacy levels. in this context, it should be noted that transaction costs for payments remain surprisingly high. on average, more than 7% of crossborder remittances are consumed by transfer costs. in the medium term, competition could be enhanced by the introduction of a single, non-exclusive and interoperable portfolio. the report highlights: facilitating micropayments for online purchases of goods; the potential of dlt at european level; difficulties related to pseudo anonymity; the creation of a task force under the commission to assess potential assessments of dlt and virtual currencies; transparency and consumer awareness; and the fight against money laundering.
in writing. the development of new technologies is a source of innovation and profound transformation of our society. the development of virtual currencies is one example of this, and we do not yet fully know its long-term potential. there are currently more than 600 virtual currency systems in the world. we know that this technology could reduce transaction costs and access to finance. however, risks may also be highlighted due to, inter alia, the lack of reliability linked to the absence of governance structures or the risk of financial instability linked to the risk of high volatility of virtual currencies and the creation of new speculative bubbles. in addition, virtual currencies could become a means of promoting the black market and money laundering. we must therefore regulate it in an appropriate way to avoid breaking the innovative potential of this new technology. i therefore welcome the fact that this report calls on the commission to set up a cross-cutting study group to better understand this phenomenon, to analyse the risks and benefits and to design stress tests to ensure its stability.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this text which states that the european framework for virtual currencies, such as bitcoin, and the blockchain technologies underlying them is not necessary at this stage. i think, however, that it is more necessary to monitor these technologies by setting up a task force at the level of the european commission. such a working group could be called upon to monitor the evolution of these innovative technologies without restricting their ability to significantly reduce the cost of financial transactions, while ensuring that they are not misused for criminal purposes. (blockchain technology is a decentralized database stored on multiple servers that allows for quick and secure verification and documentation of financial transactions despite the absence of a central clearing authority.)
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this well-balanced text. we recognise the potential benefits associated with virtual currencies and related technologies for consumers, businesses, charities and the wider economy, including increased speed and efficiency and reduced costs for payments and transfers, including cross-border payments and transfers, and potentially promoting financial inclusion and easier access to finance and financial resources for the business sector and smes.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because virtual currencies can make a positive contribution to the well-being of citizens and economic development, including the financial sector. it may, for example, entail reductions in the operational and transaction costs of payments. this could, according to an optimistic estimate, reduce the total cost of transfers by up to eur 20 billion. we must ensure that this currency is not misused by criminal circles.

in writing. ‒ since the abolition of the safe harbour, there has been a legal vacuum regarding the exploitation of personal data of european citizens by the united states. the privacy shield agreement negotiated between the commission and the united states provides some remedies to this situation. it establishes a complaints mechanism for european citizens and a us mediator to whom the european side can appeal in the event of a dispute. the european parliament will, however, have to remain extremely vigilant in ensuring effective protection of the personal data of european citizens.
in writing. ‒ i welcome the adoption by the european parliament of this resolution on transatlantic data flows. with the privacy shield, which is supposed to regulate the flow of transatlantic data for commercial purposes, about to be closed, it was essential that parliament take a stand on this issue. this is an extremely important issue and an integral part of our relationship with the united states. the privacy shield is the successor to the safe harbor, which was invalidated by the court in 2015, and must provide the best possible safeguards for the protection of personal data transferred to the united states. while improvements have undoubtedly been made to the system as it existed under the safe harbour, some shortcomings persist. the commission should therefore continue its dialogue with the us authorities in order to make the best possible use of the shortcomings highlighted by parliament here, particularly those relating to the mass collection of data.

in writing. ‒ i have approved this report on the commission communication entitled 'a new deal for energy consumers'. the report also calls for the eu to take action to ensure that the eu's energy sector is not left behind. in this context, the provision of stable, affordable, efficient and sustainable energy to citizens, as well as energy-efficient products, services and quality buildings, should be a priority. the energy union must also help to eradicate energy poverty, protect consumers from abusive or unfair practices and promote energy-saving measures.
the energy market in europe is in full swing. in order to achieve our energy and climate objectives, we will eventually have to evolve towards an economy based entirely on the use of clean and renewable energy. the report calls for the consumer to be given a privileged role in the energy market. the energy market in europe has been liberalised, but now the main task is to create a transparent and competitive retail market tailored to the consumer. the right of customers to have access to their energy consumption and the rates charged to them on the invoice even more quickly and clearly - not just once a year at the final invoice. it has been shown that 'real-time information' motivates consumers to save up to 8% on their consumption and thus also on their invoices. freedom of choice of supplier also implies that consumers should be able to switch quickly and free of charge to competing suppliers. it is also a good thing to give consumers who produce their own renewable energy at home better access to the energy market. because the more producers supply energy, the more competition there is and the more interesting the bill becomes for the end user.
in writing. ‒ in its recommendations on the 'new deal' for consumers in the energy market, the european parliament advocated a set of measures to strengthen consumers' market power in energy production and energy tariffs. to help consumers to play a more active role in the energy market, we have proposed introducing new management models such as collective purchasing systems and innovative financial instruments to stimulate increased use of self-production, self-consumption and energy-efficient tools. to ensure transparency in energy prices, we have called for more simplified invoices in terms of understanding contracts, measures to help consumers compare offers, information on the most appropriate and advantageous tariffs based on their consumption history, etc. finally, we called for a common definition of energy poverty, based on the idea that access to affordable energy is a fundamental social right, and asked the commission to prepare an action plan by 2017 to tackle energy poverty.
in writing. - i said yes to that text. the ultimate goal should be an economy based entirely on renewable energy, which can only be achieved by reducing our energy consumption, making full use of the 'energy efficiency first' principle (the 'first fuel') and prioritising energy savings and demand-side measures over supply-side measures, in order to achieve our climate objectives in line with the paris agreement scenario (1.5 °c), as well as energy security, competitiveness and, in particular, lower energy bills.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report, together with my delegation. the consumer will be at the centre of the energy network in the energy union. when the market is free to play, it is up to the consumer to make the best choice that suits him or her best. the market incentives will ensure that consumers can use energy more efficiently and that the right price is paid without market distortions. however, a market also entails certain risks for consumers who do not have the capacity to take account of this amount of information or for certain consumers who cannot pay the energy bill. the report identifies the right pain points and, while respecting subsidiarity, calls on the member states and regions to take account of this group of consumers. this report remains relatively balanced and provides a good basis for legislative work in the context of the energy union.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution to give consumers more power when it comes to energy purchases. these include price comparison methods and better information on energy efficiency, more eu funds to promote energy efficiency, self-generation of energy and other measures that can reduce the energy bill for vulnerable households and citizens. this is already possible in belgium, but not everywhere in the eu. in an age of high-technology available to all of us, citizens must be able to generate their own renewable energy and, above all, become more energy efficient. they must be able to become 'micro' energy producers themselves, which can only benefit the free market: that's what we mean by prosumers.

the rapporteur. madam president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, as you know, this week is an important milestone in the fight against tax fraud and tax evasion by multinational companies, and i would really like to thank all the fictitious rapporteurs who helped me to present this text here in the plenary. i will not go into the issues - everyone knows them, since the last financial scandals involving tax evasion, tax fraud and money laundering on an industrial scale broke out, whether in the grand duchy of luxembourg, switzerland or panama, and this continues since, as recently as last friday, france decided to sue booking.com for tax evasion amounting to 356 million. i would therefore like to remind you today why this is a crucial step we are taking here in the european parliament. as you know, since these scandals became public knowledge, the european parliament has been one of the driving forces behind a thoroughgoing reform of taxation of multinational companies in europe. it is here that political awareness has taken shape and it is here that pressure has been accumulated to make the council and the member states realise that we no longer want this two-speed europe where, on the one hand, the vast majority of citizens finance the tax and, on the other, the most powerful multinationals in the world evade this tax. this way of analysing the situation is not ideology or political positioning, it is simply a matter of wanting everyone to contribute equally to the financing of youth employment, health care, schooling, universities, housing or security. (the president cut the speaker off) multinationals cannot choose to escape the collective effort simply because they can afford financial or tax advisors whose only job is to figure out how to evade taxes - those same financial/tax advisors whose pay is set according to the amounts that are being diverted from the tax base. this report is therefore the logical continuation of our work, since a comprehensive reflection on taxation has been initiated in parliament, in particular through the special committees taxe 1, taxe 2 and the committee of inquiry into the panama papers, which will soon begin its work. the technical measures in this report are therefore intended to fill the gaps in our legislation or to correct these malfunctions. so let us get to the heart of the matter: what does this report say? firstly, the report provides that companies pay their taxes where they make their profits, and that is why it contains a whole series of precise and binding definitions of the conditions which prove that a multinational is well established in a country, since today, too often, multinationals organise themselves to transfer their profits to tax havens without having paid any taxes in the country where they actually carry out their activities. secondly, the report also provides for the establishment of a strict and common blacklist of the 28 member states of tax havens and countries that distort competition by means of favourable tax conditions, including those located in the union. in short, it is a common definition of what a tax haven is in the 28 countries. the report also proposes to clarify patent legislation, since so far too many multinationals have used patent incentives to artificially reduce their profits, whereas in the beginning it was really a policy to help countries and companies that were really innovative. the report also provides for an end to double non-taxation. in short, it is no longer possible for a multinational to be taxed anywhere because the legislation of the 28 is so complicated that some multinationals set up tax arrangements that hide their profits and the actual amount of taxes paid. as regards the switchover clause and the rules on controlled foreign companies, this report calls for the launch of a debate on a fair tax rate among all member states for corporate tax within the european union, and this measure will allow all member states to tax, at their national rates, the profits of multinationals that are not taxed or taxed at less than 15% in another country. finally, the report provides for effective control of loans between entities of the same multinational, since too often multinationals use this system of loans not to boost investment but only to evade tax. the aim of these measures is not, as i have unfortunately heard, to kill the economy, but to combat effectively tax evasion and avoidance by multinational companies. this is a further step in the process initiated by the european parliament, and i think that is exactly what the european citizens expect from us here in parliament.
i am very pleased to see that the commission has taken the initiative to make the necessary proposals to the council and parliament. how can we attract more private investment in the european union with the juncker plan efsi? i looked it up and mr bayet, rapporteur for the report we are discussing today and a member of the socialist party, also spoke in the debate. and i can agree with him 100 per cent on what he said then, namely that in the current economic climate, and i quote, "it is important that we give priority to investments that speed up recovery, that increase productivity and that promote reality". i agree with you 100% . we must give priority to these additional investments in the european union. unfortunately, with this report we are doing the opposite, we are sending the opposite signal, also led by the rapporteur, mr bayet. each country decides how much tax it levies on corporations, so that's not really the problem. on the contrary, we can all agree that taxes, especially for small and mediumsized enterprises, are too high today and must be lowered. so that's not really the problem. but there is a problem when tax structures are set up that are specifically used to artificially shift profits to countries where taxes are lower with the sole purpose of evading those taxes and the tax. we find that it is mainly multinationals who use it and that small and mediumsized enterprises cannot do so, that they must pay the full price, and that is not true. it's just not right, it's against everyone's feelings. taxes must be paid where the profits are created. that is why we must indeed adapt our european legislation to ensure that taxes are paid where economic activity takes place. but instead of tackling these fraudulent constructions, i see the report focusing on something else, namely raising taxes. i also note that the finance ministers who are discussing this report are going in the right direction and will make the right adjustments to the commission's proposal. in any case, i hope they will ignore most of this resolution and appreciate real entrepreneurs, and certainly the jobs they create.

the rapporteur. mr president, commissioner, first of all i would like to thank you all for your speeches, and i would like to thank in particular my fictitious colleagues, because in this very political and relatively technical subject i wanted to emphasise the quality of their listening and the respect they showed during all the discussions. i think you have understood, commissioner, that although the methodology or methods differ somewhat from one political group to another, parliament is unanimous in its desire to put an end to this system which allows multinationals to avoid paying taxes where they carry out their activities, to pay almost no taxes, because - contrary to what i heard earlier - the average tax in europe, which is levied on income or profits of companies, is 2.4%. in the united states, it is 19 percent. and these are not political figures. if anyone doesn't believe me here, they can check out the parliament website. these figures are based on studies carried out by the oecd and the commission. it's the reality. as a result, we do not tax more in europe than elsewhere, i would even say the opposite. of course, this notice sets out in one text a whole series of principles that we believe are essential to bringing an end to this system. as my colleagues niedermayer and calvet-chambon have said, we are not going to kill the economy, because we are obviously distinguishing between the real economy and the cheaters - the cheaters who hide their profits, the cheaters who use letter boxes in panama, for example. nor will we over-regulate, we are simply defining a whole series of loopholes in the legislation, these loopholes which are used by multinationals to avoid paying taxes. we have also spoken - as you said, commissioner - of tax regimes favourable to patents and tax havens, and my colleagues joly, de masi and valli have told you this; but, commissioner, this is no longer an administrative or institutional problem. what we want are solutions. we cannot continue with a patent system which at present allows a whole series of multinational companies to charge exorbitant amounts for years on simple logos simply to avoid paying taxes. so, "through the door or through the window", the commission will have to help us to change things. we are counting on you, commissioner, to influence the council's decisions, because if the council does not change its attitude and does not listen to us, it will be solely responsible for the future scandals that will unfortunately still happen in europe and elsewhere in the world.

in writing. ‒ the world health organization framework convention on tobacco control, or fctc, is the first global health agreement. it was created to counter the widespread use of tobacco worldwide. it focuses in particular on the illicit trade in tobacco products, which is not only a criminal offence but also a serious health risk, with one person dying every six seconds from a smoking-related disease. the protocol to prevent illicit trade in tobacco products (fctc protocol) covers the following important issues: the establishment of a tracking and tracing system, the regulation of internet sales and record keeping requirements. although there is already a comprehensive eu strategy to combat cigarette smuggling, it is important to note that a significant proportion of illicit tobacco products in the eu originate from third countries. it is therefore important to give effect to the protocol signed by the eu in december 2013. this will not happen, however, until it has been ratified by 40 contracting parties, which has not yet happened. i therefore support parliament's call for ratification by the eu and its member states to allow for a swift entry into force.

in writing. ‒ the world health organisation's protocol on illicit trade in tobacco products aims to eliminate all forms of illicit trade in tobacco products. illicit trade in tobacco products is defined in the protocol as any act or conduct prohibited by law in connection with the manufacture, dispatch, receipt, possession, distribution, sale or purchase of tobacco products. i voted in favour of this recommendation because the protocol encourages and strengthens international cooperation and contributes to the secure exchange of information, technical cooperation in law enforcement, and mutual legal and administrative assistance. this is a fearsome weapon against crime and for our health.
in writing. ‒ the markets in financial instruments directive adopted in 2014 states that the european securities and markets authority, or esma, is to work with the national competent authorities of each member state to develop a common data system. the directive requires this to be done by 3 january 2017. however, to ensure efficient and harmonised data collection, a completely new infrastructure has to be created. esma and the national authorities cannot currently guarantee that these infrastructures will be in place and ready for use by the requested date. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the directive is implemented. the amendment to the directive postpones these deadlines by a further year. i welcome this extension of time, as it is necessary to create an effective infrastructure.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the revision of the markets in financial instruments directive. mifid 2 is a revision of mifid 1 that addresses the shadow areas of the markets. mifid regulates investment services in the field of financial instruments provided by banks, as well as the operation of traditional stock exchanges and other trading platforms. the main elements are: improvement of the structure of the markets; the transparency of trading activities on stock markets will be enhanced; to regulate high frequency trading; limit the risks of destabilising speculation in commodity markets; to strengthen investor protection. the european parliament debates focused on the issue of the remuneration of financial management consultants and ways of preventing the risk of conflicts of interest. parliament has adopted the principle of remuneration by fees for independent advisers, leaving no choice to the member states. the standards will not come into force until 2018 instead of 2017 as originally planned!
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the european parliament's report on the proposal for a regulation amending, as regards certain dates, directive 2014/65/eu on markets in financial instruments. as regards exemptions, the report states that the directive should not apply to persons who trade financial instruments other than commodity derivatives or emission allowances, or derivatives thereof, on their own account and who do not provide any other investment services or perform any other investment activity in relation to financial instruments other than commodity derivatives or emission allowances or derivatives thereof, unless such persons are either members or participants of a regulated market or an mtf, or have direct electronic access to a trading venue, and in both cases apply a high-frequency algorithmic trading technique on such a trading venue. it seemed important to emphasise this.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the proposal for a directive of the european parliament and of the council amending, as regards certain dates, directive 2014/65/eu on markets in financial instruments.
in writing. ‒ the new framework strengthens investor protection by introducing robust organisational and operational requirements by july 2016. however, stakeholders such as trading venues, esma and national competent authorities cannot guarantee that the necessary data collection infrastructures will be up and running by that time. without data, trading venues and investment firms will not be able to report executed transactions to the competent authorities. in order to ensure legal certainty and to avoid potential market distortions, i voted for urgent measures to postpone the date of application of the full framework.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the european regulation on market abuse. the regulation provides for the extension of the market abuse regime to non-regulated markets and new types of financial instruments. the extension of the scope of this scheme means that issuers listed on the open market will be subject to preventive measures to combat market abuse (publication of inside information, establishment of insider lists, obligation to notify executive transactions, etc.).
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the european parliament's report on the proposal for a regulation amending, as regards certain dates, regulation (eu) no 600/2014 on markets in financial instruments, regulation (eu) no 596/2014 on market abuse and regulation (eu) no 909/2014 on improving securities regulation in the union and central securities depositories. investment firms often execute, for their own account or that of their clients, transactions in derivatives or other financial instruments or assets that include a set of related or subordinated transactions. such packages of transactions allow investment firms and their clients to better manage risk, with the price of each element of the package reflecting the overall risk profile of the whole rather than the current market price for each element. i thought it was important to emphasize that.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the amendments to this proposal. investment firms often execute, for their own account or that of their clients, transactions in derivatives or other financial instruments or assets that include a set of related or subordinated transactions. such packages of transactions allow investment firms and their clients to better manage risk, with the price of each element of the package reflecting the overall risk profile of the whole rather than the current market price for each element. packages of transactions may take different forms, such as an exchange of spot instruments (efp), trading strategies executed on trading venues, or tailor-made packages of transactions, and their different characteristics should be taken into account for the calibration of the applicable transparency regime. it is therefore appropriate to specify, for the purposes of regulation (eu) no 600/2014, the specific circumstances in which pre-negotiation transparency would not apply to bundles of transactions or to any of their elements on an individual basis.

in writing. ‒ under the guise of sustainable development, additional taxes are suggested, a common asylum and migration policy is proposed, and a proactive role for the eu and an infringement of the sovereignty of the member states and the third countries concerned are organised.
in writing. ‒ one and a half billion people live in poverty and lack access to healthcare, education and a decent income. this demonstrates the importance of policy coherence for development (pdc). in this report, which i approved, parliament considers that the dpc should contribute to the establishment of the rule of law and impartial institutions and to the challenge of good governance in developing countries. in this respect, it regrets the lack of progress in implementing the principles of the cpd and calls for a debate on this issue in the context of sustainable development by 2030. the report also calls on the commission to systematically consult human rights organisations at an early stage of the development decision-making process and calls for more institutional coordination between the eu institutions and the member states.
in writing. ‒ development policy is one of the main areas of foreign policy of the european union and its member states. the eu's contribution to international development is measured not only by the size of its official development assistance (oda) budget, but also by the efficiency with which it is spent. the nva delegation is therefore pleased that the report emphasises the added value of policy coherence. it is, however, of the opinion that certain paragraphs in the report lack focus. the proposed financial transaction taxes would increase the cost of financing for belgian companies, which would harm their competitiveness. the commission has also received comments from the netherlands authorities, which have not provided any evidence to support its view that the measure is compatible with the internal market. taxation policy is a matter for national competence. finally, it considers that stricter recommendations to encourage corporate ownership of corporate social responsibility are more realistic than developing internationally binding frameworks. the nva delegation therefore abstained from voting on this report.
in writing. the 2015 report is an important element of the union's contribution to greater policy coherence for sustainable development. while the union regularly reaffirms its political commitment to the dpc, it has yet to find the means to put this commitment into practice. the report not only takes stock of the progress made by the commission, but also identifies areas where the existing policy coherence mechanisms for development in the union can be improved. there is a need to stimulate the debate on the future of policy coherence at union level, in particular in the context of the 2030 agenda for sustainable development adopted by the united nations last september.
in writing. ‒ today, one and a half billion people still live in poverty and lack access to health care, education and decent income. in order to provide the most effective assistance to these people, it is important to ensure policy coherence for development (pdc), particularly in the design and implementation of the new sustainable development programme. in this report, the european parliament calls on the commission to systematically consult human rights organisations at an early stage of the decision-making process. this is an important element in view of the experience of these actors on the ground. the report also provided the european parliament with an opportunity to identify areas it considers to be priorities, namely immigration, trade and finance, food security, climate change and security. i have decided to vote in favour of this report, in line with many of the points.
in writing. ‒ i am in favour of the text. the previous reports of the european parliament have made a major contribution to advancing the concept of the dpc by institutionalising a permanent rapporteur on the subject in the committee on development, by affirming that the dpc falls within the political competence of the parliament (as a democratically elected institution and as a co-legislator) and by putting forward concrete proposals to move forward with the application of the concept at union level. this report not only takes stock of the progress made by the european commission and identifies areas where the mechanisms of the cpd in place in the union can be improved, but also seeks to stimulate debate on the future of the concept at the union level.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because there is often a lack of coherence when it comes to eu development policy. the emphasis in this report on the eu's external policy is absolutely necessary. as the refugee crisis and destabilisation in the eu's neighbourhood put pressure on the eu's foundations, the emphasis should be placed on external action, among other things. stabilising the eu's neighbours must be a top priority for the eu.
in writing. – i support this pcd (policy coherence for development) report because i believe that policy coherence is necessary to achieve sustainable development. in this regard, the eu can set an example for the rest of the world. the european parliament plays a great role in this. in that respect, we need to correct existing inconsistencies. this is important if we want to implement the 2030 agenda for sustainable development correctly. moreover, in order to succeed, our international partners also need to be convinced. the overall goal here, is to establish universal development goals and to overcome the outdated idea of donor-recipient. pcd promotes synergies and cooperation across different policy areas. therefore, i welcome the rapporteur’s efforts on promoting the pcd debate and the need for involving many different stakeholders, such as the institutions, civil society and think tanks. in addition, he recognises the need for a stronger focus on eu external relations, which will be needed to solve the various crises at the eu’s borders. pcd will be an important contribution to this.
in writing. ‒ the new alliance for food security and nutrition in africa, or nafsn, was launched in 2012 with the aim of complementing private investment in agriculture to improve food security and nutrition in african countries. the eu and its member states have thus become the world's largest donor of development aid. investments under nafsn have already benefited more than 8.2 million smallholders and created more than 21 000 jobs, more than half of them for women. however, it should be taken into account that at least 14% of total greenhouse gas emissions per year are attributable to agriculture. the main cause of this is the use of nitrogen fertilizers. i therefore support parliament's call for nafsn to limit the use of artificial fertilisers and pesticides to the greatest extent possible, given their environmental and health consequences. finally, however, the human rights of workers in africa must be respected alongside the environment and health. investors based in the eu must respect the rights of small farmers and the community as a whole on the ground and must not exploit their economic advantages. social responsibility is required here.
in writing. ‒ the new alliance for food security and nutrition in africa (nasan) aims to improve food security and nutrition by helping 50 million people in sub-saharan africa to lift themselves out of poverty by 2020. the participating countries have negotiated cooperation frameworks where they commit to fostering private investment in the agricultural sector in africa. i supported this resolution which calls for a review of investment strategies in agriculture taking into account the resources of the local economy, in particular smallholders and family farms. the text denounces the fact that small farmers, agricultural workers, fishermen and indigenous peoples are too little taken into account in the decision. it therefore calls for the review of all projects which directly promote land grabbing.
in writing. ‒ the n-va delegation voted in favour of the report, which is critical of the new alliance for food security and nutrition (nafsn). it goes without saying that africa needs investment in agriculture. food security is and remains a major problem that must be addressed. but the alliance is not taking the right approach. the key to n-va is that good living conditions for african farmers can contribute to a more favourable local economy. there are also fewer push factors for migration to the eu. the alliance denies that small farmers have the capacity to compete with multinationals. the report rightly calls for family businesses and local economies to be given a more central place in this cooperation. the nasfn also poses environmental risks (erosion problems, loss of biodiversity, decline in the diversity of seed supply) through its encouragement of large-scale monocultures, which in turn undermine food security.
in writing. the new alliance for food security aims to mobilise private investment in agriculture to improve food security and nutrition in sub-saharan africa. as a result, each participating african country has adopted a cooperation framework setting out commitments for legislative reforms, funding intentions from g7 donors and business pledges to invest a total of usd 8 billion. in this context, the european union is responsible for coordination in côte d'ivoire and malawi. while the new covenant's purpose is noble, it has many shortcomings, which this report is worthy of pointing out. the new alliance must not replicate the asian green revolution model in africa, marginalizing african smallholder farmers and undermining unsustainable agriculture. in my view, the union must make the new alliance a support mechanism for family farming and local economies, with the ultimate aim of fighting poverty and food and nutritional insecurity.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report, which notes that multinationals operating under the new alliance for food security and nutrition (nasan) are promoting large-scale contract farming, at the risk of marginalising small local producers, and which considers it essential to strengthen farmers' organisations, for example, so as to give them more weight in the negotiations. i also supported an amendment which deplores the fact that in the african context some companies are calling for the harmonization of seed laws which is bound to hinder the establishment and development of farmers' seed systems because they would not meet the criteria of distinction, homogeneity and stability (dhs).
in writing. ‒ we do not want ggo's in europe, but neither in africa. yet that is exactly what is happening through the so-called new alliance for food security and nutrition. this public-private partnership was launched in 2012 under the auspices of the g8. the aim is to improve food security and food quality in sub-saharan africa through private investment in agriculture. ngos have repeatedly rejected this approach because it encourages land grabbing, restricts the freedom of exchange of seed (when farmers should be able to grow their own seeds independently) and pushes ggo down the throats of african farmers, whether they like it or not. just so we 're clear , introducing new gmos into the environment poses serious problems for farmers who want to grow gm-free, as these organisms spread freely and uncontrolled in nature. the report by mr heubuch, a green member, lists all these points and is against any promotion of gmos in africa at the expense of the taxpayer. monsanto finds the report neo-colonial, which is ironic, since the industry itself is using this new alliance to bend african laws on land ownership, seeds and gmos to their advantage. i therefore voted in favour of the report with conviction.
in writing. ‒ each participating african country has adopted a cooperation framework which sets out the commitments of each of the parties concerned. these commitments cover legislative reforms in individual african countries, the funding intentions of g7 donors and the pledges of the 180 participating companies to invest a total of usd 8 billion. two companies are leading the way in terms of their share of agricultural investment: the swiss seed producer syngenta and the norwegian fertilizer manufacturer yara international. i recognize the need for african countries to invest in agriculture. while the objective of nasan is commendable, it has many shortcomings. the text voted today is a good instrument for cooperation and improvement of the agricultural situation in the framework of enhanced cooperation.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because the new alliance for food security and nutrition, despite its shortcomings, is of the utmost importance in africa. the report clearly emphasises that official development assistance (oda) should be used to combat poverty, and not to serve the interests of eu trade policy. the eu should not use oda to support transnational companies that operate as monopolies or cartels, undermining the local private sector and crowding out family farms and small farms.
in writing. – i voted in favour of this parliamentary resolution. in 2012 we launched the new alliance for food security and nutrition in africa (nafsn). this alliance is aiming to offer significant support to a variety of african countries. in order to do this we need to learn from mistakes from the past. this parliamentary resolution identifies many of these mistakes. with regard to governance and ownership, i agree that efforts need to be made to help these nations to avoid corruption. in addition, it needs to be monitored whether the country cooperation frameworks (ccf) are actually implemented. for this to happen, they need to be made public and be fully transparent. in order for the farmers to participate in farming, we also need to ensure that they maintain access to land and that malicious practises such as land-grabbing are prevented. but what i most strongly welcome is the rapporteur’s call on including women in all of our actions, to promote gender equality.
in writing. ‒ the international accounting standards board (iasb) is a neutral and independent body that develops high-quality accounting standards and a common terminology for financial reporting worldwide. since 2005, listed companies in the eu have been required to prepare their annual accounts in accordance with these accounting standards. these standards are particularly important for the establishment of a single capital market in the eu. however, the complexity of financial reporting is constantly increasing, making it difficult for smaller companies in particular to enter the stock market. i therefore welcome the commission's intention to examine with the iasb whether accounting standards can be developed specifically for smaller companies. i also support the parliament's proposal to formulate a common european position on the development of standards, because it would be a disadvantage if national and european bodies were to take different lines in the negotiations.
in writing. ‒ since 2005, publicly listed companies in the eu have been required to prepare their consolidated financial statements in accordance with international accounting standards. the incorporation of international accounting standards into european union law is governed by an adoption mechanism described in the ias regulation. two key points are made in this report:• the need to develop consistent financial reporting standards. harmonisation and consistency should be ensured in the existing body of international accounting standards, but also with regard to other union financial services regulations; • call for a further strengthening of european influence in the early stages of the development of accounting standards.
in writing. ‒ international financial reporting standards (ifrs) and international auditing standards (isa) make a major contribution to the smooth functioning of the internal market and capital markets by facilitating investor decision-making. these standards ensure, in particular, a better exchange of information between investors and companies and a better protection of investments. the consistency of these standards is therefore fundamental. in this report, parliament calls on the commission to follow a series of recommendations and calls on the standardisation body to ensure that these standards are in line with those set at world level. the clarity of these standards will enable us to increase the confidence of investors in our market, which is a significant source of growth.
in writing. ‒ the report was an opportunity to assess international accounting standards, which are one of the essential elements for the proper functioning of the internal market and capital markets. ifrs are intended to reduce the information gap between investors and firms, to protect investments, to promote transparency by improving the comparability and quality of financial information internationally, and to enable investors and other market participants to make informed economic decisions. however, ten years after they were implemented, it is time for a review - and corrections. unfortunately, i note that the commission has not yet proposed the necessary legislative changes to address the shortcomings identified in its own assessment. i support the european parliament's calls for the maystadt recommendation to be followed up on the extension of the public interest test. these standards must not jeopardise financial stability or impede the economic development of the european union. i also support the request to the commission to make a proposal to incorporate into the ias regulation the definition of the 'general interest' criterion which also appears in the maystadt report.
in writing. ‒ international accounting standards are an important component of the financial services regulation and the eu supervisory framework. they are linked to many other aspects of european financial services regulation, particularly in the area of prudential regulation. the rapporteur therefore stresses the importance of accounting standards for the establishment of a single capital market in the european union, in particular in the context of the proposed capital markets union (cmu). he said that the application of international financial reporting standards in the eu had helped to strengthen the single market and the competitiveness of the european economy by enabling businesses to attract capital and investment on global capital markets. the application of ifrs standards in the european union over the past ten years has therefore had overall positive effects. however, the financial crisis has shown that financial reporting standards need to be revised and improved. the use of the term 'fair value' and its implications for financial stability, in particular, has sparked an ongoing debate. so this text is a good signal
