in writing. ‒ i share the concern about unfair trading practices in the food supply chain, but this report puts too much power in the hands of the commission and the eu.
in writing. ‒ unfair trading practices are practices that deviate significantly from good trading practice and in which the trading partners do not see eye to eye. especially for smes and micro-enterprises, which represent over 99% of the food and drink producing enterprises, late payments, unilateral or retroactive changes to contractual terms and the refusal to sign written contracts are highly problematic. i therefore support parliament's call on the commission to submit legislative proposals to combat unfair trading practices in the food supply chain, in order to ensure adequate incomes for farmers and a wide choice for consumers.
in writing. ‒ i have approved this own-initiative report which stresses the need to eliminate unfair trading practices (restriction of market access, unilateral contractual changes, etc.) in the food supply chain, in particular to improve the situation of farmers who are heavily affected by these practices.
in writing. unfair trading practices in the food and non-food supply chain have a detrimental effect on the eu economy as a whole, depriving businesses of their capacity to invest and innovate. in this context, the weaker party often does not take any legal action because it fears that the business relationship will be terminated. while the european commission has called on member states to find ways of giving small producers and retailers greater protection against unfair trading practices, the problem is far from being solved. the reason for this is that the member states persist in adopting different positions on the matter. the report has the merit of highlighting the risks associated with unfair practices: strong and coherent action is needed at union level to eliminate these unfair practices completely. the ultimate aim is to stimulate reflection and find solutions to this problem within the european internal market.
in writing. ‒ unfair trading practices are still present in our economy, particularly in the agri-food sector. delayed payments, restricted market access, unjustified termination of contracts, pressure to lower product prices - the list goes on! these practices must stop now. the european parliament voted this week in favour of a resolution on unfair trading practices in the food supply chain. it is not just a question of ethics, but also of common sense and collective pragmatism. the food supply chain is of strategic importance for the european union; the agri-food sector employs over 47 million people and generates 4.3 percent of our gdp. as a reminder, since 2009, the european parliament has adopted five resolutions on problems in the eu distribution system. today's resolution is the culmination of that. this is to say that we will continue to protect our fellow citizens and above all that we will do everything to avoid creating a climate of uncertainty in our european market. we want to preserve the spirit of mutual trust, mutual aid and fraternity which is characteristic of our europe.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report which calls on the european executive to come forward with proposals to combat unfair trading practices (utps) in the food supply chain. in the context of the crisis - which we know - which is affecting the milk and meat sectors in particular, we have asked that the eu adopt legislation to combat these unfair practices (payment delays, limitation of market access, unilateral changes to contractual terms, unjustified termination of contracts, unfair transfer of commercial risk and transfer of transport and storage costs to suppliers). union-wide framework legislation is needed to combat pcds and to ensure that european farmers and consumers benefit from fair conditions of sale and purchase (in particular with a view to ensuring fairer and more transparent trade relations between producers, suppliers and distributors in the sector). it should be noted that the eu already had legislation to combat unfair business-to-consumer trading practices (directive 2005/29/ec), but there were no european rules to combat unfair practices between operators in the agri-food chain. unfair commercial practices were then only partially covered by the competition law.
in writing. ‒ the power of supermarkets has been known for some time and europe has already taken several initiatives to combat this. this is not the first time that these unfair trading practices have been the subject of debate. the commission is also aware of the problem, but would prefer that the food supply chain develops a self-regulatory initiative or that the member states take the initiative. we don't think that's such a good idea. large supermarkets are only growing in power and increasingly transnational. they thus have an increasing impact on pricing and contract negotiations, where terms are often changed unilaterally. these trade practices create a level playing field. moreover, the self-regulatory chain initiative does not seem to be working. farmers' organisations in several member states are already boycotting it because it is not enforceable and no anonymous complaints can be lodged. this excellent report therefore calls on the commission to come up with a legislative initiative (a directive) to combat these unfair trading practices and to give some more substance to the self-regulatory chain initiative. not only through anonymous complaints or better enforceability, but also independent management of such an initiative and better follow-up, for example through unannounced checks.

in writing. agricultural challenges are significant given the high global population growth. by 2050, the world's population will reach 9.6 billion, 2.4 billion more than today. in view of this ever-growing demand, food production will have to increase proportionately, by between 60% and 110%. the demand for safe and healthy food products for the citizens of the european union is growing. this demand is compounded by the many yield losses caused by climate change, which require adaptation of existing production models. it is therefore important to support the development of sustainable operating models by emphasising the urgent need for technological innovation. technological advances are needed to enable better use and conservation of genetic resources. in addition, it is essential to ensure that the excellence of local breeds is preserved and that farmers are allowed to select and exchange plants autonomously in order to preserve the genetic diversity of european agriculture. the development of emerging technologies within the union should therefore be encouraged in order to ensure the sustainability and competitiveness of european agricultural production on a global scale.

in writing. ‒ the first information technology trade agreement, or ita, entered into force in 1997. it was concluded between only 29 wto members at the time, but now has 82 members. according to the ita, each participant has to eliminate customs duties on all it covered goods, which has led to increased trade in the sector. although the technology has evolved and changed since the entry into force of the ita, the scope of the ita has remained the same. this is why the ita needs to be extended, as it has great potential for creating jobs and promoting growth. i therefore support the proposal for parliament's assent to the convention and share the view that more member states should join the convention.
in writing. ‒ the first information technology agreement (ita) was adopted in 1996 and was mainly aimed at eliminating customs duties on all it products covered (e.g. computers and telephones). in 2015, an agreement on an additional list of 201 products was reached and is subject to the approval of the european parliament. i have approved this point, which will allow for an increase in union exports following the reduction of tariff barriers.
in writing. i support the council decision to conclude, on behalf of the eu, the revised wto agreement on information technology (it). this revised agreement is the first tariff reduction agreement to be concluded at the wto in 18 years! the new agreement, which aims to phase out customs duties on imports of 201 information technology products, now covers products such as next-generation semiconductors, gps navigation systems, medical devices including magnetic resonance imaging equipment and ultrasonic scanning diagnostics, telecommunications satellites and touch screens. such an agreement should facilitate access to markets and offer more attractive prices for consumers. this agreement is essential when we consider that the world trade in these high tech products is worth, according to the wto, more than $1.3 trillion a year. i take this opportunity of the council's decision to recall the essential role of the wto as the global body for the establishment of trade rules and the governance of trade. such a rules-based multilateral trading system is a plus for the strength and stability of the world economy.
in writing. ‒ the european parliament wants the union to become a major player in new information technologies, as was shown this afternoon by the adoption of a report giving its consent to the extension of the ati agreement. this is a text which came into force in 1997 and which abolishes customs duties on a range of information technology products such as computers and telephones. the agreement also covers components and machinery used in the manufacture of these products. under the ati, the participants commit themselves to the progressive elimination of customs duties over a period of up to 7 years. following these negotiations, approximately 65% of the duties will be completely eliminated by july 2016. by 2019, almost all imports of the products concerned will benefit from duty-free access. the union's exports of products covered by this enlargement amount to eur 189 billion, an amount which is expected to increase as a result of the reductions in the allowances. the agreement therefore has enormous potential in terms of job creation. the annual trade in these 201 products is estimated at over usd 1 140 billion per year, or about 10% of total world trade.
in writing. ‒ i have decided to support the draft council decision to conclude, on behalf of the eu, the revised wto agreement on information technology (it). this is an important text as it is the first tariff reduction agreement to be concluded at the wto since 1995. the revised agreement extends the list of products covered to 201 new products. in addition to the inclusion of these new products, the agreement also provides for a phased commitment to reduce customs duties on these products. the european union has also succeeded in negotiating a phasing-out of tariff reductions over a longer period for certain products considered sensitive. the agreement, which was reached by ministers from 53 wto member countries on 16 december 2015, is expected to boost eu exports of these products. it should be noted that these exports now amount to eur 189 billion.
in writing. ‒ the agreement on the enlargement of the ati is historic, as it is the first major tariff reduction agreement since the creation of the wto and has enormous potential in terms of job creation and stimulating gdp growth. that is why i am pleased that the european parliament has given its approval to the conclusion of the agreement. i would like to stress, however, the importance of ensuring that more member states join the agreement so that the union can benefit fully from it.
in writing. ‒ α-pvp is a potent psychoactive substance. it has already been detected in 28 member states, as well as in turkey and norway, and is mainly imported from china into the eu drug market, mainly in powder or tablet form. two illegal manufacturing sites for this substance have already been seized in one member state, which shows that it can also be manufactured in the union. in total, 115 deaths and 191 acute poisonings have been reported in eight member states to date, where α-pvp has been detected. there is no comprehensive information or studies on the health risks (chronic and acute toxicity) of α-pvp, but animal observations suggest similar effects to those of other stimulants. the council therefore proposes that member states be obliged to subject α-pvp to the control measures and criminal sanctions provided for in their legislation in accordance with their obligations under the 1971 un convention on psychotropic substances. i have agreed to the council's proposal because i am at high risk of ill health. the substance can be harmful in large quantities. the precautionary approach in the interests of the citizens is for me a more than justified reason for supporting the introduction of control measures at union level.

in writing. due to their intercontinental nature, maritime cargoes can lead to accidents with global repercussions involving harmful and potentially dangerous substances. it is in the interest of the european union to have a uniform system of liability for environmental damage caused by the transport of harmful and potentially dangerous substances by sea. with this report we have the opportunity to achieve a uniform system of liability in the most efficient and fair way possible, without altering the uniformity, integrity and effectiveness of the common rules of union law, and without creating excessive disparities for the victims of pollution (e.g. coastal populations, fishermen, etc.) and the maritime industry. the opening of a dialogue with the council and the commission with a view to building a coherent european policy on liability and compensation for environmental damage resulting from the transport of harmful and potentially dangerous substances at sea is a step in the right direction.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the text for several reasons. tunisia has managed to consolidate its democratic transition. it now has a constitution that protects rights and freedoms, with a consolidated judiciary and an emancipated media. it is led by a broad-based government, which has been elected through free and fair elections. but tunisia is going through very difficult times right now. it has been the target of repeated terrorist attacks and bombings that have deeply affected key economic sectors of the country, such as tourism. growth, which was expected to be 3% in 2015, was revised down to 0.5% for 2016, the unemployment rate is 15% on average, 20% for women and 28.6% for young graduates of higher education. in addition, the regional security and political context is extremely volatile, due in particular to the border it shares with libya. despite all these challenges, tunisia continues to make very significant progress, anchoring the democratic transition in the country.
in writing. ‒ according to an oecd study, the aggressive tax optimisation by multinational companies reduces the budget revenues of governments worldwide by between usd 100 and 240 billion annually, about 4-10% of global revenues from taxpaying companies. to tackle this, a fair and effective corporate tax in the eu is needed. the parliament's proposal provides for the principle that companies pay their taxes where they make their profits. but above all it is also seeking a uniform approach, which i also support. a common corporate tax base would also be conceivable, allowing companies to cooperate with a single point of contact for the preparation of the tax return and the consolidation of the profit and loss account for all locations in the union.
in writing. ‒ the european parliament has approved my report on new rules to combat tax evasion. the vote advanced five points: tax payments must take place where firms make their profits, through the precise and mandatory definition of the conditions which certify thata multinational is well established in a country; the cap on interest deductions at 20% and up to €2 million, an ambitious and more balanced position than the european commission's proposal, which prevents multinationals from artificially inflating their debt; the 'switch-over' clause, which allows the regulation of controlled foreign companies; the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the following areas: an ambitious taxation of profits at the exit to reduce double non-taxation; limiting the use of patent filing, through clarification of the definition of investment in research and development. these advances are welcome, as they are part of the dynamic of restoring equality before tax.
in writing. ‒ the fight against tax evasion and aggressive tax planning is a political priority for the ecr. we therefore support the objectives of this council directive, i.e. the implementation of the measures from the oecd’s anti-beps framework directly affecting the single market. such measures should focus on artificial fiscal constructions that lack any commercial justification. the ecr abstained on this report. it goes beyond the oecd framework without any impact assessment. it calls for (double) taxation of foreign income that has been taxed under a rate of 15%, via the switch-over-clause and the cfc-rule. the ecr believes the goal should be to tax profits where economic activity takes place, not to introduce minimum effective taxation (met). secondly, the report calls to limit corporate deductions for interest payments to 20% or eur 2 million, and limits the period during which deductions can be made to five years. this risks hurting companies that apply for a loan for legitimate commercial use in order to make investments. lastly, the report calls for the commission to publish an ambitious ccctb proposal and for the council to conclude negotiations as soon as possible, and asks for the creation of a harmonised, common european taxpayer identification number.
in writing. ‒ i welcome the adoption by a very large majority of the report on the crackdown on corporate tax evasion. panama papers, luxleaks, all of them only reflect part of the iceberg. it is therefore imperative that measures to combat evasion be strengthened. the european union, the world's leading economic and commercial power, has a key role to play. following the oecd recommendations, the eu must lead the way towards a global reform of tax practices that are harmful to the economy as a whole. for this we must have a common approach. as such, i am pleased that this report supports the commission's proposal, while taking the liberty of proposing common definitions such as 'permanent establishment', 'tax havens', 'minimum economic substance', 'transfer price', 'royalties costs', 'patent-friendly measures', 'letterbox companies'. the aim of this text is to call on the council to show ambition when adopting its position on this key legislation.
in writing. ‒ while the european commission is moving in the right direction with its proposal for a directive to combat tax avoidance by multinational companies, i believe that the european union can and must be ambitious. that is why i have decided to support this report on rules to combat tax evasion which proposes improvements to the commission's original proposal. the european parliament's powers in tax matters are limited, so we are only consulted on these matters. it was therefore essential to arrive at a report that was both ambitious and supported by a large majority of meps in order to send a strong signal to the council. i am therefore pleased that this report was adopted by a large majority (486/88/103) at this plenary session. the european parliament's proposed advances include a 20% cap and up to €2 million in interest deductions on loans paid by businesses. now let us hope that the council will show the same responsibility as the european parliament and adopt an ambitious directive to combat tax avoidance.
in writing. ‒ on wednesday 8 june, the european parliament voted in plenary on the new measures proposed by mep hugues bayet to combat tax evasion by multinationals. the vote, which was broadly supported by the political groups, once again demonstrates that the european parliament is a major player in a thoroughgoing reform of the taxation of multinational companies in europe. hugues bayet, who was an excellent rapporteur, stresses that thanks to these new measures it will finally be possible to tax multinational profits where they are generated and thus avoid that they are transferred to a tax haven. this is a major challenge, as eu member states lose between €100 and €240 billion in tax revenue each year as a result of aggressive tax optimisation by multinationals.
in writing. – i voted in favour of a motion for a council directive that is based on the bayet report. based on results by the oecd, we know that multinationals are able to avoid taxes, which annually amounts to a cost between usd 100 billion and usd 240 billion worldwide. the report introduces measures which will ensure a fairer taxation of multinationals so that these do not increase our citizen’s tax burden or disadvantage other companies including sme’s. however measures must not go beyond the oecd guidelines, as this would reduce europe’s competitive position compared to 3rd countries. i also welcome the call for a stronger role for the european parliament in ensuring that other institutions follow up on their obligations.
in writing. ‒ it is the task of every state governed by the rule of law to guarantee the principle of the presumption of innocence and protection against torture. these are the principles on which the european union and all forms of liberal democracy are based. the commission has therefore adopted a proposal for a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to asbestos at work. that is why i support the majority resolution.

in writing. i welcome the adoption by the european parliament of this resolution on the use of torture by the cia. following up its resolution of last year on the us senate report, parliament reiterated its strong opposition to the use of torture and called on the us to investigate and prosecute those responsible. parliament also reiterated its call for the us to cooperate fully with the eu member states. the use of torture is an intolerable violation of the most fundamental human rights and, at a time when the fight against terrorism is giving the union and the united states greater incentives than ever to intensify cooperation, this must be based on respect for international law, human rights and fundamental freedoms.
in writing. ‒ the european parliament voted by a narrow majority (30 votes to one) on a resolution on the use of torture by the cia and the involvement of our member states in such acts. the discovery of secret cia prisons caused a great deal of stir in european public opinion when they were revealed in late 2005 by the american daily newspaper the washington post. the climate of impunity which had surrounded the cia has now ended and the european parliament continues to express its dissatisfaction with the torture methods used by the cia. the obama administration has done its best to condemn the mistakes of its officials and has made clear its full compliance with the geneva convention. but who are we to claim to have the truth? this resolution is a matter of the coué method rather than the ability to assume an inevitably security policy when the rule of law is in danger in the face of the internal threat. the resolution also sins by naivety. this is evidenced by the request made in paragraph 26 to grant asylum in the eu to all former guantánamo prisoners. that is why i abstained, as did 48 other members of the european parliament, on the final vote.
in writing. ‒ i signed the majority resolution expressing the european parliament's concern at the apathy of the member states and the european institutions towards the numerous human rights violations and the use of torture that took place during the cia's 'restitution' operations on european soil between 2001 and 2006. the text adopted urges them to investigate these violations and to bring to justice those responsible or complicit. the document also calls for further fact-finding missions to be organised by parliament in member states identified as accomplices to the cia detention and interrogation programme, such as lithuania, poland, italy and the united kingdom. the resolution also regrets that more than a year after the publication of the us senate study on the restitution programme, no responsible person has yet been held to account.

in writing. over the past 20 years, an increasing number of hormone-related disorders have been identified in humans. there is an increasing number of conditions associated with reduced fertility, dysfunction of the genital organs or premature puberty. these abnormalities and diseases are associated with chemical substances found in a wide range of products for daily use or which have been released into the environment as a by-product of human activity. these substances are believed to have endocrine disrupting properties and thus to have a potential effect on endocrine balance, metabolism and normal functioning of the human body. the environment, public health and the economic sectors concerned all benefit from the avoidance of the use of such substances. the resolution also calls on the commission to take the necessary steps to ensure that the european union's environmental policy is properly implemented. these data should have been available by the end of 2013. at the end of 2015, the european court of justice ruled that the commission had breached the law by failing to publish the criteria. it is now up to the commission to publish the scientific criteria as soon as possible.

in writing. ‒ documents are often only recognised by the authorities or courts of another state if their authenticity or evidentiary value has been established in a specific procedure. the authenticity of a foreign public document is confirmed by two administrative procedures, the hague apostille and the legalisation. the aim of this proposal is to exempt the authentication of a foreign public document from legalisation and apostille in order to facilitate acceptance and promote the free movement of citizens. the proposal also aims to simplify certification and translation processes and to introduce multilingualism in standard documents. this would affect 12 million citizens who work, study or live in another member state. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's financial resources are used to the full.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report, which approves a draft regulation aimed at promoting the free movement of citizens by simplifying the formal acceptance of certain public documents in the union. the regulation provides for exemption from legalisation and apostille for civil status documents. facilitated acceptance measures are also provided for certified copies.
in writing. more than 12 million european citizens live for various reasons in a member state other than their home member state. many documents such as marriage, birth and other certificates have a cost to the citizen. this proposal, in accordance with free trade agreements designed to facilitate the free movement of persons by the formal acceptance of public documents, is without prejudice to the substance of these documents, which remain the responsibility of the sovereignty of the member states. this regulation is a further step towards greater european integration. by reducing administrative barriers, it will facilitate the free movement of citizens between european countries, strengthen the feeling of belonging to europe and give a little more substance to the notion of european citizenship. this simplification is achieved by exempting public documents from legalisation and apostille, which are the formalities required for crossborder public documents. one regret is that diplomas, training certificates, certificates of disability and other documents useful for businesses could not be included in the text. however, the revision clauses in the text will eventually make it possible to extend this simplification further to the benefit of citizens and businesses.
in writing. ‒ today, more than 14 million european citizens live in a member state other than their home member state. even if these citizens live in europe, it must be recognised that they still have to deal with complex and time-consuming administrative procedures. this is particularly the case for getting married, declaring the birth of a child or presenting a clean criminal record. that is why i welcome the vote in the european parliament today. the adoption of new european rules to facilitate the free movement of citizens will make it easier for our citizens to have authentic civil status documents recognised. it should be noted that a revision clause has been introduced as some documents such as university degrees have not been included in the scope of the legislative proposal.
in writing. ‒ the n-va supports the free movement of citizens within the eu, and confirms that to this end the free movement of public documents must be guaranteed. it therefore supports the objective of the regulation to simplify the administrative requirements for the service of public documents in another member state. unfortunately, the regulation takes an unfortunate approach. the practical application, particularly the use of multilingual forms, will not be easy and there is a real risk of abuse. it is also conceivable that this could create a breach in the language arrangements of the member states. the n-va therefore has some reservations about this legislative instrument and abstained from voting in the plenary.
in writing. - i voted for the delvaux report. the aim of this legislation is to promote the free movement of citizens by simplifying the formal acceptance of certain public documents in the european union. it does not concern the recognition of the content of public documents, in particular to preserve the sovereignty of the member states in matters of family law. the mobility of union citizens is a reality: some 12 million of them study, work or live in a member state of which they are not nationals. at present, while citizens and businesses in the union are exercising their right to free movement or the freedoms of the internal market, they may encounter administrative complications when they need to submit public documents to the authorities of another member state, for example as a result of cross-border mobility.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report, which approves the transfer to the court of justice of the european union of jurisdiction to rule at first instance on disputes between the union and its servants
in writing. this report contains some so-called technical amendments following the latest reform of the court of justice concerning the increase in the number of judges. more specifically, this increase was conditional on the abolition of the civil service tribunal, which has seven judges. as regards the reform of the court as a whole, i have already made my views known on this point. i do not think that this reform was timely. doubling the number of judges while the judicial backlog is decreasing is not only unnecessary but constitutes a major flaw of all european institutions in times of crisis. as for the end of the civil service tribunal, i regret that decision. in addition to the fact that the litigation of the public service is very specialized, one can legitimately question the fact of having appointed 2 additional judges on march 22 who will be paid full time when we know that all the cases that have not been litigated at the last session of the tfp of march 18, 2016 will be postponed to september 1, 2016!
in writing. ‒ i voted today in favour of the legislative resolution on the draft regulation on the transfer to the general court of the european union of jurisdiction to rule at first instance on disputes between the union and its servants. in other words, the general court would be given jurisdiction to rule at first instance on disputes between any institution, body, office or agency, on the one hand, and their servants, on the other, for which jurisdiction is conferred on the court of justice of the european union. this transfer of jurisdiction will be accompanied by an increase of seven judges in the court of first instance as from 1 september 2016.
in writing. ‒ this regulation is the fourth to deal with the reform of the court of justice. the first regulation introduced various changes to the composition and procedures of the court of justice and the general court, and the second regulation created the function of acting judge at the civil service tribunal. the third and most controversial aspect of this reform was the increase in the number of judges on the court. the first increase project was to increase the number of judges from 28 to 40. the co-legislators, at the initiative of the council, finally decided to increase the number of judges in the court to 56, so that each member state could appoint two judges. this increase was conditional on the abolition of the civil service tribunal and the return of civil service litigation to the jurisdiction of the tribunal. this regulation therefore follows up the third regulation on the reform of the court of justice. the second stage of the increase in the number of judges, from 40 to 47, is to be accompanied by the abolition of the civil service tribunal, which has seven judges. i voted in favour of the text.
in writing. ‒ i supported this resolution, which approves a proposal for a regulation laying down the procedural rules governing the administrative tasks of the union institutions, the aim being to guarantee the right to good administration through an open, efficient and independent administration. the regulation thus lays down the detailed rules concerning the initiation of an administrative procedure, its management, the duty to conduct a rigorous and impartial investigation, the right to be heard, access to the file, etc.
in writing. ‒ administrative procedures are necessary for the smooth functioning of our society. nevertheless, it is essential for the commission to ensure overall coherence of the system as well. this request by the european parliament to the commission to present a proposal for a regulation 'in favour of an open, efficient and independent administration of the european union' is not new, since such a request was already made on 15 january 2013. i believe that such a request is not trivial, since it would make it possible to fill in the gaps in the union's legal system and thus contribute to respect for the rule of law. the commission is now in the driver's seat.
in writing. ‒ i voted for this resolution to highlight what better administrative support should be. the union administration should adopt administrative acts within a reasonable time. slow management is bad management. any delay in the adoption of an administrative act should be justified and the party to the administrative procedure should be duly informed and given an estimate of the date foreseen for the adoption of the administrative act.
in writing. ‒ the resolution, which i approved, recalls that the european railway equipment sector, which includes the manufacture of locomotives, rolling stock and tracks, employs 400 000 people and accounts for 46% of the world market. it points out that competitors from third countries, in particular china, pursue an aggressive expansion policy and often enjoy strong political and financial support from their home countries, where, moreover, market access often presents many obstacles for european products. it therefore stresses the need for a level playing field and fair conditions for all in global competition and reciprocal market access in order to prevent the risk of job losses and safeguard european industrial know-how. it also calls for measures to ensure that europe remains at the forefront of technology and innovation in this sector.
in writing. ‒ the european parliament adopted a resolution on the competitiveness of the european railway equipment sector. this is a major sector, which still employs 400 000 people and has a key role to play in achieving the commission's 20% industrialisation target. i have always advocated a strong european industry, one that creates jobs and growth. in this sense, i can only welcome the adoption of this resolution which makes a whole series of recommendations to improve the competitiveness of this sector. i would nevertheless like to express my disappointment at the negative vote on several amendments which i supported, calling on 'the member states to reject privatisation and to maintain and strengthen their public railway systems' and encouraging 'the member states to ensure the involvement of regional authorities, social partners and smes throughout the process of developing the railway sector'.
in writing. ‒ just over a month ago, we approved the technical pillar of the fourth railway package in this chamber by a large majority. i emphasized the importance of this regulation and two directives for the completion of the railway market for our citizens. the enhanced role of the european railway agency (era) and the revisions concerning interoperability and safety of rail transport also offer opportunities to our industry. an open european railway market will increase competition between companies active in the manufacture of rolling stock, electrification systems, signalling and telecommunications. it goes without saying that better performing companies will generate less costs, but i also look forward to the opportunities for innovation that such a large and unified market can bring. the current fragmentation, both in administrative and technical terms, is particularly difficult for many smaller firms and potential new entrants. if we want our railway companies to seize these opportunities, it is our task to ensure that the conditions for the proper functioning of this new european market are guaranteed. the report emphasises the right aspects and that is why the nva delegation voted in favour of the report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the text and the amendments advocating the defence of the public service. the european rail equipment sector, which includes locomotive, rolling stock and track manufacturing, electrification, signalling and telecommunications equipment, maintenance and spare parts services - and which includes many smes as well as large enterprises - employs 400 000 people, invests 2.7% of its annual turnover in research and development and accounts for 46% of the world market. the rail sector as a whole, including operators and infrastructure, generates more than 1 million direct jobs and 1,2 million indirect jobs in the union. i would point out that these figures clearly illustrate the importance of this sector for industrial growth, employment and innovation in europe, and its contribution to the achievement of the 20% reindustrialisation target.
in writing. – i voted in favour of this resolution for very obvious reasons. as the document states, the rail supply industry (rsi) is not only an important part of the eu economy. it also accounts for 46% of the global rsi market. in addition, it is vital in achieving our cop21 commitments. however, in order to maintain its pole position, this market needs some thorough restructuring. currently, administrative and technical fragmentation result in serious efficiency losses. especially to sme’s, this can be problematic. they are an important part of the rsi market and need to remain so in the future. as this resolution points out, we need to defragment the railway market and look for efficiency gains through synergies and increased competitiveness. it calls for a unified eu railway market. in sum, this resolution calls for support to the rsi suppliers, in particular smes, through defragmentation of the market. this will attract private investment and finally increase our rsi’s competitiveness in the global theatre.

in writing. ‒ the eu and monaco have negotiated an agreement on the automatic exchange of information on financial accounts to improve international cooperation on tax matters and tax integrity in international transactions. the agreement represents a significant step in the ongoing efforts to combat tax fraud and tax evasion and is therefore desirable. i agreed to the deal. it is intended to apply as from 1 january 2017.
in writing. ‒ i voted for this european agreement with monaco, which aims to make it harder for european citizens to evade tax by hiding cash in bank accounts. under the agreement, the european union and monaco will automatically exchange information on the bank accounts of their residents as of 2017. the european union and monaco signed an agreement on 22 february 2016 to combat tax fraud and tax evasion. the information to be exchanged concerns income, such as interest and dividends, but also account balances and profits from the sale of financial assets.
in writing. tax evasion and tax havens must be a thing of the past. we must fight against the erosion of the tax base and the transfer of profits. this must be a priority if our social model is to be sustainable. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the banking secrecy in third countries is eliminated. the eu's priority is to tackle the opaque systems of other european countries. after switzerland, it's monaco's turn to play. i therefore commend the european commission for its efforts to enable the signing of this agreement on the automatic exchange of information on reportable accounts. this is a major step forward in the fight against tax evasion.
in writing. ‒ by voting in favour of signing this protocol with the principality of monaco, the european parliament once again supports tax transparency and compliance with tax obligations at international level. following on from those signed with liechtenstein, san marino and andorra, this agreement provides for the automatic exchange of information on financial accounts between monaco and the member states of the union. this information shall be collected from 1 january 2017. the act aims above all to prevent tax evasion by european taxpayers and the concealment of capital in the form of income or assets on which tax has not been paid. in line with the global standard adopted by the oecd in 2014, monaco will have to ensure that the information exchanged covers not only income such as interest and dividends, but also account balances and proceeds from the sale of financial assets. the commission estimates that tax evasion and avoidance costs the eu up to €1 trillion a year.
in writing. ‒ the european parliament approved by 549 votes to 16, with 23 abstentions, the agreement between the european union and monaco on the automatic exchange of information on financial accounts, which was initialled in february. the agreement provides that monaco and the member states of the union shall automatically exchange, as from 2018, information on the financial accounts of their residents, which will be collected as from 1 january 2017. under the new agreement, member states will receive the names, addresses, tax identification numbers and dates of birth of their residents with accounts in monaco, as well as certain other financial information, including the balance of these accounts. the formal signing of the agreement is expected to take place before the summer holidays (note that similar agreements with switzerland, liechtenstein, san marino and andorra have already been approved by the european parliament).
in writing. ‒ the european union and the principality of monaco have negotiated an agreement on the automatic exchange of information on financial accounts, aimed at increasing tax cooperation and compliance at international level. the text of the agreement was initialled by a representative of the european commission and a representative of the government of the principality of monaco on 22 february 2016, and the formal signing is planned before the summer holidays, once the council has given its consent. the agreement marks an important step in the current efforts to combat tax fraud and evasion and reinforces the 2004 agreement which ensured that monaco applies measures equivalent to those provided for in the eu savings tax directive. the new agreement provides that the member states of the european union and monaco will automatically exchange information on the financial accounts of their respective residents, as of 2018, for information collected since 1 january 2017. the aim is to deal with situations where a taxpayer seeks to conceal capital corresponding to income or assets on which tax has not been paid.
in writing. ‒ the european union and monaco have negotiated an agreement on the automatic exchange of financial account information, aimed at improving international tax cooperation and compliance. the agreement is an important step in the ongoing efforts to tackle tax fraud and tax evasion. that is why i voted in favour of this agreement.
in writing. ‒ the european globalisation adjustment fund, or egf, was set up to provide additional support for workers who are suffering from the consequences of major structural changes in world trade patterns. trade has been severely affected by declining public and private infrastructure investment in the eu and the sharp rise in steel prices in europe. in addition, the competitiveness of european construction machinery companies has declined. as a result, 488 workers in this sector were made redundant in the hennegau region of belgium. it also affects 300 young people under 25. in order to assist the persons concerned in their reintegration into the labour market, the use of the egf would be extremely helpful. that is why i fully support belgium's proposal.
in writing. ‒ i have of course supported this eur 1 824 041 european globalisation adjustment fund intervention, which has not only helped the reintegration of workers made redundant at caterpillar and doosan, but will also support 300 neet young people from hainaut in their training and access to employment.
in writing. i voted in favour of the commission's proposal to grant eur 1 824 041 from the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf), out of a total of eur 3 000 000, to help 488 workers made redundant by carwall sa, caterpillar belgium sa and doosan sa in the province of hainaut and to help 300 other unemployed young people under 25 in that province who are not in employment, education or training (neet). hainaut, already facing a difficult labour market situation with an employment rate below the national average, is particularly affected by the decline in public and private investment in infrastructure in the european union and the significant increase in steel prices in europe, which inevitably leads to relocations. the aim was to help these 788 young unemployed and working people to enter or re-enter the labour market by providing them with active career guidance services, job search assistance, vocational training or retraining, help in setting up businesses and contribution to collective projects.
in writing. ‒ good news in a difficult social climate: the european parliament granted belgium eur 1 824 041 to support the reintegration into the labour market of 488 workers made redundant by several construction machinery manufacturers in the province of hainaut in wallonia. eventually, around 300 other young unemployed people are also expected to benefit from the support from the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf). this aid is the european contribution, up to 60%, to assist former employees of the carwall, caterpillar belgium and doosan manufacturers in their job search and, more generally, in their vocational reorientation. as with many economic redundancies, this concerns people working in a sector that is undergoing intense global competition. in this case, the decline in public and private investment in infrastructure and the significant increase in steel prices in europe have caused severe disruptions in trade, undermining the competitiveness of european construction machinery factories. this financial aid is therefore welcome for the families of these workers. the main challenge for the juncker commission is now to establish a european industrial policy capable of optimising european know-how in cutting-edge sectors.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this mobilisation of the european globalisation adjustment fund. it should be recalled that belgium had applied for a financial contribution from the european fund following redundancies in the machinery and equipment manufacturing sector in the province of hainaut. redundancies had occurred at carwall, caterpillar belgium and doosan as a result of the disruptions in the european and world market for construction machinery in recent years (demand for products at these three companies had decreased as a result). it should be noted that in addition to the 488 workers made redundant, 300 young people under 25 from the same region who are not working should be covered by the measures and benefit from personalised services co-financed by the fund, in particular: mobilisation and guidance with a view to starting new studies or specific training, personalised upgrading of skills, etc. however, the fund regulation currently provides that such access may only be granted until 31 december 2017. i would therefore like to take this opportunity to ask for the regulation to be revised as part of the revision of the multiannual financial framework so that these people can continue to benefit from this access after 2017.
in writing. ‒ the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) was established to provide additional support to workers suffering from the consequences of major changes in the structure of international trade. in accordance with the provisions of article 12 of regulation (eu, euratom) no 1311/2013 laying down the multiannual financial framework for the period 2014-2020 and article 15 of regulation (eu) no 1309/2013, the annual allocation of the egf may not exceed eur 150 000 000 (2011 prices). the necessary amounts shall be entered in the general budget of the european union as a provision. as regards the procedure, in accordance with point 13 of the interinstitutional agreement of 2 december 2013 between the european parliament, the council and the commission on budgetary discipline, on cooperation in budgetary matters and on sound financial management, the commission, in order to activate the egf when the application has been favourably assessed, shall submit to the budgetary authority a proposal to mobilise the egf and, at the same time, the corresponding transfer request. in the event of disagreement, a trilogue procedure is initiated.
in writing. ‒ the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) was set up to provide additional support to workers who are suffering from the effects of major structural changes due to globalisation. on 4 may 2016, the commission adopted a proposal for a decision on the mobilisation of the egf to support the reintegration into the labour market of workers made redundant in three enterprises in hainaut. i supported this belgian question.
in writing. ‒ in the context of the new common fisheries policy, i have approved the transposition into union law of the measures of the multiannual recovery plan for bluefin tuna in the eastern atlantic and the mediterranean adopted by the international commission for the conservation of atlantic tunas (iccst) between 2012 and 2014.
in writing. i welcome the european parliament's approval of the regulation on a multiannual plan for the recovery of bluefin tuna stocks in the eastern atlantic and the mediterranean. this step will allow the transposition into european law of the measures taken at the level of the international commission for the conservation of atlantic tunas (icsta) to restore bluefin tuna stocks. a few years ago, stocks had fallen so dramatically that the survival of the species was in jeopardy. it was now urgent to take the necessary measures to reverse the trend. i am pleased that these new measures are in addition to the efforts already made by the actors concerned to achieve a sustainable bluefin tuna fishery and thus ensure the sustainability of our fishing opportunities.
in writing. ‒ with the vote on the mato report this afternoon, parliament is committing itself to the conservation of bluefin tuna and to combating overfishing. today, two of the three species of bluefin tuna recorded worldwide are considered to be threatened by overfishing, i.e. the emergency situation. this report associates the union with the international commission for the conservation of atlantic tunas (icct) and its multiannual bluefin tuna recovery plan for the period 2007-2022. the plan includes a gradual reduction in the total allowable catches (tacs) for bluefin tuna, new fishing criteria and measures to regulate sport and recreational fishing, while strengthening the international inspection programme adopted by iccat. the report itself provides for the transposition into european law of the measures of the recovery plan adopted between 2012 and 2014: transfer and caging operations, measures to estimate tuna quantities and the number of releases to sea.
in writing. ‒ the european parliament has approved the text of the compromise between eu institutions on the multiannual programme for the recovery of bluefin tuna stocks in the eastern atlantic and the mediterranean. in adopting this document, parliament approved the text of the regulation which transposes into eu law various measures taken by iccat (international commission for the conservation of atlantic tunas) in 2012, 2013 and 2014. the objective of the regulation is to achieve a bluefin tuna biomass corresponding to the maximum sustainable yield by 2022, with a probability of at least 60% to achieve this objective. the multiannual programme for the recovery of bluefin tuna stocks started in 2007 and is to continue until 2022.
in writing. i followed the group in this vote on the conservation of bluefin tuna. while the commission proposal, on the whole, correctly transposes the relevant iccat recommendations, in some cases it goes beyond what was decided by iccat, but also beyond what is provided for in union legislation. this is the case, for example, when the individual quota for bluefin tuna is considered exhausted: the iccat recommendations and the eu regulation establishing a control regime provide that the flag member state may request and not 'order', as proposed by the commission , the vessel to proceed immediately to a port designated by it. in this respect, it should be recalled that the objective of transposing the iccat recommendations is to ensure uniform application throughout the union; it is not a question of reopening the debate on what has already been decided, often after long negotiations, where every word and every comma counts.
in writing. ‒ the european parliament calls on the european commission to take account in its bluefin tuna recovery plan of non-industrial fishing activities and the most artisanal and sustainable types of gear, such as traditional tuna traps. they specifically contribute to the recovery of tuna stocks, as they are highly selective and have a low environmental impact in marine ecosystems. the european parliament also called on the commission to be involved in future international negotiations. i agreed to that.
in writing. ‒ as i did for bluefin tuna, i approve this multiannual plan for cod, herring and sprat stocks, which takes into account the elements of the baltic sea ecosystem, environmental conditions and socio-economic impact.
in writing. i welcome the european parliament's approval of the regulation on a multiannual plan for the baltic stocks of cod, herring and sprat and the fisheries exploiting those stocks. the inclusion in the multiannual plans of concepts of responsible resource management such as the ecosystem-based approach, maximum sustainable yield and the precautionary principle perfectly reflects the european approach to fishing activities and i welcome this. only this approach can reverse the trend towards overfishing and thus towards the unsustainable exploitation of our fisheries resources, which seriously jeopardises the sustainability of fishing activities in all the regions of the world concerned.
in writing. ‒ the european parliament supports the practice of sound fishing in the baltic sea and the protection of cod, herring and sprat stocks. these three species are essential to the baltic sea ecosystem because of their strong biological interactions. the commission therefore concludes that the measures in question constitute state aid within the meaning of article 107 (1) of the treaty. unfortunately, they are being overexploited. it is therefore essential to put in place a management plan for herring and sprat stocks, as has already been the case since 2007 for cod. the walesa report voted on this afternoon by parliament is therefore in line with this logic and takes a further step by integrating all the stocks concerned into a single management plan. the latter will ensure the sustainable exploitation of stocks in accordance with the principles of maximum sustainable yield and the ecosystem approach to fisheries management.
in writing. ‒ the european parliament adopted this compromise text negotiated with the council establishing a multiannual plan for the stocks of cod, herring and sprat in the baltic sea. this report was adopted by a large majority. the baltic cod recovery plan is the first multiannual plan to incorporate the provisions of the new common fisheries policy (cfp). the text of the regulation states that the objective of the plan should be to contribute to the achievement of the objectives of the cfp, in particular to achieve and maintain a maximum sustainable yield (msy) for the stocks concerned (cabal, herring, sprat). the mdg should be achieved as soon as possible and by 2020 at the latest. the regulation also applies to by-catches of plaice, flounder, turbot and whiting. in addition, and i welcome this, geographical restrictions on fishing are maintained in the baltic to protect breeding and juvenile fish. finally, the plan implements the ecosystem approach to fisheries management to ensure that the negative impacts of fishing activities on the marine ecosystem are 'minimized'.
in writing. ‒ i agree with the general idea in the commission proposal that a multi-species management plan in the baltic sea is necessary. the multi-species management approach is much more effective than the one based on a single species. the plan should allow for the balanced and sustainable exploitation of these stocks and stable fishing opportunities and thus resources for fishermen. at the same time, it should ensure management based on the latest scientific advice as regards the state of the stocks concerned, the interactions between species and other aspects related to the ecosystem and fisheries.
in writing. ‒ in october 2014, the european commission published a multiannual plan for cod, herring and sprat stocks in the baltic sea. the proposal aims to establish a framework for the management of cod, herring and sprat stocks in the baltic sea, where fishing is concentrated on these three species. in recent years cod, herring and sprat accounted for more than 94% of the catches in the baltic sea. i voted for this.
in writing. ‒ with increasing mobility in an area without internal borders, international couples are no longer a rarity. international couples are defined as those who join together from citizens of two eu member states and then remain in a country of which neither is a national. these international couples often face difficulties both in their daily lives and in the division of their joint assets following a separation or the death of one of their partners. the new regulation aims to make this easier for married couples by determining the court with jurisdiction for them and the law applicable to their property rights. i also voted in favour of the new regulation because it will benefit many people living in border regions.
in writing. ‒ this is a case of enhanced cooperation between member states which are in favour of this in the area of international marriage regimes. the proposal aims to establish a complete body of rules of private international law applicable to the field of matrimonial property regimes. i approved that.
in writing. i supported this regulation on matrimonial property regimes which establishes enhanced cooperation, as it was time to have a clear legal framework for transnational situations within the european union, covering the determination of the competent court, the applicable law, the recognition and enforcement of decisions in this area. in a globalised world, the mobility of people within an area without internal borders is increasing, leading to a significant increase in unions between nationals of different member states and, more often, the acquisition of property located in the territory of several eu countries. this legislation is, as the rapporteur rightly says, in the interests of transnational couples.
in writing. ‒ i welcome the adoption of this report which will put an end to parallel proceedings costing nearly €1.1 billion a year in different member states whose courts have to settle property disputes. they will apply to the 18 countries which have wished to join this enhanced cooperation (namely: belgium, bulgaria, cyprus, the czech republic, germany, greece, spain, france, croatia, italy, luxembourg, malta, the netherlands, austria, portugal, slovenia, finland and sweden). the two regulations adopted, one on matrimonial property regimes and the other on the property of registered couples, will determine which court will have jurisdiction and which law will be applicable in the event of proceedings concerning the property of international couples. they will also simplify the recognition and enforcement of a judgment given by one member state on property in another member state.
in writing. ‒ this proposal for a council regulation on jurisdiction, applicable law and the recognition and enforcement of judgments in matrimonial matters is the second one on the subject. after the negotiations between member states failed - all agreements on family law had to be unanimous - this proposal was sent to parliament in the form of enhanced cooperation. as regards the procedural aspects of enhanced cooperation, the reader is invited to consult the specific recommendation on the subject. the proposal also has a double aspect, which concerns jurisdiction, the applicable law and the recognition and enforcement of decisions on the property consequences of registered partnerships. this proposal for a regulation on matrimonial property regimes is clearly in the interest of the union and its international couples. the proposed regulation will put an end to many cases of confusion and legal difficulty. the current proposal, which is the second of its kind, incorporates many of the amendments previously proposed by parliament.
in writing. – i voted in favour of this council regulation. eu citizens are increasingly moving around the eu, working, living, marrying and buying property across eu members states, other than their own. this makes things complicated if these couples separate, or when one of the two partners deceases, etc. this regulation provides clarification on which court has jurisdiction in such cases. to ensure consistency and enhance simplification, this regulation enables one regime to be applicable to property that is located outside the eu. under certain conditions, it also allows for the law of third countries to apply. citizens should be allowed to choose for themselves as to which regime will apply to their property. this will also facilitate things for citizens of third countries and for eu citizens that live outside the eu. the establishment by the regulation of means to communicate basic information to international couples will only enhance this. all of this makes life easier for people, during times that are usually the hardest to people. it puts an end to legal uncertainty for many of them and that is why i voted in favour.

in writing. ‒ this afternoon, the european parliament voted in favour of a clearer legal framework for the management and sharing of property for the 16 million international couples in the eu who have entered into a marriage or registered partnership. the proposal for enhanced cooperation aims to establish clear rules in the event of divorce or separation of these european couples by putting an end to the initiation of parallel and sometimes competing procedures in several member states. this is often a process similar to a combatant's journey. in concrete terms, the improvements consist in the possibility for a couple to determine the jurisdiction with jurisdiction to help them in the management or sharing of these assets. the agreement will also determine the applicable law where the laws of several countries may potentially apply to the case. it will in particular facilitate the recognition and enforcement in one member state of a judgment in a matrimonial matters matter given in another member state.

in writing. – i voted in favour of this proposal for a council regulation because i believe that our system needs to evolve with modern times. as europe's internal barriers disappeared and our citizens started exploring their continent more and more, an increasing amount of people started meeting their life partners abroad. together with the council regulation on matrimonial property regimes, it aims at the simplification and flexibility of legislation and procedures, for international couples, in the case of decease, divorce, etc. as with its complementary one, this regulation clarifies what the procedure, the scope, the jurisdiction, as well as the applicable law will be in such cases. at the same time, it enables, for example, the enforceability of authentic acts. this will also enhance legal certainty and predictability. finally, i welcome the fact that many of the ep's previous recommendations in this matter have been taken into account.
