in writing. as a former teacher, i am particularly concerned about the education and training of young people. quality education ensures that young people become skilled professionals, acquiring the necessary competences and skills. but education is also a value in itself. it contributes to the development of civic and moral values. responsible teachers are key players in the development of young people into conscious and engaged european citizens. youth unemployment in europe is still far too high. i therefore support the recommendations in this report calling for effective investment in education and training. for example, the establishment of partnerships between education and the labour market in the member states can be a source of sustainable growth. acquiring the necessary skills, promoting student mobility and inclusive education are priorities in the fight against youth unemployment. the call to the member states to include in the learning objectives an increased emphasis on the development of social skills, the promotion of active citizenship and european values deserves all our support. the teaching of social and human skills is an essential and effective pedagogical tool to prevent young people from becoming radicalised.
in writing. ‒ strengthening cooperation at european level in the field of education, training and innovation is one of the priorities of the european parliament, which voted this afternoon in favour of the krasnodębski report complementing the education and training 2020 (et2020) strategic framework. et2020 aims to facilitate learning and mobility for european citizens. it also seeks to improve the quality and efficiency of school education and to promote equity, social cohesion and active citizenship. these measures should help to meet the major challenges of the coming years, such as the ageing of the population, the shortage of skilled labour and the race for innovation in a context of global competition. the objectives of et2020 in terms of education are many. the aim is to increase the proportion of children in pre-primary education to 95% and to significantly reduce the proportion of young people who are not proficient in reading, mathematics and science. in the field of training, the stated objective is to target at least 40% of persons in the 30-34 age group who have completed higher education and, more generally, those aged 18-34 to study or train abroad.
in writing. ‒ with youth unemployment at its highest in europe, it is crucial to evaluate the european et2020 framework in order to increase its added value and optimise its effectiveness. the evaluation carried out by the commission in 2014 led to the adoption by the commission and the council of a series of recommendations to address the complexity of the context and governance of et2020: definition of the mandates of the new generation of working groups, mobilisation of independent experts, closer dialogue, more regular consultation and coordination between the commission, the member states and education stakeholders. the resolution adopted today contains a number of priorities and policy recommendations, including on the governance and coordination of et2020 at all levels (e.g. the commission should open up the new working groups to representatives of the different stakeholders and the results of their work should be more widely disseminated at all levels), but also on quality education (e.g. achieving the benchmarks for education and training should not be at the expense of quality, etc.).
in writing. ‒ the intensification of intra-european mobility and the current refugee crisis have posed major challenges to national education and training systems. today's classrooms are more diverse than ever, with pupils needing extra help to adapt to new curricula, academic requirements, teaching methods and often also to new languages and cultural norms. teachers need additional support, at the beginning of their training and throughout their careers, through continuing professional development courses, so that they can effectively teach immigrant children, to facilitate their integration into the host society while encouraging them to preserve and maintain their cultural heritage. there is an urgent need for measures at national and european level, also in the framework of et2020, in the field of education and training for adult asylum seekers who have recently arrived in europe. education is the key to integration and employability, and if national systems are unable to meet this challenge, it risks exacerbating social divisions and cultural segregation and thus reinforcing the emergence of already latent parallel societies.
in writing. ‒ education and training are important to help people acquire the knowledge and vocational skills they need to become competitive and innovative workers. moreover, they can play an important role in forming open-minded people. it is to be welcomed that the paris declaration of the ministers of education of 17 march 2015 has been reflected in the joint report and that et 2020 has been updated, placing the objectives of employability and the promotion of social cohesion, equality, non-discrimination and civic skills on an equal footing. it could count on my full support.
in writing. – i strongly endorse this ep resolution, because it represents our views on the commission’s evaluation of et2020 very well. it is important to follow up on such frameworks and programmes in order to observe whether the predetermined objectives are being achieved – and, if not, what action is needed. this framework is important as the future of our workforce depends on education and training. these will be the tools that will help the eu in maintaining one of the most competitive and innovative workforces in the world. in this regard, the erasmus programme plays a significant role, which the resolution recognises. i welcome the resolution’s call for quality assurance in education at all levels and its emphasis on the importance of the quality of educators, who need to be supported through continuing professional development programmes. the resolution also stresses the importance of exchange of good practices between member states.
in writing. ‒ the development of renewable energies requires a reorientation, making them the cornerstone of the union's energy model. climate change must be fought, and we have a responsibility to do so. the dependence on energy resources from other countries must be reduced if we are to achieve the goal of taking a leading role in the development of strategic technologies for the energy transition, of structuring a successful and realistic energy production model and thus of creating quality jobs. this takes account of the demand of parliament, which i can only agree with.
in writing. ‒ i have endorsed this report which, while welcoming its efforts in favour of renewable energy, encourages the commission to ensure the implementation of the renewable energy directive and to propose an ambitious legislative framework after 2020. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of renewable energy sources in the transport sector. it also stresses the importance for the renewable energy sector of sharing best practice, support schemes and access to capital, particularly for smes.
in writing. the eu is on track to meet its 2020 objectives. this is the result of an ambitious move by the eu and its member states towards a low-carbon economy based on more efficient energy use and the exploitation of renewable energy sources. in the context of the commitments it made at the paris climate summit, it is a logical next step for it, together with the member states, to raise its ambitions, invest more in energy technology and tighten the renewable energy directive. the cost of renewable energy has fallen sharply in recent years. this creates opportunities to launch an integrated, competitive and sustainable european energy policy. the optimal use of renewable energy sources, further technological innovation and the roll-out of smart energy networks are the main pillars of an ambitious, competitive european energy market. citizens should therefore be encouraged to participate actively in this energy market by generating, using, storing and selling their own energy. in some eu countries, biomass from wood is the most widely used renewable energy for heating. as forests are crucial to our ecosystem, responsible exploitation and sustainable use of our forests is important.
in writing. ‒ there is a strong chance that renewable energy will be the world's leading energy source by 2030. the european union, including belgium, therefore has every interest in investing in the clean energy sector, if only to reduce its energy dependence. this is what the lópez bermejo report, adopted this afternoon, emphasizes in a broad sense, listing in more detail the progress made in the renewable energy sector. some member states have already reached or are very close to reaching their 2020 targets, while others are lagging behind. but that would be to ignore the geographical and topographical features which really differ from one european territory to another. clearly, not all member states are equal in ensuring their energy transition. belgium, for example, has neither the mountain ranges of austria nor the forests of sweden to focus on the development of hydropower or biomass. however, as the european parliament resolution stresses, all member states must show common ambition, decarbonise their industries and aim for 30% renewable energy by 2030.
in writing. ‒ on the eve of the review of the european legislative framework in the autumn, the european parliament reaffirmed on thursday 23 june its high ambitions for renewable energy by 2030. the text of the adopted resolution emphasises the key role of self-production and self-consumption, decentralised production of renewable energy and collective energy management through municipalities, all areas in which the next revision of the renewable energy directive will have to encourage investment. i also voted in favour of an amendment which stresses the enormous job creation potential of the renewable energy sector and calls on the member states to ensure that labour standards are not weakened by the energy transition, which should also be based on the creation of quality jobs.
in writing. ‒ the development of renewable energies requires a new approach that would make them the cornerstone of the european union's energy model. our fundamental responsibility is to fight climate change, a historic task that we must do. we must also reduce our dependence on energy resources from the rest of the world if we are to structure our production model, create quality jobs and spearhead the development of the strategic technologies underpinning our energy transition. the transition to a sustainable long-term energy production model is a social priority that cannot be left to the market alone. on the contrary, we must understand that regulation and democratic participation are essential if we are to avoid serious social and environmental externalities. we must prevent energy oligopolies from dictating europe's energy future.
in writing. ‒ the development of renewable energy requires a new approach that makes renewable energy the central pillar of the european union's energy model. we have a fundamental responsibility to address climate change. this is a historic duty from which we cannot evade. we also need to reduce our dependence on energy sources from the rest of the world if we are to support our production model, create quality jobs and play a leading role in the development of strategic technology for the energy transition. the transition to a sustainable energy production model is a social priority that cannot be addressed by the market alone. we must assume that regulation and democratic participation are necessary to avoid serious social and environmental externalities. we must prevent the future of energy in europe from being determined by energy oligopolies. i voted for this strategy.
in writing. – it is clear that renewable energy is becoming increasingly important to our union in two different ways. first of all, we have to safeguard the environment, following up on international agreements such as cop 21, to which we are a signatory. secondly, we need to safeguard the eu’s energy independence. at eu level, as in flanders, we are currently working hard on achieving this goal. although the eu is moving in the right direction, i hope that this resolution will help to speed up the process and can provide extra support to those who are left with the responsibility to make it happen. i agree with the resolution’s point on the necessity of a stable framework for investment. i strongly believe that renewable energy has the best chance of succeeding if we cooperate at eu level.
in writing. ‒ between 1991 and 2014, greenhouse gas emissions in the eu fell by 23%. in the same period, gdp increased by 46%. this shows that as the climate impact decreases, businesses and citizens generate more growth, creating jobs and tax revenues. the eu is on track to meet its 2020 targets of reducing co2 emissions by 20%, increasing the share of renewable energy in total energy consumption to 20% and achieving 20% more energy efficiency. however, the high bureaucratic burden in the energy sector and the high energy prices for medium-sized business customers and households are a cause for concern. in addition, as there are also several national and european regulations, some of which are in conflict with each other, i join parliament in calling on the commission to work towards a more coherent climate and energy policy and to make additional efforts towards a pan-european electricity market design.
in writing. ‒ this report, which i approved, underlines that while the energy efficiency directive has brought about many positive improvements in the member states, its implementation remains insufficient, particularly in terms of quality job creation. it stressed the importance of initiating the transition to an energy system based on renewable energies, which would make it possible to phase out fossil fuels as quickly as possible. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of biofuels, bioliquids and biomass fuels.
in writing. efficient use of energy is crucial to achieving our climate and energy goals. although the eu is on track to achieve its 2020 targets overall, we note that the energy efficiency directive and the buildings directive have not yet been fully implemented. however, energy efficiency is the most necessary step towards a sustainable energy market which will make us more independent of energy imports, stimulate innovation and help create new jobs. moreover, both citizens and businesses have an interest in lower energy bills. in the context of the eu's commitments at the paris climate summit, it is desirable that the eu raise its energy saving targets by proposing new and innovative solutions that reduce energy consumption on the one hand and aim at a more rational use of renewable energy on the other. for example, the building sector has a lot of room to transform itself into a more energy-efficient sector. it is therefore desirable that the commission, the eib and the member states provide technical assistance and support to housing projects implementing sophisticated insulation techniques, more modern heating systems and the use of private renewable energy sources.
in writing. ‒ on the eve of the review of the legislative framework in the autumn, the european parliament reaffirmed on thursday 23 june its high ambitions for energy efficiency by 2030. the resolution on energy efficiency stresses the need for full implementation of existing eu legislation to achieve the union's 2020 energy efficiency target (20% increase by 2020). parliament also reiterated its ambition for a 40% energy efficiency target by 2030, with binding national targets for member states to redouble their efforts. i'm so happy for you. the text also calls on the eu to invest more in information and support programmes in the member states to encourage the participation of local actors in energy efficiency programmes and to promote new solutions in refrigeration, lighting, insulation, etc.
in writing. - i voted for the text. energy efficiency is crucial to achieving our climate goals as part of the goals endorsed by cop21 in paris. it is of paramount importance to reduce our dependence on imported energy, create jobs, reduce energy poverty, improve comfort and health, and boost our economy. i would point out that the energy efficiency directive has brought about many positive improvements in the member states, but that insufficient implementation is hampering its true potential.
in writing. ‒ in the eu, greenhouse gas emissions fell by 23% between 1990 and 2014. over the same period, eu gdp increased by 46%. with less and less impact on the climate, businesses and citizens are driving more growth, creating new jobs and generating tax revenues. the european union is well on track to meet its 2020 targets of 20% reduction in co2 emissions, 20% increase in the share of renewable energy in total energy consumption and 20% increase in energy efficiency. this is largely due to the successful ets scheme. this scheme not only encourages emission reductions but also investment in energy-efficient technology. i voted in favour of this report and i am also pleased that flanders is making a comeback with its new policies.
in writing. – ensuring the future of energy in the eu requires a combination of approaches. while renewable energy plays an important role in this future, we also have to work on energy efficiency. that is why i voted in favour of this resolution. it sends a positive message, stressing the progress that has been made and recognises the role of ets and the implementation of the energy efficiency directive herein. it also recognises some problems, such as the complexity of the relevant legislation. i therefore strongly welcome its call on the commission to work towards a coherent electricity market design for the eu. while the eu plays an important role as legislator, in the end it is the market itself that will be the key to the solution. as long as we ensure that energy efficiency is in the industry’s interest, the market will become more energy efficient by itself. i agree with the resolution that the correct incentive is very important in this regard.

for the greens/efa group ladies and gentlemen, there are times when political time is suspended and we have the opportunity to make a choice. in the aftermath of world war ii, the nations of europe faced a choice. they had the choice of either pursuing or breaking with the principle of indivisible national sovereignty. by deciding to share sovereignty, they ushered in a period of peace and prosperity unprecedented in european history. today, the outcome of the british referendum may bring a historic breakthrough to the project of political integration of our continent. but should that be surprising? from denmark to ireland, france, the netherlands and greece, there have been warning signs of the growing distrust of our fellow citizens towards the process of european integration. it is therefore high time that we responded to it. once again we have a choice, and the survival of the european union depends on that choice. we have three options. the first is the one that was voiced last week in the united kingdom, the one of a nationalist and - let us say - xenophobic retreat, preached by mrs le pen, mr farage, mr wilders, mr orbán, and so many others. i would like to ask the commissioner whether he has not already made a statement on the situation in the former yugoslavia, and whether he has not made a statement on the situation in the former yugoslavia. no, bringing back growth does not automatically bring back employment and reduce inequality. and, no, making the rich richer is not good for society. these political choices are the main cause of the rise in euroscepticism, as they lead to the abandonment of an increasing number of our fellow citizens. we want to be part of a third option, which is at the same time resolutely pro-european - there is no doubt about that - but which breaks with this single thought. we want the european union to return to the roots of its project, which was to secure peace on this continent through the extension of democratic freedoms on the one hand and through sustainable and shared prosperity on the other. i ask you, i ask ourselves: is it impossible to ensure the viability of the euro through a real social and fiscal union? is it not possible to make the energy transition the flagship project of our economic recovery? is it possible to ban the poisons that are killing our environment and our organisms slowly? is it possible to abandon free trade agreements which benefit only the happy few? is it not possible for europe to become once again a land of welcome for those fleeing war, persecution and poverty? is it impossible to keep our societies within the limits of our planet? is it possible to revive our democracies through more transparency and citizen participation? in short, is it not possible to put human dignity, the dignity of all human beings, here and there, now and in the future, back at the heart of politics? our answer is that yes, all of this is possible, if you want it to be. and if the european union can be the instrument of this political will, it will regain the confidence of our citizens. but make no mistake, we are running out of time. if we ignore the signal sent by the british referendum, if we misinterpret it, then the european project will be finished. ladies and gentlemen, europe has experienced enough of the worst to not only hope for the best, but to build on it. on behalf of the alde group the reform of this energy label must serve several purposes for me. first, it should encourage the manufacturer to innovate and bring more energy-efficient appliances to the market. secondly, we want better and more efficient market control. this can be achieved by improving cooperation and information exchange between the member states' control agencies. finally, it should also encourage consumers to buy more energy-efficient appliances. this will reduce consumption and lower the energy bill. i also think it is essential that we pursue these objectives in a way that is as simple as possible for the consumer, the producer and the seller. we must take account of our small, local dealers and our smes. we must not impose unnecessary costs or burdens on them. i think that with the outcome of the itre vote we have found a very good compromise between the positions of the various groups and between the interests of the various stakeholders involved. i think we've taken an ambitious approach. one that makes it clear to everyone what can and can't be done. we are still in the aftermath of the volkswagen scandal and that is why it is more important than ever that we ensure that consumers regain confidence in the labels they see. and i want to be very clear about that. a refrigerator that consumes too much electricity is as bad for me as a car that consumes too much diesel. in both cases, you are being misled as a consumer, it is bad for the environment and you will also feel it in your wallet, at the petrol station or on your energy bill. i look forward to negotiations with the member states and will defend this ambitious approach with them as well.

on behalf of the alde group. – mr president, i always find it a little difficult that mr kamall gives lessons to us. mr kamall, you are leaving the union and you are explaining here what to do in the future: it is incredible. would it not be better if you knew what to do in britain? in my opinion, the brexiteers have no clue about what needs to be done for the moment. it would be better to give lessons in london and not here in strasbourg. in fact, the brexiteers remind me of rats fleeing a sinking ship. cameron resigned, johnson abandoned ship and farage apparently wants more time for himself and his family to spend his european salary. so the leave man remains – or has disappeared for the moment. i think that the last man standing in britain will probably be a woman. that will happen and, like in the time of margaret thatcher, only a woman will be capable of managing a divided tory party, as we see it today. yes, women will rescue britain. my second surprise last week, mr tusk, was the reaction of the european council to this political earthquake – because what happened in britain is an earthquake. the only reaction i have heard from the council was that we should not change anything and that it is just a question of implementing the existing european policies. i find this shocking and i also find it irresponsible. i do not think that you understand what is happening. it is not only a brexit referendum. before that there was a referendum in denmark: negative. there was a referendum on the ukraine agreement in the netherlands: negative. now we have had this referendum in the uk. what are you waiting for? for the next referendum in france? the next referendum in italy maybe? when will the council recognise that you can no longer defend the european union of today and that europe needs to be reformed? in my opinion, a new project and a new vision should be presented to the citizens of europe because the truth is that european citizens are not against europe, they are against this europe. the proof of that is the eurobarometer. i wonder why the commission and parliament did not published this eurobarometer much earlier because it dates from a few weeks ago, in april. do you know what the results are? eighty-two per cent of people want more european action on the fight against terrorism; 77% of european citizens want more european action in the fight against unemployment; 75% of european citizens ask for more european action in the fight against tax fraud; and 74% are asking for more european action on the issue of migration. on 14 of the 15 questions put to european citizens in this eurobarometer a few weeks ago, people are asking for more european action, not less. the problem is that europe has become ... what? europe – our europe – has become an expert on legislation on the exact measurements and colour of our cigarette packets. we have become an expert in deciding the amount of water flushing in toilets and also in the level of subsidies that a local football club can receive from local government. but what the citizens want – and that is what the european eurobarometer tells us – is a european border and coast guard, a european asylum and migration policy to tackle the migration crisis, european intelligence capacity to tackle terrorism, a european government to defend the euro and a european army to defend our borders and to end conflicts in our neighbourhood. that is what the citizens are asking for here. the inconvenient truth is that more of the same will not get us out of this crisis, dear colleagues. that is burying our heads in the sand. people want you to work on another europe, a europe that delivers results. by not doing that, you are sleepwalking towards disaster, towards 27 other referendums in the near future. so let us not be naive. the real problem today – and mr pittella is right when he mentions schäuble – is intergovernmentalism. a loose configuration of nation states based on unanimity cannot work. that is the reality today that you have not recognised until now. i will conclude by saying that we are going to do our homework. parliament will be ready in october with a global plan based on three reports on the way forward. we are not going to talk –you can be sure – about federalism, integration, deepening, widening, coordination, implementation and all these other buzzwords that are at the centre of our discussions. we are simply going to go back to the ideas of our founding fathers. that is what we have to do. that is the challenge. now or never. either the union will change, mr tusk, or it will die. that is what is at stake. in writing. ‒ for a country to be included in the list of third countries whose nationals are exempt from the visa requirement in the eu, it must meet specific criteria, which are then reviewed by the council. the commission has therefore concluded that the measures provided for in this decision are in accordance with the opinion of the committee established by article 15 (1) of regulation (eu) no 182/2011. it has since been applied provisionally pending parliament's approval. the exemption is valid for a period of 180 days, for a maximum of 90 days and for all categories of persons. peru is one of the few countries in latin america which still requires a visa for entry into the schengen area. this is due to the country's history of internal conflict and, in particular, high levels of violence, drug production and trafficking. although peru is still facing some problems, other neighbouring countries, where this problem is not excluded, are already exempt from the visa requirement. since the economic and general situation in peru has improved considerably in recent years and since it would be inconsistent to exclude peru as one of the few latin american countries from the visa exemption, i have agreed to this.
in writing. ‒ i have approved this agreement on the short-stay visa waiver for a maximum of 90 days in any 180-day period for peru, a democratically stable state. this will in particular help to strengthen economic and cultural exchanges, but also to foster political dialogue on human rights and fundamental freedoms.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the draft council decision on the conclusion, on behalf of the european union, of the agreement between the european union and the republic of peru on the short-stay visa waiver. the text gives a positive opinion on this agreement which will allow peruvians to travel to the eu and european citizens to travel to peru without the need to apply for a visa for any stay of up to 90 days in any 180-day period. the exemption applies to all citizens holding a valid ordinary, diplomatic, service, official or special passport, travelling for any legitimate purpose other than for gainful employment. for peruvian citizens, each member state individually may decide to impose or lift the visa requirement for peruvian citizens and peru may choose to do the same for citizens of each member state. peru was until now one of the few countries in latin america still subject to the visa requirement. i hope that this visa waiver will deepen economic and cultural relations and intensify political dialogue, including on human rights and fundamental freedoms.
in writing. i am pleased that peru is now one of the third countries whose nationals are exempt from the visa requirement for travel within the schengen area. following the positive assessment of the situation in peru, the agreement between the union and the republic was signed on 14 march 2016. the agreement represents a further step towards increased cooperation between the two sides in areas such as trade, investment and tourism. i am also pleased that, as a result of this enhanced cooperation, the union and peru can become partners in the fight against organised crime, in particular trafficking in human beings. more generally, i welcome the strengthening of the coherence of our policy towards the south american continent, since, thanks to this agreement, peru has joined the minority of countries on the continent whose nationals are not exempt from visas.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report giving the european parliament's consent to the conclusion of the eu-peru agreement on the short-stay visa waiver signed on 14 march 2016. this agreement provides for a visa-free regime for citizens of the union and peruvian nationals in the territory of the other contracting party. the maximum duration of the stay is 90 days over the entire 180-day period. i voted in favour of this visa waiver in particular because peru is a relatively stable democracy which, like the european union, upholds the values and principles of democracy, good governance, respect for human rights and the rule of law.
in writing. - i voted for the deal. the agreement signed provides for a visa-free travel regime for citizens of the union and peruvian nationals travelling to the territory of the other contracting party for a stay of up to 90 days in any 180-day period. the visa exemption applies to all categories of persons (holders of ordinary, diplomatic, service/official or special passports) travelling for any purpose other than gainful employment.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because the aim of this agreement is to boost tourism and to contribute to closer relations in the field of trade and investment. peru is one of the countries in latin america that has experienced the strongest growth (5% in 2013, 2.4% in 2014). the country has grown by more than 80% over the last ten years, placing it among the ten countries in the world which have experienced the strongest growth during that period. in trade, the eu is peru's third largest trading partner in terms of imports (mainly machinery and transport equipment) and its first export destination (agricultural and food products and minerals). in addition, the eu remains the largest investor in peru, accounting for over 50% of total foreign direct investment in sectors such as mining, banking and finance.
in writing. ‒ non-road mobile machinery covers a wide variety of combustion engines installed in machinery ranging from small portable equipment to motor trains, locomotives and inland waterway vessels, construction machinery and generators. these engines are a major source of air pollution and account for about 15% of nitrogen oxide emissions and 5% of particulate matter emissions in the european union. i voted in favour of this proposal, which aims to protect human health and the environment and to ensure the proper functioning of the internal market as regards engines installed in non-road mobile machinery. it also intends to address compliance and competitiveness aspects. in line with the union's air quality policy, the aim is to gradually reduce emissions from new engines placed on the market and thus to replace older, more polluting engines over time. this initiative should result in a very significant overall reduction in emissions, although the reduction per engine category will vary according to the level of specific requirements currently in force.
in writing. ‒ the n-va delegation supported the agreement reached between parliament and the council on emission limit values for 'non-road mobile machinery'. emissions from engines of such machinery (such as inland waterway vessels, locomotives and construction machinery) account for 15% of nox emissions and 5% of particulate matter emissions. if action is not taken now, emissions are likely to increase in the coming years. the agreement puts forward stricter emission standards and thereby contributes to improving air quality and protecting human health and the environment. the agreement also provides for legal certainty and a reduction in administrative burdens by bringing european standards into line with international standards (such as those of the usa and japan). the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. this would enhance the green edge of the sector and stimulate innovation. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's energy policy is not undermined by the fact that the community is not able to meet its own needs. in this context, it is important to resolve the existing discrepancy between the engines recognised by the central commission for the navigation of the rhine (ccr) and the new eu standards.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report to update the type-approval rules and emission limits for engines for non-road machinery (including lawnmowers, bulldozers, diesel locomotives and certain boats). the emissions from these non-road vehicles are far from insignificant. they account for 15% of total nitrogen dioxide (nox) emissions and 5% of fine particulate matter emissions in the eu. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament and the council adopt a common position on the proposal for a directive on the approximation of the laws of the member states relating to the labelling, presentation and advertising of foodstuffs for sale to the ultimate consumer. i am pleased to note that a new control system is planned, which should bridge the gap between the values observed in laboratory tests and those observed in reality. i am also pleased with the revising clause which should allow for the revision of emission thresholds and stimulate innovation to continuously improve emissions.
in writing. the air quality in our european cities and agglomerations is not yet up to the standards we want. too high a concentration of fine particulate matter and too high an emission of nox are damaging the air quality. the vw debacle of last year has shown that there is only one remedy to put the house back in order: only clear rules, respect for the law and proper controls can restore consumer confidence and guarantee better air quality. after setting new standards for combustion plants and industrial emissions earlier this year, parliament has now also adopted a new framework for emissions from non-road mobile machinery such as generators or yard vehicles. 15% of all nox emissions in europe come from these engines. a significant reduction in emissions will yield environmental and health dividends. a transitional period was introduced for manufacturers and users to allow them to adjust to the new rules. in this case, the commission has already learned one important lesson from the vw debacle: the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council and parliament on the subject of the future of the european union.
in writing. ‒ lawnmowers, bulldozers, tractors, diesel locomotives, inland waterway vessels and other non-road motor vehicles are vehicles which have a significant impact on air pollution. it was therefore important that the european union adopt legislation to severely limit the pollutant emissions from these machines for environmental reasons as well as for public health reasons. i can therefore only welcome the adoption by a very large majority of the interinstitutional agreement on this new regulation. once the council has approved the agreement, industry will have to adapt rapidly to the new regulation. this is excellent news for the health of our european citizens and for the environment.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on emission limitation and type-approval requirements for internal combustion engines for non-road mobile machinery
in writing. ‒ i voted for this report out of concern for clean air for future generations. the purpose of this regulation is to harmonise the rules for eu type-approval of engines of non-road-type machinery. the european union is based on the continuous review of air quality policy. to this end, new emission limit values should be established, which should also apply to, inter alia, agricultural machinery. this regulation also aims to simplify the current regulatory framework and administrative procedures and to improve the general conditions for enforcement.
in writing. – i voted in favour of this proposal for a regulation because i deem it necessary. we have been working for a long time on the creation of frameworks that aim to reduce emissions. the most well-known ones are those that apply to cars. however, they are not the only polluters. for non-road mobile machinery (nrmm) we also need to strive towards emission reductions. before this regulation, nrmm was regulated by a number of directives. i welcome the commission proposal because this regulation aims to improve our environment and the health of our citizens, while at the same time enhancing the functioning of our internal market with regard to nrmm by ensuring a level playing field and remedying unfair competition.
in writing. ‒ vocational integration also promotes social inclusion. this is precisely why it is necessary to give refugees and asylum seekers the opportunity to participate actively in the labour market. it is important not to create a special labour market specifically for refugees. the promotion of languages is also important, because language is one of the biggest obstacles to the ability of these people to work. education is another important issue. most children and young people from crisis areas have had limited or no access to school for a long time. it is important to support them at the beginning of their arrival and to give them the opportunity to be educated. the report addresses important issues of social inclusion and integration into the labour market, which is why i have agreed to it.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report, which calls for measures to ensure that refugees and asylum seekers have access to housing, healthcare, education, social protection and the labour market in order to restore their dignity and promote their integration. meps stress that the labour market conditions in host countries are one of the key factors in the successful and sustainable integration of refugees. in this respect, the report stresses the importance of full and rapid integration into the labour market in accordance with the principle of equal treatment and of rapid, easy and equal access to training. to this end, it called on the european commission to consider a targeted revision of the reception conditions directive in order to ensure that persons applying for international protection have access to the labour market as soon as possible and at the latest 6 months after the submission of their application.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the employment committee's report on refugees concerning their social inclusion and integration into the labour market. the text stresses the need to provide refugees and asylum seekers with effective access to housing, healthcare, education, social protection and the labour market. access to the labour market will enable them to become economically independent and contribute to the society that welcomes them. this will not only reduce the burden on public budgets but also help to restore their dignity and self-esteem. it is therefore crucial to assess their skills in a timely and fair manner, and to recognise and validate their qualifications, so that they can get to work as quickly as possible. the resolution also insists that assistance to refugees and asylum seekers should not be financed from resources earmarked for programmes targeting other disadvantaged groups and that additional investment should be made. it also opposes the idea of creating labour markets specifically for refugees and supports the application of the respective national minimum wages to them.
in writing. the social and professional inclusion of refugees is a fundamental right that every citizen must enjoy, but also a necessity if the european union is to improve the competitiveness of its market in the long term. to ensure that the dignity of these refugees is respected, it is essential to move from dependence on aid to independence. the integration of refugees into the labour market is a duty of humanity. it is also a considerable asset for the union in terms of diversification of skills, knowledge and qualifications. in order to ensure that the process of social and occupational inclusion takes place under the best possible conditions, it is important to promote initiatives such as language learning that will allow refugees to integrate quickly into our society. equal opportunities integration should therefore be promoted to provide refugees with easy access to healthcare, social protection, the labour market and education. finally, a revision of the european blue card will provide them with better protection against all forms of discrimination in employment. i congratulate the rapporteur, mr benifiei, for making this report a plea for the fair and equal integration of refugees.
in writing. ‒ if women and men leave their country and family, it is not for pleasure. it's because they're running away from the dramatic situations they're in. we must show solidarity and ensure their protection. it is our duty to make this integration a success, especially in the labour market. it is a matter of respect for international rights, a matter of humanity but also a matter of common sense. this debate is too important to be polluted by demagogic talk of rejecting others. we need to put in place the necessary arrangements to make this integration a success and an added value for society as a whole. in this respect, i welcome the approach taken in this report to not create a second labour market for refugees. these people must be able to enjoy the same social conditions as our european citizens. it is also important to ensure that they learn the language of the host country from the very beginning, to set up a system of recognition of skills and, more broadly, to allocate the necessary resources to ensure their full integration.
in writing. ‒ the report on the social inclusion and labour market integration of refugees voted today considers the current situation to be a humanitarian crisis. the report calls for a common asylum system with a permanent resettlement mechanism and for the improvement of safe and legal migration routes. we also call on the commission to promote upward convergence of social protection standards and to work for the efficient granting of work permits in the member states. a slow and drawn-out bureaucratic procedure makes refugees and asylum seekers particularly vulnerable to undeclared work and precarious working conditions. the report also calls for the existing legislation, such as the qualification directive and the directive laying down standards for the reception of applicants for international protection, to be taken into account. this legislation provides that asylum seekers and persons entitled to international protection have the right to access the labour market and language education. in addition, the importance of civil society organisations and volunteers strengthening the resilience and integration of asylum seekers and refugees is also emphasised. it has become a very constructive report, with an eye to the people themselves, which in turn benefits our whole society. that is why i am involved in politics and why i voted for this text.
in writing. - i voted for the report. the aim of the report is to clarify the exact subject under consideration by explicitly recalling what it means to be a refugee and the main elements of the current debate. to highlight the relevant issues, challenges and opportunities associated with the social inclusion and labour market integration of refugees; analysing the development and impact of recently adopted measures, actions and practices at union and member state level in order to achieve successful integration and inclusion in our society; finally, to present a series of proposals, recommendations and suggestions to improve the social inclusion and integration of refugees in the labour market. the structure outlined in the text attempts to reflect this approach. more generally, the report attempts to outline the complexity and multidimensional nature of the subject on the one hand and the urgency and need to find a solution on the other, bearing in mind that the principles of solidarity and fair sharing of responsibilities are absolutely essential to solve this common european problem which requires a common european response.

in writing. – i voted in favour of this resolution. the recent refugee crisis has shown us that something needs to change. the eu needs stronger and more coherent guidelines on how to deal with such a crisis.. it is an eu-wide holistic approach on how to improve migrant integration processes. it recognises that one of the best tools for integration is education. this will enable us to include migrants in the labour market. as a result they will have the opportunity to become an active member of society and contribute to it. in addition, this will enable the most vulnerable groups of migrants, namely children, to pursue a vital part in their development. finally, i welcome the fact that the resolution recognises the big challenges in this area, such as budget cuts, the aftermath of the financial crisis, and the worrying rise of xenophobic movements.
in writing. ‒ sustainability and corporate social responsibility are important issues. i have advocated that further wto reforms be actively promoted to establish multinational rules for the sustainable and responsible management of large supply chains. the aim is to promote health and safety standards and social protection. in general, the eu and the member states should also promote the theme of corporate social responsibility in trade agreements.
in writing. ‒ social, environmental and human rights standards in trade agreements have become major concerns for citizens. with this report, the socialist group has raised concerns about the level of ambition that the european union must respect in international agreements. we want to see legally binding and enforceable standards that hold companies and governments to account, taking into account the important views of civil society.
in writing. ‒ as the n-va delegation, we abstain on the resolution on the implementation of the 2010 recommendations of the parliament on social and environmental standards, human rights and corporate social responsibility. indeed, greater respect for human rights contributes to a democratic, peaceful and secure international environment. trade, as the exclusive competence of the eu, plays an important role in this. trade agreements can have a positive impact on human rights. n-va therefore believes that free trade can serve as a long-term instrument for the promotion of human rights. however, trade agreements should not be confused with human rights agreements. they are there primarily to stimulate trade and investment. trade agreements should be negotiated in such a way as to provide incentives for partners to make lasting commitments to improve human rights. we cannot therefore support the demand to impose binding, conditional human rights clauses on all future or ongoing trade negotiations. if trade partners are found to be involved in conflict or to be committing widespread human rights violations, it is necessary to proceed with care, to evaluate each case individually and to intervene where necessary.
in writing. the european union is the world's leading power and enjoys extraordinary soft power. international trade is one of its pillars. in this context, parliament encouraged the commission to integrate into its trade strategy the desire to strengthen respect for human rights and to defend social and environmental standards. the european union and the member states are not the only actors. as the report stresses, the responsibility of enterprises in implementing these priorities should not be underestimated. the report calls on the commission to include corporate social responsibility in eu trade agreements.

in writing. - i voted for this report. like other colleagues, we have insisted that compliance with the eight core labour standards and the four priority ilo conventions for industrialized countries, as well as with the relevant union legislation, should be included in a social clause in all bilateral or multilateral trade agreements of the european union and that these standards should be applied. it is necessary to provide incentives to encourage undertakings to make commitments in the field of corporate social responsibility (csr) and voluntary measures to identify and prevent any violation of human rights and environmental rights, as well as any form of corruption or tax evasion, including in their subsidiaries and supply chains.

in writing. ‒ network and information security (nis) is becoming increasingly important in our economy and society, as it creates an important prerequisite for creating a reliable environment for the global flow of services. however, such systems can be destroyed by human error, natural events, technical errors, or malicious attacks. the existing nis capacities and mechanisms are not sufficient to ensure eu-wide protection against problems and risks. the proposal is to create a minimum level of national capacity and to establish nis authorities in the member states and an it emergency team. national nis authorities should cooperate as closely as possible to ensure safe coordination. i have therefore agreed to the report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this directive, which lays down measures to ensure a high common level of security of network and information systems in the union in order to improve the functioning of the internal market.
in writing. ‒ i supported this directive to establish a common level of network and information security and to strengthen cooperation between member states. the aim is to better manage cyberattacks against companies that provide essential services (such as energy, air transport, drinking water supply, banking and health services, digital services such as search engines and cloud computing services). the establishment of these first eu-wide cybersecurity rules should also help to better prevent attacks against the interconnected infrastructures of european countries, as cybersecurity incidents very often have a cross-border dimension and therefore affect more than one member state of the european union. finally, it is also one of the first legislative frameworks to apply to platforms and an important first step towards establishing a comprehensive regulatory framework for platforms within the union.
in writing. networks and information systems are the nerve centres of our societies. they play a vital role in the cross-border movement of goods, services and people. this transnational dimension requires a genuine european strategy that is responsive to the challenges of cybersecurity in a globalised world. by voting in favour of this directive, we are asking member states to establish a national cybersecurity authority, develop a national strategy and have an operational structure to assist in dealing with cyber incidents. companies will therefore have to report significant it incidents to this national authority. this is the only way for ms to help them better protect their systems and secrets. i think we should fight for europe to achieve digital sovereignty. this means a voluntary industrial policy, at national and european level, which supports our companies and smes to enable them to develop products and/or services essential for computer security, for the information and telecommunications sector.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the directive on measures to ensure a high common level of security of network and information systems in the union. while each member state is required to develop its own cybersecurity strategy, there is a need for strategic cooperation at european level. therefore, that directive provides for the establishment of a cooperation group composed of representatives of the member states, the commission and the european union agency for network and information security and the establishment of a network of national csirts in order to contribute to the building of trust between member states and to promote swift and effective operational cooperation. it is hoped that member states will soon transpose this directive to improve cybersecurity in europe.
in writing. ‒ we have just voted on the first european cybercrime rules. fake banking websites, identity theft, viruses, malware, industrial or personal espionage - these crimes claim a million victims a day and cost over 350 billion euros a year! first, companies in sensitive sectors (banking, energy, health, etc.) are obliged to report security incidents as soon as they are discovered, failing which they risk heavy fines and sanctions. secondly, these sectors have an obligation to provide efficient services, able to withstand the most hostile cyberattacks. these very strict obligations will also have to be applied to search engines such as google, cloud computing and online marketplaces such as amazon or ebay. this is a real breakthrough for the e-security of european citizens and businesses, with more than one billion data breaches in 2014 alone.
in writing. ‒ companies that provide essential services such as energy, transport, banking or healthcare or companies that provide online services such as search engines or cloud computing services need to take action to be able to repel cyberattacks. after two years, the european council, the commission and the parliament have finally reached agreement on what needs to be done to raise the level of network and information security. each member state should designate an authority to coordinate this at national level. national governments will set up computer crisis teams, as well as a national action plan to protect the cyber incident. the private and public sectors also need to cooperate and share information across borders. i voted for this report in the hope that the preparation of this european decision in belgium will not take as long as the decision itself took at eu level. in belgium, the government has already appointed a national authority to function under the prime minister. the rest of the decision needs to be implemented quickly as more and more of the lives of our citizens, children and businesses are being played out online and the protection there is not yet optimal.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this harmonisation on energy labelling, which is good for the environment because consumers can, wherever they are in the union, obtain accurate, relevant and comparable information on the energy efficiency and energy consumption of energy-related products, enabling them to make informed, cost-effective and environmentally friendly purchasing decisions, for the benefit of both the environment and their wallet.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this proposal from the european commission to introduce a new scale identifying more strictly the energy efficiency of household appliances. on the basis of the information available to us, this new nomenclature seems necessary in order to make labelling clearer, stronger and safer and to keep pace with technological progress. it will also set stricter requirements and provide further impetus for improvements in energy efficiency. the text provides that test methods and environments should be as close as possible to the real-life use of the product by the average consumer and calls on the european commission to publish transitional european measurement and calculation methods with regard to the specific requirements of the products. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'commercial vehicle' to cover vehicles with a maximum mass exceeding 10 tonnes.
in writing. energy efficiency labelling provides consumers with information on the efficiency and lifetime of energy-related products. labelling also reduces energy consumption and thus reduces the cost of energy bills for citizens. in order to continue to promote innovation in energy-saving products, i believe it is important to maintain the colour scale indicating to consumers the energy efficiency of products from a to g. this allows for greater transparency and understanding of the energy use of products on the market. this energy labelling must therefore be considered as the only valid labelling in the european union in order to ensure optimal monitoring of energy products available on the market. in order to ensure consistent implementation of energy labelling, suppliers will have to ensure that each product has a data sheet complying with european standards showing the energy efficiency of the product on the defined scale from a to g. this means that each member state will have to submit to these measures and submit an annual report, which i believe will lead to a better compliance of energy products on the european market.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of a single but also clearer labelling on the energy efficiency of household appliances. one study shows that 85% of european consumers take the energy index into account when choosing a product. however, the current system is considered unclear, since the majority of products are classified a (a+, a++, a+++). in order to make the energy labelling system easier to read and to enable consumers to make an informed choice when purchasing electrical appliances, the text provides for a scale from a to g, thus replacing the + increasingly present in the current upper class. electrical equipment suppliers will then have to refer to this new scale in all their advertising. a good step forward in the defence of european consumers.
in writing. ‒ today, when buying a refrigerator or a washing machine, you can choose from a wide variety of designations such as aaa, a+ and so on. it shows the success of the energy label: the commission has also proposed that the european parliament should be consulted on the proposal for a directive on the protection of the environment in the event of a fire. it is therefore high time that a new scale was developed so that it is clear which appliances are the most economical. the european parliament, however, is threatening to limit supervision and to completely remove the ambition of some devices. products are consuming less and less energy, which is why plus signs are being added to labels. that makes the system unclear and makes outdated techniques still seem like a good buy. the christian democrats and the liberals are ignoring outdated techniques at the expense of consumers and the climate. for example, they say that boiler labels will not be scaled up until 2030. the gas boiler manufacturers are getting their lobbying rewarded: as long as their product is in the green zone, it sells better. many of these boilers are hardly energy efficient. by giving them an a-label until 2030, you're misinforming the consumer.
in writing. ‒ there was no harmonisation of energy efficiency labelling for european household electrical appliances. this dusty find will soon be filed away in the broom closet. the european parliament will vote today on a single labelling scale from a to g to provide clearer information to consumers and reduce their energy consumption. in addition, all new products placed on the eu market will have to be registered in an online database, which will provide greater transparency and facilitate market surveillance by national authorities - both very good news for the european consumer, which will ultimately represent a saving of €15 per year per household.
in writing. ‒ the n-va delegation voted today in favour of the report on energy labelling. the energy label was in dire need of renewal because of the ambiguity it created for the consumer. by adding pluses, the incentive for consumers to make the most energy-conscious choice was gone. by establishing the scale from a to g and by providing for a system of rescheduling in case of overcrowding of the upper classes, the system is maintained at efficiency gains. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the rules are applied. the labels have proved useful in the past. the system leaves the choice to the consumer to make an informed choice on the basis of full information. with this update to the existing system, we're providing renewed clarity.
in writing. ‒ my colleague, mr wierinck, has followed this case very closely. i voted for this report because i believe it is important that consumers can make informed choices. this will make a significant contribution to energy savings and lower energy bills, while promoting innovation and investment in the manufacture of more energy-efficient products.
in writing. – i strongly support this proposal for a regulation. i am shadow on this file and i am pleased with the result. in order for the labels to fit their purpose, there was a practical necessity to rescale them. in addition, it gives the citizen a more central place in the eu energy transition, through the public interface of a database. the consumer needs to be able to quickly determine what he/ she is buying and how energy efficient their product is, relative to other ones. another important goal is to stimulate producers in creating increasingly innovative products and applications. given the recent problems with regard to emissions in the automobile industry, it is important that consumer trust is restored. therefore, compliance with new legislation needs to be thoroughly followed up on. throughout the entire process i have tried to safeguard the balance between the protection of the consumer, the protection of the producer and that of the distributors, keeping in mind the practical viability of this new regulation.
in writing. ‒ following the terrorist attacks of this and last year, ten schengen member states have reintroduced internal border controls. although this is usually only temporary, it nevertheless shows that better controls at external borders are needed to increase internal security. that is why i have voted in favour of the proposal with the greatest conviction. the powers of frontex must be considerably extended. the european union is also proposing to set up a european border and coast guard to replace frontex. this guard shall be composed of the national authorities responsible for border management, including the coast guard. the concept of european integrated management of external borders is to be legally enshrined for the first time. in addition, the agency's role in the field of return, capacity building and international cooperation with third countries is to be strengthened.
in writing. ‒ compared to the european commission's original text, the s&d group made significant progress in negotiations such as the inclusion of 'search and rescue' and humanitarian operations in the missions of the european border and coast guard agency, the reference to fundamental rights in various parts of the text and the fact that the agency will be accountable to the council and the european parliament. however, as this text was not accompanied by measures on, for example, the opening of legal migration routes, i abstained.
in writing. ‒ an agreement on a european border and coast guard has been reached in record time, so that it can start after the summer. if a crisis occurs at a european external border and a member state fails to act sufficiently, the joint border guard will be able to take over the external border surveillance. the budget of the eu border agency will be more than doubled (from eur 143 million to eur 322 million) and, together with the troops provided by the eu member states, a reserve of 1 500 border guards will be created, ready to be deployed within a week to support the countries on the external borders. effective surveillance of external borders is crucial for a good response to the migration crisis, a coherent european security policy and the avoidance of new borders in europe. concrete european responses such as these are the best defense against populists and europe-bashers.
in writing. ‒ the current migration crisis has clearly demonstrated that the schengen area without internal borders is only viable if the external borders are effectively secured and protected. i therefore welcome the creation of a european border and coast guard corps based on the frontex agency, which will be given specific powers, including direct intervention at the external borders of a failing member state by decision of the council. this is to prevent shortcomings in the management of external borders or unforeseen migratory flows from undermining the smooth functioning of the schengen area. to fulfil its new tasks, the agency's technical and operational capacity has been strengthened. it will be responsible for managing a common pool of technical equipment and will now have a rapid reaction pool of at least 1 500 border guards to be deployed from each member state within 3 working days. the creation of this new agency, with its own human and technical resources and a right to intervene at the external borders of a member state, represents a decisive step towards an integrated european system for the management of the union's external borders.
in writing. i welcome the adoption of this major new legislation establishing a european border and coast guard. this is a new step towards a genuine european management of our common borders. this review of frontex once again shows that the union is responding to the expectations of european citizens, which were also expressed in the last european barometer. the management and control of our external borders is a matter of common interest and should be a shared responsibility at union level. this new agency is a major step forward in providing real resources, both budgetary and human. the new agency will have a reserve of 1 500 staff, to be mobilised as soon as possible, and will have the capacity to acquire and use its own equipment quickly. freedom of movement in the schengen area is one of the greatest achievements of the european construction, but it is only viable if our external borders are effectively controlled. finally, i welcome the clear competences of the agency in search and rescue, as well as the reinforced rules on its liability.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the proposal for a regulation establishing a european border and coast guard corps. i would have liked this text to be more in the direction of more europe with a frontex agency with more powers. i must admit, however, that this text is moving in the right direction. with this new regulation, frontex will have more resources through a permanent reserve of 1 500 border guards who will be made available in case of need. the border guards will thus be able to provide support in the event of a sudden influx of migrants, but will also be able to combat cross-border crime and terrorist threats. it is hoped that this strengthening of the frontex agency will make it possible to provide more serene and humane care for asylum seekers in the event of a large influx. it is the duty of the european union to welcome these people with dignity, but also to support those eu countries which are most affected by these flows. this is a matter of solidarity.
in writing. - i voted yes. the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on the european border and coast guard corps aims to establish a european border and coast guard corps to ensure integrated management of the external borders of the european union. this proposal is timely and responds to the challenges facing the european union in the context of the current migration and refugee crisis. it is estimated that between january and november 2015 alone, about 1.5 million people crossed the border illegally.

in writing. – i voted in favour of this regulation because changes need to be made to the current regime. the recent migration crisis has shown that we need a holistic, coherent approach at an eu level when it comes to managing such crises. with the emergence of terrorism this has become all the more important. in order to maintain free movement within the eu, we need a common agency to protect our outside borders. the european border and coast guard will fulfil this task. it will simply be a more efficient and effective equivalent to frontex and its national counterparts through enhanced cooperation. in addition, it includes anticipatory measures such as the preventive identification of weak spots in the border control systems. i understand that, in order to achieve these goals, they will need increased resources, such as equipment, etc. finally, i welcome the fact that it stresses the importance of a high degree of accountability and transparency. this will provide the legitimacy that is needed for this agency.

in writing. brexit, the migration crisis and the persistence of high unemployment are all signals calling for a major revision of the mff budget by the eu. the uk's exit has serious consequences for the eu budget, which will be cut by some 20 billion. however, this loss will be partly offset by the uk's withdrawal from the structural funds and its financial participation in the single market, as is the case for norway and switzerland. brexit will also have repercussions on acp countries, particularly africa. around 100 trade agreements will probably have to be renegotiated as they were concluded via the eu, which will require years of readjustment. the main countries affected will inevitably be south africa, nigeria, botswana, angola, kenya, ghana and senegal: 80% of uk exports to sub-saharan africa are made in these countries. the creation of eu trust funds for africa, estimated at €405 million, is a necessity. i regret, however, the proliferation of instruments outside the eu budget. a thorough review of the mff should be carried out in 2019 on revenue and expenditure.
