in writing. ‒ last week, a report on tax rulings and other measures of a similar nature or effect was voted in parliament. the report proposes concrete measures and addresses important issues, which is why i support it entirely. the internal market and a social market economy require a fair tax system in which international companies also pay taxes where value and profits are created. tax dumping is detrimental to the general public and cannot be justified in any way vis-à-vis the small and mediumsized enterprises, which are the backbone of our european economy. the key requirements include a common approach to eu external taxation policy with exit or withholding taxation, a consolidated common corporate tax, an eu list of tax havens and a register of beneciaries. moreover, sanctions should be allowed against tax havens and against those actively involved in tax evasion. in addition, in addition to the need to curb the misuse of patent boxes, a comprehensive reform of the group's code of conduct and effective protection for whistleblowers are also essential. as for whistleblowers, it's not that courage and civic courage can be punished in individual cases, but both will have saved billions in tax revenue in the end, while politicians don't have to face personal consequences.
in writing. ‒ this report concludes the mission of the second special committee on the fight against tax evasion. i voted in favour of this text, which calls on the commission to act in many ways, including the creation of an efficient, up-to-date and easily usable database of all tax returns with effects in several countries. the report also made some recommendations to introduce the possibility of making financial institutions, banks and tax advisers jointly liable in the event of tax evasion. another key element is to strengthen european legislation to prohibit the use of fictitious patent boxes. the socialist group hopes that further progress can be made in this area, because it is important to finance innovation, but it must be real. finally, a chapter was devoted to whistleblowers, calling for a specific framework to ensure effective protection of whistleblowers through a directive. as we saw last week, european legislation in this area is essential to protect those who discover illegal or unlawful behaviour and report it in the public interest.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because it proposes measures to establish a fairer and more transparent corporate tax system in the european union, including a public register of the beneficial owners of companies, a european blacklist of tax havens, sanctions against non-cooperative tax jurisdictions, action against the abuse of patent box schemes, a code of conduct for banks and tax advisers, a withholding tax on profits leaving the european union and a common consolidated corporate tax base. in the light of the revelations of the luxleaks and panama papers cases, it seems to me essential that the european union develops a common approach to the control of the union's external tax policies, with a consolidated tax base for corporate taxes and a european register of beneficial owners of companies. i am also pleased to note that the report does not forget the plight of whistleblowers. the resolution calls on the european commission to present a legislative proposal to protect whistleblowers. future legislation should include a single european framework based on the approximation and strengthening of national legislation.
in writing. ‒ the n-va has decided not to support this report. there are good elements in the report, such as the call for the rapid implementation of the oecd recommendations to combat base erosion and profit shifting (beps) and proposals to improve the effectiveness of the council working party on codes of conduct for corporate taxation. the n-va supports this call for more correct fiscal rules. however, parliament is wrong, for example, in its call for a minimum effective tax and the abolition of unanimity in the council working party. the distinction between (illegal) tax evasion and (legal) tax avoidance is also too narrow. the n-va is also not in favour of the creation of a land register, as called for in this report.
in writing. i welcome the adoption of this second report by the taxe special committee following the luxleaks. we must strengthen our fight against tax dumping and force multinationals to take their fair share of the tax contribution. the aim of this report was to draw up a series of recommendations aimed at ensuring fairer and clearer taxation for businesses. the proposals include the establishment of a european register of beneficial owners of companies or sanctions against multinationals involved in tax evasion. a major measure of the report is also the establishment of a blacklist of tax havens. today we have 28 different lists. this puts the european union and the member states in a weak position. we must therefore agree on a common list to guarantee a single policy towards these third countries. the pressure will be much greater if the 28 come together rather than each one doing his shopping in a tax haven. the fight against tax fraud and evasion is not over.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the recommendations to make corporate taxation fairer and clearer. at a time when citizens are constantly having to make efforts and checks are being intensified on the less privileged, recent revelations have brought to light an unacceptable, shocking reality that can no longer be ignored. our recommendations include the establishment of a european register of beneficial ownership of companies, a blacklist of tax havens, to eliminate disparities between states, and sanctions against tax jurisdictions that refuse to cooperate. in the same spirit, we are advocating the creation of a code of conduct for banks and tax advisers. the fight against tax evasion must be conducted at european level, but this cannot be done without the support and the will of the states. this is a step forward, but further efforts will be needed in the future to combat tax evasion and money laundering. without equating criminal fraud with legally permitted tax evasion through tax engineering, global work is essential to prevent these few trillion euros from escaping the european union each year.
in writing. ‒ i share parliament's regret that 13 member states do not have actual rules on tax-exempt dividend movements to combat aggressive tax planning and that 13 member states have not carried out tests on beneficial owners when accepting applications for reduction or exemption from withholding tax. i also regret that to date 14 member states still do not have rules on controlled foreign companies to prevent aggressive tax planning and 25 member states do not have rules to deal with the different tax classification of a local company by another state; i also regret that to date no member state has called for a ban on aggressive tax planning structures.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on tax rulings. business taxation needs to be fairer and more transparent. i see no problem with approving a feasibility study on a global register of financial goods. it is good to have a list of pros and cons, including risks, and this can't hurt. however, this should not lead to misuse of this data by the authorities (for example, if this would lead to an automatic wealth tax). the commission will continue to monitor the implementation of the eu's new rules on the protection of personal data, in particular the rules on the protection of personal data and the rules on the protection of personal data.
in writing. – i voted in favour of this resolution. the recent panama papers scandal has proven that new legislation is needed to counter tax avoidance. while some bigger corporations are able avoid taxes through base erosion and profit shifting, it is especially the smes that suffer from others’ tax evasion. again, this is an area where only cooperation will provide a solution. the resolution calls for adherence to the oecd agreements and stresses the fact that some countries are still not cooperating even though they are members. an automatic exchange of information between nations is an important step towards fairer taxation. when such nations do not cooperate, the relevant tools should be in place for the eu to take measures against such tax havens. when looking at new tools and measures, i feel that we should consider a wide variety of options in order to ensure effectiveness and efficiency in this area. however, when invoking them, it is important that privacy is safeguarded at all times. moreover, such measures need to be both attainable and realistic.
in writing. ‒ i supported this joint resolution which recalls the necessary synergy between the european structural and investment funds, horizon 2020 and other eu innovation funds and programmes (european connectivity facility, digital single market, energy union, etc.). this should be done within a strategic planning framework that should contribute both to strengthening the single market and to delivering the 2020 strategy.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because i believe it is essential that the european commission, but also the member states, pay particular attention to the combination of the structural and investment funds on the one hand, and the horizon 2020 framework programme on the other. and i would go even further and say that it is important that our institutions ensure adequate synergy between all the funds. of course, it is also important to ensure that these synergies do not interfere with the very nature of each fund. i believe that the european social fund must be mobilised on purely social issues, otherwise it will no longer be able to achieve its intended objective. it is by ensuring appropriate synergies between the funds that we will achieve better results for each of them.
in writing. - i voted for this text. i reiterate that the links between cohesion policy and other union policies and initiatives (horizon 2020, the connecting europe facility, rural development, the digital single market and the energy union) have been strengthened within the csf introduced by the common provisions regulation which, through all its instruments and objectives, including the urban agenda, the territorial agenda, investment in smes, or the smart growth and smart specialisation strategies, therefore contributes to the achievement of the europe 2020 strategy objectives.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this joint resolution. we do need synergies for innovation: the european structural and investment funds, horizon 2020 and other european innovation funds and eu programmes.
in writing. – i voted in favour of this resolution because an efficient use of the eu's resources is important to me, as is the horizon 2020 programme that is involved. i strongly believe that synergies should be made where possible. however, when looking for these one should always keep in mind the objectives of each individual programme, safeguarding their integrity. while both programmes have different goals, they have a complementary character. for example, i applaud the mentioning of the horizon 2020's seal of excellence and the potential of its use outside the programme. the lack of funding for horizon 2020 is also rightly pointed out. i can only welcome the focus on smes throughout the entire resolution, mentioning their important role and stressing that any unnecessary administrative burden should be avoided. the cosme program plays an important role herein. to conclude, when complementary aspects between both programmes that mutually strengthen each of them exist, i am in favour of this.

in writing. antoine deltour, the luxleaks whistleblower, appeared in court in luxembourg in may alongside raphaël halet for revealing the grand duchy's tax practices. the verdict will be delivered in june, as the prosecution is seeking 18 months in prison for the two men. the minister for finance, michel sapin, gave his support to the vosgian. in the end, it's the whistleblowers who get the prison time, not the fraudsters. worse, these convictions discourage them from making these disclosures, which are in the public interest. a definition of whistleblower must be drawn up, together with a general protection regime. the reporting person shall be able to report in good faith, freely and in the public interest, from within an organisation or from outside, serious breaches of the law or serious risks to public or private interests which he or she is not responsible for. he will have the benefit of anonymity and will be able to give the alert within the institution concerned or to the ombudsman, whose independence is enshrined in the constitution. all the financial scandals of recent years, and more recently the panama papers, must accelerate the establishment of this european definition.
to date, the convention on the rights of persons with disabilities is the only international human rights treaty ratified by the european union as a whole. it is also important to note that all eu member states have signed the convention and 27 member states have ratified it. so there is a very strong political support for this treaty. the convention is considered the first human rights treaty of this century, the 21st century. the convention is legally binding and the european union must now take action to implement it fully. all legislation, both future and past, must be fully in line with the un convention and guarantee the full and equal participation of persons with disabilities in society, including at european level. the un convention does not provide new or additional rights for persons with disabilities, but it makes very explicit that persons with disabilities can also claim fundamental rights already enshrined in other conventions, such as the universal declaration of human rights, the convention on the rights of the child and other international conventions. i am really proud to have been able to involve a record number of committees in my report, ranging from the committees on transport and tourism, legal affairs and development to the committee on petitions. this proves that disability is not just a social issue but a theme that permeates all aspects of life. remember, this un convention is a human rights convention. so we are talking about the human rights of disabled people. in the spirit of the convention and the slogan of the disability movement, 'nothing about us without us', i wrote my report together with organisations of and for disabled people. i have had constructive discussions with the european disabled persons forum and its members from the outset. i therefore sincerely thank the organisations and individuals who have supported me. representatives of those organizations are sitting in the audience upstairs. i would like to applaud them very much for their tireless pursuit of their rights as persons with disabilities in our society [applause], a society that does not always take them into account and does not always understand the obstacles that persons with disabilities face every day. i would like to reiterate and emphasize that people with disabilities should not be treated as second-class citizens in europe. they should enjoy the same rights to live and work in the eu as citizens without restrictions. the european institutions must set the example. disabled employees should be supported so that they have equal access to work and occupation. citizens with disabilities should also have equal access to public information and events in the european parliament and other institutions. we cannot ask the member states to apply the convention if we do not apply it ourselves. i look forward to working with my colleagues here and in other institutions to ensure that the rights of people with disabilities are respected and taken seriously throughout europe.
rapporteur. – madam president, i would like to thank all colleagues and committees again for their valuable input in their areas of expertise, which allowed for a very concise and comprehensive report. i would also like to highlight the support from my colleagues at the disability intergroup and i am very glad that we have commissioner thyssen with us today making disability a priority at commissioner level, and i hope it stays that way. the involvement of people with disabilities was crucial during the whole process, and we should not forget that the convention puts new obligations on the eu. i can only reiterate that freedom of movement, especially for workers, is also a right for people with disabilities and this also includes full and equal access to the erasmus + programme. with regard to the exercise of political rights, this is just one example of where people with disabilities continue to be left out. changes must be made so that people with disabilities can fully exercise their right to vote and to stand as candidates during elections. again, i would like to mention the disability intergroup, who signed many amendments and were actively involved in the whole process of the report. this cross-party support from all eu countries is a significant indicator of how important the protection of the rights of persons with disabilities is everywhere, and not only in one or two areas or regions. madam president, i will do my utmost to make sure this remains not just a piece of paper, but can have a real impact on person with disabilities here at the european institutions and across europe. remember this is about human rights, not more not less. the report has shown once more that the rights of persons with disabilities are to be taken seriously and are not merely a minority issue.

in writing. ‒ the un convention on the rights of persons with disabilities entered into force in 2010 and is the first international human rights treaty to be ratified by the eu as a whole. the convention covers a wide range of rights, covering all areas of life, some of which are outside the eu's remit. member states are therefore obliged to implement the un convention accordingly at all levels, including regional and national levels. the report is addressed to the eu institutions, which are expected to take a leading role in the implementation of the convention. the convention is a major step forward in the fight against discrimination, which is why i have agreed to the report.
in writing. ‒ this report, which i have approved, is an opportunity to recall that all people with disabilities have the right to live in a society where they have the same opportunities as other citizens to ensure their full integration and participation. the eu and the member states must take measures to ensure the implementation of the rights of persons with disabilities, the promotion of their autonomy, accessibility, employment and social integration. this is particularly necessary if austerity policies are to be brought to an end, the first victims of which are the most vulnerable. it is time to revive social investment. it is also time that respect for the rights of disabled people is addressed in the work of the european semester. improving the consideration of their rights also requires a permanent and structured dialogue with organisations representing disabled people. finally, i would like to stress the importance of informing not only about the rights but also about the talents of disabled people, who are a real asset to our society.
in writing. an estimated 80 million people in the union have some degree of disability, more than half of whom are women. by acceding to the united nations convention on the rights of persons with disabilities, the eu has committed itself to reporting on a regular basis on the progress it is making towards the full integration of disabled people into our society. the report of the parliament lists the forms of discrimination which people with disabilities still face. recommendations are also made to facilitate the better integration of disabled people. people with disabilities should have the same rights as all other citizens. it is therefore evident that more efforts are being made to ensure tailored and inclusive education, to ensure the free movement of people with disabilities in europe consistently, to strengthen the implementation of eu legislation on direct access to information and communication for people with disabilities and to ensure that ehealth and mobile health services are easy to use throughout europe.
in writing. ‒ the aim of this report was to assess the implementation of the un convention on the rights of persons with disabilities. the integration of disabled people is an important issue and the union must do everything possible to ensure its success. to do this, i would urge the european union to implement fully the recommendations of the committee on the rights of persons with disabilities and to allocate sufficient resources to this end. the report also contains a series of recommendations addressed to the european commission and the member states. in line with these recommendations, i voted in favour of this report and i ask the commission and the member states to ensure the necessary follow-up. this is a matter of respect for people with disabilities.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report. the eu was the first organisation to accede to the un convention on the rights of persons with disabilities in december 2010. this is the first (and so far only) international human rights treaty that the eu as a whole has ratified. all 28 eu member states have signed the convention; twenty-five of them have ratified it, finland and ireland have not. at the time of writing, the netherlands is about to accede to the convention. the convention covers a wide range of rights, in all areas of life, some of which are outside the eu's competence. therefore, member states should implement the convention in a uniform manner at all levels, including regional and national levels. we believe that there is no hierarchy in human rights and that discrimination on the basis of disability should be addressed in the same way as discrimination on other grounds, including discrimination on more than one ground. this is particularly important for women and children with disabilities, the elderly and people in need of complex support, including those with intellectual and psychosocial disabilities.

in writing. ‒ i opposed the adoption of the commission's draft regulation. the european parliament has voted to ban certain claims used for the sale of sugary drinks and caffeinated energy drinks.
in writing. ‒ the n-va delegation supports the objection to health claims on drinks containing caffeine, mainly energy drinks. these claims would include a statement on the product that it contributes to an increase in alertness and an improvement in concentration. our main motivation for objecting to this proposal is that it goes against the spirit of the health claims legislation: the court of first instance has held that the fact that a claim is authorised creates the impression that those products are healthy or promote health, which is difficult to defend in this case. another reason to support the objection is the high sugar content of such energy drinks and the fact that children and young people are in practice important consumers of these products. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament should be consulted on the matter. finally, the efsa opinion shows how difficult it is to establish thresholds for safe caffeine use in children and adolescents. it is important to note that the objection does not oppose the placing on the market of the products concerned, but the authorisation of a health claim for these products.
in writing. ‒ i supported this objection because i believe that sugary drinks and caffeinated energy drinks should not be allowed to claim to promote alertness or concentration. such claims encourage excessive consumption of energy drinks and result in higher consumption of caffeine and sugar (a 250 ml can of energy drink can contain up to 27 g of sugar and 80 mg of caffeine) by children and adolescents, who are already the main consumers of energy drinks. studies indicate that 68 percent of teenagers and 18 percent of children regularly drink alcohol. energy drink consumption has risks in terms of obesity and medical complications in the short and long term. it is also thought to be linked to problems such as headaches, sleep problems and other behavioural problems in children and adolescents who regularly consume energy drinks.
in writing. it is commonly believed that caffeine makes people more alert and sharpens their concentration, but to conclude on this basis that coffee or caffeine has beneficial effects on health is neither recommended nor desirable. the granting of a health certificate for caffeine would thus give manufacturers of energy drinks, for example, a free hand to claim that their products are beneficial to health. a can of energy drink contains up to 27 mg of refined sugars and 80 mg of caffeine and is popular among young people. about 70 percent of youths regularly drink energy drinks, and with these, youths easily exceed the daily allowance. in a free society, citizens have the right to unhealthy love affairs. but excess is harmful and in the context of preventive health policy it is advisable to alert adults and young people to the health risks posed by the excessive consumption of certain foods.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this objection because it is a matter of public health, especially for our teenagers and children. it should be noted that 68 percent of teenagers and 18 percent of children regularly consume energy drinks. according to the world health organization, fast carbohydrates should be limited to 10 percent of the daily energy intake. the who believes that reducing intake to less than 5% a day would have additional health benefits. i therefore oppose the adoption of the commission's draft regulation and ask the member states to consider introducing rules on the marketing of high-caffeine drinks or caffeinated foodstuffs to children and adolescents.
in writing. ‒ we oppose the adoption of the commission's draft regulation. we consider that it is not compatible with the objective and content of regulation (ec) no 1924/2006. this afternoon we are voting to ban certain claims used for the sale of sugary drinks and caffeinated energy drinks. we would like to see these advertisements and all the mentions on the packaging that target children and adolescents and promote them to gain concentration, performance or alertness disappear. 68% of adolescents and 18% of children regularly consume these drinks and the consequences of excessive consumption of these products by young people can be dangerous to their health.
in writing. ‒ i voted with great conviction in favour of this objection. if you know that 68% of teenagers and 18% of children drink energy drinks regularly, that there is insufficient information available to determine a safe level of caffeine consumption for children, and that 25% of teenagers who drink energy drinks drink three or more cans in a row, then you know that there is an urgent need for action.

in writing. ‒ following revelations of rigged diesel car emissions tests, the european parliament has set up a committee of inquiry into emission measurements in the automotive industry (emis). this emis committee examines whether the eu commission or national officials knew or at least suspected of the fraud before the illegal practice was discovered in the us and why, given the differences in the different types of measurement, they did not consciously or unconsciously take a more active approach to the problem. the committee's interim report has now been presented to parliament. i have agreed to the text because i fully support a full clarification of this matter and i want measures to prevent such practices at the expense of the consumer in the future. i therefore also support the call on the commission to cooperate transparently and loyally and to provide the additional information that is urgently needed.
in writing. ‒ following the scandal of falsified emissions tests of volkswagen cars in september 2015, the european parliament decided to set up a 45-member committee of inquiry into allegations of breaches of eu law in relation to emission measurement in the automotive sector to examine these alleged breaches. for obvious environmental and public health reasons, but also for simple reasons of fairness towards citizens and fair competition between manufacturers, we cannot accept the idea that economic actors feel entitled to falsify their emissions in view of possible inadequate controls or poor application of relevant eu law. convinced of the need to send a strong message and of the ability to improve the legislation in force to prevent this kind of behaviour in the future, i voted in favour of this mid-term report of the committee of inquiry which encourages the committee of inquiry to continue its work and fulfil its mandate and supports all actions and initiatives aimed at fulfilling it.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution because it is quite clear that, at mid-term, the parliamentary committee of inquiry into automobile emissions (set up following revelations of fraudulent schemes used by the volkswagen group to reduce polluting emissions during official car tests) needs more information from the european commission, in particular on emission measurements as well as details from the expert working group on vehicle typeapproval procedures. although cooperation with the european commission seems to have improved since this summer, it is essential that the inquiry committee can determine whether the european commission and national representatives suspected or were aware of the fraud before it was discovered in the united states. it is also necessary to understand why european and national authorities have not been more cautious about the divergence of emission measurements between type-approval tests and real driving. i therefore wholeheartedly support the call on the commission and the member states to facilitate the investigation in accordance with the principle of 'fair cooperation' as defined by the european rules.
in a letter to the european parliament, the commissioner said that the eu had a duty to ensure that the eu's citizens are protected against the dangers of unfair competition. on 17 december last year, parliament rightly gave the go-ahead for the creation of a parliamentary committee of inquiry. the emis committee shall investigate infringements and mismanagement in the application of union law on emission measurements in the automotive sector. on the basis of the interim report, it is premature to attach conclusions to the mandate of this committee, but it is expected that the emis committee will present the necessary recommendations at the end of its work. in order to ensure that the committee can do its job properly, it is necessary that it has all the relevant information on the use and knowledge of tampering mechanisms in the automotive sector. it is therefore appropriate that all parties concerned provide the necessary technical and political support to the emis committee's investigation. this will enable us to improve the performance of our car industry in the future and at the same time ensure better air quality for all the inhabitants of europe.

in writing. ‒ i have approved this report on the proposal for a council decision authorising the conclusion of the agreement in the form of an exchange of letters between the union and china under certain provisions of gatt relating to the modification of concessions in the list of commitments of croatia in the context of its accession to the union.
in writing. on 1 july 2013, the republic of croatia became the 28th member state of the european union. the european customs union was thus enlarged at the same time. however, under the rules of the world trade organisation (wto), in accordance with article xxiv:6 of gatt 1994, the european union was required to open negotiations with the people's republic of china on croatia's list of commitments with a view to agreeing on possible compensation. this is necessary if the adoption of the eu external tariff regime leads to an increase in duties beyond the level to which the acceding country has committed itself in the wto. the european parliament has given its approval to the eu-china agreement on the accession of croatia. the results were negotiated by the commission in agreement with the wto members holding negotiating rights and concern industrial products and agricultural quotas. it is with this in mind that i voted in favour of this recommendation.
in writing. ‒ following the accession of croatia, the european union has enlarged its customs union. it was then obliged, under the rules of the world trade organisation (wto), to open negotiations with wto members with negotiating rights on the lists of one of the acceding countries in order to agree on compensation. like a large majority of meps, i consider the outcome of these negotiations with china and uruguay to be acceptable, which is why i have decided to vote in favour of these acts.
in writing. ‒ the european parliament followed the opinion of the committee on foreign affairs in the form of a letter; the commission considers that the draft agreement should be approved as it makes proportionate changes to the concessions and is in line with previous practices in the wto. it notes the commission reports that the compensation in question is proportionate and does not exceed the rights of china concerned by the withdrawal of concessions from croatia to china.
in writing. ‒ the accession of croatia to the union de facto extended the customs union. the people's republic of china is entitled to reestablish its former trade rights, after their slight erosion by the enlargement of the eu customs union with the accession of croatia to the eu. i voted for this recommendation.

in writing. on 1 july 2013, the republic of croatia became the 28th member state of the european union. the european customs union was thus enlarged at the same time. however, under the rules of the world trade organisation (wto), the european union had to open negotiations with the eastern republic of uruguay under article xxiv:6 of gatt 1994 concerning the list of commitments of croatia with a view to agreeing on possible compensation, since the adoption of the external tariff regime of the union had led to an increase in duties. the european parliament approved the eu-uruguay agreement on the accession of croatia, which i supported. the results were negotiated by the commission in agreement with the wto members holding negotiating rights and concern beef.

in writing. ‒ i have decided to vote in favour of this recommendation, following up on the excellent work done by my colleagues in the inta committee. the amendments referred to in this text are essentially to bring the procedures applied in the field of statistics into line with eu law on the new system of delegated and implementing acts as established by the treaty of lisbon in two specific respects.
in writing. delegating implementing powers to the commission, under the control of committees of representatives of the member states in the framework of comitology , is justified for reasons of uniformity and has existed since the 1960s. however, the lisbon treaty introduced a major reform by distinguishing implementing acts from delegated acts, placing the european parliament on an equal footing with the council and the commission, thus increasing the powers of the european parliament in the executive sphere. parliament can now put pressure on the commission and the council by threatening to block a legislative decision in codecision or a budgetary decision. with the lisbon treaty, the legislator has the right to object on any grounds and the right to simply revoke the delegation or an individual act. this is a major instrument of pressure on the commission. for my part, and in the context of the interinstitutional agreement on better law-making, i support a delegation procedure which allows the legislator to concentrate on the essentials, provided that the competence delegated to the commission is properly framed and implemented in a completely transparent manner.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the text. informal negotiations were opened under the italian presidency, following the adoption of parliament's position in plenary and first reading on 12 march 2014, with a view to reaching an agreement at second reading in a timely manner. after several rounds of trilogues, the negotiations were suspended pending the new interinstitutional agreement on better law-making, which provides, inter alia, for a horizontal solution for consulting member states' experts when preparing delegated acts. the adoption of the new interinstitutional agreement on better law-making in december 2015 thus enabled the parliament and council negotiating teams to reach an agreement on the regulation under consideration. the text of the agreement was submitted to the inta committee for approval on 21 april 2016 and was approved by a very large majority. in view of this result, the committee chairman recommended that parliament should vote in favour of the resolution.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this recommendation. the commission's proposal is to make institutional adjustments in the area of the european commission's trade policy. in the light of the changes resulting from the lisbon treaty, the commission was obliged to adapt the rules for the adoption of decisions on trade policy to the new system of delegated and implementing acts.
in writing. ‒ the legislative proposal amending the existing directive 2008/92/ec was published in november 2015 as part of the state of the energy union package. the aim of this proposal is to establish a common framework for the development, compilation and dissemination of comparable european statistics on natural gas and electricity prices for household and non-household final customers in the eu. the aim of this regulation is to make this voluntary nature compulsory in order to avoid problems in data collection, which have been reported by several member states. i agree with the commission's proposal to regulate the collection of both types of data by means of a legislative act. only in this way can the quality of the collection of electricity and natural gas prices in the household sector be guaranteed and the greatest possible transparency of the gas and electricity prices paid by industrial end-users be ensured. the markets must continue to be thoroughly covered and the price data must remain of high quality. this is best achieved by a community procedure.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this regulation, which aims to establish a common framework for the development, production and dissemination of comparable european statistics on natural gas and electricity prices to residential and non-residential end-users in the union. the text proposes that member states collect data on natural gas and electricity prices and their sub-components (network costs, taxes, levies, charges and charges) and on consumption volumes. the collection of these data is currently based on a voluntary agreement, which sometimes makes it difficult to collect complete statistics that reflect the reality of costs within the union. as the increasing complexity of the internal energy market makes obtaining reliable and up-to-date data increasingly difficult and increasingly important, a legislative act covering the collection of both types of data will be beneficial.
in writing. the creation of an energy market must first be achieved by making available reliable statistics for all member states in order to be able to compare the price of gas and electricity charged to residential and non-residential end customers within the european union. this makes it possible, in particular, to monitor the evolution of the european market and to propose appropriate responses to this vital issue. until now, the transmission of statistics has been on a voluntary basis, but it is necessary to make it compulsory. this will ensure the continued reliability of the data collected in the future. this is a crucial element because after all, our whole society, our daily lives, depend on the supply of energy. access to gas or electricity is essential, especially for the competitiveness of our companies.
in writing. ‒ i voted against the report by mrs barbara kappel on gas and electricity prices because i refuse, for obvious ethical reasons and in the name of the values of humanism and democracy, to support any legislative work carried out under the auspices of a member of the extremist, anti-european and racist group europe of nations and freedoms.
in writing. ‒ the report also addresses the following important points. firstly, the commission proposal does not specify who will be the agent responsible for providing the price breakdown, a task which cannot be fulfilled by the suppliers. second, the provision of price information becomes mandatory for large non-residential customers. finally, it should be noted that the overall average share of transport and distribution costs can only be distinguished at the level of all residential and non-residential customers. the network usage burden components may only be indicated for the whole of the residential and non-residential customer sectors, excluding individual consumption bands.
in writing. – i voted in favour of this resolution with regard to statistics on prices of natural gas and electricity in europe. it concerns an important proposal for a regulation on statistics on prices of natural gas and electricity in europe. this resolution aims at achieving more transparency for the consumers with regard to these prices, specifically aimed at the household sector and non-household consumers. in order to achieve this objective, an obligatory collection of data is needed. this should however not create additional burdens on the relevant authorities. therefore, the report that this resolution concerns, aims at making this transition possible and easier. it also gives specific recommendations on what still needs to be done. one important aspect is that it stresses the importance of protecting the confidentiality of sensitive information.
in writing. ‒ the aim of this report is to strengthen the internal energy market. furthermore, efforts must be made to ensure that electricity can be freely routed to the places where it is most needed. the aim is to maximise the benefits of crossborder competition and to provide the right signals and incentives for meaningful investment. the report also calls for the full integration of renewable energy into the electricity system, ensuring that markets are equipped to do so and promoting the share of renewable energy in the electricity market in line with the share of conventional energy sources. i have agreed to the report because i believe that a coordinated approach is necessary with regard to adequate power generation and reliability standards. this may allow for greater cross-border coordination and cooperation and a harmonised approach to capacity mechanisms. i also believe that regional cooperation in the field of energy policy should be strengthened and that a uniform european framework for the promotion of renewable energies should be established.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report, which highlights in particular the enormous potential of enhanced regional cooperation and the importance of coordinated long-term programming for the effective development of transport infrastructure and electricity markets in europe. the report also regrets that there are still major gaps in interconnection within and between some member states. the report underlines the growing share of renewable energy in the european union and stresses that full integration of renewable energy into the electricity market is essential. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of renewable energy sources.
in writing. how do we ensure that europe's energy supply remains secure in the near future? and how do we ensure that energy becomes affordable and sustainable? in order to meet these challenges, this report rightly points to the need for strengthened european energy networks. the development of a well-functioning crossborder interconnection between member states and the development of the necessary back-up systems will guarantee the supply of electricity in europe. a stronger energy infrastructure in europe would increase our energy independence. the new structure of the energy market, which will be decentralised, would also lead to crossborder competition, which would result in price advantages for consumers due to the presence of several energy suppliers. at the same time, the growing supply of renewable energy sources, the integration of those renewable energy sources into the energy market and the development of smart grids and new technologies for distributed generation will also enable consumers to play a more active role as both consumers and producers of energy. in this way, the consumer producer will be able to participate in the price formation on both the demand and supply side of the electricity market.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the european parliament's resolution on a new organisation of the energy market to make it more integrated at european level. it is normal for member states to seek to guarantee the supply of electricity to meet demand in the medium and long term. but, like the majority of meps, i believe that these member states must guarantee this supply in the context of crossborder cooperation. i am also in favour of renewable energy support schemes which are adapted to national circumstances. we are well aware that the development of these renewable energies is a necessity for the planet and is a source of jobs and inclusive growth.
in writing. - i voted for the text. indeed, the challenges facing europe in the field of energy include the dependence on oil and gas imports, which has further increased in recent years, the lack of diversification, high energy prices characterised by state duties, the growing global demand for energy, security risks for producing and transit countries, the fight against climate change, the lack of progress in energy efficiency, the growing share of renewable energy, the integration and interconnection of energy markets and market distortions due to different aid schemes.
in writing. ‒ the completion of the european internal energy market is a demand of the liberals in the european parliament. in this report we encourage the european commission to take this into account. a european internal energy market would bring with it a greater supply of affordable and renewable energy sources. we need to integrate national markets more closely by developing interconnections. we also need to speed up the development of smart grids and new technologies for decentralised generation. i voted for this report to enable consumers to play a more active role as consumers and producers, and to encourage better demand side management. in a europe without internal frontiers, we should also be able to have an energy market without internal frontiers for the benefit of all eu citizens.
in writing. – i voted in favour of this resolution because it contributes to the plans of the european commission to create an eu-wide electricity market. this will be to the benefit of both companies and eu citizens. the eu’s energy market needs to become more interconnected and integrated. in order to achieve this, specific steps need to be taken. for example, i welcome the focus on decentralisation and an increased flexibility of the market. we need to empower consumers to become ‘prosumers’ of green energy, and also the future possibilities of battery storage offer a lot of opportunities to succeed in a transition to a more sustainable energy landscape in the eu.
in writing. ‒ the commission presented its first strategy to reduce the high energy consumption, in particular of fossil fuels, in the heating and cooling sector. this is one of the priorities of the energy union. heating and cooling is one of the most energy-intensive sectors in the eu, accounting for about 50% of the eu's energy consumption, and where renewables account for only 18% of the energy consumption, compared with 75% for fossil fuels. the strategy includes plans to increase the energy efficiency of buildings and to improve the connections between electricity systems and district heating networks. the aim is to significantly increase the use of renewable energy sources and to promote the reuse of waste heat and cold generated in industry. i welcome that approach. i also share the view that europe can only remain competitive if it invests in innovative and sustainable concepts in research and development, particularly in the energy sector. i also believe that there is still a great need for action on climate change and energy efficiency.
in writing. ‒ i have approved this report, which first of all recalls that heating and cooling account for the largest share of demand in the european union. the report calls for specific long-term strategies based on renewable energy to be developed. it also called for energy efficiency standards to be strengthened and for the commission to provide appropriate co-financing for initiatives to renovate public buildings and multi-unit dwellings which are characterised by low energy efficiency. at the same time, member states are invited to phase out the use of old boilers in urban areas that generate low-level emissions. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'competent authority' to cover the whole of the eu.
in writing. half of the eu's final energy demand is still used for heating. 80 percent of that is used to heat or cool buildings. at the same time, our buildings emit 13 percent of all co2 emissions in europe. this is because the share of fossil fuels for cooling and heating buildings is still 75 percent. these are disturbing figures. bad grades like that have an advantage. if we act now, we can achieve enormous results in reducing co2 emissions in a very short time. firstly, by urgently carrying out the renovation and insulation of old buildings. insulation remains the fastest way to energy efficiency and well taken renovation and insulation projects are boosting our economy and employment. in addition, the share of renewable and recovered energy should be increased. too much heat is still lost to the atmosphere in industry. this energy can be captured and used to heat homes. i therefore support the proposals to support local authorities and private individuals through the existing structural and investment funds in the intelligent modernisation of the energy systems of public buildings, residential areas and private homes.
in writing. ‒ like most members of this house, i voted in favour of the european parliament's resolution on the european union's strategy on heating and cooling. this strategy should, in particular, help to reduce the energy poverty that still affects many european citizens today. among the ideas supported i would mention the european parliament's desire to see renewable energies more integrated into neighbourhood networks. i welcome the statement by commissioner canete, who promises an initiative on access to finance. we'll have to follow up.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the text. solar radiation is an important source of heat which is not yet sufficiently exploited. one way to do this would be to use panels to heat water or photovoltaic cells to generate electricity. given the particularly high energy efficiency of reversible heat pumps and their great potential for heating and cooling, intensive research into new innovative solutions in this area is necessary.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report, which is very broad in its content. since 'heating and cooling' accounts for the majority of energy demand in the eu, it is important that we deal with it very purposefully and carefully. we call on national, local and european authorities to create a favourable environment for tenants and people living in multi-apartment buildings to enable them to benefit from self-production, renewable heating and cooling and energy efficiency measures. we also point out that energy from waste will continue to play an important role in the field of heating, as landfilling and the use of fossil fuels are often the alternative. many of the measures requested have already been implemented in flanders, but not yet in the rest of europe. flanders often leads in this area.
in writing. – a substantial part of the eu’s energy is used to heat and cool houses and buildings across the eu. therefore, if the eu wants to increase its energy-efficiency we will have to work on the infrastructures that provide these. i voted in favour of this resolution, because it recognises the importance of thermal renovation and the efficiency gains that it can bring. i welcome its specific recommendations with regard to the renovation and insulation of buildings, as well as the use of new technological solutions and renewables. finally, becoming more energy-efficient also means that we become less dependent on third countries for our energy supply, for example, with regard to our gas supply.
in writing. ‒ the thematic objective 'enhancing the competitiveness of smes' (table 3) is of the utmost importance for achieving the objectives of cohesion policy and the europe 2020 strategy. the introduction of thematic concentration in the 2014-2020 cohesion policy programming has created an effective tool to design operational programmes with an improved focus on investment priorities. the report provides an early assessment of this thematic core objective and the first reporting on the overall implementation of the strategy in the financial planning period 2014-2020, measuring what has been achieved so far and trying to draw conclusions for the future. smes are of paramount importance to the economy of the eu regions, both in terms of employment and competitiveness. they form the backbone of our economy and create the most jobs in europe. i therefore support the creation of a wide range of measures and financial instruments to promote and strengthen the competitiveness of smes.
in writing. smes and start-ups form the bulk of our industrial fabric. they are essential for employment and competitiveness in all regions of the union. smes are the largest employer in europe. they represent more than 99% of enterprises (or 22 million enterprises in the union) and employ more than 100 million europeans. they are the engine of our economy and must be strong, competitive and innovative. access to finance is a prerequisite for this. the european investment fund (eif) responds to this demand by providing risk capital. starting a business and keeping it going is the best way to create jobs. europe will only get back on the path to growth if those who want to invest and create are given the means to do so. improve access to finance, help with flexibility, transparency, professionalisation, multiplication of financing needs and of course entrepreneurship.
in writing. ‒ smes account for 99% of all businesses and make a key contribution to the eu's economic growth by providing more than 100 million jobs, or two thirds of private sector jobs. i therefore voted in favour of this report which encourages the commission to integrate more closely the financing of the competitiveness of smes in the preparation of cohesion policy after 2020.
in writing. ‒ 23 million smes, representing 99% of all businesses in the eu, provide 100 million jobs or two thirds of all private sector jobs. they therefore make a fundamental contribution to economic growth, social cohesion, innovation and quality employment. moreover, they are a major driver of the green economy and job creation. the report on improving the competitiveness of smes provides for a very balanced approach to strengthening green smes and local markets, in particular through support for local smes. the report also highlights the importance of thematic concentration and its role in sustainable development, the quality dimension of job creation and the involvement of smes in the partnership principle, including specific organisations targeting eco-entrepreneurs. after some additions on the circular economy, the 'small business act' and youth entrepreneurship, and with a focus on green jobs and the green economy, the report meets many green requirements and i voted in favour.

in writing. ‒ in december 2013, the european council called on the commission to present an eu strategy for the alpine region (eusalp). the commission responded to this call in july 2015 by presenting the action plan for the strategy (the eu's fourth macro-regional strategy). the committee on regional development decided to draw up an own-initiative report on the basis of this action plan with a view to formulating recommendations for rapid and effective implementation. this report is now based on the principle that macro-regions are the framework for cooperation measures and for developing synergies between the various eu financial instruments. it also invites the participating member states to coordinate their national and regional actions with a view to contributing to the actions and objectives of the eusalp strategy. the aim of diversifying tourism is also supported, and the importance of improving transport and energy connections and of protecting and promoting biodiversity in the alpine region is emphasised. i support the promotion of innovation and new technologies in key sectors of the economy while preserving traditional forms of economic activity. i therefore voted in favour of the report.

in writing. ‒ the eu trust fund for africa (eutf) was established at the valletta migration summit in november 2015. in the face of irregular migration on an unprecedented scale, the trust fund was established to support the most affected african states, to bring stability to these regions and to promote eu-africa cooperation on issues such as migration management, security and development. the objective is to tackle the causes of destabilisation, displacement and irregular migration in the horn of africa, the sahel and the lake chad basin, and north africa. i support the view that one of the priorities of eu migration policy should be to tackle the root causes of migration. the trust fund shall contribute to the achievement of the long-term objectives in the beneficiary countries. it is about securing peace and bringing stability to these regions. in order to achieve these objectives, it is also necessary to systematically monitor and control the distribution of the funds from the trust fund.

in writing. ‒ this report is about the creation of a set of legislative and non-legislative measures to promote a work-life balance. the commission and the member states are called upon to create equal pay and working conditions for men and women. the report also aims to increase the participation of women in the labour market in general by modernising the existing eu legal and policy framework and adapting it to today's labour market. the importance of high-quality early childhood care accessible to all is also highlighted, as is the need to better distribute care responsibilities (for children or family members) between men and women. in recent decades, there have already been some initiatives at european and national level in the area of reconciling work, private and family life, but progress is still needed in this area. i support parliament's call for this debate to be given greater weight and for the commission to be encouraged - in accordance with the principle of subsidiarity - to step up its work in this area in general.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report calling for the introduction of a framework to guarantee the right to work-life balance as a fundamental objective of social systems. like my colleagues, i believe that well-designed and well-implemented work-life balance policies can help to strengthen economic growth, overall labour market participation, gender equality, reducing the risk of poverty, but also to have a positive impact on the eu's birth rates (which have risen from 16.4% in 1970 to 10.1% in 2014). the report proposes that the commission submit a proposal on this package of measures as part of its 2017 work programme, including gender equality as a legal basis. these measures should include policies to support the most disadvantaged or currently excluded from the legislation (single parent families, homosexual couples, self-employed workers, families with one member suffering from a disability, etc.). the report also calls for the commission to take the necessary steps to ensure that the right to maternity and paternity leave is guaranteed, as well as leave for dependants.
in writing. it remains for every father, mother, employee or self-employed person to find a satisfactory balance between work, family and private life. initiatives have been taken at both national and european level to bridge the gap between work and private life. however, demographic changes are creating new care needs and continuing the diversification of family relationships. the report should be read primarily as a call on the commission to step up its work in promoting work-life balance. by taking the lead in seeking better work/family balance, the commission can help create a level playing field within the eu in a policy to promote work/family balance. this means taking decisive steps to reverse the negative impact of parenting on the number of women in work, making the principle of equal pay for equal work a common good, promoting home and teleworking and creating workable arrangements in all member states for men and women to take on caring responsibilities.
in writing. ‒ following the publication by the european commission of the roadmap for 'a new start to tackle the challenges between work and private life', parliament adopted its position to improve this reconciliation, which i supported by voting in favour of it at this plenary session. i believe that the european union must, in particular, put in place legislative initiatives to allow for this better conciliation. this is why i have supported, in particular, the idea at european level of a parental leave of 6 months, a paternity leave of 2 weeks and a leave for dependants supplementing the provision of professional care. as regards the intervention of the various social security systems, i am of the opinion that this is a matter for the member states. as regards the maternity leave directive, i very much regret that the previous proposal was withdrawn following the impasse in the council and ask the commission to present a new ambitious proposal in consultation with the social partners.
in writing. ‒ the n-va delegation abstained from voting on this report. the n-va is determined to work towards a healthy combination of work and family life for a variety of family situations, such as single parents, dual-earner families with young children, newly formed families, etc. an appropriate legal framework should provide workers with the opportunity to juggle their daily work, family and private lives, and employers with the flexibility to respond to the rapidly changing market. however, it is primarily the member states which have to create this framework; it must be as closely as possible adapted to the needs and realities of our citizens. unfortunately, the report misses the point here. it calls for all kinds of european legislative initiatives which would clearly violate the principle of subsidiarity. the report also raises concerns about the rejection of flexible working arrangements, the demand for more eu funds and a sometimes very patronizing tone towards women.
in writing. ‒ it is time for the union to take action to promote upward convergence between member states in favour of work-life balance. it is crucial, if we are to achieve genuine gender equality, to combat work-related poverty and child and women's poverty, to make better use of skills and talents and to take action to address the union's demographic challenges. there is a need both to modernise existing european legislation to address gaps or the absence of legislation in certain areas and to strengthen coordination between member states to ensure a level playing field as regards the costs and benefits of work-life balance policies.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because it is a subject close to my heart. the report takes a broad view of work-life balance. what resources can we provide from europe to make it easier for working people to have a family life? the report includes consideration of discrimination in the workplace, childcare facilities for young children and the role that grandparents can (but should not) play in a family with working parents. of course, we also pay attention to the employees, mostly women, who work on sometimes shaky parttime contracts and have children. these single-parent families often fall victim to poverty. another important point that we in the commission are urging is to work towards a parental leave scheme which certainly includes the father.

madam president, madam commissioner, social dumping, as you know, is simply an abuse of the secondment directive, at best. in the worst cases, it is simply outright fraud or even abuse of workers. the fight against these practices will guarantee the real mobility of workers in the future, the mobility which will guarantee them the right, regardless of their nationality. the fight against social dumping also means fighting unfair competition between companies, and in particular smes, the very smes that do not resist these unfair practices. fighting fraudulent practices also means guaranteeing all member states - indeed all member states - to recover their share of the social protection of their workers. the report by mr balas which is before us proposes appropriate solutions to combat all these practices, solutions which, if implemented quickly - and i think there is indeed an urgency in this area - would make it possible to combat abusive practices in the interests of all.
madam president, i should like to begin by thanking the rapporteur and the fictitious rapporteurs for this balanced report. social dumping is a complex issue, with perceptions varying according to political sensitivities, but also according to geographical sensitivities. for some, social dumping does not exist. the differences in wage and social costs are inherent in the freedom of competition and the principle of competitiveness. they would enable less developed regions to return to the level of the so-called more prosperous economies. for others, including myself, even if i am sometimes considered a populist, social dumping is a reality, which puts whole sections of our economies at risk every day and leads to an ever-increasing rejection of the european project. beyond these differences in perception, the question of social dumping is closely linked to the revision of the secondment directive, a subject which will occupy us for many months and on which parliament will have to show its will and speak with one voice. it is a difficult task, but not insurmountable, and the proof is the compromise reached on the definition of social dumping. it is our duty to overcome sterile oppositions, to build win-win solutions to meet the expectations of european citizens, namely to allow for a more balanced economic development in the different european regions and, at the same time, to put an end to the competitions between european countries, companies, but also salaried workers.
member of the commission. – madam president, i would like to thank the rapporteur, mr balas, and all the shadow rapporteurs and other members of parliament who cooperated in preparing this report. with our social acquis, we have rules in place to prevent social dumping but we need to make sure that our rules are correctly applied. member states are responsible for enforcing labour law, rules for the posting of workers, rules on free movement and on health and safety at work, and – yes, mr balas – national labour inspectorates need sufficient resources to do that. we have already put in place several instruments that offer national authorities more and better tools to make sure that free movement is fair and well managed and that abuse is prevented. we have the platform against undeclared work, we have the enforcement directive on free movement of workers that makes mobile workers more aware of their rights and establishes national bodies to enforce those rights. we have the enforcement directive on posting of workers that introduces measures to prevent and penalise any abuses or circumventions of european rules on posting. with the upcoming social pillar – and this is important because, indeed, social dumping is not only about mobile work – and with the targeted revision of the posting of workers directive, with the amendments of the social security coordination regulation that are under preparation, with the roads initiatives, we want to make our acquis stronger and adapt it to the new challenges on the labour market. in conclusion, i am convinced that, by pooling all our efforts, we can ensure a fair labour market where there is no place for social dumping. so let us continue to work together. thank you very much for this debate.

in writing. ‒ the european community and its member states, on the one hand, and switzerland, on the other, signed an agreement on the free movement of persons on 21 june 1999. this free movement agreement entered into force on 1 june 2002. since then, the agreement has been adapted to take account of the enlargement of the european union to include new member states. it now remains to adapt that agreement to take account of the recent accession of croatia on 1 july 2013. by voting in favour of this report, parliament gives its approval to the conclusion of the protocol.
in writing. ‒ the eu-15 signed a bilateral agreement with switzerland at the time to allow participation in the single market. the agreement was subsequently amended by means of several protocols whenever the eu was enlarged by a new member state. the same procedure is now being followed for the last member state to join, so that croatia and switzerland can open up their (labour) markets to each other. as in the past, the conclusion of protocol iii requires the consent of parliament. the nva delegation agreed to this purely technical adjustment after the accession of croatia, as switzerland is the eu's third largest trading partner after the united states, china and russia, while the eu is switzerland's largest trading partner. in other words, it is of the utmost importance that the eu as a trading bloc continues to take shape in a legal way.

in writing. social dumping is an unfair practice that undermines the mobility of european workers and distorts the very philosophy of the union. we must ensure that the free movement of workers respects the rules of fair and just competition. the priority is to enforce the rules. we must have a real capacity for control, facilitate the work of our inspectors in the field and harmonize sanctions. this approach is the best shield to strengthen the free movement of workers, which is a principle cherished by the liberals and an added value of the european project. in addition, as the report points out, we must create a european social security card that is unforgeable, as proposed by the mr programme, in order to certify the payment of social contributions or to establish a european list of companies which have seriously violated our social and labour legislation. i would like to support commissioner marianne thyssen in her proposal to amend the 1996 'posting of workers' directive. it is essential to strengthen the rules to protect companies and workers from fraud and to apply the principle of 'equal pay for equal work'.
