president-in-office of the council. – madam president, first i would like to apologise because i will not be able to be here for the whole debate. the reason is that i need to rush back home because we are finalising the preparations for the meeting in bratislava. you added this point to the agenda on monday, therefore i changed my schedule because it was important to present the position but i will not be able to stay here for the debate. news of the closures announced, most recently in belgium and france, created anxiety and anger in the towns and regions concerned. the recent cases of caterpillar and alstom are a reflection of a more widespread phenomenon of mass redundancies across the eu as a result of the changing economic environment, with deep employment and social effects. the recent crisis in the steel and automotive industries, as well as the announced restructuring, show that serious reflection and action is needed in the member states and at eu level. we need to decide whether we want to let our industrial know—how slip away elsewhere or whether we should take determined action to improve the framework conditions for our industries. back in june 2013 the european council recognised the vital importance of a strong european industrial base as an essential building block of the eu’s growth and competitiveness agenda. as you noted in your resolution of 2014, there are several aspects to consider, and i will touch upon them. like parliament, the council has called for an ambitious and active industrial policy. this should include sectoral initiatives to be pursued by the commission whenever the challenges to competitiveness and the need to maintain a strong industrial base require it. to ensure an active industrial policy, industrial competitiveness needs to be mainstreamed across all relevant policy areas. infrastructures, including digital ones, must also be developed with a long—term view. labour markets should enable growth, while safeguarding the social rights of workers. in the area of financing, progress has been made through recent instruments such as the european fund for strategic investments. there is, however, still a need to remove obstacles to – and to promote – new debt and equity financing. the potential of increasingly strategic and targeted lending by the european investment bank to innovation and industrial transformation projects, notably in manufacturing and related services, could also be looked into. as local and regional decision makers are responsible for two-thirds of public investment in the eu, their interaction with business and industry is highly relevant. regions can play a key role in supporting industrial modernisation. this can be done, inter alia, by combining regional policy and industrial policy tools. as recent events show, there is also a need for effective social dialogue involving governments and the social partners. at union level there has been a growing recognition of the importance of involving the social partners at different levels. the council has welcomed the steps taken by the commission to involve the social partners in policies that may have a significant impact on the employment and social situation, but dialogue and policy also need to take into account the financial aspects. to this end the european union has developed an instrument to support workers’ employability and mitigate the adverse social consequences of restructuring. the european globalisation fund (egf) gives specific one-off support aiming to facilitate the reintegration of redundant workers suffering the shock of serious economic disruption. the egf is, however, only a tool to manage such difficult situations once they arise. together we need to engage in efforts to manage the adaptation of the current economic environment, achieving gains in competitiveness, whilst preserving quality employment. there are some excellent signs. research and innovation are essential for the sustainable development of the european economy. it is in this context that the presidency, in cooperation with the commission, is inviting representatives from european and international research, innovation communities and the business sector to a major international conference on the re-industrialisation of the european union. this event will take place in bratislava on 26-28 october 2016 and will focus on the fields of nanotechnologies, advanced materials, manufacturing and production technologies, as well as biotechnology. another key element is the digitalisation of industry, which has a cross-fertilising effect on all sectors. however, we are still lacking coherent development across europe. the eu, member states, regions and industry all have a role to play in fostering the digitalisation of business processes and in developing the industrial dimension of the digital agenda. therefore the council welcomes the recent commission communication on digitising european industry. finally, as the commission has indicated in its new skills agenda, sustained investment in education and training and better alignment of skills and labour market needs are necessary as a way of contributing to employment, growth and competitiveness. these are the different aspects we need to work on if we want to re-industrialise europe. parliament and the commission are working hard towards these goals and so is the council. re—industrialisation will be addressed by the competitiveness council on 29 september 2016, and i would remind you once again of the conference that we will be hosting in bratislava. i invite you to attend. once again i apologise that i have to leave but i am already very late.
member of the commission. – madam president, the recent announcements by caterpillar and alstom about the envisaged closings of major industrial plants in europe are a hard blow for the affected people and a severe setback for the regions concerned. i thank the european parliament for organising this debate and for making the link with the vitally important issue of the future of the european industry and the need for industrial competitiveness. in cases like these, the immediate priority of the commission is to support those directly affected. it is absolutely necessary to quickly establish a perspective for the workers, their families, as well as the local economy. europe does not stay on the side—line. we must work together at all political levels to help the workers who have lost their jobs and to assist the regions in overcoming this difficult economic and social situation. first and foremost, companies operating in europe have the legal and moral responsibility to put social dialogue at the heart of the restructuring processes. information and consultation of workers is a core feature of our european social model. it is absolutely clear that no company is allowed to escape this responsibility towards its workers. secondly, where redundancies or closing a business are linked largely to developments at global level, we have a solidarity fund, the european globalisation adjustment fund (fonds européen d’ajustement à la mondialisation), which can provide financial support for the workers and regions affected. eur 3 million have already been granted in the past years to cover redundant workers from caterpillar and some related companies in the region. seeing the context, additional financial support from the european globalisation fund can be made available, upon request from the member states concerned. financial means from the egf can be used to support, amongst others, the professional retraining of workers. in addition, the european regional fund and the european social fund can be put at the service of the conversion of the region and the affected workers. to respond to the serious situation in gosselies, we have set up a taskforce, a taskforce which will be an interface for the belgian authorities with the commission, and which will assist with any questions arising during the process ahead, for instance related to the legal framework or the use of european funds. while these measures all contribute to our short-term response, this commission has from the beginning sent a strong signal on the necessity to preserve and improve the competitiveness of our industrial economy over the long term with the investment plan for europe. in july 2016, eur 20.4 billion had already been invested in infrastructure projects, innovation and small- and medium-sized enterprises under the european fund for strategic investment. this amount is expected to generate eur 115 billion in investments. and, as announced this morning by president juncker in his state of the union address, the commission will take this further by doubling the duration of the fund, and doubling its financial capacity. this should lead to a total of at least eur 500 billion of private investments by 2020. the investment plan also aims at removing barriers to investment and at creating simpler, better and more predictable regulation in the european union. the industrial dimension is also incorporated into all other major commission policies: the single market strategy, the circular economy package, the digital single market, the energy union, the capital markets union, our research and development agenda, the better regulation agenda, the trade for all strategy and the new skills agenda for europe. indeed, in a fast-changing global economy, skills will, to a large extent, determine europe’s competitiveness and the capacity to drive innovation. they also help mobilise and attract investment and they are a catalyst in the virtuous circle of job creation and growth. our skills agenda is an agenda for all: young, old, in education, unemployed, in work or indeed in transition between jobs. our industry is strong. nevertheless, worldwide competition is increasing. so we must step up our efforts at all levels to ensure that europe remains a competitive and attractive environment for manufacturing.

vice-president of the commission. – madam president, i am pleased to have this opportunity to discuss the proposal to streamline the prospectus directive. the proposal to reform the prospectus was one of the first actions of the capital markets union action plan. prospectuses are the gateway for companies raising capital in europe. our proposal has a simple goal: to create a simpler, faster and cheaper prospectus regime. simpler prospectuses should make it easier for companies of all sizes to raise the capital they need to grow their businesses. simpler prospectuses means that less money is spent on legal formalities and more energy can be diverted to creating businesses and jobs. i am grateful to mr ježek, the rapporteur, and the prospectus negotiating team in the committee on economic and monetary affairs for the hard work they have done on the initial proposal. i also want to acknowledge the internal market and consumer protection committee's contribution and extend my thanks to mrs ford and her colleagues in imco. a prospectus should provide clear and comparable information on company so that any company can raise capital across europe with a single document; but not all companies need to or want to raise capital across europe. this is why the harmonised prospectus should not be needed if small sums are raised locally. this is why we propose that up to eur 10 million can be raised without a prospectus. this is because requiring a harmonised prospectus for such small amounts creates disproportionate cost: up to 10% of the amount raised for equity and up to 5% for debt issuance. this, we believe, is too much money spent on a prospectus. there is no point in imposing such a costly requirement on companies wanting to raise small amounts without the benefit of a prospectus passport. we are interested in parliament's proposal for creating a tailor-made eu growth prospectus for small companies and for capital issuances up to eur 20 million. the cost of producing a prospectus must be proportionate to the investment sought. for the eu growth prospectus to be truly successful, we need to make sure that it stays as light as possible for small issuers, of course without sacrificing proper investor information. you will recall that one of the reasons we proposed a new prospectus regulation with a wider range of exemptions was because a previous, supposedly lighter regime failed to be meaningfully lighter than the full prospectus itself. the prospectus summary is particularly important for retail investors. it is an area that has worked well, in writing. ‒ the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) was originally set up by regulation (ec) no 1927/2006 to help workers who had lost their jobs as a result of mass redundancies. the scope of the fund was extended to cover workers made redundant as a result of the global financial and economic crisis between 2009 and 2011 and for the period from 2013 onwards. since 2013, self-employed persons have also been covered. the main objective of this report is to review the activities, impact and added value of the fund for the period 2007-2014. the aim is also to assess the strengths and weaknesses of the reforms introduced during this period. it is important to measure such added value in order to be able to verify whether policies at union level, such as the egf in this case, are justified or need to be challenged. i believe that it is still absolutely necessary to support workers who have lost their jobs as a result of mass redundancies in the context of structural changes in the world trade structure. in the long term, however, it is also essential to create a fair and effective framework in europe in order to safeguard jobs and industrial sites in europe in a sustainable way.
in writing. ‒ i have approved this report, which underlines the court of auditors' findings that almost all workers eligible under the egf have been able to benefit from personalised and well-coordinated measures tailored to their individual needs, and that almost 50% of workers who have benefited from assistance under the egf have now returned to work. in the face of the social damage caused by deregulated capitalism, the egf is a necessary tool which has helped thousands of workers who have been made redundant. but, as the scandalous closure of caterpillar has shown once again, we must act very quickly to prevent these social and human tragedies. europe must punish severely firms that carry out redundancies. it must take strong action to end tax avoidance and the role of tax havens. finally, it must redevelop an industrial policy based on activities rich in innovation and research and development, which are not easily offshored. this must of course be accompanied by a revival of public investment, and thus demand, within the union.
in writing. ‒ i supported the report on the evaluation of the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf). i note that the egf has overall provided well-coordinated measures for redundant workers, is well managed and plays an important role in improving the employment prospects of thousands of citizens at a time of cascading industrial accidents, the latest examples being caterpillar and alstom. in this context, this tool is essential. one of its benefits is that it provides personalised support to redundant workers. it should also be noted that the egf provides for the possibility of intervening in favour of young people who are not in education, employment or training. this helps to ensure that regions with high youth unemployment can benefit from european solidarity. of course, there is room for improvement: eu governments should be asked to do more to use the flexibility of the current fund to help workers made redundant by subcontractors, who are most often smes. it is also very important that there is genuine participation of workers or their representatives, social partners and other stakeholders in decisions on implementation.
in writing. as the events we know are hitting caterpillar, the european globalisation adjustment fund is making sense. this is a real help to people who have lost their jobs so that they can re-enter other growth sectors. but the union's social action must not stop there. the commission will need to be more proactive and carry out impact assessments, highlighting the potential effects of deals such as caterpillar on employment and competitiveness and the consequences for smes. the fund cannot replace a genuine policy of prevention and anticipation of restructuring. the european social fund and the juncker plan must therefore directly complement the globalisation adjustment fund to ensure the sustainability of european industrial activity.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the european parliament resolution on the activities, impact and added value of the european globalisation adjustment fund between 2007 and 2014. let us be clear: this european globalisation adjustment fund cannot in any way replace a serious policy of preventing and anticipating restructuring. as such, i am always in favour of the establishment of a genuine industrial policy at european level. the recent announcement of the intention to close the caterpillar plant in gosselies reminds us that the road to reindustrialisation is still long and requires real political will, to be translated into legislative acts now! as regards the evaluation of this fund, i am concerned that the gef has had very limited effects on smes. the commission should redirect the egf more towards smes by making greater use of the threshold exemption.
in writing. ‒ marian harkin's own-initiative report looks at the activities, impact and added value of the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) between 2007 and 2014. this european fund was set up to support workers made redundant as a result of major unforeseen structural changes in the labour market as a result of world trade. the fund can be called upon by the member states for a minimum of 500 outputs and has a total budget of eur 150 million per year to co-finance up to 60% of the costs. between 2007 and 2014, there were 134 applications from 20 member states, representing 122 121 affected workers. the report calls for the european commission to anticipate the effects of trade agreements on the labour market and for greater coordination between the trade and employment services. this meagre fund should not be seen as a social safety net to prevent future trade agreements from having a negative impact on employment. furthermore, member states should use these funds in their services to redundant workers to promote a resource-efficient and sustainable economy. the fund shall not relieve member states of their obligations in respect of redundant workers. these are all recommendations that put the interests of the employee first. that's why i'm voting for it.
in writing. ‒ originally, financial assistance was intended for 'active labour market measures which form part of a coordinated package of personalised services aimed at the reintegration of workers who have lost their jobs' (§1). in the 2013 regulation, this scope was extended to include 'reintegration into the labour market, whether as an employed or self-employed person, in particular, of disadvantaged, elderly or young unemployed persons'. eligible actions include tailor-made training and retraining, job-search assistance, sponsorship, promotion of entrepreneurship, support for self-employment, for the creation and resumption of businesses by employees, as well as mobility allowances, subsistence or training allowances. the financing of all eligible actions is conditional on the active participation of the targeted beneficiaries in job-search or training activities. in addition, actions which fall under the responsibility of enterprises under national law or collective agreements, as well as passive social protection measures, cannot be financed.

the report aims to ensure a minimum level of legal aid in legal proceedings within the eu. we already have guidelines on the right to an interpreter or a lawyer, while this draft law deals specifically with the right to legal aid. so we're talking about access to legal information, getting a first opinion or a referral to a lawyer, free or not. the text proposed by the commission was a thin one. during the trialogue negotiations, the text was substantially amended. i'm satisfied with the increased level of protection. i also think it is only right that the same minimum level be maintained throughout the european union. for example, some eu member states do not provide legal aid for people detained under european arrest warrants. such gaps are being closed in the present text. finally, i think it is a good thing that legal aid is only offered if there can be some added value, regardless of the person's incapacity. in belgium, this is already the case with regard to the assistance of a lawyer. if he feels that his intervention has no added value, he can ask the parent agency to remove him from the case. that seems to me to be a wise use of taxpayers' money. that is why the n-va will support this proposal.

in writing. ‒ the paris agreement is a landmark event in the fight against climate change and for multilateralism. it is an ambitious, balanced, fair and legally binding agreement. the report sets out a long-term objective of taking global action to keep the increase in global temperatures well below 2°c compared to pre-industrial levels. it also introduces a dynamic mechanism for taking stock and upward adjustment of ambitions over time. the agreement provides for a legal obligation for stakeholders to take national mitigation measures to achieve the objectives set out in their contribution, but also for an ambitious solidarity mechanism between rich and less rich countries. convinced that this agreement should accelerate the transition to a climate-resilient and climate-neutral global economy, i voted in favour of its adoption.
in writing. ‒ the n-va delegation has strongly endorsed the paris climate agreement. the eu's ratification brings this historic agreement one step closer to entry into force, and that is necessary. climate change is one of the most important global challenges, along with biodiversity loss and resource scarcity. the lack of strong policies has irreversible consequences and is harmful to the planet, people and the economy. the paris agreement is the first legally binding global climate agreement and aims to limit global warming to well below 2°c. we can only fight climate change effectively with global and collective efforts. europe has been at the forefront of the fight against climate change for years, but setting a good example is not enough. the eu cannot solve the problem alone. we need allies. for the n-va, the future of our children and grandchildren comes first. so we have to address both the effects and the causes of climate change. the initiative of flemish prime minister geert bourgeois for a flemish climate and energy summit illustrates our commitment. the n-va wants to combine economic growth and prosperity with a low-carbon economy. this implies that we make sustainable, efficient and effective choices that we can sustain for years.

in writing. in the middle of the last century, the world came to the conclusion that our climate was going in the wrong direction. meanwhile, scientific research has shown that industrial activities are at the root of that climate change. in 1997, kyoto was the first to set limits on harmful greenhouse gas emissions. many more climate conferences would follow. with varying degrees of success. because either the big industrial countries like the us and china were left on the sidelines or they were given a new lease of life. that is why the paris agreement is 'historic' for several reasons. one: because all partners have now taken the climate threat seriously and are now committing to limiting temperature rise to 1.5°c. two , you 're not . the rapid ratification is the result of a strengthened multilateral approach, which provides evidence that global challenges are best addressed when they are tackled together. now we need to quickly develop a concrete and ambitious climate policy to achieve that 1.5°c target. this implies serious efforts to reduce harmful gas emissions, to introduce new energy technologies and to develop a fully sustainable economy. with this ratification, the eu reaffirms its global commitment to a better environment.
in writing. ‒ the european parliament voted in plenary to ratify the paris agreement of cop21. after the time of decisions, the time of action will come, with the cop22 to be held in marrakech, morocco. it will thus make it possible to implement the measures adopted in the paris agreement to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and effectively combat global warming. the european union and the major industrial powers must commit themselves willingly to a decarbonised economy, with the cooperation of economic actors. the fight against climate change is also a fight against respect for human rights.
in writing. ‒ the european parliament voted overwhelmingly to ratify the paris climate agreement. this is important and good news for international climate policy and shows that if there is political will, things can move forward. multilateral and international cooperation is worthwhile. the ratification by the european union is exceptional because most eu member states, including belgium, have not yet ratified. this could, in theory, lead to a situation where the eu negotiates on behalf of member states at the marrakesh climate summit, which have no say in the matter. member states are reluctant to accept this situation, but because countries like the us and china ratified so quickly, the eu had to go along. the choice was between swift ratification by the eu or an international mudslide and having no say at all as the eu. the knife was on the throat. as of now, the emissions of the six member states that have already ratified count towards the 55 percent emission threshold that brings the climate agreement into force. this will close a 3.1 percent gap in emissions. the paris agreement will officially enter into force at the beginning of november. that's just in time for the start of the climate summit in marrakech.

in writing. – i voted in favour of this legislative resolution and thereby gave my consent to the conclusion of the paris agreement. by doing so, parliament has given its contribution to reaching the required 55 signatories representing 55% of global emissions, to come into effect. this agreement is a milestone in our efforts to stop climate change. over the past years it has become clear that we have to take action in order to keep climate change under control. this agreement provides a long-term plan that includes 189 nations and the vast majority of emissions worldwide. it sets clear goals and ensures and enhances transparency and accountability with regard to commitments. at the same time, it also helps those nations to fight climate change that do not have the resources to do so. it will provide one of the cornerstones for future sustainable economic development.

in writing. ‒ i have decided to vote in favour of this text on legal aid because this proposal for a directive is aimed at nothing less than ensuring the effectiveness of the directive on the right of access to a lawyer. such legal aid would be granted to a suspect or a person prosecuted in criminal proceedings, or to a person whose surrender is sought in proceedings relating to the european arrest warrant, following an assessment of the resources of the european arrest warrant and the merits of the request. in the libe committee we also considered it necessary to suggest that the scope of the proposed directive be extended to include the right to 'ordinary' legal aid for suspects and accused persons in certain proceedings and not just the right to 'provisional' legal aid as proposed by the commission. in order to avoid preventing possible abuse, the reimbursement of legal aid costs could exceptionally be claimed from suspects, in particular if they have knowingly provided the competent authorities with false information about their personal financial situation.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the european parliament's legislative resolution giving its consent to the adoption at first reading of the proposal for a directive on provisional legal aid for suspects and accused persons deprived of liberty and on legal aid in european arrest warrant proceedings. the aim of this directive is to ensure that european citizens enjoy a minimum of judicial rights throughout the union and to improve mutual trust between the different criminal justice systems of the member states with a view to improving the correct use of the european arrest warrant. legal aid contains 6 specific measures: the right to interpretation and translation; the right to information; the right of access to a lawyer; the right to the presumption of innocence; and specific procedural safeguards for children. the eu already had minimum guarantees for access to a lawyer, but with this new directive, all european citizens will be able to make use of these rights, not just those who can afford a lawyer. all european citizens will have the same rights wherever they are in the union.
in writing. after two years of negotiations, i am pleased that the european parliament has just adopted a new directive on the right to legal aid. the right of access to a lawyer is a fundamental right guaranteed by european legislation. however, we know that in practice this right is not accompanied by measures to make it effective. some people, lacking resources, may find themselves alone with the burdens they carry. i refuse to be a party to a two-tiered justice system. we had to ensure the effectiveness of legal aid systems in the member states. the european union had to define a minimum floor to be respected. facade systems, which exist only on paper, must be brought to an end. of course, i would have preferred to take it a step further by aligning the right to access a lawyer with the right to legal aid. that was not possible. unfortunately, the legislation is limited to guaranteeing legal aid in cases of deprivation of liberty. but let's be clear, this has to include the interrogation period. we cannot accept that people are subjected to police questioning without being able to enjoy the right to have a lawyer pro deo.
in writing. ‒ this afternoon, meps added a new stone to the building block of european justice policy. the compromise reached with the council on 30 june 2016 on the proposal for a directive on legal aid does indeed grant a number of rights to litigants. in practice, this right is too often not accompanied by measures to make it effective. in the absence of resources, some individuals may be left to face the charges against them alone, which may weaken the application of the presumption of innocence. the european parliament's negotiators' determination has fortunately borne fruit, since the adopted directive includes the provision ensuring that legal aid is guaranteed throughout all criminal judicial proceedings. another victory, the police and the public prosecutor will have a very limited role in the appointment of the pro bono lawyer. it was indeed paradoxical that the police could both investigate a person and at the same time take decisions on the defence of that person.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the proposal for a directive on legal aid for suspects and accused persons and on legal aid in european arrest warrant proceedings. the commission proposal is an important step towards guaranteeing a minimum level of legal aid in all member states. other aspects of the right to legal aid have been included in a separate commission recommendation. the commission took a long time to propose the current instruments, which is why the remaining measures in the roadmap, and in particular the draft directive on legal aid, must be adopted as soon as possible.
in writing. ‒ the fragmented approach currently pursued by the commission may illustrate the sensitivity of the subject, but it does not increase legal certainty and does not allow suspects or accused persons to know to what extent they will benefit from the right to legal aid and what the quality of legal aid will be. therefore, the scope of the directive should include both provisional and ordinary legal aid in all circumstances. in this respect, the scope of the directive should be identical to that of directive 2013/48/eu on the right of access to a lawyer. prosecuted persons, suspects and requested persons may be reluctant to apply for legal aid, while member states may claim from them expenses related to provisional legal aid if they do not fulfil the eligibility criteria. it therefore seems legitimate to limit the recovery of costs to situations where the suspect, accused or requested person has knowingly provided false information.
in writing. ‒ the purpose of this directive is to ensure that the right of access to a lawyer can be effectively exercised by suspects or accused persons or persons sought in surrender proceedings. since we live in a democracy and a state of law, it is only natural that everyone should have the right to legal aid in all circumstances. i voted in favour of this proposal for a directive.
in writing. ‒ following the european parliament's awareness-raising since 2010, the commission has launched the review of the eu's export control system with a view to strengthening the protection of human rights by subjecting to controls goods and activities used, or likely to be used, to inflict capital punishment, torture or other inhuman or degrading treatment. the draft opinion of my colleagues in the inta committee aims in particular to introduce a targeted end-use clause to enable member states to prohibit or suspend the transfer of certain goods which have no obvious practical use other than the imposition of capital punishment, torture or other ill-treatment. they also propose a series of measures to ensure the effective implementation of the regulation and the establishment of a periodic review mechanism. i believe that export controls are instruments of external trade policy which can contribute to the achievement of broader strategic objectives such as the abolition of the death penalty and the fight against torture, and i therefore voted in favour of this text.
in writing. ‒ i supported the adoption of strengthened rules to prevent trade in goods and services that may contribute to torture or the death penalty. the prohibition of the death penalty and the prohibition of torture are key objectives of european trade and foreign policies. as such, it is essential that union companies do not contribute in any way to such practices. to ensure this, the union has put in place specific tools, including trade restriction regulations, which prohibit the export of products which have no practical use other than for execution or torture, as well as products which have been designed for other purposes but which could be used for torture or execution. despite these provisions, certain loopholes have allowed the trade or brokerage and advertising of such products to continue. moreover, in the face of changes and the development of new technologies, it was essential to strengthen european legislation.
in writing. it remains worrying that a high number of countries still apply the death penalty while other countries and regimes are considering reintroducing it. that is why europe continues to oppose the death penalty worldwide. and that is why it is also necessary for europe to commit itself in all areas of its foreign policy to the abolition of the death penalty. to this end, the eu adopted in 2005 an export control system for trade in goods that could be used for torture and the death penalty. since then, it has been prohibited to export such products to countries and regimes that have not abolished the death penalty. to further strengthen these rules, an updated export control system is adopted, providing for stricter customs controls, a ban on advertising, publicity and marketing services for products that could be used in torture or executions, and a better exchange of information between member states. the eu is firm in its commitment to better protection of human rights and the abolition of the death penalty. and that is why it is necessary for the eu to take the lead not only in politics and diplomacy but also in all aspects of its external action.
in writing. ‒ meps voted by 612 votes to 11, with 54 abstentions, to strengthen eu rules against trade in goods that can be used for torture or the death penalty by third countries. it will now be forbidden throughout europe to advertise goods used for torture, such as electric chairs, including at trade fairs. their transit through the eu will be completely prohibited, as will goods that are "controlled" (i.e. designed for other purposes but which could be used for torture, such as certain riot control weapons), if they are destined to fall into the wrong hands. should we recall that the death penalty is still applied in 58 states and territories around the world and that 2015 was particularly dark in this regard? amnesty international recorded its highest number of executions since 1989, peaking at least 1,634 people. similarly, the ngo reports cases of torture in at least 141 countries over the past five years, even though 156 states worldwide are signatories to the un convention against torture.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report which opposes the sinister trade in instruments of torture. this report is an important step towards closing the gaps in the prevention of torture and ill-treatment in europe.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the text proposed by my dutch colleague. export controls, which are applicable throughout the union, are instruments of external trade policy which contribute to the achievement of a wider set of strategic objectives. regulation (ec) no 1236/2005 'against torture' is a prime means of strengthening the protection of human rights by subjecting to controls the assets and activities used, or which could be used, to inflict capital punishment, torture or other cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report by my liberal colleague, mr schaake. export controls throughout the eu are instruments of external trade policy which serve a wide range of wider policy objectives. this regulation is part of the eu's longstanding policy to combat the death penalty worldwide and to prevent torture. the regulation prohibits trade in goods which can be used exclusively for torture and executions and related technical assistance and establishes a system of authorisations for goods which can be used for various purposes and could be misused for torture and executions by lethal injection .
in writing. – i voted in favour of this proposal for a regulation because it is in defence of human rights. regrettably, in some places in the world, torture and the death penalty are still executed. the least that we can do is prevent that they use our products for such goals and practices. doing so is consistent with european values and with the charter of fundamental rights of the european union. coherence in the controls of eu exports plays an important role herein. this legislation will enhance such coherence and strengthens the existing legislation. it also recognises the rapid pace of technological developments, the role these play in this matter and the challenge this poses to us. at the same time we need to ensure that controls are proportionate and that they are not creating unnecessary administrative burdens.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this own-initiative report by the socialist norbert neuser (s&d, de) on the future of acp-eu relations beyond 2020 because international solidarity was more essential than ever in this context. the report recalled the value of acp-eu cooperation and stressed the need to improve it by establishing a new structure that would preserve the acp-eu acquis, such as the commitment to human rights and gender equality, human development, good governance and democracy, and the objective of the rule of law. my colleagues in the committee on development also felt that sustainable development, the fight against poverty and inequality, human rights, democratic principles and the rule of law should be at the heart of the agreement. they also called for the establishment of a collegiate acp-eu mechanism for monitoring, justification of action and review with a view to regularly monitoring the implementation of the sustainable development goals in the member states.
in writing. the post-cotonou era is a political and strategic challenge for the eu. it is the cornerstone of our dialogue and cooperation in the political, developmental, economic and commercial fields. it structures our relationship around core principles and values shared with the acp countries, such as respect for human rights, democracy and the rule of law, and support for peace and security. it provides a framework for our development cooperation, through the edf. it allows the development of our economic and trade relations through economic partnership agreements (epas), of which i am a strong supporter. on the eve of 2020, it is not only a question of taking stock of what has been done but also of taking into account new global challenges such as the fight against climate change, international crime, the fight against terrorism and the migration crisis. we must work to improve our development cooperation policy by making it more effective, more coherent, more appropriate and more sustainable.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this own-initiative report. this is in the context of the expiry in 2020 of the cotonou partnership agreement between the eu and the acp countries. the report contains a set of objectives, principles, cooperation and financing arrangements and institutional recommendations for a future partnership. the main objective of this report is not to achieve a status quo in the face of major contextual developments in europe and the acp.
in writing. ‒ in 2020, the cotonou partnership agreement between the eu and the african, caribbean and south pacific (acp) countries will expire. this is the largest partnership between developed and developing countries in the world and the relations have been in place since the 1960s. the report put to the vote outlines parliament's vision for the future of the agreement beyond 2020. the european council welcomed the progress made in the implementation of the cotonou agreement and the new structure which will keep universal themes such as human rights and gender equality, development and democracy in a common framework, while work will have to be done in regional agreements. the green group welcomes the cotonou agreement for its development policy and binding standards on democracy, human rights and the rule of law, but considers that it has serious shortcomings: the acp group's (non-) functioning in decision-making, the systematic failure of many acp states to respect common values and the irregularity of financing are among the problems. because of these shortcomings, we with the greens would have liked to see a more open approach which includes the option of replacing acp-eu relations with direct relations between the eu and the three acp regions separately. that is why i voted against the report.
in writing. ‒ we affirm that acp-eu cooperation is a unique and valuable achievement that has strengthened the links between the peoples of the acp states and the union and between their respective parliaments over the past 40 years. we also wanted to emphasize that the common framework and regional agreements should be legally binding. finally, we call for the 2030 agenda for sustainable development and the sustainable development goals (sdgs) to be placed at the centre of the new agreement, and for robust monitoring mechanisms to be put in place to ensure that the implementation of the agreement contributes to the achievement and promotion of the sdgs.

in writing. ‒ the hague convention of 25 october 1980 on the civil aspects of international child abduction is a major legal instrument, ratified by all the member states of the european union. the convention establishes a system of cooperation among states parties to resolve cases of international child abduction. these problems are very common when a couple has separated. if the parents are from different countries, they may be tempted to take advantage of the lack of cooperation between these countries to obtain custody of the child. the convention aims to provide solutions to these situations at international level by establishing that the courts of the child's state of residence have jurisdiction and that the law of that state is applicable. the convention also establishes a system to ensure that children who have been abducted are returned immediately. the accession of peru to the hague convention is to be welcomed. here again, the more countries that sign this convention, the more effective it is. many people of peruvian origin live in the european union. children with ties to that state are thus protected from abduction.

in writing. ‒ this convention establishes a system for contracting states to cooperate in finding a solution to cases of international child abduction. this is often the case when a couple separates. for the husband or wife from another country, it may be tempting to take advantage of the lack of cooperation between the states to obtain custody of the children. the press frequently reports cases of international child abduction that occur at the time of separation or divorce. the major problem is therefore the nationalist conception underlying the legal system of the states. it is not uncommon for the courts of both states to declare that they have jurisdiction and to award custody of the child to the parent who is a national of the state in which the court is seated. the convention aims to remedy such situations at international level by establishing the jurisdiction of the courts and the law of the state in which the child resides. it also sets up a system to ensure the immediate return of the child who has been abducted.

in writing. ‒ this convention establishes a system for contracting states to cooperate in finding a solution to cases of international child abduction. this is often the case when a couple separates. for the husband or wife from another country, it may be tempting to take advantage of the lack of cooperation between the states to obtain custody of the children. the press frequently reports cases of international child abduction that occur at the time of separation or divorce. the major problem is the nationalistic conception underlying the legal system of the states. in such cases, the courts of both states often declare that they have jurisdiction and each of them grants custody of the child to the parent who is a national of the state in which it is situated. the convention aims to remedy such situations at international level by establishing the jurisdiction of the courts and the law of the state in which the child resides. it also sets up a system to ensure the immediate return of the child who has been abducted.
in writing. ‒ this convention provides for a mechanism whereby states cooperate to find a solution in the event of international child abduction. the main problem in such cases is the bias of the courts in each state. but all too often the courts in each of the two states concerned declare that they have jurisdiction and then each assigns custody of the child to the parent of its own nationality. i voted in favour of the report because kazakhstan's accession to the hague convention will bring legal certainty to children of divorced parents.
in writing. ‒ the hague convention of 25 october 1980 on the civil aspects of international child abduction is a very important legal instrument, ratified by all the member states of the european union. the convention establishes a system of cooperation among states parties to resolve cases of international child abduction. these problems are very common when a couple has separated. if the parents are from different countries, they may be tempted to take advantage of the lack of cooperation between these countries to obtain custody of the child. the convention aims to provide solutions to these situations at international level by establishing that the courts of the child's state of residence have jurisdiction and that the law of that state is applicable. the convention also establishes a system to ensure that children who have been abducted are returned immediately. i welcome the accession of south korea to the hague convention. the more countries that sign this convention, the more effective it will be. the fact that there is a large korean community in europe makes it all the more important that we accept this accession.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of south korea's accession to the hague convention. the hague convention of 25 october 1980 on the civil aspects of international child abduction is an instrument of the highest importance. it has been ratified by all the member states of the european union. the convention establishes a system for contracting states to cooperate in finding a solution to cases of international child abduction.
in writing. globalisation offers unparalleled opportunities but also requires social, economic and political responsibility of an ethical nature. every child has the right to have regular personal contact with both parents. parental abduction is a denial of this right and places the child, deprived of one of his parents, his extended family, his mother tongue and one of his cultures, in a state of stress and insecurity. the aftermath of a kidnapping is immeasurable. i therefore urge those member states which have not yet done so to recognise the accession of the republic of korea to the hague convention. child abductions are rightly experienced as tragedies, not only by the child himself who experiences a real emotional upheaval, but also by the parent who is the victim of this abduction, who is constantly in anguish at knowing that his child is deprived of his affection and protection. the eu's response must be commensurate with this unacceptable human tragedy, this nameless distress.
in writing. ‒ a very large majority of meps voted this afternoon to recognise south korea's accession to the hague convention on international child abduction, to which all eu member states are parties. the convention falls within the eu's competence and parliament has been consulted on this subject. the 1980 convention, which now has 94 signatory countries, establishes a system of cooperation to find solutions in cases of international child abduction. this situation occurs most often when a couple separates. if one of the spouses is a national of another country, it may happen that the courts of the two countries concerned declare that they have jurisdiction but reach different conclusions, particularly as regards child custody. the convention aims to remedy such situations by establishing the jurisdiction of the courts and the law of the state where the child resides and by arranging for his or her immediate return. this accession is therefore very good news for international cooperation and child safety. it will be all the more effective as the number of countries joining it will be large.

in writing. ‒ the financial instruments standard, launched in 2008 in response to the economic crisis, will be endorsed and will apply in 2018. a real big bang for financial institutions, which will have to adopt a new risk management framework. in practice, this means that in their consolidated accounts they must review the way in which all their financial assets are classified and accounted for, and also the methods of depreciating their claims. clearly, the number of cases where they will have to use the fair value method, rather than historical cost, will increase very sharply. in addition, provisioning will be made not only for actual losses related to credit deterioration but also for expected losses (which requires provisioning forecasts for loan portfolios based on different risk factors).

in writing. ‒ food comes into contact with other materials on a daily basis, such as packaging, kitchen utensils, cutlery, etc. depending on the ingredients, these contact materials may transfer elements harmful to health to food. these elements can be harmful not only because of the individual ingredients (such as bisphenol) but also because of their interaction with other substances. currently, only four of the 17 substances are subject to common eu rules. as a result, most food contact materials are regulated in a heterogeneous way, with some states being very strict and others not. the present report is therefore to be welcomed because it advocates a harmonized approach. i believe that only a uniform standard can guarantee a high standard of human health. i also fully supported the call for a total ban on bisphenol throughout the eu.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this own-initiative report by the danish socialist christel schaldemose on the implementation of the regulation on materials intended to come into contact with foodstuffs (plastic packaging, regenerated cellulose, cardboard, printing inks, etc.), as it is clear that an assessment of the hazardousness of these materials is of paramount importance for the health of citizens. the committee on the environment, public health and food safety recognises that the framework regulation in question constitutes a sound legal basis, the objectives of which remain relevant. however, they consider that union-level action is necessary to address the lack of specific union measures and the identified shortcomings in risk assessment, traceability, compliance and control. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'commercial vehicle' to cover vehicles with a maximum mass of less than 100 kg.
in writing. ‒ the n-va strongly supported the resolution on the implementation of legislation on materials in contact with food. food is very often in contact with certain materials such as cutlery, crockery, kitchenware and packaging. proper testing of these materials is essential to prevent contamination of food and to protect public health. the implementation of the existing 2004 european legislation can and must be improved. all the opportunities provided for by the legislation must be exploited: the commission has also proposed that the rules on the protection of the environment be amended to include the following: the legislation provides for the possibility of establishing european rules for 17 materials. so far, this has only been done for four materials. member states also have the possibility of drawing up their own rules in the absence of european measures, but this threatens to fragment the internal market. there is a need for a level playing field. this is a win-win for producers and consumers: companies producing fcms can compete fairly and consumers are protected equally across the eu. the federal government in belgium is supporting this and has recently sent a letter to the commission together with a number of like-minded member states calling for further harmonisation to be done urgently.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution because it is clear that the eu should further harmonise safety requirements for materials that are widely used in everyday life in the form of food packaging, kitchenware and dishware. current legislation provides for 17 substances, but only four of them are currently harmonised at european level and are therefore sufficiently controlled for their impact on human health. the remainder is left to the discretion of the member states. the lack of harmonised criteria therefore raises a number of problems. some countries have high levels of protection, others do not. however, we now know from various studies that, depending on their composition and properties, some substances in packaging can transfer their components when they come into contact with food. these substances are therefore potentially hazardous to health. this is why the eu should review current legislation so that food safety means the same thing throughout europe.
the european parliament gives the highest priority to food safety. and rightly so, for safe food is not just about what you put on your plate but also about the materials in which food is prepared, served, stored, or packaged. potentially toxic ingredients in packaging can contaminate food, posing additional health risks to the user. some of these substances have been linked to chronic diseases, metabolic disorders, allergies, and neurological defects. by eliminating the use of these substances from food contact products, you not only target prevention, you also save on health care costs. in a single european market, it is of the utmost importance to create a level playing field and to guarantee the same safe products to consumers wherever they live. implementation of the recommendations contained in this report will be an important step forward in ensuring food safety, a higher level of consumer protection and the proper functioning of the internal market for fcm. better cooperation and coordination between member states on the rapid alert system for foodstuffs should also help to prevent health risks more quickly and effectively.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution on the implementation of regulation (ec) no 1935/2004 on materials intended to come into contact with foodstuffs. this is a matter of concern to european citizens in their daily lives, since there are many materials intended to come into contact with food. this report calls on the commission to revise the current regulatory framework. it is important to strengthen the evaluation of substances in these materials and to ensure their traceability in order to protect the health of european consumers. i am also pleased that the text contains a specific amendment calling for a ban on bisphenol a in food contact materials.
in writing. ‒ food and food products often come into contact with other materials, such as kitchenware, tableware or packaging. in view of the possible 'interaction' with food, general safety rules apply in europe and specific measures can be taken for 17 materials listed in the annex. to date, there are only rules for four materials, namely plastics, ceramics, regenerated cellulose and active and intelligent materials. for the other 13 materials, member states may lay down their own rules. for example, some countries have strict regulations for paper, cardboard, metal and alloys, glass, coatings, silicones, rubber and printing inks, while others are less strict. the implementation report shows clearly how this lack of harmonisation between europe and the member states has led to a lack of protection for public health and a subordination of consumer interests. it called for specific rules to be drawn up for the most harmful and in-demand food contact materials (paper, cardboard, coatings, inks and adhesives). the greens made a link with hormone disruptors, reach, the cocktail effects and nanomaterials. and with a circular economy. we ask for better control and uniform testing. and we call for a total ban on the use of bisphenol a. so it's a good thing for our health.
in writing. ‒ packaging and containers, kitchen utensils, dishes: all materials in contact with your food but with a doubt about their safety. the european parliament's report, which was voted on this afternoon, says that there are 15,000 different substances in these materials, most of which are unknown. toxicity, traceability, lack of controls and harmonisation: the european parliament raises the alarm and considers that the danger to human health of a transfer of chemicals contained in these materials to food is real. some countries have rules in place but there is no real consistency between member states. in addition to the health risk, the situation is damaging economically. we also see shortcomings in the traceability of the various components and a lack of official controls: this is not acceptable, we are not playing with the health of citizens!
in writing. ‒ food contact materials and articles (fcms) are used in daily life mainly in the form of food packaging, kitchenware, tableware, etc. when they come into contact with food, and depending on their composition and properties, the different materials may react differently. in such cases, chemicals from fcms may pose a risk to human health or lead to adverse changes in the composition of the food. the legislation should ensure a high level of consumer protection while ensuring the proper functioning of the internal market for fcm products. that is why i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. – i voted in favour of this resolution because the health of european consumers is important to me. the food that we eat on a daily basis comes into contact with many different materials that can have a variety of chemical compositions. the regulation that this resolution concerns ensures that the safety of our food is not affected by these products. i also welcome the important role of efsa which is recognised in it and the call for increased cooperation between efsa and the european chemicals agency. it also correctly points out the importance of clarity on the use of the relevant substances for our companies, especially for our smes. this will also make it easier for them to produce the relevant safety assessments. finally, with regard to the future, we should not only regard the effects of substances in an isolated form, but further scientific research should be done on the effects of their combinations.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because i agree with the findings and proposals made by the members of the committee on legal affairs. the commission's proposal for a regulation on the application of the principle of equal treatment for men and women in matters of employment, vocational training and promotion, and working conditions, was adopted by the council on 14 june. they also call on the eu institutions to agree on more realistic deadlines for implementing regulations and directives and to increase transparency in the application of eu law. the commission is invited to present a legislative proposal on a european law on administrative procedure and to make compliance with union law a real political priority, which it will have to implement in close collaboration with parliament.
in writing. under article 17 of the treaty on european union, the commission is the 'guardian of the treaties' and ensures, under the supervision of the court of justice of the european union (cjeu), that the treaties and european decisions are properly applied. however, as in 2013, the areas most affected by infringements are those related to the environment, health, consumer protection, mobility and transport. justice is one of the pillars of our social model and community law must be respected. i therefore welcome the thirty-second annual report on the monitoring of the application of union law and would like the commission to refer the matter to the cjeu for infringement proceedings to be brought.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this motion for a resolution on monitoring the application of union law (annual report 2014). it contains important information on the actual transposition and practical application of union law. the resolution stressed in particular that the european parliament has little access to information on formal infringement procedures. the text contains a series of recommendations and proposals to overcome these problems.
in writing. ‒ the n-va abstained from voting on this report. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'competent authority' to cover all the activities of the european union. the greatest obstacle to this report, however, is what it does not say or even conceals. the report should not have omitted a reference to the principles of subsidiarity and proportionality (which was deliberately avoided during the negotiations). the same applies to the demand for better implementation of the services directive. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'competent authority' to cover all the activities of the european union. this seems like evidence, but it's not always the case. for example, the dublin rules which determine which member state is responsible for an asylum application, but which the commission apparently turns a blind eye to. another example is the no-bailout rule enshrined in the treaty, which has also been trampled on by the eu on several occasions.
in writing. ‒ we decided to follow the rapporteur on this case. the thirty-second annual report of the commission on monitoring the application of union law contains, as usual, interesting information on the actual transposition and practical application of european law. the report shows that the environment, transport, the internal market and services were the areas where most infringement cases remained pending in 2014. however, bearing in mind that parliament still has little access to information on this procedure and on ongoing cases, it seems difficult to assess to what extent the decrease in infringement procedures is really a sign of better compliance by member states with union law, rather than compromise solutions between the commission and the infringing states. we are convinced that the european parliament itself could and should play a more structured role in analysing how the applicant countries comply with union law and in developing appropriate support for them in this regard.
in writing. ‒ the european parliament prepares an annual report on the monitoring of the application of european law. it identifies the weaknesses and points out to the commission possible improvements. i voted in favour of this report because it calls for better monitoring of all the applications of european law in all the member states and also in the candidate countries, so that european law is applied equally everywhere.

in writing. ‒ the n-va delegation did not support the objections to the approval of a number of the gos for the following reasons: the complainants disagree with the current legislative framework for gmos and therefore refuse any further approval. what we are discussing today is a de facto moratorium on gmos. the commission did not exceed its mandate: where member states do not reach a qualified majority, the commission is empowered to adopt ggos on the basis of the efsa opinion. the european approval procedure for gmos is particularly strict. the efsa risk assessment plays a crucial role in this. the n-va strongly believes in a scientifically sound and evidence-based policy. biotechnology is also an important sector for innovation, research and development. flanders, and ghent in particular, is also at the forefront of such research. the objections signal that europe wants to put a brake on this investigation, which i believe is wrong and harmful. it is of course still important to distinguish between gmo technology and application. it is also clear that the (possible) use of gmos must always be within an agricultural policy that integrates the protection of human health, the environment and biodiversity, with integrated pest management being essential for the sustainable use of pesticides and non-chemical alternatives.
in writing. at the beginning of 2016, there were about 7.4 billion people on the planet. in the most conservative scenario, the world's population will have grown to 9 billion by 2050. rapid growth in the world's population implies that demand for food and crops will increase proportionately. agricultural and food business operators face major challenges. the existing agricultural area will have to be better and more carefully considered. innovation in agriculture will focus on sustainable and efficient farming techniques and plant technology will play a special role in ensuring food production. in this context, there are also no convincing scientific arguments to oppose a gm authorisation at present.
in writing. ‒ meps have given a highly political signal this afternoon by rejecting, by a large majority, five new authorisations for the cultivation of gmo maize 1507, bt11, mon810 and gm cotton 281-24-236. eighteen months after the entry into force (2 april 2015) of the legislation giving a new possibility for member states to ban the cultivation of gmos on their territory, for which i was the rapporteur, nothing has changed. the commission is trying to push through in the absence of both scientific and political consensus. this is in flagrant contradiction to the commitments made by president juncker in july 2014 to change the authorisation procedure for gmos at european level. the european parliament rightly reminds the commission that it must respect its word. even if the cultivation of mon810, which is the only gmo grown in europe, mainly in spain and since 1998, represents less than 0.10% of the agricultural area, this is a matter of principle. any decision authorising the marketing of gmos should be suspended until democratic control of commission decisions has been strengthened and they reflect the majority opinion of member states and citizens.

in writing. – i voted against this motion for a resolution. it is very important that europe can ensure its own food supply. at the same time, this needs to be done in an efficient and sustainable manner. science helps us in achieving this goal. it is important that those products that are developed in this regard are safe for both consumers and the environment. such an assessment, research and consequent conclusions need to be based on scientific processes and empirical evidence. it is efsa's task and responsibility to ensure that this is the case. this is the reason why it was established by the institutions of the european union. in this case, efsa has, upon request of the european commission, duly assessed this gmo and concluded that it is safe. in my view, efsa is the appropriate authority to give recommendations on these matters and likewise the commission is the relevant authority to act on those. therefore i have voted against this proposal that would go against efsa's judgement.

in writing. ‒ meps have sent a highly political signal this afternoon by rejecting, by a large majority of 375 votes to 193, the authorisation to place genetically modified maize 1507 on the market for cultivation. this maize expresses the cry1f protein, which confers resistance against corn pyrales and certain other lepidoptera parasites, and the pat protein, which confers tolerance to the herbicide glufosinate, classified as toxic to reproduction. meps also expressed concern about the risk of contamination with conventional crops and theosinte, the ancestor of cultivated maize. these are the reasons why the cultivation of gm maize 1507 is banned in 21 european countries and regions: wallonia (belgium), bulgaria, denmark, germany, greece, france, croatia, italy, cyprus, latvia, lithuania, luxembourg, hungary, malta, the netherlands, austria, poland, slovenia, northern ireland, scotland and wales. in practice, this majority cannot win the decision. the authorisation procedure for gmos at european level must therefore be reviewed, as the commission's president-designate, jean-claude juncker, committed to do before the european parliament in july 2014. we're still waiting for it.

madam president, ladies and gentlemen, i am of course pleased that the agreement on the iranian nuclear programme seems to be being respected. of course, i recognize that this agreement opens up new possibilities and will bring benefits to both sides by opening up the iranian market to european companies. of course, i want to open our borders to young iranians. but, madam president, ladies and gentlemen, just because the iranian regime has ceased to be a nuclear criminal, we must not give it a democratic and humanist award of honour. i believe that openness to trade and to new forms of economic cooperation, which i support, must go hand in hand with real progress in the field of human rights. i would remind you that iran is now the world champion in all categories in terms of the number of executions in relation to the number of inhabitants. i would remind you that iran executes minors, in violation of the un convention on the rights of the child, which it has signed and which prohibits the use of the death penalty against juvenile offenders. i would remind you that the iranian regime does not recognize the holocaust. i remind you that in iran, all women are second-class citizens. finally, i would remind you that the present minister of justice publicly expressed pride in having taken part in the decision to execute thousands of political prisoners in 1988. personally, i would describe these mass executions as crimes against humanity. so, madam president, ladies and gentlemen, cooperation with iran is a yes, but turning a blind eye is a no!
