in writing. ‒ the commission had drawn up a proposal for the council on 15 december 2015, which was adopted on 26 january 2016. the negotiations began on 21 september this year and a decision is expected on 3 november. this is a visa-free stay in china for all eu citizens holding an eu diplomatic passport or laissez-passer, as well as for chinese citizens holding a valid diplomatic passport and wishing to travel on european soil. the maximum duration of the visa-free stay is 90 days within a 180-day period. i support this proposal because the abolition of the visa requirement will facilitate direct personal contacts, which is an essential condition for the continuous development of economic, cultural, scientific and other links.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this agreement, which provides for a visa-free travel regime of up to 90 days in any 180-day period for citizens of the union holding a valid diplomatic passport or an eu passport and for chinese nationals holding a valid diplomatic passport travelling to the territory of the other contracting party.
in writing. i welcome the approval by the european parliament of the eu-china agreement on the short-stay visa waiver for holders of diplomatic passports. this is a further step in the eu-china dialogue on mobility issues. more generally, this visa-free agreement should strengthen the existing links between the two parties. as the union and china share a wide range of issues and themes of mutual interest, it is essential to deepen our partnership and maintain a continuous dialogue with china.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report by which the european parliament gives its consent to the conclusion of an agreement between the european union and the people's republic of china on the short-stay visa waiver for holders of diplomatic passports. this agreement provides for a visa-free travel regime of up to 90 days in any 180-day period for citizens of the union holding a valid diplomatic passport or a union laissez-passer and for citizens of china holding a valid diplomatic passport when travelling to the territory of the other contracting party.
in writing. - i voted for the text. the short-stay visa waiver for holders of diplomatic passports will represent a step towards the achievement of full and reciprocal visa waiver for holders of conventional passports. visa facilitation is a development of considerable importance, as it brings tangible benefits. the abolition of the visa requirement will reduce the waiting time at consulates and the costs associated with travel. it will facilitate contacts between peoples, which is essential for the steady development of economic, cultural, scientific and other links, and will intensify contacts between peoples. of course, visa facilitation must go hand in hand with progress in the field of human rights and fundamental freedoms, as required by article 1 of council regulation (ec) no 539/2001.
in writing. ‒ the eu commission should, under the umbrella regulation, review before 30 june 2016 inter alia the so-called 'surcharge' introduced in 2010 for the member states with the most serious budgetary difficulties. this means that those member states which are implementing adjustment programmes or have had to implement one since 2007 will receive, on request, additional payments of 10% on all expenditure declared and will continue to receive payments 10% above the maximum co-financing rate during the implementation of the programme. this allows eu payments to be made earlier than the original financing plan. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them.
in writing. ‒ until 30 june 2016, member states experiencing temporary budgetary difficulties and having received financial assistance could apply for an increase of 10 percentage points above the co-financing rate normally applicable under the european structural and investment funds (esi funds: erdf, esf, cohesion fund, eafrd and emff). in order to ensure that member states experiencing temporary budgetary difficulties can continue to implement programmes under the esi funds, the european parliament proposes in particular to cover the period up to 30 june of the year following the calendar year in which the member state ceases to receive financial assistance, thus allowing the eligibility period to be extended up to a maximum of 18 months. in view of the difficulties europe is facing in recovering from the consequences of the financial and economic crisis of 2007 and the need to make the european union a project more focused on solidarity between member states, i voted in favour of this text.
in writing. in order to cope with the economic and financial crisis, ems have had to adopt austerity measures. however, countries with budgetary difficulties (greece and cyprus) also have difficulties in finding the resources needed to ensure national co-financing of regional policy projects that provide assistance to the real economy. in order not to undermine the proper functioning of the european structural and investment funds, the common provisions regulation authorises the commission to make additional payments by increasing them by 10% above the co-financing rate applicable to the european funds (erdf, esf, cohesion fund, eafrd, eafrd), without changing the overall allocation of the esi funds. it provides for an increase in the co-financing rate for cyprus from 50% of the erdf and the esf to 85% for the period 2014-2020. by raising co-financing rates, we are helping these countries in particular to make investments that are conducive to recovery and job creation. i support this report which is intended to help greece and cyprus, which are currently in a liquidity crisis, and beyond that any member state which might find itself in the same situation.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution on the regulation amending council regulation (eu) no 1303/2013 concerning certain provisions relating to financial management for certain member states experiencing or threatened with serious difficulties with respect to their financial stability. the rapporteur stresses that this is a precise and budget-neutral solution to the temporary liquidity problems faced by greece and cyprus.
in writing. ‒ the economic and financial crisis put pressure on national economies, and member states adopted austerity measures to balance their budgets. in this context, it is important to ensure the smooth implementation of the union's main financial instrument, the european structural and investment funds (esi funds). with national budgets under pressure, it can be difficult for countries with budgetary difficulties to find sufficient resources for national co-financing of regional policy projects. the proposed legislative changes will be likely to result in a temporary increase in payment appropriations, which would be offset by reduced payments towards the end of the 2014-2020 programmes. there should be no change in the annual ceilings of the multiannual financial framework established for commitments and payments.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this legislative proposal, which aims in particular to extend the scope of the regulation on rail transport statistics to cover infrastructure data, in particular the deployment of the european rail traffic management system (ertms), which was one of the priorities of the trans-european transport network (ten-t), as it is extremely important to have a clear vision of the development of ertms in the european union. the union has spent millions of euros to finance this type of infrastructure without any concrete results to date, as the system is not operational in europe due to irregularities and delays in deployment. the european parliament also decided that eurostat should publish data on stations accessible to persons with reduced mobility and disabled persons, as well as on the use of cross-border railway infrastructure. after negotiations between parliament and the council, it was also decided to strengthen cooperation between eurostat, the commission and the european railway agency in order to avoid overlapping of their activities.
in writing. the european parliament's priority is to ensure the fullest possible access of the union's stakeholders and our citizens to statistical data on the union's policies. the commission therefore decided to extend the scope of the regulation on rail transport statistics, amending regulation (ec) no 91/2003 to cover data on more fields such as infrastructure, passengers and rail transport accidents. considers it essential that all citizens and stakeholders involved, from near and far, in the rail transport sector have the right to know, for example, the current state of the deployment of the european rail traffic management system, a project that the european union has so generously funded. they are also entitled to consult railway accident records or to find out about the facilities available for people with reduced mobility in each european station. this is to ensure that, in the long term, there is a clear vision of the existing infrastructure and policies in the railway sector in the union. this is why i am in favour of extending the regulation on rail transport statistics.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the amendment of the regulation on rail transport statistics, as regards the collection of data on goods, passengers and accidents. this data collection is particularly important in order to enable the commission to prepare and monitor union action in the field of transport safety. reliable and high-quality data are crucial for the adoption of the most appropriate policies in this regard.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the text. after lengthy negotiations, the council and the european parliament agreed that the most effective and least costly way to avoid duplication of activities between eurostat, the commission and the european railway agency was to strengthen cooperation between those institutions and to ensure that statistical data related to union policies are easily accessible to union citizens and stakeholders. agreement on the simplification of the regulation on rail transport statistics was only possible after the signing of two memoranda of understanding, one between eurostat and the commission (on 27 april 2016) and the other between eurostat and the european railway agency (on 12 may 2016). these memoranda of understanding are not only important instruments to optimise the use of existing information and reduce the administrative burden, but also respond to the need raised by the co-legislators to make better use of rail transport statistics. this will provide all categories of users with easily accessible data and reliable information on the evolution of european policies in the railway sector.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this text, which aims to extend the scope of statistics on inland waterway transport to passenger transport, not just freight, and to define and frame the commission's powers with regard to the adoption of delegated acts in this field. i agree with my colleagues in the committee on transport and tourism that if our policy of strengthening the role of inland waterway transport in the transport sector is to be effective, it must be based on reliable statistics for both freight and passenger transport.
in writing. this resolution amends regulation (ec) no 1365/2006 on inland waterway statistics by extending the data from the inland waterway sector not only to freight but also to passenger transport. inland waterway transport would thus be placed on an equal footing with maritime, air and road transport, sectors in which statistics are collected for both goods and passengers. we believe that full efficiency in the inland waterway sector can only be achieved if it is based on reliable statistics for both freight and passenger transport. we also wanted to limit the powers of the commission to adopt delegated acts under the interinstitutional agreement on better law-making.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the amendment to the regulation on statistics of goods transport by inland waterway, which concerns the conferral of delegated powers and implementing powers on the commission for the adoption of certain measures. the purpose of this amendment is to align the regulation with the treaty on the functioning of the european union as regards the conferral of delegated powers and implementing powers on the commission for the adoption of certain measures.
in writing. - i voted for this text. parliament and the council agreed to take account of passenger transport by inland waterway in the framework of the regulation. they defined the first steps towards the integration of passenger transport statistics into the regulation. first, the commission, in cooperation with the member states, will develop a methodology for the compilation of statistics on passenger transport by inland waterway. the commission will then launch pilot studies on a voluntary basis to assess the feasibility of this new data collection. finally, the commission will present the results of these studies to parliament and the council and will consider making a proposal for the revision of the regulation. those pilot projects should be financed from the union budget. parliament and the council agreed to limit the powers of the commission with regard to the adoption of delegated acts. delegated acts should only be adopted in order to adapt the regulation to changes in the codes and nomenclature at international level and to increase the thresholds. the duration of the delegation was limited to five years.
in writing. ‒ in the current state of the european customs union, 'passing through customs' is more or less expensive in terms of the risks involved, depending on the member state, as the penalties applied by eu states can range from a simple fine to a prison sentence. in view of the urgency of harmonising customs sanctions at european level, in particular to avoid the risk of 'dumping' and to ensure that the sanctions imposed are dissuasive, effective and proportionate, i have decided to vote in favour of this report, which seeks to amend the commission's proposal in this area. in particular, it is proposed to define as precisely as possible the list of offences, their classification as major or minor offences, and the criminal or non-criminal sanctions applicable depending on the nature and gravity of the offence. my colleagues felt that this directive should also cover the obligations of the member states towards the european union's trading partners, as well as towards the world trade organisation and the world customs organisation, with a view to establishing a homogeneous and efficient internal market while facilitating trade and ensuring security.
in writing. while the customs union is the basis of the european construction and the internal market, it is regrettable that there is no integrated approach to the implementation of the legislation in this area. therefore, although customs legislation is the same everywhere, the penalties applicable in the event of infringement may differ from one member state to another. it goes without saying that importers will choose the member state which is most favourable to them, thus creating market distortions. this customs dumping, which is detrimental to the eu's financial interests, is in breach of the spirit of the treaty. that is why i am in favour of the directive on the union legal framework for customs offences and the penalties applicable to them. the main objective is to harmonise the systems of sanctions and thus improve the functioning of the internal market.
in writing. - i voted for the kallas report. the customs union and trade policy are the exclusive competence of the european union. the european union is therefore the only body that can develop a common approach to the application of customs legislation. member states have committed themselves to two specific objectives: to ensure that customs administrations interact and carry out their tasks as effectively as if they were a single administration, in order to ensure controls with equivalent results, and to support legal economic activities, but also to ensure the necessary protection of the financial interests of the union. however, it is quite clear that without an integrated approach to enforcement, including through sanctions, it is not possible for the customs administrations of the member states to act as if they were a single administration, in particular in view of the significant differences in the sanction systems of the member states. these differences create a lack of mutual trust between administrations, whereas trust and cooperation between customs authorities are essential for the good administration of the customs union and the protection of the financial interests of the european union.
in writing. ‒ although the n-va is committed to the principle of a more uniform framework for the punishment of similar infringements of customs legislation in the eu, the delegation cannot agree with the practical implementation of this framework as required by this report. the nva delegation considers this a missed opportunity. many questions and uncertainties remain, for example as to the scope of the directive and its legal basis. the n-va appreciates the efforts made by the rapporteur of the committee on internal market and consumer protection (imco) in the european parliament, including the effort to come up with a minimum system of sanctions. nevertheless, the n-va cannot agree with the commission proposal which forms the basis of the imco document. it therefore feels obliged to vote against this document.

in writing. ‒ i approved this report, which first recalls that the council's decision to lift all nuclear-related sanctions against iran allowed contacts with that country to be resumed. the report stresses that the future development of relations between the eu and iran should go hand in hand with the implementation of the nuclear agreement. it called for the respect of the eu's human rights guidelines and, in particular, for an immediate moratorium on the use of the death penalty in iran. the report also calls on iran to take measures to fight corruption and to respect the fatf recommendations on issues such as disrupting financial flows to terrorist organisations.
in writing. ‒ i could not vote in favour of the report on the european union's strategy towards iran after the nuclear agreement, because it was completely unbalanced. of course, we must welcome the nuclear agreement, which is a great success of multilateral diplomacy, and european diplomacy in particular. of course, this agreement will bring benefits to both sides, offering european companies the prospect of re-entering the iranian market. but just because the iranian regime has ceased to be a nuclear criminal does not mean that we should give it a democratic and humanist award. iran is now the world champion in terms of the number of executions in relation to its population. under president rouhani, more than 2700 prisoners were executed. iran executes children in violation of the un convention on the rights of the child, to which it is a signatory and which prohibits the use of the death penalty against juvenile offenders. and i cannot understand how members of the european parliament could vote against an amendment denouncing it. cooperation with iran, yes, but turning a blind eye, no!
the nuclear agreement with iran was a major turning point in the country's relations with the rest of the world. iran was, after all, on the verge of a nuclear race. thanks to sustained diplomatic pressure and economic sanctions, iran eventually abandoned its nuclear plans. the lifting of sanctions and the restoration of relations between iran and the west open up opportunities in the interests of both parties. but a healthy democracy is not the fruit of the success of an efficient economy alone. building trust with iran involves more than just picking up economic relations. more trade between the eu and iran does not mean that we can turn a blind eye to the lack of democracy, to the egregious violations of human rights and to the fact that the region is still plagued by death and destruction every day. the authors of this report have not used the opportunity to send out stronger signals on respect for human rights, the abolition of the death penalty, hostile statements against israel and the need to make constructive efforts to promote stability in the region. all this has not been done sufficiently and that is why i have not approved this report.
in writing. ‒ meps adopted this afternoon, by 456 votes to 174, with 67 abstentions, a resolution which i strongly oppose, which aims to define the european strategy towards iran after the nuclear agreement. the agreement, which entered into force on 16 january 2016 after 12 years of negotiations between iran, the european union and the five permanent members of the un security council, lifted sanctions imposed on iran by the major powers in return for a curtailment of its long-term nuclear programme. despite the adoption of some of the amendments i co-signed, in particular on the situation of human rights and political prisoners in iran, the continued denial of the shoah and the state of israel by the iranian authorities, and their support for the terrorist organisation hezbollah, the european parliament's resolution remains unbalanced in tone and substance. it is a blank cheque to iran and it is regrettable that the economic prospects promised by the lifting of sanctions take precedence over the political and geopolitical realities of the region. it is feared that such an attitude will contribute to the european union's isolation on the international scene.

in writing. ‒ i have endorsed this own-initiative report which recalls that the majority of migrants worldwide are hosted by developing countries. it firstly stresses to states their international obligations in the field of migration and the abolition of punitive legal frameworks that penalize migration. it recalls the particular vulnerability of certain migrant groups such as unaccompanied women and girls, migrant children, the elderly, disabled people and lgbti migrants. the report stresses the need for the eu to strengthen its policies for peace and stability in regions where war and conflict are causing huge migration flows. it also stressed the usefulness of resettlement programmes and thus the importance of development aid. the report also calls for the eu to take action to combat terrorism and to ensure that the eu is able to take action to combat terrorism.
in writing. the right to leave one's country is enshrined in article 13 of the universal declaration of human rights. the internal and external aspects of migration policy are closely linked. if europe is to assume its responsibilities, the countries of origin must assume theirs. it is about meeting the common security and development challenges together. there will be no development without lasting peace and security, just as there will be no social, human and economic development without prosperity. it is not enough to resettle refugees or to meet their basic needs. there is a greater need to launch actions in countries of origin to build resilience, improve stability and encourage development. let us not forget that 1% of growth in africa brings in more than all official development assistance. it is clear that trade, when accompanied by national policies and trade aid, is a growth engine. as regards the emergency trust fund for africa, which was initially allocated eur 1.8 billion by the commission, it is urgent that member states and other donors fulfil their commitments to double these amounts.
in writing. ‒ the syrian conflict reminds us every day that in addition to the civil war, there is an unprecedented humanitarian crisis with some 7.6 million internally displaced people and 4.2 million refugees in neighbouring countries. that is to say, if the world is facing the reality of migration today, since according to the un, almost 244 million people are considered international migrants. they are victims of conflict, persecution, violations of human rights and, more generally, of all kinds of poverty. a complex problem which concerns the european union as a host country, but also and above all third countries, the subject of the vergiat report which i supported with a majority of members of the european parliament this afternoon. beyond the resolution's finding that it is difficult to distinguish between refugees, asylum seekers and migrants, the text specifies what should be done and still has not been done. this concerns, as a matter of priority, the opening of safe and legal pathways for migration as a means of preventing trafficking in human beings, and the particular attention that the union should pay to the rights of migrants in the context of country-specific human rights strategies.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this motion for a resolution on human rights and migration to third countries because it is a key issue. despite the fact that it contains several repetitions and is not arranged in the most relevant way, it precisely points out the urgency of establishing legal migration routes and draws attention to the need for the european union to respect the rights of migrants and to include this issue in its external policy.
in writing. ‒ i voted for my colleague's proposal, although i regret some compromises made with an unconstructive epp. parliament expressed its solidarity with those who are forced to leave their country because of conflict, persecution, human rights violations and poverty, among other factors. it also expressed its deep concern at the serious violations of human rights suffered by many migrants in many countries of transit and destination. finally, we should stress that special attention must be paid to the dignity and human rights of migrants.
in writing. – i voted in favour of this resolution, since in the liberal view, human rights and a well-managed migration process, are fundamental for the progression of society as a whole. changes in migration flows, especially in times of crisis, have far-reaching economic, social, and political repercussions for migrants’ countries of origin and for their countries of destination, so it is really important to focus on this issue. this is one of the priorities of the eu and our union will show again the great values of which it is made of. i agree with the resolution since it calls on states to recognise their obligations under international law with regard to asylum and migration and to enact national laws for the effective implementation of those obligations.
in writing. ‒ i have of course approved this report which calls on the union and the member states to define precise rules clearly stating that companies established in their territory and/or under their jurisdiction are obliged to respect human rights in their activities, including outside the union. the report suggests that, in order to raise awareness among producers and consumers, a voluntary eu-wide identification label should be established to ensure respect for human rights. the label would be accompanied by an independent monitoring body with inspection powers whose role would be to verify and certify that no infringements have been committed at the various stages of the manufacturing chain of the products concerned.
in writing. i have approved this report because it is in line with the substance of the previous initiatives i have taken in parliament on the need to establish mandatory due diligence requirements and a regulatory framework for the extraction and supply chains of so-called conflict minerals and minerals from risk areas. this report makes recommendations for the effective implementation of corporate social responsibility in a globalising economy, and thus meets my ambition to prevent and prevent human rights violations by companies in an effective and coherent manner. in this context, progress should be made in the work towards a binding un convention on business and human rights. it is also recommended that the eu, its member states and other countries should have enforceable trade rules for international companies in the event of human rights violations. companies that conduct all their business activities in accordance with the principles of corporate social responsibility today not only gain in social benefits but also strengthen the trust of their customers and consumers.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this motion for a resolution on corporate responsibility for serious human rights violations in third countries because globalisation and the increasing internationalisation of business activities and supply chains increase the role of companies in ensuring respect for human rights. european (and other) companies and member states must jointly ensure that human rights are respected in third countries. in this context, the resolution calls for the adoption of binding instruments to protect these rights.
in writing. ‒ the european parliament will vote this afternoon on its proposal for clear european rules to require companies established in eu member states or under their jurisdiction abroad to respect human rights in all their global activities. we also offer a label certifying that human rights are respected in third countries during the manufacture of a product. the aim is clearly to promote the own enterprises, as opposed to the still too many enterprises which are unscrupulous about the working conditions of their workers throughout the world.
in writing. – i voted in favour of this resolution, since i want these rules to become binding and enforceable towards corporations, and since eu technologies are still causing human rights violations. the eu is founded on the values of respect for human dignity, freedom, democracy, equality, the rule of law and respect for human rights, including the rights of persons belonging to minorities. i strongly believe in these values and as a liberal, i believe that everyone should be treated fairly, also in the working environment. i agree that a global holistic approach to corporate liability for human rights abuses is still lacking.
in writing. ‒ the full integration of liquefied natural gas and gas storage will make a major contribution to the goal of a crisis-proof energy union in the future. for this purpose, priority should be given to market-based solutions and the use of existing lng infrastructure. in particular, a careful analysis of the alternatives and options for the supply of lng at regional level should be preferred to a decision on new infrastructure. this would make more efficient use of the existing infrastructure.
in writing. ‒ i have approved this report, which first recalls that the eu strategy for liquefied natural gas and gas storage is an element of the energy union. it calls for better use of existing liquefied natural gas and gas storage capacities, increased cooperation to build new facilities and stronger support for less connected regions to diversify sources of supply.
in writing. the eu has the ambition to become a world leader in sustainable energy use in the long term. it will do so in stages, including by developing a shock-resistant energy union that includes liquefied gas and gas storage. an eu strategy for liquefied gas and its storage is also vital to reduce our energy dependence on foreign suppliers. that way we can guarantee that the customer can still pay the bill. but natural gas remains a fossil fuel, and its use contributes to the warming of our climate. that is why i have, with some colleagues, proposed a number of amendments to this report which place the energy challenge in the wider environmental context. in those amendments we emphasize that the eu's energy policy must be in line with the paris environmental agreements. the ambition is to limit global warming to 1.5°c. by focusing on reducing demand, optimising energy efficiency and phasing out the use of fossil fuels, including gas, we are strengthening europe's climate and energy goals.
in writing. ‒ let us say it straight away: it is regrettable that the european union uses only 20% of its liquefied natural gas (lng) import capacity. diversifying your sources of supply is always a winning choice in the long run. there are certainly objective reasons for this situation, such as the uneven distribution of the locations of methane terminals on european territory. this should not prevent the union from having a genuine strategy for liquefied natural gas and gas storage. this is a political choice which must be made if the eu is to be more competitive and less dependent in the future, especially on russian gas. the gyürk report adopted this afternoon also underlines the importance for the union of initiating this rapid transition to a sustainable energy system. but this race to lng must not be carried out without caution or control. we all know that natural gas is a fossil fuel which can emit large quantities of methane which is harmful to the ozone layer. this is one reason, if any, to place the energy union strategy within the broader framework of the paris agreement climate goals, with a focus on reducing demand and improving energy efficiency.

in writing. i welcome the adoption by the european parliament of this resolution on the harmonisation of fisheries controls across europe. inspection procedures too often suffer from differences which can lead to discrimination in their implementation by the member states. parliament therefore called for greater harmonisation of national control methods. it proposes, in particular, to harmonise penalties for infringements (including the criminal or administrative nature of such penalties) and to introduce uniform training for fisheries inspectors at european level. these recommendations of the european parliament should be taken fully into account in order to avoid any feeling of discrimination against certain fishermen.
in writing. ‒ how can fisheries controls be made more uniform across europe? this is a very important question to which the european parliament tried to give an answer this afternoon by approving the thomas report. the current situation is not satisfactory insofar as there is real or perceived inequality among fishermen in terms of factors as varied as the regularity, rigor, duration, intensity, effectiveness and methods of fisheries controls in europe. among the obstacles to effective controls, the text pointed out that some member states organised checks from machine to plate and others only on certain links in the chain, excluding for example the transport or catering part. the resolution also calls for the eu to take action to ensure that the eu's fishing fleet is not disrupted by the introduction of new fishing gear. the european parliament is also realistic and calls, above all, for the full implementation of regulation (ec) no 1224/2009 on fisheries control. the commission also stressed the need for greater flexibility in the application of the landing obligation, which represents a radical change for fishermen.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this european parliament resolution, which proposes several ways of making fisheries controls more homogeneous. the text, which is part of the revision of the fisheries control regulation, proposes, for example, to harmonise the scope of application of existing community legislation and sanctions or to set up genuine european training for fisheries controllers. these recommendations are in the right direction: to establish true equality between all european fishermen.
in writing. - i agree with my colleague isabelle thomas on this matter. fishermen often complain that fisheries controls are much stricter in their own country than in their neighbours, whether in another member state or in another fishery. fishermen also say that they are the most regulated profession in the world. this feeling of injustice raises a real question: that of the homogeneity of the application of the regulation and, therefore, of its effectiveness. for if it is possible to suspect that the rules are not applied with the same rigor, it is to be feared that we will reach a situation where the rule is no longer respected because it is not the same for everyone. the aim is twofold: to identify the shortcomings in the application of the rules that lead to this sense of inequality and to propose solutions to improve the harmonisation of control of the common fisheries policy, one of the most integrated policies in europe.

in writing. ‒ the eu must address all breaches of democracy, the rule of law and fundamental rights, including those occurring in the member states without a strict link to eu secondary law. however, recent events in hungary, poland and some other member states show that there are gaps in european legislation. there is currently no instrument that meets parliament's legitimate demand for the existing procedures to be applied on a permanent basis to all member states. the report therefore proposes a system of permanent monitoring of the situation in the member states, with a prominent role for independent experts. this panel of experts will be set up under the control of the commission and will present a report each year analysing the situation in all member states. the report must then be approved by the commission, after which the council and parliament will debate it. the commission shall then decide whether the infringement procedure should be initiated. the system proposed in this report is a suitable starting point for good negotiations with the commission and the council of ministers. it is a first step in the right direction and that is why i support the report.

in writing. ‒ europe has a long tradition of democracy, the rule of law and citizens' rights. these concepts, which originated with athenian democracy, are found in roman law, the magna carta of 1215, the declaration of the rights of man and of the citizen of 1789, the european convention on human rights and, finally, the charter of fundamental rights. moreover, the european union enshrines them among its essential principles and objectives, set out in the first articles of the treaties, and in the criteria for accession to the union. while attempts to include a reference to europe's judeo-christian roots in the treaties have been unsuccessful, they nevertheless affirm that the union is perceived as a community of shared values. in its external actions, the union puts human rights and democratic governance at the forefront, and migrants arriving in europe are asked to respect and embrace our common values.

on behalf of the group of the european right i support the resolution before us. you are right, commissioner. scientific research has shown that excessive intake of trans fatty acids significantly increases the risk of cardiovascular disease. although the intake of trans fatty acids in the eu is generally quite low, we find a particularly high concentration in certain diets. so a thoughtful approach is required. the experience of denmark and other countries, as we have just heard, shows that a binding limit value is an effective instrument. the danish measure has a demonstrable positive effect on public health without a negative impact on the food sector. i also think that a limit value is a realistic measure. it is not a question of zero tolerance. allowing a minimum will avoid the complete exclusion of natural trans fats. finally, i would like to stress that a trans fat measure should naturally be part of an integrated approach to healthy nutrition and can be compatible with other agreements, such as voluntary agreements. i am also convinced that a constructive dialogue with the sector is essential and necessary to achieve a good result.
in writing. cardiovascular disease, infertility, alzheimer's disease, diabetes and obesity are the risks faced by the european citizen who consumes excessive amounts of trans fatty acids in his diet. the problem is that only 30% of consumers know what a trans fatty acid (tfa) is, exposing the other two thirds of europeans to potentially serious medical problems. that is why, by voting this afternoon, we want clear labelling, but that is not enough: we must also limit the presence of these acids. the consumption of agts increases the risk of cardiovascular disease, especially coronary heart disease, which is estimated to cause some 660 000 deaths in europe each year, or 14% of all european mortality. the text we have voted today therefore supports the imposition of mandatory limits on industrially produced trans-fatty acids which are excessively present in the diet. we cannot accept that citizens put their health at risk any longer. in the absence of national legislation in many countries, europe must take the lead.
for the greens/efa group mr president, indignation, protest and rejection are what the european project is increasingly attracting from too many of our fellow citizens. some people here would like to see it as a sign of identity retreat. but this anger is first and foremost a cry for help against policies that are increasingly out of touch with the public interest. it is quite symbolic when the epicentre of the protest is in wallonia, the host country and one of the most pro-european and supportive regions of the union. all this is about a free trade agreement with canada, which was the main topic of last week's european council. this is not by chance: for three years now, free trade agreements have been the subject of a new kind of citizen mobilization in french-speaking belgium. under this pressure, the french-speaking elected representatives of belgium seized the ceta and dissected it as few in europe have done. all this led to a reasoned resolution in may 2015 on the initiative of the greens, expressing very serious reservations about a ceta designed to assert the supremacy of a chimerical right to profit over all other rights and the power of companies, their shareholders and their leaders over that of democracy. far from being the troublemaker of europe, wallonia has now become the representative of all citizens who reject a commercial policy in the service of multinationals. no, contrary to what we are led to believe, wallonia is not isolated, quite the contrary. is it necessary to recall that 1 500 european towns and cities have declared themselves outside ttip and ceta, that 3 400 000 petitioners reject the project of arbitration between investors and states, that a majority of austrians, germans, french and slovenians are opposed to ceta? the response of the commission and the european governments was a four-stroke waltz. first, there was the denial of the letter from the minister-president of wallonia expressing the reservations of his parliament. then came the condescension: "if you disagree with us, you have not understood, so we will explain it to you again". then there was the intimidation: wallonia has two days to decide, mr tusk. finally, there was the tinkering with a jumble of statements of dubious legal value which added to the confusion of opacity. the pressure exerted by the walloons to lift the block on ceta contrasts sharply with their silence in the face of the block on the part of some member states, some of which are much less populated than wallonia - let me tell you this - on, for example, the fight against tax evasion or financial regulation. even more sickening is the stark contrast in the decisions of the european council last week, mr tusk. between the frantic free trade bias and a migration policy whose key words have become refoulement and keeping at a distance. the european union's heads of state or government, for example, believe that goods, services and finance should be able to move freely, but especially not human beings. a few weeks ago, before the failed summit in bratislava, you said, mr tusk: 'european citizens want to know whether the political elites are able to take europe that protects, preserves our european way of life and empowers our citizens. take advantage of the opportunity that the french-speaking people of belgium offer the commission and the european governments. the european union is committed to the principle of subsidiarity and the principle of subsidiarity must be respected. affirm their right to decide freely which activities will be entrusted to the public service and which will be entrusted to the market; finally, you can remove all doubts about the compatibility of this treaty with european law by referring it to the court of justice of the european union. will it take time? yes, it is the time of democracy. you know, we have, for centuries, traded with canada without ceta. so what does a few more months matter? the walloon surge must be the occasion, ladies and gentlemen, not of a halt to the union's trade policy, but of its reversal, because most of our fellow citizens are not opposed to trade. in the 21st century, the objective of trade agreements cannot be to maximize flows, because that is incompatible with environmental constraints. it cannot be maximising profit for the few, because that is not the role of politics. their primary objective must be to promote the highest standards of social, environmental, health, fiscal and democratic standards. these standards set the binding framework within which trade can develop. trade policy can no longer be decided in secret. on the contrary, the terms of office must be decided in full transparency and negotiations must be conducted under the constant supervision of the elected representatives. it is only under these conditions, and i conclude, mr president, that this trade policy will regain the confidence of our citizens. the walloon no in writing. ‒ this directive aims to introduce new accessibility rules to ensure that public sector websites and mobile applications are accessible to all. the aim of this directive is to enable people with disabilities or the elderly in particular to have access to information and services on the internet without barriers. this can be done by providing subtitles to videos, offering image enlargement programs, or creating tools that allow you to use a computer without a mouse. i welcome this proposal.
in writing. ‒ this proposal for a directive concerns the accessibility of the content of public sector bodies' websites and of websites operated by entities carrying out public tasks for all users, and in particular for disabled and elderly persons. i voted in favour of this text because it seems important that all european citizens should be able to benefit from the information they need in their interactions with public administration. in order to achieve this objective, this proposal for a directive aims to approximate the laws, regulations and administrative practices of the member states. it lays down minimum requirements for the websites and mobile applications of public sector bodies while ensuring that they do not impose a disproportionate burden on those bodies. member states will also have to encourage and facilitate training programmes on the accessibility of websites and mobile applications.
in writing. i voted in favour of this resolution which aims to make websites and applications of public administrations, hospitals, courts and other public sectors more accessible to people with disabilities and older people. these sites and applications used on mobile devices will now have to meet common accessibility standards. public services will now have to provide and regularly update a detailed, comprehensive and clear accessibility statement on the compliance of their websites and applications with these standards. a reporting mechanism should also be put in place to allow users to indicate problems and to request specific information if the content is not accessible. however, certain types of content are excluded from the scope of the directive. this is content that is not necessary in administrative procedures.
in writing. the number of websites providing e-government services (approximately 380 500 in the union) and public sector websites (over 761 000 in the union) is increasing rapidly. most member states have already adopted legislative or other measures on web accessibility. however, there are still considerable differences between these laws and measures. however, non-harmonised national approaches to web accessibility create barriers within the european internal market. this directive aims to approximate the laws, regulations and administrative practices of the member states as regards the accessibility requirements for the websites and mobile applications of public sector bodies, in order to improve the functioning of the internal market. it lays down rules under which member states are to ensure that websites, irrespective of the device used to access them, and mobile applications of public sector bodies comply with accessibility requirements by making them perceptible, usable, understandable and robust. i therefore welcome this objective of harmonisation.
in writing. ‒ the european parliament today approved a new directive ensuring that public sector bodies' websites are always accessible to people with disabilities. the report also calls for the eu to take action to combat terrorism and to ensure that the eu is able to take action to combat terrorism. the daily struggle of the blind, the deaf, and the physically handicapped will thus soon be over. with this new directive, citizens with visual impairments will, for example, hear descriptions of images when using a screen reader, and hearing impaired people will see subtitles for audiovisual files if they access public sector bodies' websites within the union. accessibility for all citizens will now be the law of the land in europe for all government websites and applications. since the promotion of equality must not stop at the digital door, it is important to consider the next step already, namely to consider the adoption of a legislative act on the accessibility of the private sector web (online commerce, banking and insurance) for people with disabilities.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this draft legislative resolution on the council's position at first reading on the directive on the accessibility of public sector bodies' websites and mobile applications. the directive will improve the accessibility of public sector bodies' websites and mobile applications for people with disabilities. this is essential as more than 80 million people in the union are affected by disability and is part of the european disability strategy 2010-2020 and article 9 of the un convention on the rights of persons with disabilities. its forthcoming entry into force underlines europe's will to play a leading role in this area.
in writing. ‒ far too many public sector websites and mobile applications are not yet accessible to all. in europe, 15% of the total population, or 80 million disabled or elderly citizens, suffer from this condition. filing a tax return, applying for unemployment benefits, paying a bill, or enrolling a child in school becomes a grueling adventure. after the european parliament's vote this afternoon, public administrations, hospitals, courts, universities or other public sector bodies will be forced to be fully accessible on the internet or through mobile applications.
in writing. ‒ the council's position indicates that the accessibility of websites is of great importance to public authorities, as it enables them to increase their reach and fulfil their public tasks. the number of websites offering egovernment services (approximately 380 500 in the eu) and public sector websites (over 761 000 in the eu) is growing rapidly. most member states have already adopted legislation or other measures in the area of web accessibility. however, there are major differences between these laws and measures. the proposal aims to harmonise the national legislation of the member states in order to remove obstacles to the internal market. this proposal on the harmonisation of national public sector measures at eu level was supported by me.
in writing. ‒ parliament had adopted a regulation to curb the introduction and spread of plant pests such as the olive tree killer bacterium xylella fastidiosa. the new regulation, which i welcome, introduces preventive and rapid reaction mechanisms for suspect plant imports, intensifies pest control efforts in the eu and requires all member states to draw up outbreak plans.
in writing. ‒ the eu's regulatory framework for plant health aims to protect european agriculture and forestry by preventing the entry and spread of non-indigenous pests. however, the current regulatory framework suffers from some limitations in view of new challenges linked to globalised trade and climate change such as the more frequent arrival of new pests and the establishment of organisms that previously did not survive in europe. given the importance of establishing a regulatory framework capable of protecting the health of our citizens as well as our economy, i therefore voted in favour of this proposal for a directive. the commission proposes to redefine the rules for determining the phytosanitary risk posed by any species, strain or biotype of pathogenic agent, animal or plant parasite harmful to plants or plant products and the measures to reduce this risk to an acceptable level. in particular, member states will have to draw up and maintain a separate plan for each priority quarantine facility likely to enter and establish itself on their territory. the text also provides for the modernisation of trade-related plant health instruments (in particular through improved traceability in the internal market).
in writing. ‒ the european parliament has given the green light to new measures to improve plant protection against diseases. the council has already reached agreement on this. the nva delegation supports this agreement. the regulation is part of a package of measures designed to strengthen health and safety standards throughout the agri-food chain. a european approach is needed here: pests and diseases do not stop at the border. a well-known example is xylella fastidiosa, a wood-eating bacterium that infects olive trees. the new rules should enable member states to take decisions more quickly, react more quickly and cooperate better. moreover, it is a balanced and proportionate agreement which avoids unnecessary administrative burdens and does not unnecessarily impede free trade.
in writing. ‒ parliament endorsed this afternoon a common position agreed with the european council to better prevent the entry of plant pests into europe and to improve the control of possible epidemics. insects, fungi, bacteria and other viruses can cause serious damage to crops and crops, a trade worth €201 billion in europe (€7.4 billion in belgium). we remember xylella fastidiosa, which devastated nearly 30,000 hectares of olive groves in the italian region of puglia in 2014. the new rules will strengthen the european plant health regime around three axes. particular attention will be paid to prevention, to assess plants at risk from third countries more rapidly and upstream. better control instruments will be put in place against the spread of parasites that have managed to reach european territory, in particular through mandatory national emergency plans. the practice of plant passports will be extended to all plants intended for sale in europe in order to enhance the traceability of movements within the internal market and the safety of consumers and producers alike.
in writing. ‒ i voted against the alde group amendment to the legislative resolution, which aimed to reject the council's position at first reading with a view to adopting the regulation of the european parliament and of the council on protective measures against organisms harmful to plants, amending regulations (eu) no 228/2013, (eu) no 652/2014 and (eu) no 1143/2014 of the european parliament and of the council and repealing council directives 69/464/eec, 74/647/eec, 93/85/eec, 98/57/ec, 2000/29/ec, 2006/91/ec and 2007/33/ec. given the scale of such phenomena, it was appropriate to confirm the agreement reached by the european parliament and the council. these new measures are essential because they will harmonise the existing plant passport regime and will make it possible to eradicate early outbreaks of pests more effectively.
in writing. ‒ i have of course voted in favour of the text proposed by my colleague mr mcintyre on the council's position at first reading with a view to adopting a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on protective measures against organisms harmful to plants, amending regulations (eu) no 228/2013, (eu) no 652/2014 and (eu) no 1143/2014 of the european parliament and of the council and repealing council directives 69/464/eec, 74/647/eec, 93/85/eec, 98/57/ec, 2000/29/ec, 2006/91/ec and 2007/33/ec.
in writing. ‒ i did not agree with the council's position because a total ban on imports is not proportionate to the risk. i believe that a system is being created which makes it too easy for member states to ban imports of virtually all plants and plant products on the basis of too weak a prior assessment. in addition, the resulting bureaucratic hassle for traders would lead to a significant increase in costs and trade disruption, and threaten eu trade in plants (worth some eur 30 billion). we must ensure that our commercial interests are not harmed by very broad precautions.
in writing. – i voted against the council position on this issue. imports of plants products and material should be analysed using a risk-based approach. there is a restriction on the import, in order to not allow import of diseases.

in writing. in a common space, such as the european union, it is essential that member states coordinate their economic and budgetary policies in order to ensure a certain degree of cohesion. the annual european semester phase is essential at this level if we are to restart growth and create jobs. i would like to stress once again the need to strengthen the major european projects under way such as the banking union, the capital union and even the energy union. in any case, what is striking is the glaring lack of investment. the european union has a major role to play here, notably through the juncker plan, which must be strengthened if the european economy is to boost. but we also need to look for other alternatives that complement it in order to create a dynamic framework that allows investors to feed the european economy. as regards the budgetary positions of the member states, i would once again call on the commission to ensure a certain flexibility in order to allow member states to invest in both tangible and intangible assets if such expenditure guarantees greater growth.

in writing. ‒ the resolution aims, among other things, to introduce binding limits for industrial trans-fatty acids (tfa) in food. tfs increase the risk of cardiovascular disease, infertility, alzheimer's disease, diabetes and obesity, and are mainly contained in industrially produced partially cured vegetable oils. i am in favour of the introduction of such a limit. in denmark, the introduction in 2003 of an industrial tfs cap limiting the tfs content in oils and fats to 2% has significantly reduced the number of deaths due to cardiovascular disease.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution which stresses the need to reduce trans fatty acids (tfa) in food and therefore considers it necessary to take ad hoc measures both at european and national level. the committee also welcomed the commission's proposal to introduce a new system of labelling for foodstuffs containing egt, which would be more effective in reducing the consumption of egt in the eu.
in writing. ‒ people who eat foods high in industrial trans fats are three times more likely to die from cardiovascular disease. moreover, the current, separate approach in the different member states leads to complex regulations for european companies. in addition to reducing the amount of trans fatty acids, there is also a need for greater awareness of the risks. in belgium we have had these trans fats under control for several years, but the import of foodstuffs has not solved the problem. they are also more common in cheaper food, making them more likely to affect certain groups of the population. the european commission must now come up with binding limit values within two years.
in writing. it would be good to eliminate trans fats from our diet. trans fatty acids do not contribute to a better nutritional value or a higher quality of the diet. on the contrary, the consumption of trans fats in the diet is a huge risk to our health, and trans fats have been shown to increase the risk of cardiovascular disease, alzheimer's disease, diabetes and obesity. consumers are barely aware of the health risks of trans fatty acids. it seems plausible that labelling, even mandatory labelling, could lead to a change in consumer behaviour. however, in my view, this does not guarantee a reduction in consumption and hence in health risks. the resolution also calls for better information to be given to consumers about the risks through other channels and for maximum standards to be imposed on food manufacturers for the use of these harmful fats. in denmark, a maximum standard of 2% is applied for trans fatty acids. the positive health effects of this have now been clearly demonstrated. in the us, trans fats will be banned from foods in 2018. so if we want to do a service to public health and preserve the export opportunities for quality food to the usa, we would do well to limit the use of trans fats in food.
in writing. ‒ the european parliament adopted a resolution this afternoon by an overwhelming majority of 586 votes to 19 to limit trans fats in the diet as much as possible. these added industrial fatty acids are bad for our health, raising bad cholesterol and putting us at greater risk of developing cardiovascular disease, diabetes, obesity and so on. agts are found in large quantities in products as varied as snacks, ice cream, pastries, frozen pizzas and margarines. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'common carrier' to cover the transport of dangerous goods by road. these, according to the doctors, are not a problem. it is hoped that the commission will soon make a proposal based on today's vote to limit the presence of agt in oils and fats to 2%. the european union would thus translate across the 28 member states the ambitious policies put in place in denmark in 2003 and in three other member states since then, which have reduced the number of deaths caused by cardiovascular diseases.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution on industrially produced trans fatty acids (tfa) calling for community action to reduce their general consumption. the european union has adopted a new food law on the labelling of foodstuffs containing agt.
in writing. ‒ trans fatty acids are a type of unsaturated fatty acids which, unlike unsaturated fats, are not good for health. they occur naturally in ruminants, whose gut bacteria naturally harden these fats. it is mainly the industrially produced, partially cured vegetable oils that have a negative effect on cardiovascular diseases. trans fats are mainly found in baking and braising fats, frying oils and hard margarines, and are found in pastries, cakes and snacks. every year, 660,000 people die of heart disease or vascular disease, which is 14% of all deaths. in a report of december 2015, which follows on from regulation 1169/2011, the european commission shows awareness of the problem, considers different options to limit the use of trans fats and points out the consequences of this ban, but does not make a legislative proposal. the resolution i co-approved today reiterates the call for a serious reduction in industrial trans fats for all sections of the population. although the christian democrats are satisfied with the clearer labelling of these trans fats on foodstuffs, the resolution clearly advocates the limitation of industrial trans fats. studies show that cutting down on trans fats leads to health gains very quickly.
in writing. ‒ cardiovascular disease, infertility, alzheimer's disease, diabetes and obesity are the risks faced by the european citizen if he consumes excessive amounts of trans fatty acids in his diet. the problem is that only 30% of consumers know what a trans fatty acid (tfa) is, exposing the other two thirds of europeans to potentially serious medical problems. that is why, by voting this afternoon, we want clear labelling. but this is not enough: the presence of these acids must also be limited. in the text voted today, we therefore support the imposition of mandatory limits on industrially produced trans fats which are excessively present in the diet. we cannot accept that citizens put their health at risk any longer. the lack of national legislation in many countries means that europe must take the lead.
in writing. ‒ trans fats are unsaturated fatty acids that are not good for health. it is mainly the industrially produced trans fats that have a negative effect on cardiovascular diseases. trans fats are mainly found in baking and braising fats, frying oils and hard margarines, and are found in pastries, cakes and snacks. the resolution we adopted reiterates the call for a serious reduction in industrial trans fats for all sections of the population.

in writing. security in the world has deteriorated considerably, due in particular to global and multidimensional threats. the international community must redouble its efforts to achieve the objectives of the treaty on the non-proliferation of nuclear weapons (npt), which aims in particular to eliminate nuclear arsenals and to prevent new states from acquiring nuclear weapons. but, as mr ban ki-moon said, multilateral nuclear disarmament has reached a dead end. tens of billions of dollars are spent on maintaining and improving nuclear weapons systems. thus, in defiance of the international community, north korea is increasing its nuclear tests in order to build up a nuclear arsenal and ballistic missiles. it is our duty, for the good of humanity, to prevent these weapons from spreading across the world, thanks to scientific and technological progress. the npt, although not perfect, is a means of combating the establishment of anarchy in the world. it is therefore essential that the union strongly reaffirms its commitment to ensuring security in the world. the next round of review of the treaty on the non-proliferation of nuclear weapons will begin in 2017. the world cannot afford another cycle of inaction.

in writing. ‒ global security, and in particular that of the eu, has deteriorated significantly: she's more erratic and less predictable. international peace, security and stability are facing a variety of developments: the commission has also been asked to provide information on the situation in the former yugoslavia, the deteriorating relations between nuclear-armed states such as russia and the united states and further developments in north korea's nuclear capabilities. the proliferation of nuclear weapons of mass destruction remains one of the major concerns of the global community. for these reasons and in the public interest, the european parliament is proposing a resolution to address these problems and to encourage the european union to take action in the field of nuclear safety and non-proliferation. the priorities include preventing the acquisition or use of nuclear weapons by terrorists or by additional states, reducing and eliminating all nuclear arsenals and working towards a world without nuclear weapons. the resolution also highlights important developments and concerns and makes some compelling recommendations. as nuclear safety and non-proliferation are extremely important issues for me and for the green group as a whole, i have co-signed this resolution and adopted it with full conviction.

mr president, i am going to raise a dissonant voice here in relation to all the colleagues i have heard so far. i am a supporter of the time change, and especially of daylight saving time. why would you do that? because when i was 13 years old and at school at the collège saint-roch de ferrières in belgium, after the easter holidays of 1976, the time change was applied for the first time. thanks to daylight saving time, we were able to play football and basketball in the sports fields that had no lights. from this real-life example, i just wanted to tell you that the lighting later in the evening allows children in particular - and it is good for their health - to stay a little more outside in physical activity, while leisure activities - we know - have become very sedentary. the second benefit is the terraces and the conviviality. instead of swallowing pills to fight depression, let's sit on a deck, it's the best antidepressant. it's good for business and for people to talk to each other. therefore, the change to daylight saving time makes it easier to get along with people. it's not the merchants who will contradict us. there are other benefits to returning to daylight saving time. as mrs reid has just said, wintertime is the best time to take advantage of natural daylight. when the sunlight is less, the return to daylight saving time allows for a little earlier morning light and therefore perhaps more safety, especially on the way to school. that is why i think harmonization is obviously useful. we know that the united kingdom has often made different choices. it's normal, the greenwich meridian passes through his territory. i was listening to the canary islands being mentioned earlier. since they are at 28 degrees west latitude, it makes sense that they have a different time. however, harmonization throughout europe and a simultaneous change from wintertime to summertime and vice versa are obviously fundamental. don't change anything tell mr. timmermans he can sit on that file, too. let's not change anything! the ecb is perhaps the only central bank in the world, and perhaps in history, to have become a political body to such a large extent. it is perhaps the only central bank that has extended its mandate to the point of becoming a de facto political body, but without any democratic control, which is perhaps the purpose of all this. i mean, it makes sense that evolution would happen. where a normal central bank is an instrument of a political government, the central bank operates in the eurozone, a zone that has no real political authority. it operates in an area where political authority is being reconstructed in some way or the appearance of it is being given by a stability pact, by a european semester, by a banking union, by a deposit insurance scheme and so on. this is an attempt to compensate for the fact that in the eurozone, in the european union, there is no political authority to justify the existence of a single currency. keeping that vehicle on track, along with all the money you are pumping into it, along with the funds that are to be used for that, a vehicle that is doomed from the start to collapse, that keeping it on track is the stage we are at now, with an ecb that has become more and more part of the political mandate that it has given, that it has actually given itself. the promise to do 'whatever is necessary', quantitative easing, the purchase of securities or worthless securities, the powers of attorney, the special powers which the ecb can use without fear of much control: this is a situation that is causing fear among the citizens. the aim was to stimulate inflation, but this led to deflation. growth would be encouraged, but there is almost a growth stop that carries all the risks that the debt bubble you have created yourself would burst. the lack of trust among the people is something we can fully understand.

in writing. with the arrival of trump it is becoming increasingly clear that we will no longer be able to automatically count on the support of the us for our security. we are now approaching the moment when we must work on a concerted effort and coordination of our police and military services to combat the terrorist threat effectively and to guard our external borders effectively. bilateral cooperation projects should be the stepping stone to programmes where we coordinate european defence efforts even more. the belgian-dutch renewal of the defence fleet is already a good example. the eu-28 spends €195 billion on defence every year. if we can better match these costs, we can save up to 26 billion euros and therefore use them more wisely. the battle groups must evolve into permanent multinational corps under a single european command. they should not only be used for peacekeeping operations but should form a single bloc within nato which can act when nato is unwilling or unable to do so. europe is still a peace project and resolves conflicts primarily at the negotiating table. but in times of crisis, we must send a clear signal that we are ready to act as one. don't mess with europe.
in a few months' time we shall be celebrating 25 years of the maastricht treaty. that treaty laid down how the member states are responsible for their social policies, for their economic policies and that they must carry out those policies within the budgetary framework we have agreed together. it is up to the european commission to ensure that these rules are respected, that everyone stays within the lines of the chalk and to impose sanctions when necessary. i think we must return to the logic of the maastricht treaty. the accounts must be in order and we must hold those member states which refuse to cooperate to account. we must also be able to impose sanctions on these member states, to take them out of the eurozone if necessary. but what do we see? that the european commission today does not seem to be planning to celebrate the maastricht treaty, but rather to bury it. what she's proposing doesn't fit within the agreed framework. the commission sees itself as a kind of european finance ministry. it is proposing matters for which it has no competence, but above all it is proposing matters which are not sensible. our structural problems, as mr hökmark has already said, will not melt away. we cannot buy growth on the cheap. in the short term, that might help us, but in the long term, it just creates more problems. besides, it's perfectly possible to save smart and grow smart. we see this in countries like the netherlands, germany and austria. that is precisely the path we must take with this european union.

in writing. i welcome the approval by the european parliament of the amendment to the regulation establishing a long-term plan for cod stocks and the fisheries exploiting those stocks. the updated regulation, which is now in line with the new common fisheries policy (cfp), will ensure that all catches are complied with. by removing the provisions on the calculation of fishing effort, the new regulation puts an end to incentives to discard catches at sea and thus allows fishermen to fully comply with the discard ban as required by the european fisheries policy. this is therefore a further step towards the responsible and sustainable management of our fisheries resources.
in writing. ‒ this afternoon, parliament approved the update of a 2008 regulation for a long-term plan for more rational fishing and better conservation of cod stocks. this fish, which is widespread in the atlantic and in our european waters, has been threatened by overfishing and intensive exploitation for years. europe accounts for 70% of the world cod market and the state of stocks in the north sea and ireland and west of scotland remains critical despite efforts already made. the amendments approved on tuesday will bring about a common method of calculating fishing effort for all member states and will relax catch limits while respecting scientific advice. the aim is to reduce the incentive to discard fish of lower value, which then have a low survival rate. the restriction of this practice should promote better management of the ichthyans and better use of exploited marine resources, and ensure the sustainability of a whole part of the european economy, since the fisheries and fish processing sector employs more than 350 000 people.
