in writing. ‒ on the basis of the annual report of the european central bank, the european parliament shall draw up an annual report on the activities of the european system of central banks and on the monetary policy of the eurosystem. the main tasks of the escb, which include ensuring price stability and supporting the general economic policies of the union, are the central themes of the ecb's annual report and parliament's response to it. in addition, the main issues for the calendar year 2015 were the recovery of the euro area economy, the persistently low inflation rate, the effects of low interest rates and the ecb's decision to expand its asset purchase programme. i have agreed to the report, which also criticises the ecb's actions, and i hope that the ecb will take note of these criticisms.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report which gives a general assessment of the ecb's monetary policies, with clear references to the asset purchase programme (app), the main refinancing operations (mros) and the targeted longer-term refinancing operations (tltros i and ii). the report underlines that the euro area continues to suffer from high unemployment, excessively low inflation, large macroeconomic imbalances, including current account imbalances, and very low productivity growth as a consequence of lack of investment. this clear reference to the lack of investment is a point on which we have insisted. the report calls for the completion and full implementation of the banking union, the building of a capital markets union and a solution to the problem of non-performing loans to improve the effectiveness of the single monetary policy and mitigate the risks of a financial sector shock.
in writing. the situation remains worrying. the euro area continues to suffer from high unemployment, too low inflation, very low levels of productivity growth and a lack of structural reforms. in addition, there is a high level of public debt and an undercapitalised banking sector. it was therefore essential that the ecb continue the extraordinary measures in order to bring inflation back to the medium-term target of 2%. the ecb is now fulfilling its role of doing everything it can to defend the euro. but that alone will not be enough. we need to strengthen structural reforms in the eu, implement the banking union and create a capital markets union.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the european parliament resolution on the european central bank's annual report 2015. in this report, the european parliament underlines its fears that the ecb is downplaying the link between the central bank's provision of liquidity to banks and lending to the real economy. banks must take their share of responsibility in reviving our economy. the report also stresses the need for structural reforms, given the average performance of some euro area countries, particularly in terms of employment. on this point i am very clear: these reforms must not weaken the workers in any way. on the contrary, it is crucial to secure the careers of our european workers and to provide support for those who are out of work.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the european central bank's annual report for 2015. the euro area continues to suffer from high unemployment, excessively low inflation and still significant macroeconomic imbalances, including excessive current account imbalances. in addition, it is faced with a very low level of productivity growth, which results in particular from the absence of investment - 10 percentage points below pre-crisis levels - a lack of structural reforms and weak domestic demand. the high level of public debt, and in particular the huge volume of non-performing loans in the banking sector, as well as a still undercapitalised banking sector in some member states, continue to fragment the euro area financial market, reducing the room for manoeuvre to support the most fragile economies. only sound fiscal policy and socially balanced structural reforms aimed at boosting productivity can bring about sustained positive economic development in these member states.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour because the ecb supports the framework for simple, transparent and standardised securitisation and the resulting lower capital requirements, which will revitalise both the securitisation markets and the financing of the real economy.
in writing. – i voted in favour of this resolution since i support the role that the ecb has of defending the euro. i support the gradual implementation of the full banking union and i also believe that the distortion of competition has to be avoided. as a liberal i support transparency, so i believe that there has to be more information on asset purchases. in this time of economic and political turmoil, the credibility of the european central bank is fundamental in order to make the european economy work. i believe that the ecb has to analyse the different situations across member states before the implementation of new monetary policies, and thus analyse which member state relies more on banks or capital markets for the financing of the economy, in order to prevent bad impacts on those economies. i agree that single monetary policies alone cannot stimulate aggregate demand unless it is complemented by efficient fiscal policies and socially balanced reform programmes at member state level.
in writing. ‒ the objective of this report is to further develop the internal market for financial services for retail customers. it is important to identify the specific obstacles faced by consumers and businesses in using the internal market and to develop solutions to overcome those obstacles. digitalisation is providing important impetus that can help to remove such barriers to cross-border activities. i voted in favour of the draft because the establishment of an internal market for financial services for private customers has not yet progressed sufficiently. it is therefore of particular importance that the choice of supply, transparency and competition be improved across borders to the benefit of the european consumer.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report which is the ep's contribution to the commission's green paper on retail financial services to prepare the action plan to be proposed in 2017, while supporting the commission's priority of identifying the specific obstacles faced by consumers and businesses and ways to overcome them. the report stresses the need to ensure good consumer protection through additional actions to empower consumers to make informed decisions, increase transparency in retail financial products and remove barriers, associated costs or product withdrawal. the report calls for full implementation of the various legislation already adopted (mortgage credit directive, payment accounts directive, payment services directive 2, mif regulation, insurance distribution directive) and calls on the commission to take further initiatives, including a proposal for an eu savings account, and to encourage financing of sustainable and green investments.
in writing. ‒ the european parliament today adopted by a large majority a report calling for more efforts to be made in the area of crossborder financial services for consumers. the european and national markets for pension, insurance and investment products, among others, are still too often characterised by fragmentation and lack of competition. this sometimes leads to consumers paying too high a price for their products or not being able to take full advantage of offers abroad. on the other hand, companies also face many obstacles when trying to find their way to the foreign customer. the report therefore calls on the commission to explore ways of encouraging cross-border demand and supply of consumer financial services. it is important that the commission should respect the social and fiscal powers of the member states. that is why the n-va meps voted in favour of this report.
in writing. i welcome the commission's green paper on retail financial services as it allows for a fruitful debate and public consultation of the various stakeholders involved, which will lead to better products, more choice and more opportunities for consumers and businesses. the green paper seeks to identify how to improve the supply, transparency and competition in the retail financial services sector for the benefit of european consumers, and how to enable firms to offer these financial services directly in other countries.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the own-initiative report on the european commission's green paper to combat the fragmentation of retail financial products. it is crucial to defend european consumers, in particular by ensuring that the products offered to them are transparent, simple and cost-effective. i had supported the amendment calling for the creation of a european consumer protection authority, which i considered to be a step towards better consumer protection. i therefore regret that this amendment was not adopted, but i have nevertheless decided to support this text, which contains some interesting elements.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this green paper. we have to make sure that everyone is included. financial exclusion is a serious and widespread problem in europe. life becomes very complicated for those who do not have access to at least the most essential financial services. we need to keep the perspective of inclusion in mind in everything we do in the retail financial services sector. a general and permanent objective must be to reduce exclusion. the new payment account directive, due to be fully implemented in the autumn, will give every consumer the right to have a basic payment account. while this is a big step in the right direction, it is far from enough. a much greater effort is needed. we have a lot of work to do. building a functioning single market for retail financial services is a huge project. at the same time, it is a worthwhile project. this is clearly a case where the european union is creating real added value.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour because a european market for retail financial services is only conceivable if it offers real added value to consumers by ensuring effective competition, accessibility and consumer protection, particularly in relation to products that are genuinely necessary for participation in economic life.
in writing. – i voted in favour of this resolution since i support the improvement of advice and information to investors. in my opinion it is important that the commission comes up with concrete proposals on eliminating identified obstacles and barriers to an internal retail finance market. as a liberal i believe in transparency, so i support the call on the commission to increase the consumer transparency framework, trying to reach a supervisory convergence between member states. the establishment of a european consumer protection authority can help in this task. i believe that there is a need to analyse the potentials of giving companies a greater regulatory flexibility in order to experiment and innovate, without disregarding consumer protection and safety.
in writing. ‒ this parliament resolution calls for eu member states to step up their security and defence cooperation in the face of an increase in hybrid threats, threats to energy security, cybersecurity or terrorism, paving the way for a european defence union. the resolution calls for spending 2% of gdp on defence, the deployment of multinational armed forces and the establishment of an eu headquarters for the planning and conduct of joint operations. the european council is also called upon to take a leading role in the design of a common union defence policy and to provide additional funding for its implementation. the house also called for a review of the common security and defence policy (csdp) and for closer cooperation between the eu and nato. i support the idea of extended union defence cooperation. the current developments present us with security policy challenges which we can only tackle effectively together.
in writing. ‒ given the different situations facing europe in its neighbourhood, closer cooperation between member states in defence matters is necessary. i therefore endorsed this report which encourages the european council to be the driving force behind the progressive definition of the edu and to provide financial resources for this purpose. the european council is invited to take concrete steps towards the harmonisation and standardisation of the union's armed forces in order to facilitate cooperation between armed forces under the umbrella of a new european defence union. parliament is urged to set up a full committee on security and defence to monitor the implementation of permanent structured cooperation.
in writing. today, european security is increasingly under threat. the surveillance of our borders raises many problems and uncertainties. the union is not equipped to deal with this range of defence threats. the last thirty years have been characterized by constant cuts in the defence budgets of the ems and occasional cooperation. there is no community of destiny without common defence. there can be no foreign policy without a defence policy of the union commensurate with its economic capacity. we need to be more coherent and bring our military forces together. we need to implement a new approach that takes into account the profoundly changed security environment and make the union a more important player in the field of security. europe can no longer rely on the us strategic shield. it must develop a defence and be the armed arm of nato. according to the european parliament's study on the cost of non-europe 2014-2019, the potential efficiency gains from better coordination at european level on security and defence could reach €26 billion.
in writing. ‒ the european parliament voted 369 to 255 with 70 abstentions to ask the council this afternoon for the means to develop a genuine european defence policy. the current geopolitical situation, the terrorist threats, but also the cost of non-europe in this area (€26 billion per year) make a defence union more necessary than ever. a recent survey shows that 66% of europeans (63% of belgians) want the union to do more in this area. with three weeks to go until a european summit on this issue, the report voted on today gives very clear directions to the council. member states should devote at least 2% of their gdp to defence, and establish multinational forces and a european headquarters to plan and command crisis management operations. equally important, especially in terms of employment and economies of scale, is the creation of the conditions for a military schengen area and the development of a european defence industry. the union must also work to better complement nato's action, and be ready to take its place when it does not wish to engage. all this is essential and should lead to a thorough review of the common security and defence policy.
in writing. ‒ a common security and defence policy (csdp) is high on the european agenda, but it is difficult to reach agreement on it between the different member states and political families. each report on this subject is a lengthy list of all the matters that have a direct or indirect bearing on military or defence matters. it's like a letter to santa claus. we are now seeing the outlines of a european army emerge, and then the desire to increase the defence budget so that there is money to invest in drones or military research. however, there is a constant lack of a clear vision of defence and security for the outside world or for foreign embassies. it is therefore difficult to vote in favour of such a report. the green group wants a common security and defence policy to focus on humanitarian missions, peacekeeping and crisis management rather than on warfare and defending our homeland. instead of increasing the defence budget, we should look at how we can use the 200 billion euros a year more efficiently: by joint procurement, joint military research and, above all, by increasing transparency in the 'military market' simply by respecting european public procurement rules. but this is in the deaf ears of many.
in writing. - i voted for the paet report. i also think that european defence is a good thing to bring about more coherence and also to enable some member states to reduce their military budgets in favour of an efficient union army.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour because the security situation in and around europe has deteriorated significantly over the past few years, posing difficult and unprecedented challenges that no country and no organisation can tackle alone.
in writing. – i voted in favour of this resolution because i believe that in europe a stronger security must be ensured. i agree with the idea of creating a recurrent council-type meeting between the ministers of defence from each member state, in order to sustain and coordinate better the defence union. given the recent terrorist attacks, citizens in europe are feeling more threatened than before. that is why the creation of a european defence union becomes very urgent. the creation of this union could also benefit smes, europe’s defence industry and capabilities, allowing positive consequences for growth and jobs. i believe that key eu stakeholders and companies will have to be involved in the european defence industry. since i am a strong supporter of research, i support the plan of creating an eu defence research programme. technological innovation is fundamental in this context in order to reach a more efficient and effective use of the defence and security budgets of each member state.
in writing. ‒ i have endorsed this report, which recalls that the transport of passengers by water in the context of coastal or maritime navigation represents a great potential in view of the available infrastructure and is an important factor in strengthening cohesion between the various regions of the european union. the commission is invited to finance better organised and more efficient integrated transport service projects to ensure the efficient and intermodal management of passenger transport.
in writing. europe's geography is characterised by relatively large bodies of water, which offer extraordinary prospects for water transport. whether ferry or cruise ship, they play an important role in the mobility of eu citizens. as many as 400 million people pass through eu ports every year, 120 million of whom are transported between ports in the same member state. however, the waterborne passenger transport sector faces multiple challenges and needs in terms of infrastructure, environment, operational processes, safety and port-city links. i therefore welcome this report, which aims to place greater emphasis on the environmental sustainability, safety and security, quality and accessibility of services of passenger transport by water in the transport policy agenda of the union and its member states.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on exploiting the potential of passenger water transport as passenger water transport plays a key role in enhancing the sustainability and efficiency of the european transport sector. improving the use of available capacity for passenger transport by water would reduce congestion and co2 emissions, but also improve air quality and transport services. the development of innovative technologies based on solar and wind energy would also make ships cleaner and more economical. moreover, the measures provided for in this legislation would help to revitalise the tourist potential of many regions of europe. finally, this legislation also provides for the enhancement of the safety of passengers carried by ships by ensuring that these ships meet the common safety standards of the union.
in writing. - i voted for the report. while water transport is already one of the most sustainable modes of transport, it is possible to make ships cleaner and more energy-efficient through investment in research and innovative technologies, for example in solar and wind energy, shore-based electricity and alternative fuels, while applying the principle of technological neutrality. this goes hand in hand with the availability and use of union resources, such as the cohesion, structural and regional funds, interreg, horizon 2020, the esm, the ten-t and the efsi.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour because in recent years there has been a trend towards intensive development of vessels for various waters, for example river and sea vessels, which meet the requirements for seagoing vessels and can also sail in shallow water.
in writing. ‒ this report aims to promote the effectiveness of development cooperation. it calls on all development actors to build on the commitments of the paris to busan agreements to make their efforts as effective as possible towards the ambitious goals of the 2030 agenda, while further promoting the optimal use of public and private development resources. as the world's largest donor of development aid, the eu has a particular responsibility to improve the effectiveness of eu aid worldwide and its accountability. i share the rapporteur's view that the eu should take a leading role in the global effort to advance the development effectiveness agenda and ensure that transparency, good governance and the rule of law remain a key concern in developing countries.
in writing. ‒ the report, which i endorsed, recalls that aid effectiveness principles have made a significant contribution to progress towards the millennium development goals in many countries, but that progress remains uneven. it also stressed that official development assistance could help to implement the principle of democratic ownership of aid by the countries concerned. the report also calls for the eu to take action to ensure that the eu's energy policy is not undermined by the threat of nuclear power. these are based in particular on sufficient funding for development policy, which must be put at the service of poverty eradication and the promotion of the sustainable development goals. but to do that, donors must meet their commitments, because there is a gap of more than two trillion dollars in aid to developing countries to meet the millennium development goals. the report also stresses the need to improve the transparency of development aid and to combat corruption in recipient countries, which poses a serious threat to democratic legitimacy and public support for development aid in donor countries.
in writing. ‒ today the n-va delegation voted to increase the effectiveness of development cooperation. we are aware that valuable resources are being lost at many levels, and we therefore call for less capital-intensive and more efficient development cooperation. however, in order to achieve this, our delegation believes it is essential that all cash flows, both direct and indirect, are clearly identified. we can only look for economies of scale and other optimisations if we have a complete picture of the financial support to all the countries concerned. our party therefore believes that the oda (official development assistance) calculations should not be limited to direct cash flows but should also disclose indirect cash flows.
in writing. the european union is the largest contributor of development aid. by voting in favour of enhancing the effectiveness of development cooperation, we are once again demonstrating the importance we attach to our commitment to contribute to the achievement of the sustainable development goals (sdgs) as set out in the 2030 agenda. we recognize that the eradication of all forms of poverty requires first of all a cooperative approach with the least developed countries, which have the primary responsibility for achieving these goals. our commitment in busan reminds us that the effectiveness of this cooperation also depends on its inclusive aspect, involving international and regional organisations, but also national bodies (parliaments, civil society and the private sector). this should be strengthened by mobilising more development actors who are fully capable of recognising their responsibility to improve development in an environment of peace, respect for human rights and the rule of law.
in writing. ‒ with just a few days to go until the conference of the global partnership for effective development cooperation, parliament sent a clear message of support for this oecd initiative. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environmentally friendly use of energy. founded in 2011, this forum brings together the different actors (beneficiaries, donors, the private sector, civil society) to boost development policies. while welcoming the efforts made, the report stresses that civil society and the private sector are key partners, that transparency is paramount and that national policies on development aid in recipient countries are needed. the text stresses in particular the 2005 commitment of member states to devote at least 0.7% of their gross national income to development by 2015. although the eu was the world's largest donor of development aid last year with €68 billion, only five countries actually met this target: sweden (1.4%), luxembourg (0.93%), denmark (0.85%), the netherlands (0.76%) and the united kingdom (0.71%). so we're way off the mark.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of enhancing the effectiveness of development cooperation, on the eve of the high-level meeting of the global partnership for effective development cooperation, to be held in nairobi next week. the european union, a true pioneer of development, must strengthen existing strategies and orient them towards tangible results by complementing national actions. inclusive partnership, transparency and mutual accountability are 'driving forces for achieving the sustainable development goals'. we need to achieve our commitment target and ensure the quality of the assistance provided and the monitoring of the actions undertaken, in view of the implementation of the 2030 agenda. this requires relying on the national strengths of the countries, but also involving civil society and all frontline actors. it also requires respect for governance, democratic values and fundamental rights.
‒ the european union is a leader in development cooperation. while much good has been done in this area, more can be done to increase the effectiveness of aid and development, both at eu and global level. by focusing on greater involvement of national parliaments, civil society and citizens in the countries receiving aid, their democratic input is increased and the way to greater autonomy is opened. the global partnership for effective development cooperation (gpedc), which oversees the busan agreements, is meeting at the end of november to take the lead in improving development cooperation. the rapporteur believes that the success of this meeting depends on the emergence of new ideas for sustainable development and the transparency of the concrete contribution of each participant. we welcome the report, but the european union is losing sight of important principles by increasingly spending development funds on the reception of refugees. this expenditure is not a structural and sustainable solution that contributes to socioeconomic development. the financial capacity for development cooperation is also declining, which makes the seriousness of the matter very clear. we regret this very much and for that reason we shall abstain.
in writing. ‒ i spoke in favour of this report when it was voted. the european union, as the world's largest donor of development aid, has a particular responsibility to improve aid effectiveness and accountability around eu support around the world. beyond this, the union should spearhead global efforts to advance development effectiveness and ensure that transparency, good governance and the rule of law in developing countries remain at the heart of concerns.
in writing. ‒ i voted to emphasise the encouragement of national development aid policies by the parliaments of recipient countries, to ensure greater accountability of donors and recipient countries, including local authorities, to improve the financial management of public funds and absorption capacity, to eliminate corruption and all forms of fragmentation of aid, to make tax systems more efficient and to improve the conditions for eligibility for budgetary aid and to become less dependent on development aid in the longer term.

in writing. ‒ in the light of the vw scandal and the issue of real-world emissions, air quality is more topical than ever. air pollution has a high environmental and health impact. poor air quality causes about 400 000 premature deaths in the eu every year. parliament therefore voted in favour of new rules setting national emission reduction commitments for the pollutants sulphur dioxide (so2), nitrogen oxides (nox), volatile organic compounds other than methane (nmvoc), ammonia (nh3) and fine particulate matter (particles less than 2.5 microns in diameter). the proposed stricter limits are a step in the right direction. the aim is to reduce the impact of air pollution on public health by about 50% by 2030, which is certainly a reasonable goal.
in writing. ‒ i have approved this report which proposes to limit national emissions of certain air pollutants. this should aim in particular at air quality levels that do not result in major adverse impacts or risks to human health and the environment. this requires member states to commit themselves to reducing their emissions to more ambitious levels by 2030, to protecting the health of vulnerable groups or, of course, to supporting the transition to investments in clean and efficient technologies through tax incentives. the commission should facilitate access to finance to ensure that measures can be adopted to meet the objectives set by the directive.
despite the fact that progress has been made in recent years in the fight against air pollution, air quality in europe is still a matter of concern. moreover, despite some good measures, road traffic, industry, electricity generation, household emissions and the burning of fossil fuels continue to cause significant damage to the environment and to the health of citizens. according to the latest report by the european environment agency, in 2013, particulate matter was responsible for more than 400 000 premature deaths in the european union. nitrous oxide caused another 70,000 additional deaths. because air pollution also leads to additional health care costs and poorer agricultural yields, the annual cost of this is estimated to be at least eur 330 billion. that is why i fully support the european parliament's decision to significantly tighten up the standards by 2030 and to introduce stricter and binding national emission ceilings for sulphur dioxide, nitrogen oxides, particulate matter, volatile organic compounds and ammonia. the introduction of stricter emission standards is a major step forward that could save many lives and significantly improve the quality of life of people in cities and densely populated areas.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution calling for the european authorisation of the herbicide bentazone, which expires on 30 june 2017, not to be renewed until its safety has been confirmed. it appears that bentazone can easily reach groundwater and may be toxic to human reproduction. i also note that the european food safety authority (efsa) has proposed that the active substance bentazone be classified as toxic to reproduction category 2. therefore, until the consumer risk assessment is finalised and data are available, in particular on potential groundwater exposure, i would advocate strict application of the precautionary principle.
in writing. we call on the commission not to take any premature decisions but to base an authorisation for the renewal of the use of the active ingredient bentazone in plant protection products on all the necessary information needed to take that decision. the marketing authorisation for bentazone is due to expire on 30 june 2017. this means that the commission has until then to take a decision on the basis of a complete dossier, including data on the impact of bentazone on humans, animals and the environment.
in writing. ‒ the european authorisation of bentazone should not be renewed until its safety has been demonstrated. in summary, this is the message sent by the european parliament's plenary on wednesday in a non-binding resolution targeting this herbicide which acts against broadleaf weeds and is commonly used in the agricultural sector. the objectors, first and foremost mr pavel poc, focused in this resolution exclusively on the procedural aspects of this authorization. a difficult but necessary work! on the one hand, some data were still recently requested from the applicant company in the context of the 'data confirmation procedure', a practice that had been strongly criticised by the european ombudsman in a decision of february 2016. in addition, the commission granted a maximum authorisation of 15 years, until 31 january 2032, despite the absence of data on human and animal toxicity and ecotoxicity as indicated in the efsa study. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'common carrier' to cover all transport services, including the carriage of goods by road, rail and inland waterway.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the european parliament resolution calling on the commission to withdraw its draft implementing regulation to extend the approval of the active substance bentazone until 31 january 2032. the reason for my choice is simple: there is currently insufficient evidence to say that this substance may not have harmful effects on human or animal health or on groundwater or have an unacceptable impact on the environment. therefore, for obvious public health reasons, it was important to oppose any extension of bentazone. i also welcome the fact that this resolution calls on the commission and the member states to fund research and innovation into viable and cost-effective solutions to replace these pesticides for health reasons.
in writing. - i voted for this resolution. the evaluation of the representative uses of the active substance bentazone is not sufficient to conclude that, for at least one of the representative uses, a plant protection product containing the active substance bentazone may not have adverse effects on human or animal health or on groundwater or have an unacceptable impact on the environment.
in writing. i voted in favour because the inherent properties of bentazone make it very likely that the active substance bentazone will end up in groundwater.
author. on the eve of the international day for the elimination of violence against women, it is absolutely unacceptable that there is little progress in combating violence against women and gender-based violence. according to a recent fra study, one in five women in the eu has experienced physical violence by someone other than their partner since the age of 15. in particular, women with disabilities are estimated to be one and a half to 10 times more likely to be abused than women without disabilities. violence against women, but certainly also against men and children, is a violation of fundamental rights and an extreme form of discrimination that is both a cause and consequence of gender inequality. the commission proposed on 4 march 2016 that the eu accede to the istanbul convention: the first legally binding instrument at international level for preventing and combating violence against women. only 14 eu countries, including belgium, have ratified the treaty. i am naturally in favour of the eu's accession to the istanbul convention. of course, it is in principle up to the member states to do their job and protect women from violence, but the eu can act in a complementary way, for example in relation to victims' rights and protection orders and in the area of judicial cooperation in criminal matters.
madam president, simone de beauvoir said: 'it will take a political crisis, an economic crisis or a religious crisis for women's rights to be called into question. these rights are never acquired". today we are experiencing the three crises: a political crisis with a rise of populism and conservatism, an economic crisis, of course, and a religious crisis - just look at what is happening today in syria and the victims, especially women, in these migration movements. these three crises should make us even more vigilant in regard to violence against women, because we can of course expect that there will be further increases in this violence against women. it is not just a matter of denouncing, which is what we are doing today, of course. what we are asking for by ratifying the convention is action. we must ensure that there are concrete action plans to combat this violence, and that there are legislative instruments to enable us to play our role as parliamentarians and to be able to impose certain things. therefore, to all those who say that we do not have the tools to act - as the council said earlier when it said that there were things to be settled on the legal level - i say that we can act, and i would even say that we must act.
no is no. leave me alone is no. i don't feel like it is a no. not doing is no. i don't want to is no. this, my friends, we can say in all the languages of the hemisphere. and yet, one in three women is a victim of violence. i am glad that we are here today to take the step of accession to the convention, but let us be honest: we need to do more. we need to come up with a real plan of action. we need to get to a situation where the men are holding the women's hands. we need to get to a situation where we actually protect victims, where sexual assault complaints are taken seriously, where victims are helped. colleagues, i call on you here today, let's all stand up together on this hemisphere today, please stand up with me and shout: no to violence against women.
mr president, commissioner, like other members of this house, i of course welcome the commission's decision to put in place an action plan on vat. i think that there is a real need for a reform which will establish a single community area in the field of vat. we know that vat in europe is an important issue. in 2014, it represented €1 trillion in revenue, or about 7% of the union's gdp, and, above all, it is part of the union's own resources that allow us to finance a whole series of interesting projects for our fellow citizens, whether it be the youth guarantee, cultural programmes, aid to the poorest or aid to the dismissed of multinationals. but, as we all know, there is still too much fraud. i therefore believe that this text will really help us to improve the vat collection system, to eliminate vat fraud and to reduce administrative formalities. i think this last point is important because it will simplify the business operations of smes and, more importantly, it will underline the need for harmonisation at the level of the european union in the area of tax policy. we have also appealed to the member states because - as we all know - this is a national policy, but it is good to converge towards an equivalent rate of vat in the various member states if we want to find a solution to this problem. we also ask for a regular review of the annex to the vat directive containing the list of goods and services subject to vat, because i would like to point out that vat is still an unfair tax which affects all categories of the population in the same way. it seems to me therefore essential to support the reintroduction of a higher vat rate, particularly for all luxury goods, but also - as my colleague denanot has just said - to remove social services of general interest from the law of the market and, as regards the application of vat, to maintain the exemptions enjoyed by public services. finally, commissioner - and this is the most important request i have made to the commission - we must assess the impact of the lack of harmonisation of tax rates at european union level. i think that is what will really convince the member states, given the cross-border fraud.
in writing. the development of second pillar pension schemes (employer pension) should not be at the expense of the statutory pension (first pillar), which still provides the best guarantee against poverty in old age. after all, people are being pushed into pension schemes where they share the risks but cannot reap the benefits of equities. a stress test showed that there is a gap of 430 billion euros between the promised revenues and the actual resources available to deliver on the promises. this could amount to eur 770 billion in a stable economic climate. withdrawing the pocket from the statutory pension may patch up the numbers, but it does not offer a lasting solution. we do not want to encourage the crossborder pension market. i fully support the report, however, because the investment and risk management procedures also include criteria on environmental, social and governance aspects. this not only makes pension funds more transparent, but also gives them the legal guarantee that an environmentally responsible investment strategy cannot be sued if it would yield less than a social or environmentally unfriendly investment. and that is unique in european law.
for the ecr group shocking numbers of elephants, tigers, rhinoceroses, and other species are killed for gadgets and souvenirs, so-called medicines, or useless fashion accessories. unconscionable poachers and traders are selling nature for a lot of money, and we all need to put an end to this. illegal trade in wildlife is one of the most important forms of organised crime in the world. the trade brings billions of euros into the hands of criminal organisations every year, is linked to drug and arms trafficking, and funds militias and terrorist groups. moreover, illegal activities are increasing dramatically. illegal trade is not only deadly for many protected species, it is also extremely dangerous. trade is leading to insecurity and instability, for example in central africa, and this has also been explicitly recognised by the un security council. the eu is a party to the case. europe is not only a market for illegal products, it is also a hub. reasons enough to fight this illegal trade vigorously. for the sake of nature and our safety. a european action plan is not too soon. we have a good plan of action, but that's not the end of the story. the big challenge is to effectively translate words into action. the implementation, enforcement and monitoring of the action plan and of existing legislation are crucial. i can only thank mr bearder and the other members for the pleasant and constructive cooperation.
in writing. drug trafficking, human trafficking and arms trafficking are the three most lucrative criminal activities. at the bottom of the list, with up to 20 billion euros in annual profits, is the illegal trade in wildlife, plants, and other products. the situation is getting worse every year, leading to the extinction of some species. the horror of it all is that the rarer a species becomes, the higher the price of the products associated with these killings, thereby causing the slaughter to escalate. the european parliament proposes an action plan and calls for exemplary sanctions to combat this scourge. without biodiversity, there will be no humanity. we are calling for severe sanctions to be taken on european soil against traffickers and for the establishment of a european coordinator for the fight against this type of crime. europol must consider this activity as a form of organised crime. finally, we are calling for legislation inspired by the american model and in which it is clearly stated that if a product has been made or obtained illegally in one country, it is also illegal in the country of destination.

in writing. ‒ the current eu common vat system was created in 1993 as a transitional solution on the way to a definitive system. the report is the eu parliament's response to the commission's vat action plan presented in april. the current legal situation is extremely complex, with a wide variety of vat rates and exemptions. the action plan provides for the introduction of a simpler, fairer and definitive vat system based on the principle of taxation in the country of destination of goods and services. parliament welcomed the plan and called, inter alia, for the goods and services to be determined at eu level and for member states to be allowed to set their own rates of taxation as long as they were above a fixed minimum rate. i support the report of parliament, because simplification of the vat system is necessary to guarantee the functioning of the digital single market and to improve the situation of smes operating across borders.
in writing. ‒ vat raised almost €1 trillion in 2014. however, massive fraud is found in most member states. this corresponds to a loss of almost 170 billion euros. in this report we propose measures to improve the vat collection system, to eliminate vat fraud and to reduce administrative formalities. the aim of this text is to simplify the business operations of smes and to underline the need for harmonisation at eu level in the field of taxation policy. we also call for a regular review of the annex to the vat directive with the list of goods and services subject to reduced vat. i would remind you that vat is an unfair tax which affects all categories of the population in the same proportion. here, too, it is the workers and pensioners who finance the tax reductions for the richest and the most wealthy.
in writing. ‒ next year, the european commission will present a proposal for a definitive vat system. in the run-up to this, the commission launched an action plan on vat in april. the general outline of the proposal is good, but we have to wait for the concrete results. it is important that there should finally be a definitive vat system based on the principle of taxation in the country of destination. it is also important to pay more attention to e-commerce and smes, to tackle fraud and to give member states more freedom in terms of tariffs. the nva voted against this report, which expresses parliament's views, because it calls for less freedom for the member states and more harmonisation. unfortunately, parliament is going against the good intentions of the commission to give the member states a little more freedom.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the european parliament resolution on 'towards a definitive vat system and the fight against vat fraud' because i believe it contains interesting recommendations, particularly with a view to combating tax fraud. i am in favour of a better exchange of information between the tax authorities of the member states. according to the commission, as much as €160 billion of vat revenue has been lost since september 2014 due to legal tax optimisation, fraud, errors, inaccuracies and negligence, late payments or bankruptcies. let us hope that the vat package which the commission will present will put an end to these practices which are at best ethically dubious and at worst fraudulent.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this text denouncing the commission's cold-blooded position. the proposed initiatives and timetable are far from being a particularly decisive step forward. instead of reforming a transitional system that came into force more than 20 years ago, the commission is content to propose increased cooperation, to hope for greater trust between tax administrations, to set a timetable and to carry out further assessments of the situation. a sustainable vat system could consist in extending the self-liquidation mechanism to all transactions between traders throughout europe. in this model, there is no longer any upfront tax collection and refund. in the absence of financial flows, all risks of fraud disappear. this would significantly reduce distortions of competition. in addition, it would be a considerable relief for companies in terms of financing and administrative obligations. invoicing would be considerably simplified. entrepreneurs should no longer pre-finance the vat upfront.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour because vat fraud is a very harmful practice that drains member states' budgets of considerable sums and undermines their efforts to consolidate public finances.
in writing. – i voted in favour of this resolution since i believe that the existing vat system should be improved, allowing for fewer exemptions. in my opinion an efficient vat system is fundamental for the functioning of the single market. in order to reach a definitive vat system, but also to detect vat fraud, the efforts among member states become fundamental. the current system is not totally bad, but it can be simplified, making member states comply with minimum tax rates. very important in my opinion is that vat are equal for public and private companies. so even if tax-legislation is exclusive competence of each member state, there is a need for higher harmonisation.
in writing. ‒ wildlife trafficking is an international organised crime that generates around €20 billion a year for criminals and has serious impacts on biodiversity. this report, which i have approved, calls on the european commission, the member states, europol and eurojust to recognise that wildlife crime is a serious and growing threat and to combat it today with the utmost political will. the report stresses the need for comprehensive and coordinated strategies in the targeted areas of action, for adequate resources and for a permanent monitoring and evaluation mechanism to measure progress. it also stresses the need to provide assistance, guidance and training to the authorities in the countries of origin, transit and destination with regard to investigations, as well as law enforcement and judicial procedures at local, regional and national levels.
in writing. ‒ the european parliament responded this afternoon to the commission's action plan to combat wildlife trafficking. this highly lucrative trade generates between $8 billion and $20 billion annually and threatens the survival of many species - including rhinos, elephants, great apes, tigers, and pangolins and sturgeons. two strong proposals are made: firstly, to ban all purchases of ivory and rhino horn within the union. the reality of the figures cannot be ignored: an elephant is killed every 12 minutes, and ivory from its tusks brings in more money in africa than drug trafficking! the union must empower europol to combat this criminal activity more effectively. it is also essential to harmonise criminal sanctions within the union and to ensure that they are truly dissuasive. it is unacceptable that in some eu countries traffickers are only fined a maximum of eur 15 000, while rhino horn on the black market can fetch up to eur 50 000. defending large mammals and all endangered species is a moral duty for europe and europeans. that should be a priority.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the parliament's resolution on the european union action plan against wildlife trafficking. i want to be very clear on this. the european union must immediately and without exception ban the trade in ivory and rhino horn within its borders. i am also in favour of harmonising the sanctions against those who commit these atrocities. the resolution also contains other recommendations that the commission and the member states should follow up on in order to effectively combat wildlife trafficking.
in writing. ‒ illegal trade in wildlife by criminal organisations is becoming an increasing problem. the link between the two lies in the fact that the proceeds generate a large amount of profit in a relatively easy way and thus are an attractive source for criminals to finance their activities. the european union has drawn up an action plan to combat this trade as far as possible. it states, among other things, that prevention is better than cure and that campaigns should therefore focus on reducing the demand for and supply of wild animals and plants. the correct punishment of illegal traders can also reduce such practices. close cooperation between countries of origin, destination and transit of illicit trafficking is essential in this respect. together with a shared responsibility of all member states on these points, we can save different animal and plant species and ensure the preservation of our ecosystem. the green group supports this plan, but calls for radical additions. the commission has already taken a number of measures to combat illegal hunting and poaching.
in writing. ‒ drug trafficking, human trafficking and arms trafficking are the three most lucrative criminal activities. at the bottom of the list, with up to 20 billion euros in annual profits, is the illegal trade in wildlife, plants, and other products. the situation is getting worse every year, leading to the extinction of some species. the horror of it all is that the rarer a species becomes, the higher the price of the products associated with these killings, thereby causing the slaughter to escalate. the european parliament proposes an action plan and calls for exemplary sanctions to combat this scourge. without biodiversity, there will be no humanity.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour because the illegal trade in wildlife has become a multibillion-dollar criminal industry dominated by organised criminal groups.
in writing. ‒ all the companies in question play a crucial role in the transport of passengers and goods by adding fuel to the wheels of a mobility that has historically been structured by the 'big boys'. through better local market knowledge, greater proximity to the customer and/or often agility and innovation, small businesses improve individual passenger transport, especially during the fateful last mile in densely populated areas. similarly, in landlocked areas where the construction of railway infrastructure or the organisation of public transport would be too costly, the private car is often the only means of transport available to certain categories of the population. small transport companies are therefore at the heart of european mobility. but they are full of talents who need a favourable environment to develop. this is where the regulator can and must do its job by creating the most favourable regulatory, social and fiscal environment possible. this will enable small transport enterprises to turn the many challenges they face today, most notably the ict revolution, into opportunities.
in writing. ‒ small transport companies with a diverse profile, from family businesses to smes, from craft enterprises to start-ups and innovative companies, play a major role in the transport of both goods and passengers. as they tend to have a better knowledge of the local market and are closer to their customers, they often provide very valuable services, including and especially in the delicate transport network. as new information and communication technologies have now become accessible to these small transport enterprises, the sector can be fully modernised, which will not only benefit the supplier and the customer, but also have positive effects on the sustainable use of the limited capacity of our transport infrastructure. it is of course very important that european policy does not impede this development by poorly designed rules which are tailored only to the needs of the larger companies. this report strives to create the most favourable regulatory, social and fiscal environment for small transport companies, so that they too can adapt and take advantage of the opportunities offered by these new technologies. the n-va meps therefore support this report.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending regulation (eu) no 952/2013 establishing the union customs code, as regards goods which have temporarily left the customs territory of the union by sea or air. as things currently stand, there is no legal basis for requiring the presentation of goods which are unloaded or transhipped at the place where they are re-introduced into the customs territory of the union after temporarily leaving it. this makes it difficult for the customs authorities to control the goods. the proposal to amend article 136 aims to fill this legal vacuum, to guarantee equal treatment for all goods and to re-establish the legal basis provided for by the old customs code.
in writing. i voted in favour of the proposal to amend regulation (eu) no 952/2013 of the customs code of the union (ccu) as regards goods which have temporarily left the customs territory of the union by sea or air. this proposal will improve the efficiency of customs supervision. until now, the absence of a legally binding text has prevented the competent authorities of the em from implementing the provisions of article 136 of the cdu requiring the presentation to them of goods which have temporarily left the customs territory of the union. these customs authorities will now have enhanced controls to enable them to correctly collect import duties and other taxes, to properly apply non-tax measures such as veterinary or phytosanitary checks, and to correctly identify risks relating to goods arriving at their ports or airports. these measures are important and are in line with our efforts to strengthen consumer protection.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the european parliament's position at first reading of 1 december 2016 with a view to the adoption of regulation (eu) no 952/2013 of the european parliament and of the council amending regulation (eu) no 952/2013 establishing the union customs code as regards goods temporarily removed from the customs territory of the union by sea or air. the amendment of article 136 of regulation (eu) no 952/2013 allows for better account to be taken of the difference between non-union goods and union goods.
in writing. ‒ the full entry into force on 1 may 2016 of the provisions of regulation (eu) no 952/2013 of the european parliament and of the council of 9 october 2013 laying down the union customs code, as well as the implementing and delegated acts resulting therefrom, has brought to light certain shortcomings in the wording of the text. these provisions apply to the specific case where goods have temporarily left the customs territory of the union by direct route between two points in that territory by sea or air, without a stop outside the territory of the union. the absence of a clear legal basis for requiring the presentation of these goods to customs authorities makes it more difficult for the latter to monitor the goods. the current proposal to amend article 136 aims to fill this legal vacuum, to guarantee equal treatment for all goods and to re-establish the legal basis provided for by the old customs code.

in writing. ‒ the european parliament voted in favour of the agreement on a reciprocal visa waiver for european and kiribati nationals by a large majority of 567 votes to 51, with 24 abstentions. this flexible visa regime for stays of less than 90 days, already provisionally applied since the signing of the agreement on 13 june 2016, benefits all categories of persons travelling for any purpose other than gainful employment. the agreement strengthens the economic, cultural and political relations between the european union and the republic of kiribati, which are already governed by the cotonou agreement (acp-eu). another proof of their mutual commitment and good faith to the comprehensive economic partnership between the european union and 14 pacific countries. it is an additional means of continuing the political dialogue with kiribati on priority issues such as human rights and fundamental freedoms. in addition to bringing european and pacific peoples closer together, this new visa system will encourage potential investment and tourism development in these pacific archipelagos, which are visited by only 4000 tourists a year.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the european parliament legislative resolution of 1 december 2016 on the draft council decision on the conclusion, on behalf of the european union, of the agreement between the european union and the republic of kiribati on the short-stay visa waiver. following the work on this subject in the committee responsible, i have come to the conclusion that this short-stay visa exemption is fully justified.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report which proposes that the european solidarity fund can provide aid more quickly and effectively following natural disasters in the eu. given the scale and severity of some disasters, it is important to be able to improve the responsiveness and efficiency of emergency funding in the member states. although the fund underwent a major reform in 2014, efforts can still be made to reduce the time taken to process applications from beneficiaries, which is often considered too long.
in writing. ‒ the solidarity fund is an instrument to provide assistance to member states affected by a major natural disaster. it goes without saying that the union must be able to act with urgency in such cases. the n-va supports the findings of this report and is convinced of the importance of this expenditure when it can help victims of natural disasters to recover and get back on their feet in a timely and effective manner.
in writing. in 2002, following the tragic floods, the european union set up the european union solidarity fund. the fund is intended for both member states and candidate countries and helps countries affected by natural disasters. while it is impossible to foresee all emergencies and disasters, it is nevertheless possible to improve the management of their consequences. the report highlights various aspects of management, such as the speed of action by the solidarity fund, the need for a preventive policy that goes hand in hand with the necessary complementarity between the eusf and other european instruments, in particular cohesion policy, and the effective collaboration between the national level and regional or local authorities. the european union solidarity fund is an immediate expression of the union's solidarity with countries affected by major natural disasters. it is therefore essential to evaluate this instrument with a view to its continuous improvement. i therefore welcome this report without any hesitation.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the european parliament's position which aims to change the way the european union solidarity fund operates. among the recommendations made by the european parliament, i would like to highlight the possibility for member states to make a joint request for assistance in the event of a crossborder disaster. i think this is a sensible amendment. the european parliament also voted in favour of reducing processing times for applications from six to four weeks and raising the threshold for advance payments from 10% to 15%. these are important demands which i hope will be implemented as soon as possible in european legislation.
in writing. ‒ following the tragic floods of 2002, the european union set up the european union solidarity fund (regulation (ec) no 2012/2002). it is an immediate expression of the union's solidarity with countries affected by major natural disasters. it is addressed not only to the member states but also to the candidate countries. i believe that better communication to the public throughout the process is needed to enable beneficiaries or interested persons to follow the procedure better for each specific application. this could be organised at european commission level, provided there is a good flow of information between the different operational levels.

in writing. ‒ although it was tabled by my group, i voted without hesitation against this resolution requesting the opinion of the european court of justice on the compatibility of the framework agreement with the european treaties. under the guise of rigour, it was in reality nothing more than a last-ditch delaying manoeuvre to prevent the approval of the framework agreement. i am glad that a majority of this house rejected this text. clearly, some are more concerned about a hypothetical non-compliance than about increasing citizens' rights and enhancing their security.
in writing. i voted against this resolution seeking the opinion of the court of justice of the european union on the compatibility of the framework agreement with the treaties. such a request would have had the effect of suspending the implementation of the agreement and, ultimately, would have been liable to jeopardise its conclusion. this agreement brings the personal data of european citizens to a level of protection for which the european union has been fighting for years. it seems to me therefore unacceptable to prevent the immediate implementation of an agreement which represents an undeniable step forward for europeans.
in writing. ‒ i share the rapporteur's view that there is legal uncertainty as to the compatibility of the envisaged agreement with the provisions of the treaties, in particular article 16 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union, and the charter of fundamental rights of the european union, in particular articles 7 and 8 thereof, article 52 (1) thereof as regards the right of individuals to the protection of personal data, and article 47 thereof as regards access to an effective judicial remedy.
in writing. - i abstained on this text. it provides protection (including the right of access and rectification under certain conditions) to european citizens whose data is exchanged with the united states in the fight against crime and terrorism. this is an improvement because in some cases this protection was weak. however, the european parliament's legal service considers that the agreement does not respect the treaties or the charter of fundamental rights, in particular because it does not provide sufficient legal remedies before the us authorities and it excludes the additional safeguards that the data protection directive could bring with its entry into force in 2018. i also supported the resolutions requesting the opinion of the court of justice on this matter.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the umbrella agreement on the protection of personal data transferred and processed in the context of the prevention and detection of criminal offences, including terrorist offences. this was a longstanding request from the european parliament. this historic agreement, negotiated for several years between the european commission and the united states, aims to guarantee a high level of protection of personal information and to strengthen cooperation between the united states and the european union in the prevention and detection of criminal offences. the agreement does not allow any transfer of data. once in force, it will strengthen the safeguards for the protection of all personal data transmitted by judicial authorities on both sides of the atlantic on the basis of other agreements, such as the eu/us air passenger name record (pnr) agreement. it will also put european and us citizens on an equal footing before us courts, as it will allow european citizens to bring legal proceedings in the event of misuse of their personal data or if they are subsequently made public, a right previously reserved for us citizens only.
in writing. i voted in favour of the umbrella agreement, an agreement between the european union and the united states to strengthen the protection of personal data of european citizens when transferred to the united states by judicial and police authorities in the context of criminal cooperation. this agreement does not constitute a basis for data transfers, but adds additional safeguards to the protection of personal data already transferred on the basis of other agreements. among other things, european citizens will now have access to legal remedies in the event of misuse of their data in the us. this is a historic victory for europeans. this was a longstanding request of the european parliament.
in writing. i supported the us-eu agreement on the protection of personal information processed in criminal matters, as it is essential that the eu and the us are on the same page when it comes to protecting the data of european citizens in the us and work hand in hand, as the eu has been doing for years. the principles and safeguards established when personal data are to be transferred for criminal purposes will also apply to private entities, such as european aviation authorities, in the context of the pnr. another important development of this agreement is that it also includes bilateral agreements between the member states and the united states.
in writing. ‒ following calls by the european parliament, the council adopted on 3 december 2010 a decision authorising the commission to open negotiations for the conclusion of an agreement between the european union and the united states of america on the protection of personal data in the context of police cooperation and judicial cooperation in criminal matters (hereinafter referred to as the 'framework agreement') concerning the protection of personal data in the context of the transfer and processing of such data for the purposes of the prevention, detection, investigation and prosecution of criminal offences, including terrorism. on 28 march 2011, the commission opened negotiations with the us department of justice. parliament has been kept regularly informed of the progress of the negotiations, in accordance with article 108 (10) of the tfeu, and your rapporteur has drawn up a series of working papers to facilitate the discussions in the libe committee. i finally abstained on the final text, as i did not receive sufficient guarantees as to the effectiveness of the manoeuvre.
in writing. ‒ i voted against the conclusion of this interim bilateral agreement. it was concluded in 2007 and in the meantime negotiations for a regional agreement have been opened. i therefore think it is better to concentrate our efforts on reaching a regional agreement, rather than on this obsolete bilateral agreement.
in writing. ghana and the eu have important trade relations. last year, trade between ghana and the eu accounted for 20 percent of ghana's foreign trade. in view of the delay in the conclusion of the eu-west africa economic partnership agreement and in order to ensure the continuity of trade relations between the eu and ghana, it is desirable to adopt a temporary economic partnership agreement. in this way, trade between ghana and the eu is guaranteed, the framework for promoting economic investment in ghana remains stable and phytosanitary assistance to ghanaian exporters is maintained.
in writing. ‒ on thursday, meps approved the 2007 interim economic agreement with ghana by 375 votes to 220, with 46 abstentions. since june 2014, the eu and west africa (which includes 16 countries) have been trying to ratify a regional economic partnership (rep) agreement for economic growth and free trade. however, the partnership still needs the approval of nigeria, the gambia and mauritania before it can be ratified, leaving the other 13 signatory countries to do so voluntarily. this could have had damaging consequences for ghana if the current ghana-eu economic agreement, which expires at the end of the year, had not been followed up. the european parliament has therefore made the right decision in supporting the position of its rapporteur, mr fjellner, in favour of free customs-free access to the european market for ghanaian products. with over 20% of external trade going to the european union, amounting to €5.4 billion in 2015, this temporary solution was essential for ghana's stability, development and economic growth.
in writing. ‒ by signing the interim economic partnership agreement (iepa) with the eu, ghana may avoid tariff problems, but it also sacrifices the regional integration of ecowas. to keep out cheap eu products, ecowas members might raise their tariffs on ghana. after a five-year moratorium, ghana will have to release eu imports, which will only increase competition. it also contains a clause which makes a rapid opening to the liberalization of services and other disciplines of free trade. knowing that ghana is a privileged partner of the united kingdom, one can only guess at the consequences of brexit. this is why we cannot call the iepa a step up, but rather a pit into which the whole epa-eu ecowas process is falling. the fact that the commission's trade dg is behind this is worrying. the promising integration process is on the wane and the agreement is aimed primarily at the economic interests of the major european players. it is also contrary to european principles such as policy coherence in development cooperation and the agreed development goals. ghana also had the option of the gsp+ regime, with special preferential tariffs for vulnerable countries. this agreement has such far-reaching implications that i cannot possibly approve it.
in writing. - i voted against the fjellner report. i think it is high time we reviewed our approach to agreements and considered africa as our dumping ground, with the great risk of impoverishing the local and regional population by unbalancing the trade and economic flow of the countries concerned!

in writing. council decision 2014/335/eu, euratom on the system of own resources of the european union has led to a reduction in the cost of collecting the union's traditional own resources, a reduction in the vat call rates for some member states and gross reductions in the annual contributions based on gross national income for others. amending budget no 5/2016 aims to incorporate, in the revenue part of the 2016 budget of the union, the effect of the adjustments to the own resources linked to the implementation of decision 2014/335/eu with retroactive effect to the financial years 2014, 2015 and 2016. the draft amending budget no 5/2016 therefore leads to a modification of the contributions of the individual member states, but has no effect on the overall revenue or expenditure side of the union. these reasons led me to vote in favour of draft amending budget no 5/2016.

in writing. following particularly severe flooding in the region of niederbayern (lower bavaria) in may and june 2016, germany submitted an application to the solidarity fund on 19 august 2016. the floods caused considerable damage to public and private infrastructure, private homes and agricultural facilities. in addition, more than 47 000 people were affected, and two months after the disaster, more than 2 000 people were still unable to return to their homes. in view of the scale of this disaster, i have decided to vote in favour of an amount of eur 31 475 125 in commitment and payment appropriations from the solidarity fund, not only because the request fulfils the conditions for granting financial assistance, but also because i am convinced that the damage cannot remain unaddressed. the eu combines the values of solidarity and responsibility, so it was only natural that it should act as effectively as possible in such a situation.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the mobilisation of the european union solidarity fund for germany, and more specifically for lower bavaria, in view of the sudden and violent floods that occurred in may and june 2016. this natural disaster affected more than 47 000 people, including many families who were unable to return to their homes. the town of simbach am inn was almost completely destroyed and was without a municipal water supply for three weeks. the cost of the urgent emergency measures is estimated by the german authorities at eur 94.196 million, and the total amount of the proposed aid is eur 31 475 125. may the german people put these tragic events behind them as soon as possible.

in writing. the aim of the solidarity fund is to enable the european union to respond to emergency situations in order to express solidarity with people affected by natural disasters. the proposal for a decision aims to add a maximum amount of eur 50 million in commitment and payment appropriations to the general budget of the union for the year 2017 in order to be able to pay out rapid and efficient aid advances in the event of a natural disaster in 2017, in advance of the final allocation decision. the amount of such advance shall not exceed 10% of the amount of the financial contribution provided for and shall not exceed eur 30 million, on the one hand, and the maximum amount granted to the fund shall not exceed eur 500 000 000 on the other hand. i support this proposal for a decision which enables the eu to face up to its responsibilities and to show solidarity with countries affected by natural disasters. it seems to me important that it can act as quickly as possible in order to limit the damage and improve the safety and conditions of the affected population.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the mobilisation of the european union solidarity fund for the purpose of payment of advances under the general budget of the union for 2017. this fund is intended to deal with emergencies resulting from natural disasters. it is one of the european union's important solidarity tools, without which the affected regions would not have been able to recover. this requires that the affected countries receive an advance before the final decision on allocation is taken, so that they can provide effective help to the affected citizens and can do so quickly. each year, a maximum of eur 50 million will be entered in the budget in commitment and payment appropriations to ensure the timely availability of budgetary resources. this is both a positive and a necessary decision.

in writing. access to electricity is universal except in africa. the stability of africa is the stability of europe and the world. although africa has the greatest potential for renewable energy on the planet, it is the continent with the greatest backlog of electrification. access to energy is an accelerator of development. it opens up opportunities for businesses, develops employment, improves economic growth. it is therefore essential that the eu, through official development assistance, and the african continent focus their efforts on energy, prior to health, education, access to water, women's empowerment, the agri-food industry... access to energy for all is a guarantee of social peace, solidarity and sustainable development. as a sister continent to africa, the eu has a role to play in the eu-africa energy partnership. our inaction would cost a hundred times more than action in terms of radicalisation, chaos, immigration, political and social destabilisation. but impulses that do not come from the african continent have little chance of success. the future of africa is therefore closely linked to that of europe and vice versa, but nothing can replace the will of africans.
