in writing. i voted in favour of a more adequate application of the european order for payment procedure, which is intended to facilitate the recovery of sums due in cross-border cases. in short, this procedure makes it easier for creditors to obtain an injunction to recover uncontested claims in civil and commercial matters. the european order for payment procedure is automatically issued on the basis of the application alone, but the debtor may lodge an objection within 30 days. if there is an objection, the injunction is terminated and the opposite court proceedings may be commenced.
in writing. the european order for payment procedure for crossborder claims uncontested by the defendant simplifies, speeds up and reduces the costs of settling disputes involving more than one eu country. the regulation establishes a uniform procedure leading to a judicial decision which is enforceable in all the member states without prior recognition. however, the regulation needed to be revised to improve its efficiency, to update some data, to adopt new versions of some forms, to improve its clarity.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the european parliament resolution of 1 december 2016 on the application of the european order for payment procedure. parliament welcomed the good functioning of the european order for payment procedure in all member states, a procedure for uncontested claims applicable in civil and commercial matters and aimed mainly at simplifying and speeding up the cross-border procedure for the recognition and enforcement of the rights of creditors in the european union. however, i regret a number of things, in particular the significant delay of almost two years in sending the commission's report reviewing the application of regulation (ec) no 1896/2006, the fact that the commission's report does not include an extended impact assessment for each member state and that the use of the european order for payment procedure varies widely between member states.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the european order for payment procedure, which is designed to facilitate the recovery of sums due in crossborder cases. the procedure is optional, which means that it can replace many equivalent national procedures in crossborder cases. in short, this procedure makes it easier for creditors to obtain an injunction to recover uncontested claims in civil and commercial matters. this procedure can be applied by post or by electronic means (which is more often the case), does not require the assistance of a lawyer and can be used in the other member states without any additional formalities.

member of the commission. – mr president, honourable members, let me thank all of you for your thoughts and comments on the clean energy for all european package. the commission has been very attentive to the proposals made by this house when preparing the legislative measures included in the package. many of the views suggested over the months by this house have been incorporated in the package and are reflected in the pages of the legislative proposal. i am aware that on some issues this house has advocated slightly different positions from the ones put forward by the commission in its proposal, so allow me to emphasise this: the commission proposals are in themselves no easy targets. they will require considerable efforts by member states to meet their international and domestic obligations, and to get them right we have assessed our proposals along several dimensions, including energy system impacts, macroeconomic impacts, environmental effects, social impacts, including affordability issues, energy-related investments, and, finally, energy system costs. and of course our proposal fully respects the right of member states to choose their energy means as stated in article 194 of the treaties. many of you have referred to renewable energy. the proposal revising the renewable energy directive is ambitious and improves upon the previous directive, in particular by putting an end to retroactive measures and launching a europeanisation process. but the measures favouring renewables go beyond this text: the market design, energy efficiency, the energy performance of buildings and the governance of the union all contribute to reaching our policy goals and targets in a cost-effective way, paving the way for further deployment of renewables in buildings, transport and industry. the revised proposal also goes beyond reaching the 27% target. it is about bringing sustainable jobs to the market, creating local added value, locking in investment potential, and fostering innovation. the target – at least 27% –represents the cost-optimal contribution of renewables in 2030 towards meeting the european union’s long-term decarbonisation objectives, and it reflects the european union’s fair and ambitious contribution to the paris agreement. for the first time; the package is proposing a clear framework on cell consumption and production, energy communities and demand response, and this will help drive the energy transition by unlocking private capital for investment in renewables and make the electricity system more flexible in order to help renewable integration. the european union’s binding 30% energy efficiency target for 2030 is ambitious but balanced and consistent with other targets of the 2030 framework for energy and climate. it is also the target which vice-president šefčovič and myself promised the european parliament at our hearings two years ago: this is what we have delivered. we are going beyond what strictly speaking would be necessary to ensure that the target of at least 40% for production is met, and any claim that our targets and proposal are insufficient to honour our commitment under the paris agreement is simply wrong. with this package we will take the decisive step forward to ensure that the energy transition will continue and that the targets agreed upon will be met. for sure, a lot of real political engagement will be needed in both parliament and the council to reach a compromise, and i am counting on you to improve them and make them a reality soon for the benefit of all our citizens.

critical remarks and the calls to be more ambitious and are ready to work very closely with you on this package. just to complement miguel’s remark about energy poverty, i think it is very important that we clearly recognise energy poverty as an important challenge in our package. we recognise it as a very important challenge which we have to tackle together with the member states but we want to do our utmost at european level. we are addressing the energy poverty issue in our governance system. we want to make sure that renovations, issues of social housing, and long—term innovation plans clearly factor in the issue of energy poverty. miguel elaborated on the importance of energy efficiency and we see it as a very strong instrument in tackling energy poverty as well. in electricity market design we are proposing a clear procedure which would prevent people from being unfairly disconnected, not to mention eco-design and energy labelling where already today our citizens are saving hundreds of euros thanks to our efficient electric appliances. i would also like to respond to one remark and express the support of the commission for all those who are pushing for the completion of the internal energy market in a prompt and smart way. i think a lot of positive things are happening in the baltic and nordic countries. we are seeing positive developments in south—east europe through our cesec initiative, and i would like to assure you that we are bringing new dynamism to managing our projects of common interest. we are also encouraging the member states to present more projects in the area of smart grids. to conclude, i would like to thank all members who recognised the high level of ambition in this proposal. its truly transformational nature should deliver the in writing. ‒ a highly symbolic vote this afternoon with the adoption by the european parliament of a new regulation banning fishing beyond a depth of 800 metres in the north-east atlantic. it is the main fishing area for the eu member states, accounting for around 70% of the global fish catch. this prohibition of deep-sea fishing will apply to bottom trawling, which often destroys seabed habitats, and will limit deep-sea fishing to the area where it occurred between 2009 and 2011. other important measures include the obligation for member states to provide information on the location of vulnerable ecosystems and stricter controls at sea: 20% of european vessels will have to have a (scientific) observer on board to ensure timely and accurate data collection. the text therefore addresses some of the problems raised by the ngos. but in the long term, the eu will have to commit to doing more if it really wants to protect its fisheries resources, for example through a planned phase-out of bottom trawls and bottom set-nets in deep-sea fisheries. this is precisely what the european commission proposed back in 2012.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this recommendation by my colleague maria arena, which proposes, by means of a protocol, to extend the cooperation agreement establishing a partnership between the european communities and their member states, of the one part, and uzbekistan, of the other part, to bilateral trade in textiles, taking into account the expiry of the bilateral agreement on textiles. this would include, inter alia, the granting of most favoured nation status on a reciprocal basis, trade free of quantitative restrictions, a safeguard clause and the principle of transit. the negotiations for the implementation of this protocol were facilitated in particular by the fact that child labour in the cotton harvesting sector had been virtually eliminated according to the last ilo monitoring mission to uzbekistan in 2015. unfortunately, the same cannot be said for the situation of forced labour. the report therefore states that parliament will adopt appropriate measures if the uzbek authorities suspend implementation of their commitment to abolish forced labour.
cotton production is the most important economic sector in the eu-uzbekistan trade relationship. this separate resolution evaluates the cooperation between the uzbek government and the international labour organisation. this cooperation will allow an assessment of the steps taken by the uzbek authorities to end child and forced labour during cotton harvesting in uzbekistan. i am glad that this cooperation has led to the reduction of child labour and its social tolerance. but despite this measurable progress on child labour, this is not yet the case for forced labour in the cotton industry. it is therefore appropriate and necessary to encourage the uzbek government to carry out national awareness campaigns and to carry out intensive controls aimed at improving working conditions in its country. therefore, the cooperation agreement should not only be read as the logical conclusion of the efforts made to eliminate child labour but also as a permanent instrument of the european union to evaluate the commitments on better working conditions to which the uzbek government is committed.
in writing. ‒ in december 2011, parliament had already adopted an interim report on the issue, which made the consent of the house conditional on improvement of the human rights situation in uzbekistan. since then, the international labour organisation has conducted three observation missions, which have resulted in the near-eradication of child labour. it was on this basis that parliament agreed, among other things, to include textiles in the 1999 eu-uzbekistan partnership and cooperation agreement. the decision was intended at the time to encourage the government of the country to pursue the eradication of all forms of forced labour and to strengthen its cooperation with the european union. in the non-legislative resolution adopted at noon, parliament welcomed the fact that uzbekistan had started to cooperate with the international labour organisation, but urged the uzbek authorities to speed up the deployment of national awareness campaigns to eradicate the practice altogether. parliament will therefore continue to follow the case and could still, as a last resort, ask the european commission and the council to suspend the agreement if the authorities do not comply with their commitments to abolish forced labour.

in writing. ‒ i supported the accession agreement of ecuador to the trade agreement between the eu, colombia and peru. this agreement is crucial for the economy of ecuador, which has been hit hard by the fall in oil prices and exports, and by the high costs of reconstruction after this year's earthquake. it can pave the way for progressive social and environmental policies. the eu also has a lot to gain from this, as as soon as the agreement comes into force, ecuador will remove customs duties on 60% of its imports from the eu. ecuador will also benefit from optimized access to the eu for its main exports, such as fish, cut flowers, coffee, cocoa, fruit and nuts. some products will also benefit from a preferential rate, but a stabilisation mechanism, set up through other legislation, will ensure that the interests of european producers are protected.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report setting out the amendments to be made to the eu-colombia-peru trade agreement to take account of the accession of ecuador. this agreement, which will enter into force on 1 january 2017, is essential for ecuador. it will stimulate trade and investment between the two sides, thus contributing to economic growth and job creation. it will allow ecuador to integrate into the regional and global economy. this asymmetrical agreement, designed to contribute to the development of ecuador, provides, as in the epas, for a gradual liberalization of customs duties over a period of 17 years. ecuador will benefit from better access to the european market for fishery products, cut flowers, coffee, cocoa, fruit and nuts. bananas will be granted a preferential tariff with a stabilisation mechanism, as is the case with the other countries party to the agreement. with this agreement, ecuador will be able to take better advantage of the opportunities offered by international trade.
in writing. ‒ trade negotiations between the european union and colombia, ecuador and peru started in january 2009. negotiations with ecuador were concluded on 17 july 2014. by joining the agreement, ecuador will retain its preferential access to the eu market, which it would have lost as a result of a reform of the european system of preferences. i voted in favour of this recommendation, which is a vital agreement for the country's economy, which has been hit hard by the fall in oil prices and exports and by the high costs of reconstruction following this year's earthquake (for reference: a disaster that killed 673 people and injured tens of thousands more).
in writing. ‒ in 2012, the european union and the 28 member states concluded a trade agreement with colombia and peru. now they want to bring ecuador into the fold. the ecuadorian government is feeling internal pressure from actors who are in favour of accession for alleged economic benefits. the greens are against, as we were against the conclusion of an agreement with colombia and peru. we do not accept the idea that the far-left rapporteur is ideologically supporting the left government in ecuador. it is important to us that civil society in ecuador is against it. there is a broad front, from environmental organizations to farmers' organizations, that is expressly opposed to this course of action. environmental ngos fear that accession will be a step backwards and a return to the model of depletion, which will mainly affect indigenous peoples and small farmers. i do not support such an economic model. so i voted against it with conviction.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the european parliament legislative resolution on the draft council decision on the conclusion of the agreement between the european union and the kingdom of norway on reciprocal access for vessels flying the flag of denmark, norway and sweden to fishing activities in the skagerrak. i agree with parliament that this agreement should be concluded.
in writing. - i voted for the text. traditionally, fishermen do not fish in certain waters but fish for specific stocks or species in the waters where those stocks and species are found, and they follow migratory species. this tradition predates the creation of states and the recognition of territorial waters and exclusive economic zones, which appeared much later. the skagerrak and kattegat area is a typical example of this situation. swedish, danish and norwegian fishermen have been fishing together in these waters for the same stocks since at least the middle ages. the fact that two of these three countries have become member states does not alter the principle that fishermen from these three countries should be able to enjoy historical fishing rights in the skagerrak and kattegat area. respect for these historic fishing rights is of the utmost importance.

in writing. ‒ three texts were on the table for the vote on the fourth railway package: one on the standardisation of accounts, one on governance and the last on the public service obligation. we did not reject the first two. in the report on the governance directive, we have achieved our red line: private competition can be restricted if it infringes public service obligations. we have, however, strongly opposed the last text which called for a more advanced liberalisation of the public passenger rail service. this liberalization will not only be harmful to rail users but is even more so at the expense of workers, particularly because it does not introduce the automatic and compulsory transfer of staff in the event of a change of operator. the socialist meps felt that such a strong social guarantee was essential to ensure that competition did not come at the expense of workers' rights and did not open the way to other forms of social dumping. we led the way in parliament but we lost the vote to reject this text by 15 votes out of 751, the right wing having massively supported it.
in writing. the market part of the fourth railway package contains three legislative proposals. one of them is a commission proposal to repeal regulation (eec) no 1192/69. the purpose of the latter is to allow states to compensate railway undertakings for the costs of obligations, while other undertakings using other modes of transport are not covered. the 40 formerly state-owned enterprises receiving the aid are listed in the annex to the regulation. i voted in favour of this proposal to repeal regulation (eec) no 1192/69 because i believe that it no longer meets the needs of the present situation. in today's world, with the liberalisation of the railway market, this regulation no longer meets the challenges of today. the rail sector has undergone many changes and the regulation is no longer in line with the current legal environment and even discriminates against some companies not listed. it is time to have legislation that is in line with reality and able to meet the challenges of our time.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the fourth railway package because this package of legislation aims to improve the competitiveness and quality of rail services by reducing administrative costs, introducing more competition in the passenger services sector and ensuring a level playing field for operators. at national level, my country has always been in favour of a deliberate opening up of the passenger transport market. following the adoption of the fourth railway package, the belgian authorities will still be able to award contracts directly to sncb, without competition, but on condition that the contracts include stricter performance requirements. in this case, the contracts shall contain requirements for punctuality and regularity of service, train quality and sufficient capacity. i consider this to be a breakthrough which will benefit users.
in writing. by voting for this report, which favours a deliberate opening-up of the passenger transport market, i am one of those who wish to improve the quality of railway services and services for users, and to increase the modal share of the train in passenger travel. this openness, together with a number of new rules applicable to all market participants in the interests of fairness, preserves the principle of direct award of public service contracts, a transitional period and the guarantee of optimal protection of workers in the event of public service contracts being transferred to new tenderers. our advantage is that we can continue to award public service contracts directly where the characteristics of an infrastructure do not lend themselves to a transition to the tendering procedure. this is a considerable concession for many member states, including belgium. it goes without saying that this direct allocation will have to lead to an improvement in the quality of services and/or cost efficiency; the proposal does not require any such requirement in the case of a tender procedure (no quality criterion, no performance monitoring).
in writing. ‒ i supported, as did a large majority of the plenary, the van de camp report amending regulation (ec) no 1370/2007 as regards the opening of the market for national rail passenger services. the main elements of the agreement reached with the council relate to the maintenance of public service missions, compensation linked to the net financial impact of public service obligations and social provisions, including rights and obligations relating to the transfer of staff. these are potentially explosive subjects, but they have been the subject of a well-balanced compromise. some important priorities for my political group have been taken into account by this trilogue agreement, which is good news. this is the sharp reduction in the direct award clauses, thus outside a genuine tender procedure, and the provision providing for better access to rolling stock for the traveller. is it necessary to recall that while the average price of a train ticket increased by 42,6% between 2005 and 2015, the satisfaction index of travellers decreased overall during the same period? the latter often deserve the title of 'rail adventurers'.

in writing. the planning, development and operation of the trans-european transport network contribute to the achievement of important union objectives, such as the smooth functioning of the internal market and the strengthening of economic and social cohesion. the maritime network is an integral part of this, since 319 ports through which 96% of eu goods and 93% of eu passengers pass are covered by the guidelines on the trans-european transport network. however, we need to move towards more homogeneity in terms of quality of service within the ports of the trans-european transport network and improve their governance to attract investors. with this resolution, we will contribute to a more efficient, interconnected and sustainable functioning of the trans-european transport network by creating a framework for ports to improve their performance and better cope with changing transport and logistics requirements.
in writing. ‒ after more than 15 years of debate on european port policy, the european parliament finally reached agreement this afternoon: the existing port management models can be maintained and, as a novelty, the focus is finally on good working conditions, which are an important part of the competitiveness of ports and which in my view were non-negotiable. the lack of clear rules on public funding of port infrastructure and charges for its use has so far hampered investment in ports. the new provisions adopted today are aimed in particular at making ports more efficient and more attractive to investors. these new rules will apply to more than 300 ports in the union mentioned in the guidelines for the trans-european transport network (ten-t). these include requiring ports to clearly show public funding received in their accounting systems and improving transparency so that port services and infrastructure charges are fixed. in order to ensure quality services, new requirements are therefore also laid down for port service providers to provide adequate training for employees, with particular emphasis on health and safety aspects.
in writing. ‒ this report on greater financial transparency in ports is misleading, as it only concerns the smaller ports in the southern member states. the new rules will not apply to the larger ports in the north and their structures will not therefore change. the report also lacks any convincing content and is mainly intended to save the commission's face. he doesn't want to be left out after two previous rejections of the port directive. the proposal we are voting on concerns the liberalization of services in marginal and restricted segments. the controversial freight and passenger handling is not included. what the sector needs - and there is agreement on this - is clarity on state aid. the commission has been promising this for 12 years, but has still not put it into practice. we tried with the greens to include measures on the environment and working conditions in the text, but almost everything was voted down, including the question of clarity on state aid. the report is so weak that it will pass under the rubric of 'no good, no harm', and in the meantime the commission will leave the sector alone. but i don't call that policy. that is why i did not support the report.
in writing. ‒ i support the commission's proposal in many respects, particularly in all aspects of financial transparency, but would nevertheless like to propose a number of amendments to improve it. only port services offered directly to the user should fall within the scope of the regulation. dredging is therefore excluded, as it is not a service offered directly to the user, but rather a maintenance task to maintain the practicability of access to the port.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour because ports can contribute to the long-term competitiveness of european industry on the world market and at the same time create jobs in all the union's coastal regions.
in writing. – i voted in favour of this resolution since i believe that ports are a very important contribution to the long-term competitiveness of european industries in world markets. moreover, ports are great providers of jobs in all european coastal regions. i believe that delays at ports represent a major obstacle to the competitiveness and efficiency of short sea shipping at union ports and this is often due to the complexity of administrative procedures for customs clearance. so a big economic advantage for ports could be achieved with a simplification of customs procedures. i support the use of a risk-based policy approach in order to avoid distortion of competition. i agree that a single system is not appropriate for the organisation of port services because this system is very diverse and includes many different models.

for the greens/efa group madam president, ladies and gentlemen, in july 2014, president juncker, right here, said that if there were to be new structural adjustment plans - which he did not believe in - they should be subject to a social impact assessment. a year later, a new structural adjustment plan is imposed on greece, and the social impact, which has never been studied, has become quite visible: one million jobs lost since 2008, a third of the greek population exposed to poverty and exclusion, one in six workers exposed to poverty, while millions of greeks no longer have access to health care. meanwhile, the member states and the imf are joining forces to impose a new set of measures on greece, targeting the labour market once again, with the abolition of collective bargaining and the total liberalisation of redundancies. the juncker commission is not obliged to carry out social impact assessments. however, the commission itself has a legal obligation to be the guardian of the treaties, to enforce the law of the european union, including the charter of fundamental rights. it is well known that the measures advocated by the creditors in this and previous plans are in flagrant breach of european law. if the european union really wants to help greece, it can focus on four points. first, to ease the burden of the greek debt which is not repayable by the state. secondly, to help greece to establish an effective tax administration to combat fraud and evasion, an area in which successive greek governments have not really excelled. thirdly, stop sending refugees back to greece and, on the contrary, relieve greece frontline country of the burden of receiving refugees. it is probably the eu country with the least resources to do so. and finally, to mobilise investment. you will say to me: 'there is the juncker plan'. that's good. there is the juncker plan: 3% of the investment in the juncker plan goes to greece and, at the same time, 10% to germany, a country which no longer knows what to do with its savings. everyone will have understood that it is no longer a question of helping greece, but of teaching the lesson that there is no alternative to neoliberal globalisation. madam president, i will conclude by saying that they should begin to understand that 'who sows neoliberal globalisation reaps national populism'. when will they understand ?
madam president, i shall concentrate solely on the question of social dialogue, because i believe that our european model is based on this social dialogue. commissioner, you have said that you are willing to work with the social partners, and yet at present the greek social partners are no longer free to define the appropriate level of their consultations, with the direct effect of a drastic weakening of the protection of greek workers. so, commissioner, this is a serious breach of european fundamental rights. but you, commissioner, are responsible for ensuring that these fundamental rights are respected, not violated. it is therefore your duty to re-establish european law in greece and to give the social partners back the right to negotiate collective agreements at the level they consider appropriate.

mr president, daesh is a monster, a criminal monster, no one doubts that. in addition to the testimonies of the victims still alive, the mass graves that are discovered every day in syria and iraq bear tragic witness to this. daesh is a criminal monster, guilty of genocide, guilty of the whole panoply of crimes against humanity, for which the initiators, the perpetrators, the financiers, the accomplices and the executors will have to answer to international justice. but criminal monsters have other faces too. what else can be said about those who are now bombing the women and children of aleppo? what else can be said of those who today starve their own people and bomb hospitals in defiance of all the laws of war? in the face of such atrocities, statements are not enough. i ask the european council meeting today not to be content with press releases but to take decisions, to make vladimir putin understand that he has crossed the line and that the european union will not tolerate any more. i am proud to be european, and i don't want to start feeling ashamed of it.
in writing. ‒ i have approved this report, which revises the mechanism for suspending the visa exemption for nationals of certain countries. the activation of this mechanism may be requested by a member state or the commission itself in the event of a sudden and significant increase in the number of irregular migrants from third countries, an influx of unfounded asylum applications by third country nationals, a decrease in the cooperation of a third country with regard to readmission applications and, henceforth, in the event of an increased risk or imminent threat to public policy or national security. the commission will have to examine the request of the member state concerned and take a decision by means of a delegated act, which will require extensive consultations and a thorough examination of the situation. the european parliament will also play a role in this, which was not the case before. he shall be kept informed by the commission and may reject any proposal for extension of the temporary suspension period made by the commission.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the proposal to revise the visa suspension mechanism regulation. since 2001, the union has pursued a visa liberalisation policy with many countries. it therefore has a common list of countries whose nationals must be in possession of a visa to cross the union's borders and a list of countries whose nationals are exempt from this requirement. this proposal for a review is linked to the proposals to grant visa-free access to the union to georgia, ukraine and kosovo. visa liberalisation for an increasing number of countries makes it necessary to establish a temporary visa-restoration mechanism. it may happen that the visa exemption leads to such a massive influx of third country nationals that it becomes difficult to control. security considerations may also result in the reintroduction of certain forms of control, in particular by the reintroduction of visas. in reality, the visa liberalisation policy and the temporary visa-restoration mechanism are the two complementary aspects of a responsible policy on access to the territory of the union.
in writing. i welcome the adoption by the european parliament of a text on the suspension mechanism applicable to visa liberalisation agreements. it aims to facilitate the triggering of the mechanism and to speed up the procedure, since the visa exemption for third-country nationals is to be suspended. the grounds for suspension have also been extended. i would also like to stress the establishment of a monitoring mechanism to ensure that third countries continue to comply with the conditions that prevailed at the time of visa liberalisation.
in writing. ‒ i welcome the adoption of this tool which should bring more flexibility and operability. under the new rules, visa-free agreements with third countries may be suspended, in which case citizens of these countries will again need a visa to travel to the union. both the member states and the european commission will be able to trigger the suspension mechanism. the text underlines that the decision to temporarily suspend the visa waiver must be based on relevant and objective data. after a notification by a member state (or a request from a simple majority of member states), or on the basis of its own report, the commission will have one month to decide whether to suspend the visa exemption for a period of nine months. this decision will take effect automatically. the commission will also be responsible for closely monitoring the situation in the countries benefiting from the visa exemption and for informing parliament and the council, at least once a year, of whether or not the conditions for exemption (in particular with regard to respect for human rights) have been met.
in writing. ‒ n-va is particularly in favour of a strictly revised suspension mechanism, so that we can temporarily suspend and even revoke the visa exemption granted to a certain country if necessary. unfortunately, what's on the table doesn't go far enough. there's been some progress. there will be tighter deadlines and additional grounds for suspension. the visa exemption may be withdrawn when a country refuses to take back rejected asylum seekers and economic migrants. however, there are several elements that call into question the underlying political agenda. is it really the intention to develop an efficient suspension mechanism? does anyone want to use the introduction of this suspension mechanism as an argument to grant a quick visa exemption to, say, turkey? are there sufficient guarantees that this will not circumvent the correct use of the asylum procedure? why is the scope narrowed down to only certain categories of passport holders as opposed to an entire nationality? a strengthened suspension mechanism is necessary, but it must be effective and put in place with the right motivation. there are still too many questions about that today. the n-va delegation, by abstaining, calls for a clear answer to these questions. in any event, we will take the objections and concerns raised into account in considering all future requests for visa exemption.
in writing. ‒ i agree with the rapporteur that from a legal point of view it is desirable and essential that the european parliament be involved in the decision-making process, since the reintroduction of the visa requirement for third-country nationals is one of the most drastic political measures that can be applied. in accordance with the above, the suspension mechanism should be amended as regards the use of delegated acts following the judgment of the court of justice of 16 july 2015, which has already ruled on the issue related to the reciprocity mechanism. the two mechanisms are two sides of the same coin and constitute legislative and policy counterbalances with similar effects, the procedures of which need to be harmonised.
in writing. ‒ i have approved this resolution, which considers that the commission's proposal for an implementing directive is not in line with union law, as it is not compatible with the objective of regulation (eu) 2016/2031, which is to determine the phytosanitary risk posed by any species, strain or biotype of a pathogenic agent, animal or plant parasite harmful to plants or plant products, or with the measures to reduce the risk to an acceptable level.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this objection because, at present, the measures envisaged to prevent the introduction into the union of new plant pests, which attack citrus fruits, are not sufficiently stringent to protect union producers. the draft implementing directive, as proposed by the commission, does not reduce the risks of importing exotic pests. it is therefore urgent to introduce stricter rules to protect citrus fruit in the union and thus prevent the spread of, inter alia, citrus blackheads and false carpocapse. we cannot afford to be passive or passive in the face of this problem. it is important to act quickly!
in writing. during the summer months, europe imports its citrus fruits from third countries. but just as the eu in an open economy sets high standards for food produced and harvested within the eu, we apply the same criteria to food imported. in the specific case of citrus imports, we must be able to offer consumers good quality fruit, but at the same time we must ensure that the feared pathogens do not gain a foothold here. i am very interested in the certification and labelling of foodstuffs. this allows the producer to assure the customer of the best quality of his products and, if a food incident occurs, to address the problem directly at source. that is the proposal for an opinion which i have approved. by imposing preventive cold treatment on imports of citrus fruit for a period of 27 days, the commission has taken a hasty measure which precludes any other effective measure, is not sufficiently scientifically based and will raise prices for citrus fruit on store shelves. i voted against this, not least because you can prevent possible incidents with citrus fruits at source rather than on the way.
in writing. ‒ i supported this resolution, which calls on the commission to amend its directive. the draft implementing directive, as proposed by the commission, does not, as it stands, reduce the risks associated with the import of exotic pests to an acceptable level, which is why we want stricter rules. the european parliament voted against the proposal and wanted to introduce appropriate rules to avoid a tragedy similar to that of the xylella bacteria in the areas of the union that produce citrus fruit. for example, to prevent the introduction into the union of black spot disease of citrus fruits, a fungal disease, it will now be necessary to prove that at least 600 fruit samples from each 30 tonne lot have been checked before packaging and that fruit showing symptoms of the disease are properly tested. citrus fruit potentially infected by a false carpocapsa larva will then have to undergo cold treatment or other equally effective and long-lasting treatments before being imported into the union. the text also aims to improve the traceability of imported citrus fruit.
in writing. - i agree with the rapporteur. i consider that the commission's proposal for an implementing directive is not in accordance with union law, as it is not compatible with the objective of regulation (eu) 2016/2031, which is to determine the phytosanitary risk posed by any species, strain or biotype of a pathogenic agent, animal or plant parasite harmful to plants or plant products.
in writing. ‒ i have approved this joint resolution, which first recalls the tragedy caused by the marketing of thalidomide in the late 1950s and early 1960s, which led to the death or deformation of thousands of newborns in many european countries. it also called on the member states and the commission to coordinate actions and measures to officially recognise and compensate survivors of thalidomide. it also called on the german government to provide access for victims recognised by the thalidomide foundation for the disabled. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environmentally friendly use of energy.
in writing. ‒ i supported this resolution because i am in favour of better access to compensation for thalidomide victims. this german drug, prescribed to pregnant women for morning sickness, caused many malformations and even deaths of newborns in the 1950's and 1960's. following the revelations about the disastrous consequences of taking this medicine, i find it unacceptable that at the present time victims are still fighting for fair compensation in several eu countries. i think it is important that the citizens concerned have access to similar compensation in all the member states. to this end, it is urgent that the european commission establishes a framework protocol at european level under which all eu citizens affected by thalidomide would receive such compensation. it is also important that the commission develops as soon as possible a european programme of aid and support for victims and their families.
it is now more than 50 years since the use of the german-made "safe" drug thalidomide for morning sickness led to many thousands of children being poisoned in the womb and born with severe disabilities. many are still waiting for fair compensation for the daily discomforts and limitations they experience as a result of thalidomide. the resolution urges the german authorities to provide access to the available financial resources for recognised victims so that they have the appropriate means to improve their quality of life.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the european parliament resolution on support for thalidomide survivors. this drug, marketed in the 1950s and 1960s to treat headaches, coughs, insomnia, colds and nausea related to pregnancy, has actually been found to cause newborn deaths and serious birth defects. at the time of the trial against the manufacturer grünenthal gmbh, his guilt could not be established in a genuine manner because of interference in criminal proceedings. in the face of the limited efforts made since then to help thalidomide survivors, the european parliament had already raised its voice at its march 2016 plenary session to underline the urgency of providing assistance and improving the quality of life of those affected by this scandal. the european parliament resolution calls on the member states and the commission to coordinate actions and measures to officially recognise and, above all, compensate survivors of thalidomide, in particular by establishing a framework protocol at european level.
in writing. - i voted for this resolution. the claims of surviving thalidomide victims in europe must be fully recognised in order to ensure their autonomy, access to medical care and a good quality of life. we call on the commission to deliver on the commitments made by commissioner andriukaitis at the parliament's plenary session on 9 march 2016 by establishing an assistance programme that complements member states' action to provide financial support to thalidomide victims and their families.
in writing. – i support this resolution because i think it is important for the victims of thalidomide to get the recognition and support they deserve. many errors have been made in the past, among them a lack of pharmacovigilance, and it is important that the survivors can get compensation for the harm done.
mr president, we need politicians who are committed to supporting access for children to innovative medicines, despite their cost. i therefore cross my fingers for the vote in plenary on thursday, 15 december, and also for the follow-up to be given by the european commission, and i welcome our commissioner, who is here today. i just read you an excerpt from the email, amongst all the others, that i received the day before yesterday. this one is from mrs. heynens, one of the mothers i worked with to write this resolution. rhabdomyosarcoma is the most common soft tissue cancer in children and adolescents. treatment involves chemotherapy, surgery and, in many cases, radiation therapy today. it is obviously a heavy one, and because it is unacceptable that in the last ten years only two innovative medicines specific to children have been developed, we must impose this virtuous circle, force the development of treatments for cancer and other diseases that affect children. protecting the weakest among us is more than ever our mission, it is more than ever europe's mission.
in writing. ‒ i supported, with the whole socialist group, this resolution which aims to amend the regulation on paediatric medicines. the resolution, which was approved by a large majority in the european parliament, calls on the european commission to draw up a detailed report on the obstacles which still hinder innovation in paediatric medicines. on this basis, it will have to make the necessary proposals for amendments to remove these obstacles. in view of the tragedy of childhood cancer, every effort should be made to provide the most effective medical solutions.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this text which calls on the commission to present the report on paediatric medicines in a timely manner and stresses that this report must allow for a full identification and in-depth analysis of the current barriers to innovation in medicines for children. the adopted text also calls on the commission to examine the possibility of amending the regulation on medicinal products for paediatric use, including through legislative revision, to take better account of the following: paediatric development plans which should be based on the mechanism of action and not only on the type of disease; models that should be developed to prioritise diseases and medicines in a way that takes into account unmet paediatric medical needs, incentives that should be put in place to better stimulate research and better meet the needs of the paediatric population, while ensuring that an assessment of research and development costs is carried out and ensuring full transparency of clinical outcomes, etc.
in writing. - i voted for this proposal. we ask the commission to present the report provided for in article 50 of the paediatric medicines regulation in due course. the report should allow a comprehensive identification and in-depth analysis of the current barriers to innovation in paediatric medicines.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour because significantly better access to innovative therapies can save the lives of children and adolescents with life-threatening diseases such as cancer.
in writing. – i fully support the resolution on paediatric medicines because there is clearly a lack of focus on children’s diseases. in general i think we have to set the right framework that offers incentives for these companies to make the large investments necessary in terms of r&d to fill this gap. the paediatric medicines regulation has already addressed this problem to an extent, but revision is necessary, especially in the light of a lack in advances in paediatric oncology and neonatology. we need to do whatever we can from a regulatory perspective to ensure that new and innovative medicines can make it to the patient as fast as possible.
in writing. the right to petition is of great importance as a pillar of european citizenship and an element of participatory democracy. it recognises the right of eu residents and citizens to express directly to the ep their concerns about policies and legislative measures affecting them. in 2015, the european parliament received 1 431 petitions. these mainly concerned the environment, justice, the internal market and fundamental rights. the petitioners use this tool of democracy to make their proposals for european policy-making heard, but also to challenge decisions taken by national authorities, or to denounce shortcomings in the application of eu law.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report, which stresses that the right of petition has the role of strengthening the european parliament's capacity to react, by helping to solve problems related mainly to the application of union law, since petitions which fall within the union's fields of activity and meet the admissibility criteria are a valuable source of information for detecting possible breaches of european legislation. the adopted text calls on the commission to make greater use of its powers to ensure effective implementation of eu legislation, in particular by using the infringement procedure under articles 258 and 260 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union more quickly. in 2015, 431 petitions were received by the committee on petitions, a decrease of 47% compared to 2014, when the european parliament received 2 714 petitions.
in writing. - i voted for this report. the 2015 annual report aims to provide an overview of the work of the committee on petitions, whose timetable does not correspond to the european commission's legislative programme but is set by citizens who, in exercising their right to petition the european parliament, raise concerns about the various union policies and legislative measures. this annual report is intended to give a precise and complete picture of the work of the committee on petitions. it presents statistics on the number of petitions received, processed or closed by the committee on petitions, the countries concerned and the topics covered. these statistics are an important quantitative tool for evaluating the work of the commission. this report also looks at other aspects of the commission's work, such as relations with the other european institutions and with national and regional authorities.
in writing. ‒ as the european commission proposed in its aviation strategy for europe to open negotiations on civil aviation safety with japan and china, and on air services agreements at union level with china, turkey, mexico, six gulf cooperation council member states, armenia and asean, and as parliament's consent is required for the conclusion of international agreements in areas where the ordinary legislative procedure applies, i supported this report which expects the european executive to inform the competent committee of parliament of its intention to propose the opening of negotiations for the conclusion and amendment of international air services agreements.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution, which is the result of a relevant question to the commission. in order to be able to decide whether to give its consent or not at the end of the negotiations, parliament must follow the procedure from the outset. it is also in the interest of the other institutions to identify and resolve as soon as possible any problems which might dissuade parliament from giving its consent in advance.
